**Provisional recommendation.** Reposition L9 as a cross-cutting plane drawn alongside the control-plane components (C1 to C8) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It should have a firm-owned telemetry and evidence spine, and the products should sit on it as replaceable backends [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


## 8. Data extraction, ingestion and web

> L8 turns source material (enterprise documents, scans, spreadsheets, slides, e-mails and web pages) into clean, structured, permission-tagged content that retrieval (L7/L6) and agents can trust. The graphic treats it as a shelf of parsers and scrapers. Since then the products have moved: LlamaParse is now the name of LlamaIndex's whole document platform [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S080: LlamaIndex README (company focus shift to LlamaParse) (LlamaIndex, Inc. (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/run-llama/llama_index/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S008: LlamaParse (formerly LlamaCloud) (LlamaIndex) <https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/framework/llama_cloud/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Mistral OCR is at version 4.1, with 4.0 retired on 30 September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S014: Mistral docs Changelog; OCR 4.0 model page; OCR 4 governance page (Mistral AI) <https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/changelogs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Docling graduated within LF AI & Data in August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S091: Docling - LF AI & Data project page; LF press release 29 April 2025 (IBM contributes Docling, Data Prep Kit, BeeAI) (LF AI & Data Foundation) <https://lfaidata.foundation/projects/docling/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; and Firecrawl's server is AGPL-3.0, with its enterprise controls offered only in the Cloud [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S053: Firecrawl README (Firecrawl (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S079: Open source or Firecrawl Cloud (docs source) (Firecrawl (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docs/main/contributing/open-source-or-cloud.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Of the ten products assessed, only Unstructured's open-source connectors carry access-control metadata into the pipeline [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07], and none emits lineage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S096: OpenLineage README (OpenLineage (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The parsers are commodity components; the enterprise value is in the control plane that wraps them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** standardise on a self-hosted, open document model (Docling as default, Unstructured ingest where connectors with ACLs are needed), put managed parsers and OCR engines behind that model as replaceable engines, and build the lineage, classification, entitlement and incremental-indexing envelope yourself [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 8.1 Responsibility

L8 owns the path from an approved source to an indexed, governed unit of content: source → acquisition → parsing → OCR → structure extraction → cleaning → chunking → metadata → indexing (plan §5), across PDFs and scans, tables, PowerPoint and Excel, websites, e-mails, enterprise documents, structured data and multimodal documents [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The layer has two distinct jobs, and the graphic blurs them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

1. **Acquisition:** getting bytes from a source the firm is entitled to use. Web acquisition (Firecrawl, Crawl4AI, Apify) raises questions of law, terms of service, robots.txt and provenance. Enterprise acquisition (connectors into SharePoint, OneDrive, Confluence, S3) raises questions of entitlements and change detection [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
2. **Document understanding:** turning bytes into faithful structure: text, reading order, tables, figures and their coordinates. Docling, LlamaParse, MinerU, Reducto, Unstructured, Mistral OCR and Google Document AI compete here [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**

- **Downwards (sources and C3).** L8 receives documents only from sources on an approved-source register, and it receives classification and PII policy from C3 [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Upwards (L7 and L6).** L8 hands over chunks wrapped in a metadata envelope (source, version, ACL principals, classification, PII flags, parser manifest, lineage run ID). L7 embeds those chunks and L6 stores them with the envelope intact, so that retrieval-time filtering can enforce entitlements [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Sideways (L4).** L8 is not the agent's live web tool. Firecrawl, Crawl4AI and Apify all expose agent-facing interfaces (MCP or search endpoints) that overlap L4 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S077: Firecrawl Billing (docs source) (Firecrawl (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docs/main/billing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S074: Crawl4AI README (UncleCode / Crawl4AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unclecode/crawl4ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S089: Apify MCP server (docs source) (Apify Technologies s.r.o. (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apify/apify-docs/master/sources/platform/integrations/ai/mcp.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Batch ingestion into a governed corpus belongs to L8. Runtime browsing by an agent belongs to L4 and is governed as a tool call [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **To C8.** Lineage events and parse manifests flow to the governance and evidence store [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 8.2 Why it matters

L8 failures surface as model failures [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A merged table cell becomes a "hallucinated" number; a permission that never reached the index becomes a data leak; a web page with hidden instructions becomes an indirect prompt injection; a parser upgrade silently shifts chunk boundaries [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. ESMA expects "ex-ante input controls and frequent ex-post output controls" for AI used in investment services [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S058: IOSCO FR/02/2026 Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (May 2026) <https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD823.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S059: ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) and 2026 briefings <https://www.esma.europa.eu/document/public-statement-ai-and-investment-services> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. In a RAG system, L8 is where the input controls live [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A multi-asset fund's monthly factsheet has a performance table with fund, benchmark and relative columns. After a routine library upgrade, the parser starts merging two header cells, so the "relative" column shifts one place left for a single share class. Nothing fails: parsing succeeds, chunks are indexed and retrieval works. The commentary agent retrieves last quarter's factsheet as context and repeats a relative-return figure that is really the benchmark return. The reviewer checks the current month's numbers against the attribution engine but not the prior-period comparison that the draft quoted. Nothing in the pipeline records which parser version produced the chunk, so nobody can tell which other documents are affected. The firm has to re-parse and re-review a quarter's corpus by hand. The cause was an unpinned parser and the absence of any table-reconciliation check, not the LLM [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 8.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Table cell exact-match | Share of numeric table cells reproduced exactly (value, sign, unit, row/column) | ≥ 99.5% on a golden set of house documents; 100% for any table feeding a published number | Golden set of factsheets and reports with hand-keyed tables; run on every parser or model change |
| Text fidelity (OCR) | Character error rate on scanned pages | Set per document class; track the trend after each engine change | Sampled pages against reference transcriptions |
| Structural fidelity | Correct reading order, headings and table boundaries | ≥ 95% of sampled pages judged correct | Reviewer sample, stratified by layout type |
| Envelope completeness | Share of indexed chunks carrying source ID, version, ACL, classification, parser manifest and lineage run ID | 100% (hard gate: no envelope, no index) | Index-time validation rule |
| ACL propagation lag | Time from a permission change at source to the index reflecting it | Under 1 hour for confidential sources; under 24 hours otherwise | Synthetic permission-change probes |
| Deletion propagation lag | Time from source deletion to removal from every index and cache | Under 24 hours | Tombstone probes |
| Residual PII rate | PII found after redaction in sampled chunks | Zero for classes that must be masked | Second-pass scanner on samples |
| Reproducibility | Share of re-parses with a pinned manifest that produce identical output hashes | 100% for self-hosted engines; documented exceptions for hosted ones | Periodic re-parse jobs |
| Unapproved-source ingestions | Documents ingested from sources not on the register | Zero | Register check at acquisition |
| Cost per 1,000 pages | All-in parse, OCR and compute cost | Budgeted per document class | FinOps tags (C6) |

### 8.4 How it works

```text
 Approved-source register (owner, licence/ToS, legal basis, default classification, residency)
        |
        v
 [A] ACQUISITION -------------------------------------------------------------+
     web: crawler (robots/ToS checked)     enterprise: connector (+ACL digest) |
        |  raw object + content hash + source version + ACL snapshot         |
        v                                                                     |
 [B] PRE-PARSE CONTROLS: malware/type check -> classification -> PII/DLP (C3) |
        |                                                   (quarantine) <----+
        v
 [C] DOCUMENT UNDERSTANDING (replaceable engines behind one interface)
     layout/parse (Docling | Unstructured | LlamaParse | Reducto | MinerU)
     OCR engine (built-in | Mistral OCR | Document AI)
        |  canonical document model + parse manifest (engine, version, model ID, config hash)
        v
 [D] VALIDATION: table reconciliation, confidence thresholds, injection scan
        |
        v
 [E] CLEAN + CHUNK + METADATA ENVELOPE (source, version, ACL, class, PII, manifest)
        |
        v
 [F] INCREMENTAL INDEX (hash + ACL-digest diff; tombstones) --> L7 embed --> L6 store
        |
        +--> lineage events (OpenLineage run/job/dataset + custom facets) --> C8
```

**Content-type coverage.** Docling covers PDF, DOCX/XLSX/PPTX, legacy Office, HTML, CSV, images, audio and video [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S111: Docling supported formats (docs source) (Docling Project (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/docs/usage/supported_formats.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. MinerU covers PDF, Office, EPUB, OFD, HTML and CSV [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S055: MinerU README (MinerU 4.0) (OpenDataLab MinerU Team (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/master/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. LlamaParse claims 130+ formats [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S080: LlamaIndex README (company focus shift to LlamaParse) (LlamaIndex, Inc. (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/run-llama/llama_index/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. E-mail (with attachments and thread structure) is not documented as a first-class format for any L8 product in the fact base [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Structured data should bypass document parsing and enter through governed data pipelines or L4 tools [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Mechanics by stage.**

- **Acquisition.** Firecrawl respects robots.txt by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S053: Firecrawl README (Firecrawl (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Its X and LinkedIn data are routed through third-party providers at separate prices [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S077: Firecrawl Billing (docs source) (Firecrawl (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docs/main/billing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S053: Firecrawl README (Firecrawl (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07], so the provenance of that content is one step further removed [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. On the enterprise side, Unstructured's SharePoint, OneDrive and Confluence connectors compute a `permissions_version` SHA-256 digest of the ACL at index time. In incremental mode (`reprocess_all=false`, `reprocess_on_permission_change=true`), a change to the ACL alone triggers reprocessing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The connectors also record an unavailable permission fetch separately from an empty permission set [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. That distinction is what stops a failed lookup from being read as "public" [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Parsing and OCR.** Mistral OCR 4 returns paragraph-level bounding boxes, structural block labels and block-level confidence scores [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S135: Mistral OCR 4 : SOTA OCR for Document Intelligence (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/ocr-4/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Google Document AI's Layout Parser includes initial chunking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S101: Document AI pricing (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. MinerU 4.0 adds citation locators for agent reading [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S055: MinerU README (MinerU 4.0) (OpenDataLab MinerU Team (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/master/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Keep coordinates, confidence scores and locators rather than flattening to Markdown; reconciliation and citations depend on them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Validation.** No product in this layer offers reconciliation of parsed tables against an authoritative source; that has to be built [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Firecrawl offers an opt-in prompt-injection check for JSON extraction [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S077: Firecrawl Billing (docs source) (Firecrawl (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docs/main/billing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. No equivalent was found in the document parsers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Lineage.** OpenLineage defines run, job and dataset entities extended by facets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S041: OpenLineage README (OpenLineage (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Its changelog has no GenAI-, LLM-, embedding- or vector-specific facets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S042: OpenLineage CHANGELOG (OpenLineage (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07], so parse, chunk, embed and index steps must be modelled as generic jobs or custom facets [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. OpenLineage supports user-supplied tags facets, which can carry classification labels [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S042: OpenLineage CHANGELOG (OpenLineage (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Apache Airflow ships an OpenLineage provider [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S045: apache-airflow-providers-openlineage on PyPI (PyPI / Apache Software Foundation) <https://pypi.org/pypi/apache-airflow-providers-openlineage/json> accessed 2026-10-07], so an Airflow-orchestrated ingestion pipeline can emit lineage without new tooling [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 8.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security.**

- Treat every ingested document as untrusted input. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 lists ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-OWASP-AGENTIC: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S042: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (launched 9-10 December 2025) (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Indirect injection through documents an agent reads is the L8 route to it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Scan before parsing, and quarantine anything that fails [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Run parsers with no outbound network access, so that a malicious document cannot exfiltrate data [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Data protection.**

- Classify and apply DLP before content reaches any third-party engine, not at the prompt [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Presidio (MIT, now community-governed under Data Privacy Stack) and Google Sensitive Data Protection are the C3 candidates for this step [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S040: Presidio has transitioned to a community-owned project (project_transition.md) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/docs/project_transition.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07].
- Presidio's own README warns that it is not guaranteed to find all sensitive data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S068: Presidio README (GitHub, data-privacy-stack) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/README.MD> accessed 2026-10-07]. Sampling for residual PII is therefore a KPI, not an option [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Entitlements.**

- Capture ACLs at acquisition, carry them on every chunk, and fail closed when the permission fetch fails [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- The Unstructured connector pattern (ACL digest, separate "unavailable" state, reprocess on change) is the reference behaviour to require of any connector, bought or built [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Reproducibility.**

- Pin every engine version and model ID, and write them into a parse manifest stored with the output [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Store parsed outputs, not just raw documents. Docling had reached 2.135.0 by 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S008: PyPI JSON metadata: docling (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/docling/json> accessed 2026-10-07], and Mistral retired OCR 4.0 on 30 September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A hosted model that has been retired cannot reproduce last quarter's parse [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and cost.**

- Route by document class: a cheap OCR tier for simple scans and expensive agentic tiers only for complex layouts [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Published prices differ by more than an order of magnitude between engines. Document AI Enterprise OCR costs US$1.50 per 1,000 pages [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S101: Document AI pricing (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/document-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Mistral OCR 4.1 costs US$4 per 1,000 pages [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Reducto Parse costs US$10 per 1,000 pages [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S113: Reducto Pricing <https://reducto.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. LlamaParse tiers run from 1 to 45 credits per page [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S116: Pricing - LlamaParse documentation (LlamaIndex, Inc.) <https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. All prices are as of 7 October 2026.

**Portability and observability.** Keep one canonical document model in-house with engines behind an adapter; a passing golden-set regression run is the switching test. Emit lineage events and pipeline metrics (quarantine rate, confidence distribution, reconciliation failures) to L9 and C8 [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns** [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- Approved-source register as the only entry point.
- Dual-parse reconciliation for tables that feed numbers.
- Incremental indexing on content hash plus ACL digest, with tombstones for deletions.
- Quarantine queue with human release.
- Parse manifest with every output.

**Anti-patterns** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- Letting a vendor's managed index become the system of record for entitled content.
- Using a model "latest" alias in production.
- Flattening tables to prose before validation.
- Treating an agent's live web fetches as ingestion.
- Indexing first and classifying later.
- Using marketplace scrapers on any non-public data.

### 8.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in L8 |
|---|---|
| Technical capability | Table and layout fidelity on *your* golden set; format coverage; coordinates and confidence output; connector ACL capture |
| Enterprise readiness | SSO, RBAC and audit on the hosted service; support terms; for libraries, an API-server mode |
| Security and compliance | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scoped to the parsing service (and BYOC installs); retention controls; training-use terms; CVE handling for open source |
| Deployment flexibility | Self-hosted, in-VPC or air-gapped options; EU and UK processing regions; network-isolated operation |
| Ecosystem | Connectors to your sources and stores; orchestration and lineage hooks (Airflow, OpenLineage) |
| Reliability and maturity | Deprecation and model-retirement windows; governance (foundation, single maintainer, venture-backed) |
| Cost / TCO | Price per 1,000 pages by tier; GPU needs for self-hosting; licence thresholds; operations burden (browsers, proxies, anti-bot) |
| Lock-in / portability | Open output format; ability to re-parse elsewhere; licence (AGPL, custom thresholds, attribution); platform reach into L6/L3 |

Vendor accuracy claims, such as Unstructured's statement that its API gives 2x table content accuracy and 58% less invented content than the open-source library, are reported claims only [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A1-S075: Unstructured open-source library README (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. They should not be used as decision inputs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

#### Document understanding

**Docling (LF AI & Data Foundation; started by IBM Research).**

IBM Research Zurich started it, IBM donated it to LF AI & Data in March 2025, and it reached Graduate tier in August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S091: Docling - LF AI & Data project page; LF press release 29 April 2025 (IBM contributes Docling, Data Prep Kit, BeeAI) (LF AI & Data Foundation) <https://lfaidata.foundation/projects/docling/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. It runs as a library, CLI, docling-serve REST API (stable v1) or MCP server, and IBM offers a managed "Docling for IBM watsonx" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S082: Docling Serve README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling-serve/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S110: Docling managed service (Docling for IBM watsonx) (docs source) (Docling Project (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/docs/usage/api_server/managed.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The current version is 2.135.0, released 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S008: PyPI JSON metadata: docling (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/docling/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Project hygiene:* it publishes a security policy with private vulnerability reporting, takes part in the OpenSSF Best Practices badge programme and signs its releases on PyPI, Quay.io and GHCR [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S001: Security and Disclosure Information Policy for the Docling Project (Docling Project (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/.github/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08].

The DoclingDocument can serve as the firm's canonical document model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* the README and docs navigation show no ACL, PII or lineage features [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Individual models carry their own licences [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Releases are very frequent, so pinning is mandatory [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* documents must stay in your estate and you want an open format that outlives engine changes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you have no platform team to run a Python service [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Unstructured, MinerU, LlamaParse.
- *FS note:* the default engine for confidential and client documents, provided the parse manifest is recorded [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. Flag: none.** Inherits host controls.

- *Limitations:* model-version churn is the operational risk: about five weeks passed between 4.1 GA and 4.0 retirement [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S130: OCR 4.1 - Mistral AI docs <https://docs.mistral.ai/models/ocr-4-1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S014: Mistral docs Changelog; OCR 4.0 model page; OCR 4 governance page (Mistral AI) <https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/changelogs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. That window is short for a regulated re-validation cycle [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Self-hosting terms and sizing are unpublished [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Audit logs that cannot be exported cannot be held in the firm's own archive, so ask for an export route in due diligence [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you need an EU or self-managed OCR engine behind your own pipeline [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you cannot re-validate within weeks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Google Document AI, Docling's built-in OCR, Reducto.
- *FS note:* pin the dated model ID and treat each retirement as a change-control event [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical. Flag: none.**

Agent, Browser, dashboards and enterprise controls are Cloud-only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S053: Firecrawl README (Firecrawl (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S079: Open source or Firecrawl Cloud (docs source) (Firecrawl (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docs/main/contributing/open-source-or-cloud.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S002: Firecrawl LICENSE (AGPL-3.0) (Firecrawl (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-08]. The privacy policy places servers and data in the US [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S134: Firecrawl Privacy Policy <https://www.firecrawl.dev/privacy-policy> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. ### 8.9 Decision tree

```text
START: Is the source on the approved-source register (owner, licence/ToS, legal basis, classification)?
  ├─ No  → STOP. Register it first. Never ingest from an unregistered source.
  └─ Yes → What kind of source?
      │
      ├─ PUBLIC WEB
      │   ├─ Is this an agent fetching pages at run time?  → Not L8. Govern as an L4 tool call.
      │   ├─ Does robots.txt / ToS permit it, and is the content licensed for this use? No → STOP.
      │   └─ Batch ingestion into a corpus:
      │       ├─ Must processing stay in the EU/UK or in your estate?
      │       │   ├─ Yes → Self-host: Crawl4AI (pilot) or Firecrawl server (after AGPL review)
      │       │   └─ No  → Firecrawl Cloud with ZDR (+ PII redaction if any personal data may appear)
      │       └─ Long-tail site with an existing maintained scraper, public data only → Apify
      │
      └─ ENTERPRISE DOCUMENTS
          ├─ Does the source carry permissions (SharePoint, OneDrive, Confluence)?
          │   └─ Yes → Unstructured ingest connectors (ACL digest, reprocess on change),
          │            or build a connector that meets the same contract. Fail closed.
          ├─ May the content leave your estate (classification, client contract, residency)?
          │   ├─ No  → Self-hosted engine: Docling (default); MinerU only after licence review;
          │   │        Mistral OCR self-managed or Reducto on-prem if a commercial engine is needed
          │   └─ Yes, region-bound →
          │        ├─ EU/UK required → Mistral OCR (EU API), LlamaParse EU, Reducto EU endpoint,
          │        │                   Unstructured in-VPC
          │        └─ GCP is the approved cloud → Google Document AI (confirm processor region)
          ├─ Mostly scans or handwriting? → put an OCR engine behind the parser interface;
          │                                 route by confidence score
          └─ Do tables feed numbers anyone will quote?
              └─ Yes → dual-parse + reconciliation; quarantine on mismatch; numbers stay
                       non-authoritative (authoritative figures come from L4 data tools)
```

### 8.10 Lock-in classification

| Class | Where it applies | Rationale | Abstraction to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Acceptable** | Docling; the Unstructured open-source library and connectors; OCR engines (Mistral OCR, Document AI OCR) used purely as OCR | Docling is MIT under neutral governance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S057: Docling README (Docling Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/docling-project/docling/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07], and Unstructured's library is Apache-2.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S011: PyPI JSON metadata: unstructured (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/unstructured/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. An OCR engine's text-plus-coordinates output is easy to swap once a golden set exists [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. | A canonical document model (DoclingDocument or an in-house JSON schema) and an engine adapter interface [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| **Manageable** | LlamaParse Parse/Extract; Reducto; Firecrawl Cloud; Unstructured Transform API | All four have proprietary APIs or credit models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S116: Pricing - LlamaParse documentation (LlamaIndex, Inc.) <https://developers.llamaindex.ai/llamaparse/general/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A1-S093: Reducto Python SDK API reference (api.md) (Reducto (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reductoai/reducto-python-sdk/main/api.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S079: Open source or Firecrawl Cloud (docs source) (Firecrawl (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-docs/main/contributing/open-source-or-cloud.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Outputs can be converted into your model, so switching costs a re-parse plus a regression run [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. | The same adapter; store your own copy of every parsed output; keep the parse manifest [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| **Unacceptable** | A vendor-managed index (for example LlamaParse Index) as the system of record for entitled content; Apify Actors in core pipelines; MinerU above its thresholds without a commercial licence; a modified Firecrawl server exposed without AGPL compliance | These create regulatory or legal exposure. An index outside your L6 store weakens entitlement and erasure control. Third-party Actors are outside Apify's control [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S086: Apify shared responsibility model (docs source) (Apify Technologies s.r.o. (GitHub docs source)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apify/apify-docs/master/sources/platform/security/shared-responsibility.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. MinerU rights terminate on breach [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S054: MinerU Open Source License (OpenDataLab MinerU Team (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opendatalab/MinerU/master/LICENSE.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. | Keep indexing in your own L6 store; keep licences in the OSS register; scrape only via reviewed code [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |

### 8.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Ingestion is where data decisions are made.** Residency, PII classification and entitlements are decided when a document is acquired and parsed; once a document has gone to a third-party parser and been indexed without its ACL, no prompt-level control can undo that [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Model risk (SS1/23, SR 26-2).**

- SS1/23 applies to vendor models and is technology-agnostic [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Its Principle 1.1(b) lets firms apply relevant MRM aspects to material, complex deterministic quantitative methods that are not models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S061: SS1/23 model definition and Principle 1.1(b); PS6/23 feedback (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2023/ss123.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and expressly excludes generative and agentic AI. For out-of-scope tools, the firm's own governance applies [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Parsers are not themselves "models" in either definition [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. They are, however, data-preparation components whose errors flow straight into an LLM's inputs. The inventory should record parser and OCR engine versions as dependencies of each AI use case [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**

- Annex III high-risk duties apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S012: AI Act (regulatory framework page) and AI Act Service Desk FAQ (European Commission) <https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The commentary agent is not an Annex III use case [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Where a high-risk deployment does arise, Article 26 requires relevant and representative input data where the deployer controls it, and logs kept for at least six months [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S016: AI Act Article 26 Obligations of deployers; Article 25 Responsibilities along the AI value chain (European Commission AI Act Service Desk) <https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-26> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S017: AI Act Annex III; Article 27 FRIA; Article 72 post-market monitoring (European Commission AI Act Service Desk) <https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-3> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S018: AI Act Article 50 Transparency obligations; Commission Article 50 guidelines C(2026) 5054 (European Commission) <https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-50> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Separately, ESMA expects ex-ante input controls and due diligence on third-party AI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S059: ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) and 2026 briefings <https://www.esma.europa.eu/document/public-statement-ai-and-investment-services> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. L8 validation and the approved-source register are those controls [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Third parties (DORA, PS7/26, SYSC 8).**

- **DORA.** DORA requires a register of information covering all ICT third-party arrangements, and Article 30 contract terms [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. For an EU entity, every SaaS parser or crawler is such an arrangement [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Concentration.** The first CTPP list (19 providers) includes hyperscalers such as Google Cloud EMEA Limited, and no AI model provider [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S020: The ESAs designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA (with List_of_designated_CTPPs.pdf, 18 Nov 2025) (EBA / ESMA / EIOPA (Joint ESAs)) <https://www.eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/european-supervisory-authorities-designate-critical-ict-third-party-providers-under-digital> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S022: DORA's CTPP Oversight Regime: From Designation to Litigation (with ESAs JC 2026 Work Programme) (Oxford Business Law Blog) <https://blogs.law.ox.ac.uk/oblb/blog-post/2026/04/doras-ctpp-oversight-regime-designation-litigation> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Specialist L8 vendors are therefore overseen only through the firm's own third-party risk management [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **UK.** PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A hosted parser that processes client documents for an important business service could be such an arrangement [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **FCA FG16/5.** The guidance covers data location, effective access, concentration and exit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Exit is cheap only if the firm holds its own parsed outputs in an open model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 8.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

The performance-attribution commentary agent drafts monthly Brinson-style commentary (allocation, selection, currency) for a generic multi-asset fund. A portfolio manager approves every draft. L8 supplies three corpora [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

| Corpus | Source class | L8 treatment [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|
| Fund factsheets (prior months) | Internal, approved; contains tables | Self-hosted Docling. Dual-parse every performance table and reconcile it against the stored attribution output for that period; quarantine on any mismatch. Tag every numeric cell as `document_derived=true`. |
| Prior commentaries and house style guide | Internal, entitlement-restricted per fund and client | Connector with ACL capture (Unstructured ingest pattern). Chunks carry fund ID, client restrictions and approval status. Draft commentaries are excluded; only approved versions are indexed. |
| Market notes | Third-party research and public sources on the register only | Licence and redistribution terms recorded on the register entry. Web content is acquired in batch by a self-hosted crawler and injection-scanned. No live web fetching by the agent. |

**What the agent needs from L8** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- Retrievable prior commentary with citations back to a specific document version.
- House-style passages that are current, not superseded.
- Market context only from approved sources.
- Enough metadata for the evidence pack (C8) to record which chunks, from which document versions, parsed by which engine versions, were in context.

**What L8 must never do** [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- **Supply a number as authoritative.** Every figure in the commentary comes from the attribution engine through read-only L4 tools. Numbers parsed from documents are context only, and the L9 numeric-faithfulness eval checks the draft against the engine output, not against parsed text. A parsing error must never be able to become a published figure.
- **Ingest from a source that is not on the register.** This includes an analyst's ad-hoc upload of a broker note whose licence has not been checked.
- **Index a document without its ACL, or index it as "public" when the permission fetch failed.**
- **Send client-identifying content to a parser outside the approved residency.**
- **Lose the parse manifest.** Without it, last month's draft cannot be reproduced.

- No L8 product emits lineage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S094: unstructured-ingest CHANGELOG (Unstructured Technologies (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Unstructured-IO/unstructured-ingest/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A1-S096: OpenLineage README (OpenLineage (LF AI & Data)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

The provisional architecture has six components [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
1. **Approved-source register.** The single entry point. It records owner, licence or ToS, legal basis, default classification and residency.
2. **Acquisition contract.** Every connector, bought or built, must emit a content hash, source version and ACL snapshot or digest. It must have a distinct "permission unavailable" state that fails closed.
3. **Pre-parse classification and DLP** using a C3 engine (Presidio or a cloud DLP service). This step decides which parsers a document may be routed to.
4. **Parse manifest.** Engine, version, model ID and config hash, stored with the canonical document model output.
5. **Metadata envelope on every chunk**, enforced as an index gate: source, version, ACL principals, classification, PII flags, manifest, and lineage run ID.
6. **Lineage and incremental indexing.** OpenLineage events with custom facets, emitted from the orchestrator (for example the Airflow OpenLineage provider). The index diffs on content hash and ACL digest, and tombstones propagate deletions to L6 and caches.

The open question for synthesis is whether this control plane is an L8 sub-layer or part of C3/C8. The provisional view is that it lives in L8, with policies supplied by C3 and evidence consumed by C8 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.


## 7. Embeddings and reranking

> **Executive summary.** This layer turns text, and now images, audio and PDF pages, into vectors that a retrieval store can search. It then reorders the candidates so that the few passages handed to the model are the right ones. Three things have changed since the original graphic.
