Choose the models by in-domain evaluation. For regulated data, prefer options that run in your own estate or in a verified region [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 7.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- **Representation.** Encoding chunks and queries into a vector space in which "similar meaning" means "near". This covers dense vectors and, increasingly, sparse and multi-vector forms.
- **Precision at the top.** Reordering the first-stage candidates with a more expensive model (a cross-encoder or listwise reranker) so that the top 5–10 results are correct.
- **Version discipline.** Making sure every vector in an index came from one known model version with one known configuration (dimensions, quantisation, instructions).

**Hand-offs** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

| Direction | Layer | What crosses the boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Below (input) | L8 ingestion | Clean chunks with lineage, classification and access-control metadata. L7 never decides who may see a chunk. |
| Beside | L6 stores | Vectors, sparse terms and metadata are written to the store. At query time the store does filtered first-stage retrieval and fusion. |
| Above | L3 orchestration, L1 models | A short, ranked, entitlement-filtered context list with scores and document identifiers. |
| Across | L9, C5, C8 | Retrieval metrics feed L9. Model and version identifiers are C5 configuration. Retrieved document IDs and scores go into the C8 evidence pack. |

**A boundary that has moved.** The reranker is no longer always an L7 service. MongoDB runs Voyage cross-encoders inside an aggregation stage (`$rerank`, public preview, 8.3+) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Pinecone hosts its own reranker, Cohere Rerank 3.5 and bge-reranker-v2-m3 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S101: Introducing cascading retrieval: Unifying dense and sparse with reranking (Pinecone) <https://www.pinecone.io/blog/cascading-retrieval/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Elastic's `semantic_text` field embeds automatically and defaults to Jina v5 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The responsibility still belongs to L7 even when the compute runs in L6: someone must own the model choice, the version pin and the evaluation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 7.2 Why it matters

**What breaks when this layer is badly designed** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Silent relevance decay.** The system still returns something, so nobody notices it is wrong.
- **Mixed-version indexes.** Scores from two model versions are not comparable; quality drops without an error.
- **Unplanned re-embedding.** A model is retired or replaced and the corpus must be re-processed under time pressure.
- **Entitlement leakage through ranking.** A reranker will promote another client's document if unfiltered candidates reach it.
- **Cost surprises.** Full-precision 3,072-dimension vectors held in memory across a large corpus. Cohere's own worked example shows 100M chunks shrinking from about 819 GB to 3.2 GB once reduced dimensions and binary output are used [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S013: Embed 5: Frontier Embedding Models for Enterprise (Cohere) <https://cohere.com/blog/embed-5> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A platform team upgrades its embedding model on a Friday, applying the new model to the ingestion pipeline and to the query path. Nobody re-embeds the existing 4 million chunks. New documents land in the new vector space; old documents remain in the old one. Queries are now embedded with the new model and compared against mostly old vectors. Nothing errors. Over the next fortnight the commentary assistant starts citing last month's market notes and missing the house style guide, which has not changed since the spring. The defect is found only when an analyst asks why the draft quotes a superseded style rule. Nothing records which model produced which vectors, so the team cannot tell which documents are affected and has to rebuild the whole index. The controls that would have stopped it are a model-version tag on every vector, a query path that refuses to mix versions, and a retrieval regression suite in L9 run on every configuration change.

### 7.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recall@k (first stage) | Share of golden-set queries whose relevant chunk appears in the top k candidates (k = 50–100) | ≥ 0.95 on the in-domain golden set | L9 offline evaluation on a labelled query set, on every model or config change |
| nDCG@10 / precision@5 (after rerank) | Ranking quality of the final context list | Agreed baseline; no regression > 2 points on release | Same golden set, graded relevance labels |
| Entitlement-violation rate | Retrieved items the requester is not entitled to see | 0, as a hard gate | Synthetic cross-tenant probe queries in CI and production canaries |
| Version consistency | Share of vectors in a live index carrying the index's declared model-version tag | 100% | Index metadata audit job |
| p95 query-embedding latency | Time to embed one query | < 100 ms in-region | Gateway or service traces (OTel spans) |
| p95 rerank latency | Time to rerank the candidate set | < 300 ms for 50 candidates | Service traces; alert on breach |
| Cost per 1,000 queries | Embedding plus rerank cost | Tracked and budgeted per use case | C6 FinOps attribution |
| Full re-embed time | Wall-clock time to re-embed the corpus into a shadow index | Inside the agreed change window; tested twice a year | Dry-run migration |
| Multilingual parity gap | Recall gap between English and other in-scope languages | ≤ 5 points | Golden set stratified by language |

The targets are starting points for a firm to calibrate. They are not industry benchmarks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 7.4 How it works

**Two paths share one model configuration.** At ingestion, each chunk is embedded (dense) and, where used, encoded as sparse terms. Both are written to the store with metadata: source, classification, entitlements, model version and chunk hash. At query time the query is embedded with the same model version. The store runs a filtered dense search and a lexical (BM25) or sparse search, fuses the two lists, and passes the top candidates to a reranker that reads query and passage together [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
INGESTION (L8 -> L7 -> L6)
 chunk + lineage + ACL metadata
   -> embedding service [model=X, version=v3, dims=1024, quant=int8]
   -> dense vector + sparse terms + {model_version, chunk_hash, acl, fund_id}
   -> store index "commentary_v3"          (raw text retained)
QUERY (L3 -> L7/L6 -> L3)
 query + caller identity
   -> embed query with SAME model_version as target index
   -> L6: entitlement filter FIRST (acl, fund_id, client_id)
        -> dense ANN top-100  +  BM25/sparse top-100
        -> fuse (RRF or weighted)
   -> reranker [model=R, version=r2] on top-50 (already filtered)
   -> top-5..10 with doc_id, scores, versions  -> L3 / L1
   -> trace to L9 and the C8 evidence pack
```

**The mechanics that matter for decisions:**

- **Bi-encoder vs cross-encoder.** An embedding model encodes query and document separately, so documents can be pre-computed. That is fast, but it is coarse [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A reranker reads the query and each candidate together. That is slower, but more precise, which is why it is applied only to a short candidate list [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Current rerankers take long inputs: Cohere Rerank 4 handles 32K tokens and JSON documents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S009: Rerank 4: Cohere's Most Powerful Reranker Yet <https://cohere.com/blog/rerank-4> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Voyage rerank-3 has a 32K-token context [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S034: rerank-3 and rerank-3-lite: the next generation of Voyage rerankers (Voyage AI (MongoDB)) <https://blog.voyageai.com/2026/09/30/rerank-3/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Jina reranker v3.5 is listwise, scoring candidates jointly [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S026: jina-reranker-v3.5: Faster Listwise Reranking with Hybrid Attention and Self-Distillation (Jina AI (Elastic)) <https://jina.ai/en-US/news/jina-reranker-v3-5-faster-listwise-reranking-hybrid-attention-self-distillation/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Sparse plus dense.** Lexical matching catches exact identifiers that dense vectors blur: fund codes, ISINs, share-class names [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Fusion is now a store feature: Qdrant weighted RRF [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S103: Qdrant 1.17 - Relevance Feedback & Search Latency Improvements <https://qdrant.tech/blog/qdrant-1.17.x/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Elasticsearch RRF and linear retrievers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], MongoDB `$rankFusion`/`$scoreFusion` [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Pinecone "cascading retrieval" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S101: Introducing cascading retrieval: Unifying dense and sparse with reranking (Pinecone) <https://www.pinecone.io/blog/cascading-retrieval/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] and pgvector `sparsevec` [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S063: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector project) <https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Sentence Transformers trains Sparse Encoders [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Evidence for the two-stage pattern.** Anthropic reports that contextual embeddings plus contextual BM25 cut top-20 retrieval failures by 49%, and that adding a reranker raised the cut to 67% [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A2-S070: Introducing Contextual Retrieval (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval> accessed 2026-10-07]. The author is an Anthropic model, so this is one vendor's measurement on its own data. It shows direction, not a decision input [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Matryoshka dimensions and quantisation.** Several models let you truncate vectors and lower precision with a controlled loss:
  - Gemini Embedding 2: 128–3,072 dims [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S005: Embeddings (Gemini API docs) / Gemini Embedding 2 preview model (Google) <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
  - Cohere Embed 5: 256–2,048 dims; float, int8 and binary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S012: Announcing Cohere's Embed 5 Models <https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/embed-v5> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
  - voyage-4: 256–2,048 dims, with binary among its quantisation options [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S007: Voyage AI Embedding and Reranking Models Overview - Voyage AI by MongoDB <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/models/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S006: The Voyage 4 model family: shared embedding space with MoE architecture (Voyage AI (MongoDB)) <https://blog.voyageai.com/2026/01/15/voyage-4/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
  - Qwen's hosted model: 64–2,048 dims [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S022: Embedding - Alibaba Cloud Model Studio <https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/embedding> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]
  - OpenAI: a `dimensions` parameter [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S001: text-embedding-3-large Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-large> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]

  Stores quantise as well: Elasticsearch uses BBQ quantisation by default since 9.1 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Dimension and precision are therefore index-design parameters, and they must be recorded with the model version [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Shared embedding spaces.** Voyage 4 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S006: The Voyage 4 model family: shared embedding space with MoE architecture (Voyage AI (MongoDB)) <https://blog.voyageai.com/2026/01/15/voyage-4/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Cohere Embed 5 Pro/Fast [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S012: Announcing Cohere's Embed 5 Models <https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/embed-v5> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] and Jina v5-omni and v5-text [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S025: jina-embeddings-v5-omni: Embeddings for Text, Image, Audio and Video (Jina AI (Elastic)) <https://jina.ai/news/jina-embeddings-v5-omni-multimodal-embeddings-for-text-image-audio-and-video/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] put several model sizes in one space. You can index with the large model and query with the small one. This reduces re-embedding inside a family; it does nothing for a move between vendors [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Contextualised chunks and late interaction.** voyage-context-4 embeds a chunk with awareness of its surrounding document [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S007: Voyage AI Embedding and Reranking Models Overview - Voyage AI by MongoDB <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/models/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Sentence Transformers v6 added a Multi-Vector Encoder for ColBERT-style late interaction [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S028: Sentence Transformers is joining Hugging Face! <https://huggingface.co/blog/sentence-transformers-joins-hf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. ColPali-style page-image retrieval was not evidenced in this research [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Multimodal.** Gemini Embedding 2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S004: Gemini Embedding 2 is now generally available (Google) <https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-embedding-2-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Jina v5-omni [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S025: jina-embeddings-v5-omni: Embeddings for Text, Image, Audio and Video (Jina AI (Elastic)) <https://jina.ai/news/jina-embeddings-v5-omni-multimodal-embeddings-for-text-image-audio-and-video/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Cohere Embed 5 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S012: Announcing Cohere's Embed 5 Models <https://docs.cohere.com/changelog/embed-v5> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], voyage-multimodal-3.5 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S007: Voyage AI Embedding and Reranking Models Overview - Voyage AI by MongoDB <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/models/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], NVIDIA VL models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S031: Get Started With NVIDIA NeMo Retriever Embedding NIM (2.3) <https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/nemo-retriever/embedding/2.3/getting-started.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] and Qwen3-VL [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S021: Qwen3-VL-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Reranker: A Unified Framework for State-of-the-Art Multimodal Retrieval and Ranking (Alibaba Qwen (arXiv)) <https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04720> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] embed images alongside text. This matters for scanned factsheets and charts; text-first corpora gain little [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Benchmarks.** The MTEB results repository was still maintained on 21 September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S046: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (GitHub organisation) (MTEB project) <https://github.com/embeddings-benchmark> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The live leaderboard could not be fetched, so this section asserts no current ranking [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Vendor scores quoted anywhere in this section are [R] and are not decision inputs.

### 7.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Embeddings derived from client or personal data are a derivative of that data. Classify, retain and delete them with the source.
- Enforce entitlements in the store's pre-filter, before ANN search, fusion and reranking. Never post-filter after the reranker, and never rely on the reranker to "down-rank" forbidden content.
- The operative reference is the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S041: OWASP GenAI Security Project Unveils 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications, New Agent Control Standard <https://genai.owasp.org/2026/09/01/owasp-genai-security-project-unveils-2026-top-10-for-llm-applications-new-agent-control-standard-and-sponsors-as-community-tops-30000-members/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Its full contents were not retrieved, so its identifier for this risk is not given [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. For traceability, the 2025 list named it LLM08 "Vector and Embedding Weaknesses" [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A8-S040: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-llm-applications-2025/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Scalability and cost** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Choose dimensions and quantisation per index tier, by measurement.
- Batch ingestion through Batch APIs where offered. OpenAI's Batch API halves the 3-large price, and Gemini's Batch is 50% of standard [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S035: text-embedding-3-small Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-small> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S005: Embeddings (Gemini API docs) / Gemini Embedding 2 preview model (Google) <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Cap the rerank candidate count (typically 25–100) and measure the recall it buys.

**Resilience** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Hosted embedding APIs are on the query path. An outage stops retrieval even if the store is healthy.
- Keep a warm fallback route for the same model, such as a second region or a marketplace deployment, or degrade to lexical search.
- Never fall back to a *different* embedding model against the same index.

**Governance and change** [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Treat `{embedding model, version, dims, quantisation, instruction prefix}` and `{reranker model, version, candidate k}` as versioned C5 configuration, promoted through environments with an L9 regression gate.
- Write the configuration hash into every vector's metadata and every trace.

**Observability** [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Emit spans for embed, retrieval, fusion and rerank with model version, latency and top document IDs.

**Portability** [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Always store the raw chunk text and its hash next to the vector, so you can re-embed without re-parsing.
- Put an internal embedding-service interface in front of every provider.

**Patterns**

| Pattern | Use |
|---|---|
| Dual-index migration (blue/green) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Build `index_v4` in shadow from stored raw text. Run both, compare on the golden set and on shadow traffic, switch the read alias, keep `index_v3` until the rollback window closes. |
| Hybrid first stage + cross-encoder rerank [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Default for enterprise text. Lexical catches identifiers; dense catches paraphrase; the reranker fixes the order. |
| Index-large / query-small in a shared space [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Cuts query latency and cost within one vendor family. |
| Domain fine-tune of an open model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Use Sentence Transformers to adapt an Apache-2.0 model on in-domain pairs when vendor models underperform on house vocabulary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07]. |

**Anti-patterns** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}
- Mixing model versions in one index.
- Selecting a model from a leaderboard instead of an in-domain test.
- Post-rerank entitlement filtering.
- Letting a store auto-embed with a default model nobody pinned.
- Discarding raw text after embedding.
- Treating rerank scores as calibrated probabilities across queries.

**What re-embedding actually costs.** The API bill is the small part. A corpus of 2 million chunks at about 500 tokens each is roughly 1 billion tokens. At list prices as of 7 October 2026 that is about US$130 with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, about US$60 with voyage-4, or about US$120 with Cohere Embed 5 Pro [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S001: text-embedding-3-large Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-large> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S007: Voyage AI Embedding and Reranking Models Overview - Voyage AI by MongoDB <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/models/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S013: Embed 5: Frontier Embedding Models for Enterprise (Cohere) <https://cohere.com/blog/embed-5> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The arithmetic is the author's own [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The real costs are elsewhere [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- running a second index in parallel
- re-running the retrieval evaluation and any downstream answer-quality evaluation
- revalidation and change-control evidence
- the migration window

This is why model version belongs in production configuration and in the exit plan.

### 7.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical capability | Recall and nDCG on **your** golden set, in your languages and document types; reranker availability; Matryoshka and quantisation; context length; sparse, multi-vector and multimodal support; domain models |
| Enterprise readiness | SSO, RBAC and audit logs for the console and API keys; per-project keys; usage reporting; support and model-retirement notice periods (ask for them in writing) |
| Security and compliance | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope covering the **embedding endpoint**; ZDR; CMK; DPA; sub-processors |
| Deployment flexibility | In-region processing (UK and EU separately); VPC or marketplace deployment; self-hosting and air-gap |
| Ecosystem | Native support in your L6 store; Sentence Transformers or vLLM compatibility for open models; marketplace availability |
| Reliability and maturity | GA vs preview status; deprecation policy; model-retirement history; ownership stability |
| Cost / TCO | Per-token price, Batch discount, rerank pricing basis (per search or per token), GPU and licence cost if self-hosted, storage effect of dimensions |
| Lock-in / portability | Weights availability and licence; shared-space families; store bundling; re-embedding cost |

**Enterprise controls for hosted embedding APIs are unevenly documented.** The CP2 review found SSO, RBAC and audit-log documentation for the OpenAI API platform [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S004: Single sign-on (SSO) setup for OpenAI products <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9534785-configuring-sso> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REV-S005: Manage permissions in the OpenAI platform <https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rbac> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REV-S006: Admin and Audit Logs API for the API Platform (OpenAI) <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9687866-admin-and-audit-logs-api-for-the-api-platform> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], IAM and audit logging on Google Cloud [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S007: Agent Platform access control with IAM (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REV-S008: Agent Platform audit logging information (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/audit-logging> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and SSO and RBAC on Elastic Cloud for the Elastic Inference Service route [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S019: Elastic Cloud Feature Matrix (and EIS, Jina models docs) (Elastic N.V.) <https://www.elastic.co/subscriptions/cloud> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Cohere documents only Owner and User team roles for its hosted platform [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S013: Teams and Roles on the Cohere Platform <https://docs.cohere.com/reference/teams-and-roles> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and Voyage's Atlas API is accessed by model API keys [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S018: Voyage AI: Embeddings and Rerankers (MongoDB product page and docs) (MongoDB, Inc.) <https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/ai-search-and-retrieval> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], which Atlas organisation and project roles govern [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S028: Manage Voyage AI Model API Keys (and Organization and Project Access) (MongoDB, Inc.) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/management/api-keys/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Under the user's CP2 answers, any one verified control lifts the NPV cap to 3 (rule 7), and services consumed through AWS, Azure or Google Cloud inherit the platform's IAM, SSO and audit logging as presumed, scoring 4 (rule 6). On that basis Gemini Embedding scores 4 through Vertex AI, Cohere 4 through Microsoft Foundry or SageMaker (3 on its direct API), and Voyage 3 on Atlas [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. These controls usually come from the platform account already contracted for L1, so verify them per endpoint in due diligence; platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 7.7 Product deep dives

Each deep dive gives the current state as tagged facts, then judgement. Totals are FS-weighted.

**OpenAI embeddings: text-embedding-3-large / -3-small (OpenAI).**
- *What it is now:* OpenAI's embeddings are still the text-embedding-3 generation, released 25 January 2024; no newer model was found as of 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S001: text-embedding-3-large Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-large> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S002: New embedding models and API updates (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/new-embedding-models-and-api-updates/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. 3-large defaults to 3,072 dimensions, can be shortened with `dimensions`, and accepts 8,192 tokens [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S001: text-embedding-3-large Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-large> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S003: Vector embeddings (guide) (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/embeddings> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Prices are US$0.13 per 1M tokens for 3-large (US$0.065 on Batch) and US$0.02 for 3-small [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S001: text-embedding-3-large Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-large> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S035: text-embedding-3-small Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-small> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No OpenAI reranker was found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S001: text-embedding-3-large Model (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-large> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Residency and certifications:* the endpoint is ZDR-eligible and in scope for EU storage and processing, which requires Modified Abuse Monitoring or ZDR; the UK is storage-only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S144: Data controls in the OpenAI platform <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Certifications include SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27701, and a HIPAA BAA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S036: Security and privacy at OpenAI <https://openai.com/security-and-privacy/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S144: Data controls in the OpenAI platform <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Access control:* the API platform documents SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM, organisation and project roles with custom roles, an Admin API and audit logs of administrative events [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S004: Single sign-on (SSO) setup for OpenAI products <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9534785-configuring-sso> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REV-S005: Manage permissions in the OpenAI platform <https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rbac> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REV-S006: Admin and Audit Logs API for the API Platform (OpenAI) <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9687866-admin-and-audit-logs-api-for-the-api-platform> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* a stable, cheap, well-controlled text baseline [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* it is text-only, hosted-only and has no reranker. The generation is ageing, and its successor's timing is unknown [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Audit logs exclude request content and are kept on a best-effort basis [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S006: Admin and Audit Logs API for the API Platform (OpenAI) <https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9687866-admin-and-audit-logs-api-for-the-api-platform> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], so they must be exported to the firm's archive [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* OpenAI is already the approved L1 provider and EU processing under ZDR suffices [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* UK processing or self-hosting is required [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Gemini Embedding, Cohere, Voyage.
- *FS note:* exit means re-embedding everything [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical. Flag: none.** FS 3.20.

**Gemini Embedding 2 (Google).**
- *What it is now:* gemini-embedding-2 went GA on 22 April 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S004: Gemini Embedding 2 is now generally available (Google) <https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-embedding-2-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. It maps text, images, video, audio and PDFs into one space across 100+ languages, with Matryoshka output from 128 to 3,072 dims [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S004: Gemini Embedding 2 is now generally available (Google) <https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-embedding-2-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S005: Embeddings (Gemini API docs) / Gemini Embedding 2 preview model (Google) <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. It runs on the Gemini API and on Vertex AI, now documented as Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, with global, us and eu endpoints [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S039: Data residency (Vertex AI generative AI) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The eu multi-region excludes the UK and Switzerland [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S039: Data residency (Vertex AI generative AI) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Text costs US$0.20 per 1M tokens online and US$0.10 on Batch (as of 7 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S038: Gemini Developer API pricing (Google) <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Certifications:* Generative AI on Vertex AI holds SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001, HIPAA and FedRAMP High, but per-model coverage is not confirmed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S043: Cloud compliance and regulations resources (Vertex AI) (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/vertexai-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Under CP2 rule 8 that scores security 4, not 5 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Access control:* access runs through Google Cloud IAM (predefined, custom and endpoint-level roles) and Cloud Audit Logs, where Data Access logs for predict calls must be switched on [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S007: Agent Platform access control with IAM (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/access-control> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REV-S008: Agent Platform audit logging information (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/audit-logging> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Under the CP2 hyperscaler presumption (rule 6), enterprise readiness scores 4 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Strengths:* a natively multimodal option with strong platform certifications [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* it is hosted-only and has been GA for under six months. The `task_type` parameter is unsupported [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S005: Embeddings (Gemini API docs) / Gemini Embedding 2 preview model (Google) <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Google's reranker is a separate service, the Vertex ranking API (semantic-ranker models, with version 005 in preview from 1 September 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REV-S026: Improve search and RAG quality with ranking API (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/generative-ai-app-builder/docs/ranking> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* the estate is Google Cloud-centred and the content is multimodal [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* UK-only processing is mandatory [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Cohere, Voyage, Jina.
- *FS note:* Google Cloud EMEA Limited is a designated DORA CTPP and UK CTP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S020: The ESAs designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA (with List_of_designated_CTPPs.pdf, 18 Nov 2025) (EBA / ESMA / EIOPA (Joint ESAs)) <https://www.eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/european-supervisory-authorities-designate-critical-ict-third-party-providers-under-digital> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Consuming the model through Vertex AI therefore places it with a designated provider, but the firm's own SYSC 8 or SS2/21 duties remain [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: where Google Cloud is your primary cloud (CP3 Q2, rubric rule 10) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Flag: none.** FS 3.20. It is Google's lead embedding model, consumed through Vertex AI; the condition excludes estates where UK-only processing is mandatory, because the eu multi-region excludes the UK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S039: Data residency (Vertex AI generative AI) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Deployment and lock-in at 2 are accepted under rule 11 because the condition is an existing platform commitment, and the dual-index migration route in this section limits the re-embedding cost of exit [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 7.9 Decision tree

```text
START: a corpus to make retrievable (one decision per corpus / index)
1. Does the corpus contain client, personal or confidential data?
   ├─ No  → go to 3 (any approved hosted API is acceptable)
   └─ Yes → 2
2. Where may it be processed?
   ├─ Only inside our estate (or air-gapped)
   │    ├─ Need vendor support?
   │    │    ├─ Yes, NVIDIA AI Enterprise already licensed → NVIDIA NeMo Retriever NIMs
   │    │    ├─ Yes, otherwise → Cohere private / on-prem deployment
   │    │    │                   (or Jina on-prem licence if Elastic is the store)
   │    │    └─ No → Sentence Transformers serving an Apache-2.0 model
   │    │            (Qwen3 only after provenance review; voyage-4-nano is another option)
   ├─ UK processing required
   │    └─ None of the hosted APIs here verified UK processing for embeddings
   │       → treat as "own estate" (above) or a VPC/marketplace deployment in a UK
   │         region (Cohere on SageMaker/Foundry, Voyage on SageMaker); confirm the region
   └─ EU processing acceptable
        ├─ Store is MongoDB → Voyage via Atlas EEA Geography (accept preview status,
        │                    obtain the SOC 2 report)
        ├─ Store is Elasticsearch → Jina via Elastic Inference Service (pin the model)
        ├─ Google-centred estate, multimodal → Gemini Embedding 2 on the 'eu' endpoint
        ├─ OpenAI already approved, text-only → text-embedding-3 on an EU project with ZDR
        └─ Otherwise → Cohere (SaaS with ZDR, or VPC)
3. Do we need a reranker? (almost always yes for precision-critical answers)
   ├─ Same vendor offers one and it passes in-domain eval → use it
   ├─ Embedding vendor has none in the same API (OpenAI; Google's is the Vertex ranking API)
   │    → Cohere Rerank 4, Voyage rerank-3 (Preview), or a self-hosted cross-encoder
   └─ Store hosts it (MongoDB $rerank, Pinecone, Elastic) → acceptable if the
        model version is pinned and logged, and entitlement filtering precedes it
4. Exact identifiers matter (fund codes, ISINs, share classes)?
   └─ Yes → hybrid first stage (BM25/sparse + dense, fused) before rerank
5. Scanned pages, charts or images matter?
   └─ Yes → multimodal model (Gemini Embedding 2, Cohere Embed 5, Jina v5-omni,
            voyage-multimodal-3.5, NVIDIA VL), chosen by in-domain eval
6. Always: pin versions in C5, keep raw text, tag vectors with model_version,
   and migrate by dual index behind an L9 regression gate.
```

### 7.10 Lock-in classification

| Lock-in source | Class | Rationale | Abstraction to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reranker choice | **Acceptable** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Stateless and applied at query time. Swapping it needs no re-index, only re-evaluation. | Internal `rerank(query, candidates)` interface; reranker version in C5 |
| Embedding model (hosted, proprietary) | **Manageable** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Vectors are model-specific, so switching means re-embedding [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The API bill for that is small; evaluation and revalidation are the real cost (§7.5). | Internal embedding service; raw text stored; `model_version` on every vector; dual-index migration runbook tested twice a year [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |

### 7.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk.** SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026, and it expressly excludes generative and agentic AI. Firms are left to govern those under their own frameworks (R-US-MRM) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S003: OCC Issues Updated Model Risk Management Guidance (NR 2026-29) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-29.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. PRA SS1/23 is the operative UK anchor where it applies. It covers vendor models and requires a complete inventory that includes AI/ML (R-PRA-SS123) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. For this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- Record the embedding model and the reranker in the inventory as components of each GenAI system, not as stand-alone "models".
- Treat a change to either as a material change that triggers the L9 retrieval regression and sign-off.
- Retrieval quality is part of the system's validation evidence. An unvalidated embedding swap is an unvalidated system change.

**EU AI Act.** Annex III high-risk duties apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, and GPAI obligations have been enforceable since 2 August 2026 (R-EUAIA, R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S012: AI Act (regulatory framework page) and AI Act Service Desk FAQ (European Commission) <https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The worked example is not an Annex III use, and a firm consuming embedding APIs is a deployer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Whether any embedding model is itself a GPAI model was not established [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Article 26 deployer logging folds into financial-services record-keeping (R-EUAIA) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S016: AI Act Article 26 Obligations of deployers; Article 25 Responsibilities along the AI value chain (European Commission AI Act Service Desk) <https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-26> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; logging the retrieval step is good practice regardless [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**DORA, CTP and outsourcing.**

- DORA's first CTPP list (18 November 2025) and the UK's first CTP designations (8 July 2026) cover hyperscalers, but no model vendor (R-DORA, R-UK-CTP) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S020: The ESAs designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA (with List_of_designated_CTPPs.pdf, 18 Nov 2025) (EBA / ESMA / EIOPA (Joint ESAs)) <https://www.eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/european-supervisory-authorities-designate-critical-ict-third-party-providers-under-digital> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S024: HM Treasury makes first designations under UK CTP regime (with Lewis Silkin, S&C) (Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer) <https://www.hsfkramer.com/notes/fsrandcorpcrime/2026-posts/hm-treasury-makes-first-designations-under-uk-ctp-regime> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- An embedding API consumed through Vertex AI, or a marketplace deployment, therefore sits on a designated provider. A direct Voyage, Cohere, Jina or OpenAI contract does not, which leaves oversight with the firm [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Every hosted embedding or rerank service is an ICT third-party arrangement for the DORA register [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require third-party notifications from 18 March 2027 (R-PRA-SS221, R-FCA-SYSC8) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S053: PS7/26 - Operational resilience: Operational incident and third-party reporting (with SS2/21 March 2026 update; FCA PS26/2 and FG26/4) (Bank of England (PRA) / FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A new embedding vendor that supports an important business service may need notification lead time [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Residency.** The key-facts table in §7.8 gives the verified position per vendor. For UK firms two points dominate: OpenAI's UK region is storage-only for embeddings [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S144: Data controls in the OpenAI platform <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Gemini's 'eu' endpoint excludes the UK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S039: Data residency (Vertex AI generative AI) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No hosted API in this layer verified UK processing, so UK-only data points to in-estate or UK-region VPC deployment [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Treat embeddings as the same class of data as the text they encode** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Vectors computed from client documents can leak information about that text, so they inherit its classification, retention and deletion obligations [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A right-to-erasure request must reach the vector index as well as the document store [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. For EU/UK personal data sent to US-hosted APIs, the transfer basis rests on the Data Privacy Framework or SCCs. The DPF appeal C-703/25 P was pending as of 7 October 2026 (R-DATA-TRANSFERS) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S059: European Court of Justice to Review Challenge to EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (with ieu-monitoring on Microsoft intervention, digitalpolicyalert) (WilmerHale) <https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/blogs/wilmerhale-privacy-and-cybersecurity-law/20251201-european-court-of-justice-to-review-challenge-to-eu-us-data-privacy-framework> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Concentration.** Database companies now own two of the graphic's vendors (Voyage and Jina) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S033: MongoDB Announces Acquisition of Voyage AI to Enable Organizations to Build Trustworthy AI Applications <https://investors.mongodb.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mongodb-announces-acquisition-voyage-ai-enable-organizations> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S023: Elastic Completes Acquisition of Jina AI, a Leader in Frontier Models for Multimodal and Multilingual Search <https://ir.elastic.co/News--Events/news/news-details/2025/Elastic-Completes-Acquisition-of-Jina-AI-a-Leader-in-Frontier-Models-for-Multimodal-and-Multilingual-Search/default.aspx> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. For important business services, either accept the bundle consciously and record it in the exit plan, or keep the embedding vendor independent of the store [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Auditability.** For every retrieval, the C8 evidence pack should hold [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- query hash
- embedding model and version
- index version
- filter predicate (entitlements)
- candidate count
- reranker version
- final document IDs and scores

That is enough to show what the model was shown, and to reproduce it while the index version is retained.

### 7.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**Context.** The performance-attribution commentary agent drafts the monthly commentary for a generic multi-asset fund. It explains Brinson-style allocation, selection and currency effects against the benchmark. A portfolio manager approves every draft (plan §11) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the agent needs from L7** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
1. **Comparable past commentary.** The fund's own approved commentaries for prior periods, and approved commentaries from comparable periods (for example, months with a large currency effect). These serve as style and structure exemplars.
2. **The house style guide and terminology glossary.** For example: "allocation effect" vs "asset allocation contribution", how interaction is reported, and rounding and sign conventions.
3. **Approved market-context notes** for the period, from L8's approved sources.

**How the layer serves this** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- **Hybrid retrieval.** Lexical retrieval matters because queries carry exact tokens: the fund code, share-class names and period labels ("Q3 2026"). Dense retrieval matters because "the overweight in Japanese equities detracted" must match "the allocation to Japan cost relative performance".
- **Domain terminology.** Run an in-domain bake-off on 100–300 labelled queries written by analysts. Compare a general model, a finance-domain model and a fine-tuned open model:
  - Voyage publishes voyage-finance-2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S007: Voyage AI Embedding and Reranking Models Overview - Voyage AI by MongoDB <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/voyageai/models/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
  - Sentence Transformers supports fine-tuning [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S029: sentence-transformers - PyPI (PyPI / Hugging Face (maintainer)) <https://pypi.org/project/sentence-transformers/> accessed 2026-10-07].

  Pick by recall@20 and nDCG@10, not by vendor claims [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Reranking for the right fund and period.** The reranker receives the instruction-style query with the fund name, the period and the attribution theme. It is evaluated on whether the top 3 contains this fund's most recent comparable commentary and the current style guide. Metadata boosts for `fund_id` and `period` are applied in fusion. They are not left to the reranker alone.
- **Entitlement first.** The store filters on `fund_id`, `client_id`, document classification and approval status *before* ANN search, BM25 and reranking. The reranker only ever sees documents the analyst is entitled to.

**What it must never do** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- **Retrieve another fund's or client's data.** Cross-fund probes run in CI and must return zero hits.
- **Supply numbers.** Retrieved past commentary contains old figures. Those figures must never flow into the new draft as data. All figures come from the attribution engine through L4 tools, and the L9 numeric-faithfulness eval checks that every number in the draft traces to that output.
- **Retrieve unapproved drafts** or superseded style-guide versions. Approval status and validity dates are filter fields.
- **Run on an unpinned model.** The commentary index carries one `model_version`, and the evidence pack records it alongside the reranker version and the retrieved document IDs.
