- The two are evaluated together, and they are versioned together.

The same evidence also shows the compute moving into L6, because MongoDB, Pinecone and Elastic host embedding and reranking natively [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S101: Introducing cascading retrieval: Unifying dense and sparse with reranking (Pinecone) <https://www.pinecone.io/blog/cascading-retrieval/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The provisional view is to **merge** the graphic's "Embeddings" and "RAG re-rankers" into one retrieval-optimisation layer, defined by responsibility rather than by where the compute runs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. That layer owns model choice, version pinning, hybrid fusion policy and the retrieval evaluation gate, whether the models run as APIs, in the firm's own estate, or inside the store. Embedding-model versioning should be named explicitly as a governed configuration item, because it is the one decision in this layer that carries a corpus-wide migration cost [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.


## 6. Retrieval and knowledge stores (vector databases)

> **Executive summary.** This layer stores the vectors, text and metadata that an agent searches, and returns a small, permitted, relevant set of passages. It must do so fast, under filters, for many tenants, and with the same security and records discipline as any other store of client data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Four things have changed since the original graphic. First, hybrid retrieval is now standard. turbopuffer ranks by vectors and BM25 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S056: turbopuffer (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / turbopuffer) <https://pypi.org/project/turbopuffer/> accessed 2026-10-07], Chroma Cloud offers vector, hybrid and full-text search [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S060: chromadb - PyPI (PyPI / Chroma) <https://pypi.org/project/chromadb/> accessed 2026-10-07], Milvus ships BM25 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S054: milvus-lite - PyPI (PyPI / Milvus contributors) <https://pypi.org/project/milvus-lite/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S117: Release Notes - Milvus (Milvus project) <https://milvus.io/docs/release_notes.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Elasticsearch, MongoDB, Qdrant and Pinecone all fuse sparse and dense results [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S103: Qdrant 1.17 - Relevance Feedback & Search Latency Improvements <https://qdrant.tech/blog/qdrant-1.17.x/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S101: Introducing cascading retrieval: Unifying dense and sparse with reranking (Pinecone) <https://www.pinecone.io/blog/cascading-retrieval/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Second, general-purpose databases have absorbed vector search: pgvector reached 0.8.7 on 1 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08; V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and MongoDB Vector Search is GA on self-managed Community and Enterprise Advanced as well as Atlas [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S137: MongoDB Search and Vector Search Now Run Anywhere <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/mongodb-search-vector-search-now-run-anywhere> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S035: MongoDB Delivers Accurate AI Retrieval Wherever Enterprise Data Lives; Community Edition product page (MongoDB, Inc.) <https://investors.mongodb.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mongodb-delivers-accurate-ai-retrieval-wherever-enterprise-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Third, vectors are moving onto object storage: Amazon S3 Vectors has been GA since December 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S081: Amazon S3 Vectors is now generally available with 40 times the scale of preview (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/amazon-s3-vectors-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S030: Amazon S3 Vectors is now generally available with 40 times the scale of preview; S3 Vectors limitations; March 2026 region expansion (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/amazon-s3-vectors-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], Milvus 3.0 is "lake-native" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S118: Zilliz Announces Milvus 3.0, Making the World's Most Adopted Open-Source Vector Database Lake-Native <https://zilliz.com/news/milvus-3-0-lake-native-vector-database> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and turbopuffer keeps all durable state in object storage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S124: Architecture - turbopuffer <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/architecture> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Fourth, vendors are repositioning above the store: Pinecone now sells Nexus, a "knowledge engine for agents" (GA 6 August 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S073: General Availability of Pinecone Nexus Proves Knowledge Drives Real Outcomes for Agentic AI <https://www.pinecone.io/newsroom/general-availability-of-pinecone-nexus-proves-knowledge-drives-real-outcomes-for-agentic-ai/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S029: General Availability of Pinecone Nexus (press release); Nexus GA blog <https://www.pinecone.io/newsroom/general-availability-of-pinecone-nexus-proves-knowledge-drives-real-outcomes-for-agentic-ai/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The term "vector database" now describes a feature more than a product category [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** treat this layer as a retrieval and knowledge store that is always a *derived index*, never the system of record. Start with vectors inside the database or search engine you already run (PostgreSQL with pgvector, Elasticsearch or MongoDB). Move to a dedicated engine (Qdrant or Milvus, self-hosted or in your own cloud account) only when scale, filtered latency or tenant isolation demand it. Enforce entitlements as filters applied before ranking, in every case [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 6.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns.** It persists retrievable representations of approved content and answers the question "which of the passages this caller is allowed to see are most relevant to this query?" [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Six jobs make up the responsibility:

- **Indexing.** Store dense vectors, sparse or lexical terms, the raw chunk text (or a pointer to it) and metadata, and keep the index current as documents are added, changed and deleted [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Candidate retrieval.** Run approximate-nearest-neighbour (ANN) search and lexical search, and fuse the two [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. pgvector provides HNSW and IVFFlat indexes over dense and sparse vectors [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S063: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector project) <https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Elasticsearch combines BM25, quantised vectors and RRF or linear fusion [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S042: Jina models (Elastic docs) <https://www.elastic.co/docs/explore-analyze/machine-learning/nlp/ml-nlp-jina> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Filtering and entitlements.** Apply structured filters (fund, client, document class, date, approval status) so that ranking only ever sees permitted candidates [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tenant isolation.** Keep one client's or fund's material physically or logically separate from another's [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Lifecycle.** Retention, deletion (including erasure requests), backup, restore and re-indexing after an embedding-model change [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Evidence.** Return stable document and chunk identifiers, versions and scores, so the evaluation layer (L9) and the evidence pack (C8) can show exactly what the model was given [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**

| Direction | Counterpart | What crosses the boundary [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|
| Below | L8 ingestion | Parsed, chunked, classified documents with lineage, ACL metadata and PII flags (the H7 contract) |
| Beside | L7 embeddings and reranking | Vectors and sparse terms written with a model-version tag; at query time, first-stage candidates passed to the reranker |
| Above | L3 orchestration, L4 tools, L5 memory | A retrieval call carrying the caller's verified entitlements; results with IDs, scores and provenance |
| Across | C3 data governance, C4 identity, C8 audit | Classification and residency policy; caller identity and entitlements; retrieval logs |
| Across | L9 evaluation | Retrieval recall and precision, filtered-latency and leak tests |

**What the layer does not own.** It does not decide which content is approved for retrieval; that is L8 and C3 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It does not own embedding-model choice or version policy, which belong to L7, even when the store runs the embedding model itself, as MongoDB Automated Embedding, Elastic `semantic_text` and Pinecone integrated inference do [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S078: Unlocking AI Search: Introducing Automated Embedding in MongoDB Vector Search <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/unlocking-ai-search-introducing-automated-embedding-in-mongodb-vector-search> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S051: pinecone (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / Pinecone Systems, Inc.) <https://pypi.org/project/pinecone/> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It does not own agent memory semantics (L5), although the same engines often host memory [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 6.2 Why it matters

A badly designed retrieval store fails quietly [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The model receives plausible context and writes fluent text, so the failure surfaces as a wrong fact, a stale citation or, worst, another client's information in a draft [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Four failure modes dominate:

- **Entitlement leakage.** Permissions applied after ranking, or only in the application, let restricted passages reach the prompt. The model then repeats them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Filter collapse.** A restrictive filter applied after ANN search leaves too few results, so recall drops or the system silently widens the filter [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Index drift.** Deletions, retractions and superseded versions do not propagate, so the agent cites withdrawn material, and an erasure request is honoured in the source but not in the vector copy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Unplanned dependency.** A store chosen for a prototype becomes a critical system with no exit plan, no backup and no tested rebuild [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The layer also holds a copy of the firm's most sensitive unstructured content in a second representation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Embeddings are derived from that content. They should be treated as data of the same classification as the text they came from, including for residency and erasure [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A multi-asset team builds a commentary assistant on a single shared vector index holding prior commentaries for all its funds. Fund identity is a metadata field. The application retrieves the top 20 passages and then removes any that belong to other funds. For most funds this works. For a small segregated mandate, a query about currency hedging returns 20 passages from larger funds; after the post-filter, none remain, so a fallback path retries without the fund filter "to avoid an empty context". The draft for the segregated mandate's client report now quotes a hedging rationale written for a different client, including that client's benchmark name. A reviewer catches it, but only because the benchmark name is unfamiliar. The incident review finds three faults: the filter ran after ranking, the fallback removed it, and no test checked for cross-fund leakage. Filtering inside the search, a hard "no results" outcome instead of a fallback, and a leakage test in the L9 suite would each have prevented it. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### 6.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entitlement leakage | Results returned that the caller is not entitled to see | Zero; any occurrence is a severity-1 incident | Adversarial test queries per tenant in CI (L9); production sampling against the entitlement service |
| Filtered recall@k | Recall@k measured with production-like filters applied, not on the unfiltered index | Within an agreed tolerance of unfiltered recall for the same queries | Labelled query set run with and without filters |
| p95 latency under filter | Retrieval latency at the 95th percentile for the most selective realistic filter | Budget per use case (interactive versus batch) | Load test with tenant-skewed data |
| Hybrid uplift | Change in recall or groundedness from adding lexical retrieval and fusion | Positive on the firm's own corpus before adoption | A/B evaluation in L9 |
| Freshness lag | Time from approval in the source to searchability | Hours for commentary corpora; minutes where markets data drives content | Canary documents written and queried |
| Deletion propagation time | Time from deletion or retraction in the source to absence from results and from the index | Within the records-policy and erasure service levels | Canary deletions; index scan |
| Rebuild time (RTO) | Time to rebuild the index from the source of truth with the pinned embedding model | Inside the exit-plan tolerance; tested twice a year | Timed dry run |
| Residency conformance | Share of vector, text and backup copies held in approved regions | 100% | Configuration evidence and cloud inventory |
| Patch latency | Time from a store CVE to production fix | Days for high severity (pgvector's 0.8.7 fix was CVSS 8.8 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]) | Vulnerability management records |
| Cost per 1,000 queries and per GB-month | Loaded cost including idle capacity | Budget per use case | Billing and capacity data |

### 6.4 How it works

**Write path.** L8 delivers chunks with metadata. L7 produces dense vectors and, where used, sparse vectors or lexical terms. The store writes vectors, text or text pointers, and metadata to an index, often partitioned by tenant [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Engines differ in where durable state lives. pgvector stores vectors in PostgreSQL tables beside relational data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. turbopuffer writes to a write-ahead log in object storage and serves from SSD and memory caches [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S124: Architecture - turbopuffer <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/architecture> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. S3 Vectors stores vectors in vector indexes inside vector buckets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S094: Announcing Amazon S3 Vectors (Preview) - First cloud object storage with native support for storing and querying vectors (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/07/amazon-s3-vectors-preview-native-support-storing-querying-vectors/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S083: Limitations and restrictions - Amazon S3 Vectors (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-vectors-limitations.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Milvus 3.0 builds indexes over vectors kept in object storage and open formats [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S118: Zilliz Announces Milvus 3.0, Making the World's Most Adopted Open-Source Vector Database Lake-Native <https://zilliz.com/news/milvus-3-0-lake-native-vector-database> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Query path.** A query carries the caller's entitlements from C4. The store applies the filter, runs ANN and lexical search over the permitted candidates, fuses them, and returns a few dozen candidates to the L7 reranker [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Fusion is now a store feature: Qdrant weighted RRF [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S103: Qdrant 1.17 - Relevance Feedback & Search Latency Improvements <https://qdrant.tech/blog/qdrant-1.17.x/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Elasticsearch RRF and linear retrievers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], MongoDB `$rankFusion` and `$scoreFusion` [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S141: Context Engineering Has a Retrieval Issue: Introducing rerank-3 and Native Reranking (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/introducing-rerank-3-and-native-rerank> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] and Pinecone cascading retrieval with a sparse model [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S101: Introducing cascading retrieval: Unifying dense and sparse with reranking (Pinecone) <https://www.pinecone.io/blog/cascading-retrieval/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Filtering mechanics.** There are three broad approaches [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- *Post-filtering* runs ANN first and discards disallowed results. It is cheap, and it is the cause of filter collapse and of leakage when combined with fallbacks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Pre-filtering or filter-aware traversal* restricts the search to permitted candidates as it runs. Qdrant added ACORN-based filtered search in 1.16 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S103: Qdrant 1.17 - Relevance Feedback & Search Latency Improvements <https://qdrant.tech/blog/qdrant-1.17.x/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. pgvector 0.8.0 added iterative index scans and better cost estimation for index selection when filtering [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08]. Elastic reports DiskBBQ at least three times faster with restrictive filters in 9.4 [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Partitioning* gives each tenant its own namespace, collection or index, so the filter becomes an address. Pinecone and turbopuffer route every query to a namespace [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S051: pinecone (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / Pinecone Systems, Inc.) <https://pypi.org/project/pinecone/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S056: turbopuffer (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / turbopuffer) <https://pypi.org/project/turbopuffer/> accessed 2026-10-07], turbopuffer isolates namespaces as prefixes in object storage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S124: Architecture - turbopuffer <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/architecture> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Qdrant has tiered multitenancy with tenant promotion [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S103: Qdrant 1.17 - Relevance Feedback & Search Latency Improvements <https://qdrant.tech/blog/qdrant-1.17.x/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Chroma scopes access control to the tenant, with databases beneath it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S008: Chroma Security; architecture overview; CMEK changelog <https://www.trychroma.com/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

```text
WRITE (L8 -> L7 -> L6) [AJ]
  approved doc --> chunk + metadata {doc_id, version, fund_id, client_id,
                   classification, region, retention_until, embed_model_version}
            --> dense vector (+ sparse terms)
            --> STORE: partition = tenant (namespace / collection / schema)
                       index    = ANN (HNSW / IVF / centroid / DiskANN-type) + BM25
                       payload  = text or pointer to source of truth (L8)

QUERY (L3 -> C4 -> L6 -> L7 -> L3) [AJ]
  caller identity --> C4 entitlements {fund_ids, client_ids, max_classification}
            --> L6: select partition(s) the caller may use
                    filter INSIDE the search (never after ranking)
                    ANN + BM25 --> fusion (RRF / linear) --> top-N candidates + IDs
            --> L7 reranker --> top-k passages + provenance
            --> L3 prompt assembly;  retrieval log (IDs, versions, scores) --> C8 / L9

LIFECYCLE [Rec]
  source delete / retraction / erasure --> delete by ID --> compaction / vacuum
  embedding model change --> shadow index --> evaluate (L9) --> cut over --> drop old
  backup = rebuild-from-source (primary) + store snapshot (secondary)
```

**Storage economics.** Memory-resident graph indexes give low latency at a high RAM cost [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Quantisation and disk-based indexes trade some recall for cost: Elastic's BBQ has been the default since 9.1 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S133: Elastic 9.5: Columnar, VectorDB index mode & auto-calibration, and AI-driven alert triage <https://www.elastic.co/blog/whats-new-elastic-9-5-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Qdrant added TurboQuant quantisation and a low-memory mode in 1.18 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S102: Releases - qdrant/qdrant (Qdrant) <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Weaviate previews 4-bit rotational quantisation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S110: Weaviate 1.39 Release <https://weaviate.io/blog/weaviate-1-39-release> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Object-storage-first designs push the trade further. turbopuffer reports a cold-query p50 of 874 ms against 14 ms cached on 1M documents [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A2-S124: Architecture - turbopuffer <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/architecture> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. S3 Vectors has no provisioned compute and is priced per GB stored, per PUT and per query [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S087: Amazon S3 Pricing (S3 Vectors section) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Vendor latency figures are context, not decision inputs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 6.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security and entitlements**

- **Filter before rank, inside the store.** Entitlements arrive from C4 as signed claims and become mandatory filter clauses. The application must not be able to omit them, and there is no "retry without filter" path [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Do not rely on the store for row-level permissions you have not tested.** turbopuffer states that permissions must be implemented with filters because it has no built-in row- or document-level RBAC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S002: turbopuffer Regions; Security; Permissions; Roadmap & Changelog; Private Networking <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/regions> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Most engines are in the same position: they provide the filter mechanism, and the firm provides the policy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Use engine-native document security where it exists.** Elasticsearch offers field- and document-level security (Platinum tier when self-managed) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S134: Use a customer-managed encryption key - Elastic Cloud <https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/encrypt-deployment-with-customer-managed-encryption-key> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Qdrant issues JWT keys scoped to read or read-write on individual collections [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S007: Qdrant Cloud RBAC role management; enterprise SSO announcement; database security (JWT RBAC) <https://qdrant.tech/documentation/cloud-rbac/role-management/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Weaviate supports RBAC with custom roles and OIDC users and groups [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S009: Weaviate RBAC configuration; Authentication (OIDC); Logging (audit) <https://docs.weaviate.io/deploy/configuration/configuring-rbac> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **Lock down self-hosted defaults.** Chroma removed its built-in authentication in 1.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S131: Migration - Chroma Docs <https://docs.trychroma.com/docs/overview/migration> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Milvus Lite has no authentication, users, roles or TLS [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S054: milvus-lite - PyPI (PyPI / Milvus contributors) <https://pypi.org/project/milvus-lite/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Qdrant 1.19.2 now warns at start-up when no API keys are configured [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S102: Releases - qdrant/qdrant (Qdrant) <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. None of these should run on a shared network without an authenticating proxy [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Patch the store like a database.** pgvector 0.8.7 fixed an IVFFlat index-build buffer overflow rated CVSS 8.8 that could allow code execution by a user able to create such indexes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. 0.8.2 fixed a parallel HNSW build overflow (CVE-2026-3172) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S062: pgvector 0.8.2 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-082-released-3245/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08]. Managed hosts lag upstream: the latest Amazon RDS release seen carries pgvector 0.8.2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S004: Extension versions for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL; RDS PostgreSQL release notes; Aurora pgvector announcements (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], while Cloud SQL moved to 0.8.5 in August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S005: Vector search in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server; Cloud SQL vector embeddings; AlloyDB vector search overview (Microsoft; Google Cloud) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/how-to-use-pgvector> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Restrict index-creation privileges and track the host's pgvector version, not only the upstream one [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Encrypt with keys you control where the data is client-confidential.** Customer-managed keys are documented for Pinecone (project level) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S096: Trust and Security (Pinecone) <https://www.pinecone.io/security/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], turbopuffer (per namespace, Enterprise) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S123: turbopuffer pricing <https://turbopuffer.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S077: turbopuffer Security & Compliance; pricing; CMEK; BYOC; roadmap <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], Zilliz Cloud (Business Critical) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S120: Zilliz Cloud Pricing <https://zilliz.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Elastic Cloud Hosted (Enterprise) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S134: Use a customer-managed encryption key - Elastic Cloud <https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/security/encrypt-deployment-with-customer-managed-encryption-key> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], MongoDB Atlas [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S139: Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management - Atlas (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-kms-encryption/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], Chroma Cloud [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S008: Chroma Security; architecture overview; CMEK changelog <https://www.trychroma.com/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] and S3 Vectors (per bucket or index) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S090: Data protection and encryption in S3 Vectors (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-vectors-data-encryption.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Atlas covers search indexes with CMK only on dedicated Search Nodes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S139: Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management - Atlas (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security-kms-encryption/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and S3 Vectors keys cannot be changed after index creation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S090: Data protection and encryption in S3 Vectors (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-vectors-data-encryption.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Scalability and performance**

- Measure recall and latency *with filters and tenant skew*, on your own corpus. Unfiltered benchmarks overstate both [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Prefer partitioning by tenant when tenants are numerous and roughly independent; prefer a shared index with a mandatory filter when cross-tenant search by authorised staff is a real requirement [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Keep the raw text and the embedding-model version beside every vector, so the index can be rebuilt without re-parsing (the L7 rule) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Resilience, backup and exit**

- **The source of truth is outside the store.** The primary recovery path is a rebuild from L8's approved corpus with the pinned embedding model. Store snapshots are the secondary path [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Test the rebuild.** Rebuild time is an exit-plan metric, because SS2/21 expects documented and tested exit plans [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Watch upgrade paths.** Qdrant cannot skip 1.16 on upgrade because of a storage migration [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S102: Releases - qdrant/qdrant (Qdrant) <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/releases> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Milvus 3.0 is not guaranteed compatible with 2.6 servers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S117: Release Notes - Milvus (Milvus project) <https://milvus.io/docs/release_notes.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Pinecone's Python SDK v10 introduced breaking API changes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S051: pinecone (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / Pinecone Systems, Inc.) <https://pypi.org/project/pinecone/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S072: ZoomInfo and Pinecone Bring Real-Time, AI-Powered Contact Recommendations to Go-to-Market Teams <https://www.pinecone.io/newsroom/zoominfo-pinecone-drn/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Weaviate supports only its latest three minor versions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S109: Releases - weaviate/weaviate (Weaviate) <https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate/releases> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Governance and lifecycle**

- Deletion must propagate within a defined service level, and must be verified by canary [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Engines differ in how deletes become physical: pgvector's 2026 fixes include HNSW vacuuming corrections [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08], which is a reminder that deletion depends on background maintenance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Retention metadata (`retention_until`) should travel with each chunk, and a scheduled job should delete expired chunks [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Record which documents, versions and chunks each answer used, in the evidence pack (C8) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Observability and cost**

- Emit retrieval spans (query, filter, partition, candidate IDs, scores, latency) to the L9 collector, with text redacted where necessary [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Pricing units differ widely: read and write units (Pinecone) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S099: Understanding cost - Pinecone Docs <https://docs.pinecone.io/guides/manage-cost/understanding-cost> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], data scanned and returned (turbopuffer) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S123: turbopuffer pricing <https://turbopuffer.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], GiB written, stored and queried (Chroma) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S128: Pricing - Chroma <https://www.trychroma.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], per-query data processed (S3 Vectors) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S087: Amazon S3 Pricing (S3 Vectors section) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], hourly Search Nodes (MongoDB) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S140: Search Node Costs - Atlas (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/search-node/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] and plain database compute (pgvector) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Model the firm's query mix before committing [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** vectors in the existing operational database for modest corpora; a search engine for lexical-heavy corpora; tenant-partitioned dedicated engine for many clients; object-store cold tier behind a hot tier; rebuild-from-source as the backup; retrieval logs into the evidence pack.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** post-filter permissions; an unfiltered fallback; the vector store as the only copy of approved content; a prototype store (embedded, unauthenticated) promoted to production; one shared index for segregated mandates without leak tests; embedding inside the store with an unpinned model; a "knowledge engine" adopted as the system of record without an export route.

### 6.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Dense and sparse vectors; BM25 and fusion; filter-aware search and recall under selective filters; multi-tenancy model; scale (vectors per index, tenants); deletes and updates; quantisation and disk indexes; transactional integration with operational data |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC with scoped keys, audit logs of data access, SCIM, SLA; whether controls cover the data plane as well as the console |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 within the product's scope; CMK/BYOK granularity (project, index, namespace); private networking; HIPAA as a proxy for mature controls; CVE handling for self-hosted engines |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | SaaS, BYOC (data plane in the firm's account), self-host, on-premises and air-gap; UK and EU regions |
| Ecosystem (5%) | Open query interfaces (SQL, OpenAPI, standard drivers); framework support; hyperscaler integration |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | Years in production; release cadence; breaking upgrades; governance (foundation versus single vendor) |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Pricing unit and minimums; idle cost; operations burden; RAM versus disk versus object storage economics |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Licence (permissive, AGPL, SSPL, open core, proprietary); proprietary query language; bundled embedding; export and rebuild path |

**Two calibration rules applied in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** First, *no ISO 27001 means a security score of at most 3*, whatever else is present; this applies to Qdrant, turbopuffer and Chroma. Second, *store-only engines are scored on the store*, so a vendor's adjacent products (Nexus, Voyage models, Jina models) affect lock-in but do not raise the technical score.

### 6.7 Product deep dives

**PostgreSQL with pgvector (open-source project).**
- *What it is now:* an extension that adds vector types, including `sparsevec`, and HNSW and IVFFlat ANN indexes to PostgreSQL, so vectors live beside relational data and SQL filters [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S063: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector project) <https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Version 0.8.7 was released on 1 October 2026 and announced on 5 October [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08; V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The extension is under the PostgreSQL License, which is permissive and OSI-approved [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S021: pgvector LICENSE (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Security record:* two 2026 fixes matter. 0.8.2 (February) fixed a parallel HNSW build buffer overflow, CVE-2026-3172 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S062: pgvector 0.8.2 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-082-released-3245/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08]. 0.8.7 fixed an IVFFlat index-build buffer overflow (CVE-2026-103484, CVSS 8.8) that can allow arbitrary code execution by a user able to create IVFFlat indexes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S022: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Stage A noted that the CVE number format looks unusual [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S061: pgvector 0.8.7 Released (PostgreSQL Global Development Group (news post by pgvector p) <https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/pgvector-087-released-3392/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; cite the PostgreSQL.org announcement rather than the number alone [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Managed hosting:* Amazon RDS and Aurora PostgreSQL support pgvector, and Aurora can serve as a Bedrock Knowledge Base [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S004: Extension versions for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL; RDS PostgreSQL release notes; Aurora pgvector announcements (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/PostgreSQLReleaseNotes/postgresql-extensions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Azure Database for PostgreSQL requires the extension to be allowlisted, adds a DiskANN index, and cannot index vectors over 2,000 dimensions; Azure manages the extension version [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S005: Vector search in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server; Cloud SQL vector embeddings; AlloyDB vector search overview (Microsoft; Google Cloud) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/how-to-use-pgvector> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Cloud SQL moved to pgvector 0.8.5 on 27 August 2026, and AlloyDB adds a ScaNN index to a customised pgvector [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L6-S005: Vector search in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server; Cloud SQL vector embeddings; AlloyDB vector search overview (Microsoft; Google Cloud) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/extensions/how-to-use-pgvector> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Filtering:* 0.8.0 added iterative index scans and improved index selection when filtering [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S020: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Strengths:* transactional integration (vectors, metadata and entitlement tables in one ACID database) and the lowest operational increment for any firm that already runs PostgreSQL well [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* HNSW indexes are memory-hungry, so cost tracks database RAM [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. There is no BM25 ranking in the extension itself; hybrid needs `sparsevec` or application-side fusion [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S063: pgvector CHANGELOG.md (pgvector project) <https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Large-scale behaviour under heavy write and filter load is not evidenced in the fact base [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Adjacent forks add scale features: pgvectorscale (Tiger Data, formerly Timescale) and VectorChord, which succeeded the deprecated pgvecto.rs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S064: Tiger Data Documentation - Changelog (Tiger Data (formerly Timescale)) <https://www.tigerdata.com/docs/about/latest/changelog> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S066: VectorChord (TensorChord) <https://vectorchord.ai/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S065: TimescaleDB - Wikipedia <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TimescaleDB> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S067: pgvecto.rs deprecated, support for VectorChord - immich-app/immich Discussion #16335 (Immich project) <https://github.com/immich-app/immich/discussions/16335> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* the corpus is in the millions of chunks rather than billions, PostgreSQL is a standard platform, and entitlements already live in relational tables [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need thousands of isolated tenants with independent scaling, or low-latency search over a very large corpus under selective filters [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* MongoDB Vector Search, Elasticsearch, Qdrant.
- *FS note:* run on the firm's managed PostgreSQL in a UK or EU region; track the host's pgvector version against upstream CVEs; restrict index-creation rights [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. No flag.** Scored under rubric rule 2 (self-hosted software), with host controls presumed on the hyperscaler services (CP2 Q1).

Nexus benchmark figures are vendor-reported and not relied on here [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- **Tier: Tactical. No flag.** It scores 3.80 FS, above the Strategic guide. It is held at Tactical because lock-in scores 2 and the vendor is widening its scope into L5 and L8, so it should not be a foundational dependency without a decided exit route [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The same lock-in score is accepted as a Strategic condition for MongoDB because there it rides on an existing platform commitment; for Pinecone it would be a new proprietary dependency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- *Regions and price:* about 34 Regions, including AWS GovCloud (US) and the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S084: AWS Regions, endpoints, and quotas for S3 Vectors (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-vectors-regions-quotas.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S085: Amazon S3 Vectors expands to 17 additional AWS Regions (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/s3-vectors-expands-17-regions/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Storage is US$0.06 per GB-month, with per-PUT and per-query charges; AWS's worked example of 50M vectors and 1M queries costs US$178.61 per month (as of 7 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S087: Amazon S3 Pricing (S3 Vectors section) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S030: Amazon S3 Vectors is now generally available with 40 times the scale of preview; S3 Vectors limitations; March 2026 region expansion (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/12/amazon-s3-vectors-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* very low cost per stored vector with no capacity to manage, inside the firm's existing AWS controls [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* AWS-only API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S092: Amazon S3 Vectors (feature page) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/features/vectors/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Vector and metadata only, so hybrid needs OpenSearch [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S083: Limitations and restrictions - Amazon S3 Vectors (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/s3-vectors-limitations.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S093: Selecting a vector store for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases (Amazon Web Services (AWS Machine Learning Blog)) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/selecting-a-vector-store-for-amazon-bedrock-knowledge-bases/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Limits and prices changed several times in 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S086: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports up to 10,000 similarity search results per query (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/s3-vectors-supports-10000-search-results-per-query/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S088: Amazon S3 Vectors reduces query charges by up to 80% for large vector indexes (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/06/s3-vectors-reduces-query-charges-80-percent-large-indexes/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* you are AWS-centred and need a cheap, durable tier for large or infrequently queried corpora, or a Bedrock Knowledge Base [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need lexical search, low tail latency or a multi-cloud exit route [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* turbopuffer, Milvus 3.0, pgvector on Aurora.
- *FS note:* enable CloudTrail data events on regulated indexes; set the KMS key at index creation; record S3 Vectors under the AWS CTPP concentration entry [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical, default in AWS estates as the low-cost vector tier. No flag.** Enterprise readiness at 4 under the hyperscaler presumption: platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. Rubric rule 10 (CP3 Q2) does not make it Strategic, because it is not AWS's lead vector-search service: AWS positions it as a durable tier behind OpenSearch [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S092: Amazon S3 Vectors (feature page) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/features/vectors/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The borderline call was resolved against the Anthropic-related item.

### 6.9 Decision tree

The central question is whether a dedicated vector database is needed at all [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Most regulated asset-management corpora (commentaries, research notes, policies, style guides) are in the range that an existing database or search engine handles, and every additional store is another copy of confidential content to secure, retain, back up and exit [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
STEP 0 [Rec]: Non-negotiables, whatever the store
  - Source of truth for approved content lives in L8/C3, not in the store.
  - Entitlements from C4 are applied as filters INSIDE the search; no unfiltered fallback.
  - Every chunk carries doc_id, version, tenant ids, classification, region,
    retention_until and embed_model_version; raw text (or pointer) kept.
  - Rebuild-from-source is tested twice a year; it is the primary backup and exit route.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Do you need a dedicated vector database at all?
  Is the content already in, or naturally owned by, an operated database or search platform?
  ├─ PostgreSQL is a firm standard
  │     → pgvector on the managed PostgreSQL service (UK/EU region),
  │       entitlement tables joined in SQL; track host pgvector version vs CVEs
  ├─ Elastic (or OpenSearch) is an operated platform, or the corpus is lexical-heavy
  │     (ISINs, tickers, fund codes, share-class names)
  │     → Elasticsearch hybrid (BM25 + vectors, RRF) with document-level security
  │       (OpenSearch if licence policy requires Apache-2.0)
  ├─ MongoDB is the system of record for these documents
  │     → MongoDB Vector Search on dedicated Search Nodes (CMK), Voyage features off
  │       until GA and Geography-scoped
  ├─ AWS-centred, Bedrock Knowledge Bases, large or rarely queried corpus
  │     → S3 Vectors as the cost tier; OpenSearch in front if hybrid or low
  │       latency is needed; CloudTrail data events on
  └─ None of these → go to STEP 2

STEP 2 [Rec]: Which trigger makes a dedicated engine necessary?
  Proceed only if at least one is evidenced in a load test on your own data:
  (a) filtered p95 latency or filtered recall fails the budget in the existing platform
  (b) tenants must be isolated at scale (hundreds or more clients/funds with separate
      keys, quotas or deletion), beyond what schemas or indexes can manage cleanly
  (c) corpus size or write rate makes the existing platform's RAM or ops cost
      disproportionate
  No trigger → stay in STEP 1.

STEP 3 [Rec]: Dedicated engine, by where it must run
  Must run in your own estate or air-gapped?
  ├─ Yes → Qdrant (self-host or Private Cloud; collection-scoped JWT keys)
  │        or Milvus (Standalone/Distributed; LF AI & Data governance) for very large corpora
  └─ No, but data plane must be in your cloud account (BYOC)?
       ├─ Open-source engine preferred (exit by self-hosting)
       │     → Qdrant Hybrid Cloud, or Zilliz Cloud BYOC (Milvus)
       ├─ Managed, proprietary, strongest control set → Pinecone Enterprise BYOC
       │     (Dedicated Read Nodes only; Nexus is a separate decision)
       └─ Very many tenants, object-storage economics, per-tenant keys
             → turbopuffer BYOC (author conflict disclosed; alternative: Zilliz BYOC)
  Vendor-hosted SaaS acceptable (non-confidential corpora)?
       → any of the above in a UK/EU region; Weaviate if hybrid plus ISO 27001
         managed service matters and the licence position is settled

STEP 4 [Rec]: Prototypes and harnesses
  Notebook, evaluation harness, single-user tool, non-confidential data
       → Chroma (embedded) or pgvector in a local container. Never promoted to
         production without returning to STEP 1.

STEP 5 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Leak test per tenant passes (zero)?  Filtered recall within tolerance?
  Deletion canary within SLA?  Rebuild time inside exit-plan tolerance?
  All copies (vectors, text, backups, caches) in approved regions?
  Store recorded in the outsourcing / ICT register with an exit plan?
```

### 6.10 Lock-in classification

| Element | Classification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Rationale | Abstraction to use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vector index and data | **Acceptable**, if rebuildable | Vectors are derived; with raw text and the pinned model kept outside, any index can be rebuilt (the L7 rule) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Rebuild-from-source pipeline; per-chunk metadata contract |
| Query API | **Manageable** | Proprietary APIs (Pinecone, turbopuffer, S3 Vectors) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S051: pinecone (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / Pinecone Systems, Inc.) <https://pypi.org/project/pinecone/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S056: turbopuffer (Python SDK) - PyPI (PyPI / turbopuffer) <https://pypi.org/project/turbopuffer/> accessed 2026-10-07; A2-S092: Amazon S3 Vectors (feature page) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/features/vectors/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] versus SQL (pgvector) and open-source engines (Qdrant, Milvus) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S108: qdrant/LICENSE (Qdrant) <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/blob/master/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S118: Zilliz Announces Milvus 3.0, Making the World's Most Adopted Open-Source Vector Database Lake-Native <https://zilliz.com/news/milvus-3-0-lake-native-vector-database> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | A thin internal retrieval interface (query, filters, tenant, top-k, returns IDs and scores) used by L3; no store SDK in agent code |
| Filter and entitlement logic | **Unacceptable if only in the store's proprietary syntax** | The entitlement policy is the firm's control and must survive a store change [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Policy held in C4; compiled into each store's filter syntax by the retrieval service |
| Licence | **Manageable** | Permissive (pgvector, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S021: pgvector LICENSE (pgvector (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pgvector/pgvector/master/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-08; A2-S108: qdrant/LICENSE (Qdrant) <https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/blob/master/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S118: Zilliz Announces Milvus 3.0, Making the World's Most Adopted Open-Source Vector Database Lake-Native <https://zilliz.com/news/milvus-3-0-lake-native-vector-database> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S060: chromadb - PyPI (PyPI / Chroma) <https://pypi.org/project/chromadb/> accessed 2026-10-07]; AGPL, SSPL or ELv2 (Elastic) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S132: Elasticsearch Is Open Source. Again! <https://www.elastic.co/blog/elasticsearch-is-open-source-again> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; SSPL (MongoDB) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S137: MongoDB Search and Vector Search Now Run Anywhere <https://www.mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/mongodb-search-vector-search-now-run-anywhere> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; open core in transition (Weaviate) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S115: weaviate/weaviate (README and licence files; PR #13360) (Weaviate) <https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S070: weaviate/weaviate README (Community vs Enterprise Edition), releases, PR #13360, PR #12942 (Weaviate (GitHub)) <https://github.com/weaviate/weaviate> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] | Licence review before standardising; OpenSearch as the Elastic exit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S136: Release Schedule and Maintenance Policy - OpenSearch (OpenSearch project (Linux Foundation)) <https://opensearch.org/releases/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| Store-bundled embedding and reranking | **Manageable**, becoming **unacceptable** if the model is unpinned | Leaving the store then also means re-embedding (L7 §7.10) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Pin the model explicitly; keep embedding in the L7 service where possible |
| Knowledge-engine layer (Pinecone Nexus, KnowQL) | **Unacceptable as the only home of curated knowledge; manageable as a derived layer** | It compiles data into vendor-specific artifacts queried in a proprietary language [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S073: General Availability of Pinecone Nexus Proves Knowledge Drives Real Outcomes for Agentic AI <https://www.pinecone.io/newsroom/general-availability-of-pinecone-nexus-proves-knowledge-drives-real-outcomes-for-agentic-ai/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Keep curated sources and lineage in L8/C3; treat compiled artifacts as disposable |
| Object-store format | **Manageable** | Milvus 3.0 uses open formats [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S118: Zilliz Announces Milvus 3.0, Making the World's Most Adopted Open-Source Vector Database Lake-Native <https://zilliz.com/news/milvus-3-0-lake-native-vector-database> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; turbopuffer's and S3 Vectors' formats are proprietary [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Rebuild route regardless of format |
| Hyperscaler-native stores | **Manageable**, with concentration noted | S3 Vectors is AWS-only and AWS is a designated CTPP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S092: Amazon S3 Vectors (feature page) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/s3/features/vectors/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Exit plan names an alternative store and the rebuild time |

### 6.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk.**
- *What is in scope.* A retrieval store is not a model under SS1/23 or SR 26-2 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. SS1/23 applies to banks and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and places generative and agentic AI outside its scope [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Why it still matters.* The retrieval configuration (index, filters, fusion, embedding version) determines what the generative system sees, so it is part of the system that the firm's own validation must cover [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Changes to it should trigger the same regression suite as a model change (L9) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- *Deployer logging.* Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to keep logs for at least six months [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Scope here.* Commentary drafting is not Annex III [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Recording retrieved document IDs per output is nevertheless the cheapest way to make any output reproducible [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Operational resilience and outsourcing.**
- *Register.* For EU entities, a vector-database SaaS is an ICT third-party service that belongs in the DORA register of information, with Article 30 terms and an exit strategy where it supports a critical or important function [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Concentration.* The first DORA CTPP list (18 November 2025) includes AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S020: The ESAs designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA (with List_of_designated_CTPPs.pdf, 18 Nov 2025) (EBA / ESMA / EIOPA (Joint ESAs)) <https://www.eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/european-supervisory-authorities-designate-critical-ict-third-party-providers-under-digital> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The UK designated the same three and Oracle on 8 July 2026, in force 13 July [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No vector-store vendor is designated [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. However, Pinecone, Zilliz, Qdrant Cloud, Weaviate Cloud, turbopuffer, MongoDB Atlas, Elastic Cloud and Chroma Cloud all run on those hyperscalers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S069: Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) - Pinecone Docs <https://docs.pinecone.io/guides/production/bring-your-own-cloud> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S121: Zilliz Cloud Now Available in AWS Europe (Ireland) <https://zilliz.com/blog/zilliz-cloud-now-available-in-aws-europe-ireland> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S105: Qdrant Security: Compliance, Isolation, and Encryption Across Every Deployment <https://qdrant.tech/security/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S111: Vector Database Pricing - Weaviate <https://weaviate.io/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S125: turbopuffer BYOC <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/byoc> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S140: Search Node Costs - Atlas (MongoDB) <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/search-node/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S135: Elastic Cloud Hosted regions <https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/cloud/cloud-hosted/regions> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S129: Chroma Cloud - Chroma Docs <https://docs.trychroma.com/cloud/getting-started> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], so their outages correlate with the cloud platform's [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Record the underlying cloud for every L6 service [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Notification lead time.* PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A new SaaS vector store supporting an important business service should be planned with that lead time [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Exit.* SS2/21 expects documented and tested exit plans, including stressed exit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. For this layer the exit plan is the rebuild: approved source corpus, pinned embedding model, rebuild runbook and measured rebuild time [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Export features are a secondary route [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Residency, transfers and erasure.**
- *Vector copies are personal or confidential data.* Embeddings derived from documents that contain client or personal data should inherit that classification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Residency must cover the vectors, the raw text payload, caches, replicas and backups [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Location controls.* FG16/5 expects data location, effective access and exit planning for outsourced IT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. EU-to-US transfers rely on the Data Privacy Framework or SCCs, and the annulment appeal (C-703/25 P) is pending [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. ### 6.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from L6 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary (allocation, selection, currency, benchmark-relative return) for a generic multi-asset fund. Authoritative numbers come from the attribution engine through read-only L4 tools; L6 supplies only words and context. It needs:
1. **Three logical collections, one store.**
   - *Prior commentaries:* approved monthly commentaries for this fund, with fund, share class, period, author, approver, approval date and version.
   - *House style guide and glossary:* firm-wide, versioned, with an "effective from" date.
   - *Approved market notes:* house views and market summaries approved for external use, with an expiry date.
2. **Fund-level entitlement filters, applied inside the search.** Each request carries the analyst's entitlements from C4 (permitted fund IDs, client IDs and maximum classification). The store returns only chunks whose `fund_id` is in that set, or which are tagged firm-wide (style guide, approved market notes). Segregated mandates get their own partition (schema, collection or namespace) so that isolation does not depend on a filter clause alone.
3. **A hard empty result.** If no permitted passage meets the relevance threshold, the store returns nothing and the workflow drafts from the attribution output and the style guide only, flagging "no comparable commentary". There is no retry without filters.
4. **Hybrid retrieval.** Lexical matching for fund names, benchmark names, share-class codes and currency pairs; dense retrieval for phrasing; fusion in the store; rerank in L7.
5. **Freshness and expiry.** Market notes past their expiry date and superseded style-guide versions are excluded by filter, so the agent cannot cite a withdrawn view.
6. **Provenance for the evidence pack.** Each retrieved passage returns document ID, version, chunk ID, approval date and score, written to the C8 evidence pack alongside the trace ID, so the reviewer can see which past commentary shaped which sentence.
7. **Retention aligned to the records policy.** Each chunk carries `retention_until` from the records policy. Expired chunks are deleted by a scheduled job, and deletion is verified by canary query. Store snapshots follow the same retention.
8. **Residency.** For a UK or EU fund, the store, its replicas and its backups sit in UK or EU regions; for most firms that means pgvector on the firm's managed PostgreSQL, or Elastic if already run.

**Recommended configuration [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** pgvector on the firm's managed PostgreSQL in a UK or EU region, with one schema per segregated mandate and a shared schema for pooled funds and firm-wide material. Entitlements are joined from the firm's entitlement table inside the same SQL statement. If Elastic is already the firm's search platform, use it with document-level security instead. Move to a dedicated engine only if the load test in §6.9 step 2 fails.

**What L6 must never do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- return another fund's or client's material, by filter omission, by fallback or by a shared partition for segregated mandates
- serve numbers: attribution figures in past commentaries are context, never a source for this month's figures
- keep content after its retention date, or keep a vector copy after the source has been deleted or erased
- hold the only copy of an approved commentary or style guide
- run an unauthenticated store, or hold client content in a region the residency policy does not allow

**H5 ("vector database" should become "Retrieval / Knowledge Stores"). Provisional view; verdict in synthesis.**
