- **Vendors are repositioning above the store.** Pinecone sells Nexus as a "knowledge engine for agents" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S073: General Availability of Pinecone Nexus Proves Knowledge Drives Real Outcomes for Agentic AI <https://www.pinecone.io/newsroom/general-availability-of-pinecone-nexus-proves-knowledge-drives-real-outcomes-for-agentic-ai/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Chroma calls itself data infrastructure for AI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S060: chromadb - PyPI (PyPI / Chroma) <https://pypi.org/project/chromadb/> accessed 2026-10-07]; Elastic calls itself "the Search AI Company" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S023: Elastic Completes Acquisition of Jina AI, a Leader in Frontier Models for Multimodal and Multilingual Search <https://ir.elastic.co/News--Events/news/news-details/2025/Elastic-Completes-Acquisition-of-Jina-AI-a-Leader-in-Frontier-Models-for-Multimodal-and-Multilingual-Search/default.aspx> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Qdrant frames composable vector search as core infrastructure [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S107: We Raised $50M to Build Composable Vector Search as Core Infrastructure (Qdrant) <https://qdrant.tech/blog/series-b-announcement/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

Retrieval-quality evidence points the same way. Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval study reports that combining contextual embeddings with contextual BM25 cut top-20 retrieval failures by 49%, and adding reranking by 67% [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A2-S070: Introducing Contextual Retrieval (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/news/contextual-retrieval> accessed 2026-10-07]. Anthropic is the author's developer, so this is a conflict of interest; the figure is vendor-reported and not a decision input [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The counter-evidence is that dedicated engines still differentiate on filtered search, tenant isolation and scale [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S103: Qdrant 1.17 - Relevance Feedback & Search Latency Improvements <https://qdrant.tech/blog/qdrant-1.17.x/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S124: Architecture - turbopuffer <https://turbopuffer.com/docs/architecture> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A2-S117: Release Notes - Milvus (Milvus project) <https://milvus.io/docs/release_notes.md> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], so the category does not disappear; it becomes one implementation option inside a wider layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. "Knowledge store" also risks overlapping with L5 memory and L8 ingestion, because Nexus reaches into both [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A2-S073: General Availability of Pinecone Nexus Proves Knowledge Drives Real Outcomes for Agentic AI <https://www.pinecone.io/newsroom/general-availability-of-pinecone-nexus-proves-knowledge-drives-real-outcomes-for-agentic-ai/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Provisional recommendation.** Rename the layer "Retrieval and knowledge stores" [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Define it by responsibility (a derived, entitlement-filtered, rebuildable index over approved content) rather than by engine type, and show four implementation options beneath it: vectors in the operational database, search engines, dedicated vector engines, and object-store tiers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Knowledge-engine products should sit at the boundary with L5 and L8, with their curated outputs treated as derived data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


## 5. Memory

> **Executive summary.** This layer decides what an agent carries from one interaction to the next, where that state is stored, and who is allowed to change, inspect or erase it. Four things have changed since the original graphic. First, the independent products have moved apart: Mem0 removed every external graph store from its open-source build on 14 April 2026 and replaced it with entity linking, which is not a queryable graph [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S043: Open Source: Migrating to the New Memory Algorithm; SDK changelog; Highlights (Mem0) <https://docs.mem0.ai/migration/oss-v2-to-v3> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Zep deprecated its Community Edition, so Graphiti is the only open-source path [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S044: Announcing a New Direction for Zep's Open Source Strategy; Zep FAQ <https://blog.getzep.com/announcing-a-new-direction-for-zeps-open-source-strategy/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Letta pivoted to Letta Code, an agent harness, and retired its V1 server [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S060: letta-ai/letta README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S093: Letta's Next Phase (Mar 2026) <https://www.letta.com/blog/our-next-phase/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; and LangMem has had no release since 27 October 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Second, the hyperscalers now ship memory as a platform feature: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory has been GA since 13 October 2025 and Google's Memory Bank since December 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S047: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available (Oct 2025) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S087: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore FAQs; release notes (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; V1-S088: Vertex AI release notes (Agent Engine Sessions and Memory Bank GA; pricing) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Third, every product stores memory in ordinary vector, graph, relational or file stores [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S064: supermemoryai/supermemory README (Supermemory (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07], so memory is a data-architecture problem as much as an agent feature [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Fourth, memory is now a named attack surface: OWASP's Agentic Top 10 includes memory and context poisoning (ASI06) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S001: Memory Is a Feature. It Is Also an Attack Surface (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/2026/05/13/memory-is-a-feature-it-is-also-an-attack-surface/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. No independent product in this layer reaches Strategic tier; the two hyperscaler memory services are Strategic only on the condition that their cloud is the firm's primary cloud (CP3 Q2) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** treat agent memory as a governed record class held in the firm's own retrieval and data stores (L6), written only through an approved, logged write path with subject-scoped erasure and versioning. Build it last, after evaluation, gateway, retrieval, workflows and tools, as the plan's build order already says. Use the agent platform's native memory (AgentCore Memory or Memory Bank) where the runtime already lives there, and self-hosted Mem0 or Graphiti only behind the firm's own memory API [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 5.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns.** It manages state that outlives a single model call and is fed back into later calls [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. That state is of different kinds, and the plan asks for them to be kept apart (plan §5, L5) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

| Memory type | What it holds [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Typical lifetime [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Where it physically lives [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Product evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Conversation** | The turns of the current dialogue | One session | Context window; session or event store | AgentCore short-term memory stores raw session events (messages, tool calls) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; OpenAI's Conversations API persists conversation state as a durable object [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S110: OpenAI API: Conversation state (and Help Center: Memory FAQ) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| **Working** | Scratchpad, plan, intermediate tool results for the task in hand | One task or run | Context window; orchestrator state (L3 checkpoint store, KV cache, Redis) | Letta tracks memory blocks and all context in a git-backed memory filesystem [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; Cognee uses a Redis-compatible cache [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| **Episodic** | Records of specific past events: "on 3 March the PM rejected this phrasing" | Months to years | Event log plus vector index; graph nodes with timestamps | Graphiti stores "episodes" with provenance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; AgentCore offers an episodic extraction strategy [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| **Semantic** | Distilled facts and preferences: "Fund X calls its benchmark the 'reference index'" | Until contradicted or expired | Vector store plus relational fact table, or graph store | Mem0 stores facts in SQL, embeddings in a vector store and entities in an entity store [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]; Memory Bank extracts facts and preferences and consolidates them [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| **Procedural** | How to do things: rules, refined prompts, skills | Versioned releases | Prompt and config store (C5), skill files, Git | LangMem includes prompt refinement to optimise agent behaviour [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; Mem0 lists procedural memory [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| **Organisational** | Shared, curated knowledge for a team or firm: glossaries, house style, approved positions | Records-policy lifetime | Document and knowledge stores (L6/L8), with owners and approval | No product here offers organisational approval workflows as a documented feature [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| **Long-term (user/agent)** | Anything above that persists across sessions for a user, agent or entity | Policy-defined; often unbounded by default | Vector, graph and relational stores behind a memory API | AgentCore long-term records have no built-in time limit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Memory Bank TTL is optional and off by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| **Knowledge base** (not memory) | Authoritative, curated corpora: policies, factsheets, prior approved commentary | Records-policy lifetime | L6 retrieval stores fed by L8 ingestion | Out of scope for this layer; L6 and L8 own it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |

The useful distinction for an architect is not the cognitive label but **who writes the record and how authoritative it is** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A knowledge base is written by an accountable owner through ingestion (L8). Memory is written by the agent, or by an extraction model, as a side effect of interactions. That makes memory the least authoritative and least reviewed data the agent reads, even though it is fed into the prompt in the same way as approved knowledge [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**
- **Up to L3 (orchestration):** the workflow decides when memory is read and when a write is proposed. Conversation and working memory are mostly L3's checkpoint state [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Down to L6/L7 (stores and embeddings):** long-term memory is physically a set of rows, vectors and graph edges in the same kinds of stores that serve retrieval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Embedding and reranking choices (L7) apply to memory recall too [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Sideways to the controls:** C3 (DLP/PII) screens what may be written; C4 (identity) scopes whose memory is read; C5 (prompt and config) holds procedural memory; C8 (governance) holds the retention schedule, erasure evidence and audit; L9 evaluates whether recalled memory helped or harmed [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the layer does not own.** It does not own authoritative business data. Numbers, holdings and client records come from systems of record through read-only tools (L4) and must never be served from memory [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 5.2 Why it matters

A badly designed memory layer fails slowly and invisibly [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The agent's behaviour starts to depend on state that nobody reviewed: a mistaken "fact" extracted from one conversation is recalled in hundreds of later ones; a stale preference overrides a newer instruction; a client's name surfaces in another user's session because the scope key was too broad. Because memory is fed into the prompt like any other context, an injected instruction that lands in memory keeps working long after the original input has gone [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. OWASP's GenAI Security Project describes memory and context poisoning (ASI06) in the same terms: attacker-controlled content that the system continues to trust over time, shaping later planning, tool use and behaviour [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S001: Memory Is a Feature. It Is Also an Attack Surface (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/2026/05/13/memory-is-a-feature-it-is-also-an-attack-surface/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

Memory also creates a regulatory object that did not exist before: a growing store of extracted personal and business information, created automatically, with no natural expiry [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. AgentCore Memory long-term records have no built-in time limit, and AWS recommends a pruner using timestamp filters [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Mem0's open-source extraction is now ADD-only, so memories accumulate rather than being overwritten [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Graphiti invalidates old facts rather than deleting them, keeping history [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Each design choice is defensible for recall quality, and each makes erasure and retention an explicit engineering task rather than a default [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

Finally, memory breaks reproducibility [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A system whose output depends on what it has accumulated cannot be re-run to the same result unless the memory state at the time of the run was captured. That matters for model validation and for explaining a past output to a client or a regulator [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A fund-reporting team enables "learn from feedback" memory on its commentary agent, using a hosted memory service with default settings. In month one, an analyst types a correction into the chat: "the currency effect was negative this month, not positive". The extraction model stores this as a durable fact about the fund: "currency effect: negative". Three months later, with the currency effect now positive in the attribution engine, the agent drafts "currency again detracted", because the recalled memory sits in the prompt next to the tool output and the model reconciles the conflict in the wrong direction. The numeric-faithfulness check catches the sign mismatch, but only for the sentence that contains a figure; two qualitative sentences pass. Separately, a client complaint in the same chat had mentioned a named individual, and the extraction model stored that too. When the client later exercises the right to erasure, the operations team finds that the memory store has no index by data subject, the long-term records have no expiry, and the vendor's deletion API works per record, not per person. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident. It shows three failures that the design in 5.4 and 5.5 prevents: memory used as a source of numbers, unscreened writes, and no subject-scoped lifecycle.

### 5.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Write precision | Share of memory writes a reviewer judges correct, useful and in policy | ≥0.95 for any memory read by a regulated workflow | Sampled human review of the write log |
| Policy-violating writes | Writes containing prohibited classes (client identifiers, special-category data, numbers presented as facts) | Zero reach the store; every block logged | C3 DLP verdicts on the write path, reconciled with store contents |
| Recall usefulness | Share of recalled memories that the eval judges relevant to the task | Rising trend; falls trigger review | L9 evaluation of recalled items in traces |
| Harmful-recall rate | Runs where recalled memory contradicted an authoritative source or a newer instruction | Zero tolerated for numeric content; any case is a defect | L9 contradiction check: memory versus tool output |
| Provenance coverage | Memories carrying source interaction, writer identity, timestamp, approval status and version | 100% | Schema validation on write |
| Erasure completion time | Request received to deletion confirmed across store, indexes, revisions and backups (backups "beyond use") | Within the one-month UK GDPR response window [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S005: Right to erasure (Information Commissioner's Office) <https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/individual-rights/individual-rights/right-to-erasure/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], with an internal target well inside it | Erasure job logs and evidence in C8 |
| Retention conformance | Records older than their retention class that still exist | Zero | Scheduled reconciliation of record ages against the schedule |
| Reproducibility | Runs whose memory state can be reconstructed exactly (snapshot ID or version hash in the trace) | 100% for regulated outputs | Trace completeness check (L9) |
| Scope-leak incidents | Memory recalled outside its scope (user, fund, team) | Zero | Red-team tests and production sampling |
| Memory cost per task | Extraction LLM calls, embeddings, storage and retrieval per completed task | Budget per use case | Gateway (C1) and C6 cost attribution |

The erasure KPI deserves emphasis. The ICO expects erasure from live systems and steps to deal with backups, which may be put "beyond use" until overwritten [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S005: Right to erasure (Information Commissioner's Office) <https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/individual-rights/individual-rights/right-to-erasure/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Its storage-limitation guidance expects periodic review and deletion or anonymisation of data no longer needed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S006: Principle (e): Storage limitation (Information Commissioner's Office) <https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/data-protection-principles/a-guide-to-the-data-protection-principles/storage-limitation/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Memory products do not do this by default, so the KPI measures a capability the firm must build [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 5.4 How it works

Every memory system has a write path and a read path, and the governance sits almost entirely on the write path [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Write path.**
1. **Capture.** The orchestrator passes interaction events (messages, tool calls, reviewer edits) to the memory service. AgentCore stores these as short-term events, with expiry configurable between 7 and 365 days per the API reference (the stated minimum conflicts between pages) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
2. **Extraction.** An LLM proposes candidate memories. Memory Bank uses Gemini models to extract facts, preferences and context asynchronously [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. AgentCore offers semantic, summary, user-preference, episodic and custom strategies [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Mem0's April 2026 algorithm uses single-pass ADD-only extraction with entity linking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Cognee can extract locally with a small model (GLiNER) without an LLM key [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
3. **Consolidation.** New candidates are reconciled with existing memories. Memory Bank resolves contradictions and may delete contradicted memories or honour explicit "forget" instructions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Graphiti marks old facts invalid with validity windows rather than deleting them [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Supermemory handles temporal changes and contradictions and forgets expired information automatically [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S064: supermemoryai/supermemory README (Supermemory (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
4. **Storage.** The record is written to ordinary stores: SQL plus a third-party vector store plus an entity store (Mem0, default local Qdrant in open source) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]; Neo4j, FalkorDB or Neptune (Graphiti) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; SQLite, LanceDB and an embedded graph package by default, or Neo4j, Neptune or Postgres/pgvector (Cognee) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; a LangGraph BaseStore (LangMem) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; a git-backed filesystem (Letta) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Read path.** At the start of a step, the orchestrator queries memory by scope (user, agent, run, namespace) and by similarity, and injects the results into the prompt. Mem0 fuses semantic, BM25 and entity signals [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S001: PyPI JSON metadata: mem0ai (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mem0ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Graphiti combines semantic, keyword and graph search [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Memory Bank retrieves by exact scope with optional similarity search [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. These are the same hybrid retrieval techniques L6 and L7 use for knowledge bases [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Where the governance controls belong [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The vendor products automate steps 2 to 4. An enterprise design inserts a policy gate between extraction and storage, keeps a write log, and attaches provenance and a retention class to each record:

```text
                         WRITE PATH (governed)                                    READ PATH
 interaction events ─► extraction (LLM) ─► POLICY GATE ──────────► memory store ─► scoped recall ─► prompt
 (L3 workflow,          proposes            │ C3 DLP: no client IDs,   │ rows (SQL)      │ by user/fund/
  reviewer edits)       candidate facts     │   no special-category    │ vectors (L6)    │ team scope (C4)
                                            │ type allow-list          │ graph edges     │ + similarity
                                            │ "no numbers as facts"    │ files/Git       │
                                            │ human approval for       │                 ▼
                                            │   organisational memory  │        trace: memory IDs +
                                            ▼                          │        version hash (L9)
                                     write log (C8) ◄──────────────────┤
                                     who, what, source, approval       │
                                                                       ▼
                         LIFECYCLE: retention class per record · TTL/pruner · subject index for erasure
                                    · revisions purge · snapshot per release for reproducibility
```

The **subject index** is the key design choice [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Every memory that may contain personal data must be findable by data subject, so that an erasure request can be satisfied by one query across rows, vectors, graph nodes, revisions and caches. AgentCore supports per-user erasure by listing and deleting a user's namespace records [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Memory Bank purges by filter with a dry run [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Mem0 has delete, delete_all and per-memory history in both open source and Platform [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Each of these works only if scoping was designed for it from the first write [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 5.5 Enterprise design principles

**Governance (the centre of gravity for this layer)**

- **Decide what may be remembered before choosing a product.** Write an allow-list of memory types per use case (for example "terminology preferences: yes; client facts: no; figures: never") and enforce it at the policy gate [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Separate proposal from commitment.** Organisational and procedural memory (house style, glossaries, prompt rules) should be proposed by the agent but committed only after human approval, as a versioned artefact [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Per-user preference memory can be committed automatically if it passes the gate and is user-visible and user-editable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Anthropic's Claude app memory, for example, offers a user-editable memory summary, project-scoped memory and an admin switch to disable memory on Team and Enterprise plans [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S071: Bringing memory to Claude (11 Sep 2025; updated 23 Oct 2025) (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/news/memory> accessed 2026-10-07]. (Conflict-of-interest note: the author is an Anthropic model; the same pattern of user-visible, admin-controlled memory is available in ChatGPT, where memory can be switched off [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S110: OpenAI API: Conversation state (and Help Center: Memory FAQ) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].)
- **Every record carries provenance and a retention class.** Source interaction ID, writer (user, agent or extraction model and version), timestamp, approval status, scope, data-classification label and expiry [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Erasure is designed, not assumed.** Product behaviour differs widely. Vendor-hosted chat memory and chat history can be separate: deleting a ChatGPT chat does not delete its saved memories, and deleted memory logs may be kept for up to 30 days [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S110: OpenAI API: Conversation state (and Help Center: Memory FAQ) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Memory Bank keeps memory revisions for 365 days by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. AgentCore harness-managed memory cannot be deleted through the Memory APIs, and deleting the memory resource removes all its events and records [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Test the erasure path end to end, including revisions and indexes, before go-live [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Memory never outranks authority.** In the prompt, memory is labelled as such and placed below tool outputs and approved knowledge. The workflow, not the model, resolves conflicts in favour of the authoritative source [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Auditability of recall.** Record which memory IDs and versions were injected into each run, so a past output can be explained and reproduced [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Zep's audit logs cover web-app member actions only, not API or SDK calls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], so recall auditing must come from the firm's own traces in that case [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Security**

- Treat memory as a persistent prompt-injection vector. Screen writes for instructions as well as for PII, and red-team the memory path against ASI06 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S001: Memory Is a Feature. It Is Also an Attack Surface (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/2026/05/13/memory-is-a-feature-it-is-also-an-attack-surface/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Enforce scope at the identity layer (C4), not by convention. Memory Bank's scope is immutable and retrieval returns only exact-scope matches [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], which is the right default [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Use customer-managed keys where available. AgentCore Memory encrypts at rest with an AWS-owned key by default and accepts a customer-managed KMS key, set at creation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S002: Encrypt your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory (and AWS Config / Security Hub / SRA pages) (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/storage-encryption.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Memory Bank lists CMEK, but not on its global endpoint [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S004: Scale your agents / Set up Memory Bank / release notes / data residency terms (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Zep offers BYOK on Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S090: Zep Enterprise (and Emerging Companies programme page) <https://www.getzep.com/enterprise/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Restrict who can read memory directly. AWS's security reference architecture recommends limiting IAM access to memory APIs such as ListMemoryRecords and DeleteMemoryRecord [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S002: Encrypt your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory (and AWS Config / Security Hub / SRA pages) (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/storage-encryption.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A memory store is a concentrated index of what users said, so treat it like a trace store [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability, resilience and cost**

- Extraction is LLM spend on every interaction. Mem0's self-hosted cost is driven by the vector store, LLM extraction calls and the embedder [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Memory Bank bills LLM usage for memory generation separately from its per-memory charges [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S088: Vertex AI release notes (Agent Engine Sessions and Memory Bank GA; pricing) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Graphiti's README warns of LLM rate-limit errors at default concurrency [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Run extraction asynchronously and only for workflows that need it [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Memory must degrade gracefully: if the memory service is down, the workflow runs without it rather than failing [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Observability and evaluation**

- Every recall and every write is a span in the trace (L9), carrying memory IDs and the gate verdict [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Evaluate memory as a retrieval component: relevance of recalled items, and contradiction with authoritative sources [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Portability**

- Put a thin firm-owned memory API (write, recall, forget-by-subject, snapshot) in front of any product, and keep the canonical record in a store the firm controls [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Mem0 open source already supports 14 or more vector stores, including PGVector, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch and MongoDB [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], so the backing store can be the firm's existing L6 platform [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** policy-gated write path; subject index for erasure; "style memory" as a versioned, approved artefact in Git or the prompt store; memory snapshot hash recorded per run; memory below authority in prompt assembly; hyperscaler memory only inside that hyperscaler's agent runtime.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** free-form "remember everything" memory on regulated workflows; memory as a source of figures; one shared memory scope across clients or funds; vendor default retention ("none") left in place; graph "invalidation" mistaken for erasure; memory switched on before evaluation and tracing exist; extraction sent to an unassessed third-party LLM.

**Why memory is built last.** The plan's day-one build order puts memory in phase 6, after governance (0), evaluation and observability (1), model access through the gateway (2), retrieval and knowledge (3), agent workflows (4) and tools (5) (plan §12.6). The reasoning holds up [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- Memory changes behaviour over time, so its effect can only be measured once evaluation and tracing exist (phase 1) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Extraction is a model call, so it should route through the gateway, with its residency and logging controls (phase 2) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Memory is stored and recalled with retrieval infrastructure, so the L6 store, embeddings and access model should be settled first (phase 3) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- The write and read points are steps in a workflow, and the safe pattern is a deterministic workflow that decides when to remember (phase 4) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Authoritative data must already flow through read-only tools before memory is added, so that memory never becomes the easiest place to find a number (phase 5) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Many first use cases, including the worked example, deliver most of their value without long-term memory at all: retrieval of approved knowledge plus session state is enough [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 5.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Coverage of the memory types in 5.1; extraction quality and control (custom prompts, type allow-lists); consolidation and contradiction handling; temporal validity; scoping model; hybrid recall; deletion granularity (record, subject, namespace, revisions); procedural memory |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC and audit logs that cover API reads and writes, not only console actions; admin APIs; SLA; multi-tenancy that maps to funds, teams and clients |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in the product's scope; CMK/BYOK; residency; DPA; erasure and retention features; screening hooks on the write path |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Self-host or BYOC so memory, which concentrates personal data, can stay in-estate; choice of backing store |
| Ecosystem (5%) | Framework integrations (LangGraph, ADK, Strands, CrewAI); MCP; supported vector and graph stores |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | Release cadence and breaking changes (four of the six original products changed architecture or cadence materially in 2025–26); funding stage; pre-1.0 status |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Extraction LLM spend, per-memory pricing, storage; licence gates on production features |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Whether the canonical record sits in a store you own; export; proprietary graph engines; Platform-only features |

**Vendor benchmark scores are not decision inputs.** Mem0 reports LoCoMo 92.5 and LongMemEval 94.4 for its managed platform [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], and Supermemory claims first place on LongMemEval, LoCoMo and ConvoMem [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S064: supermemoryai/supermemory README (Supermemory (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Test recall on your own data instead [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 5.7 Product deep dives

**Mem0 (Mem0).**
- *What it is now:* an open-core agent memory layer. The Apache-2.0 open-source library and self-hosted server extract facts from conversations and agent actions, scope them by user_id, agent_id and run_id, and retrieve them with entity-aware ranking; add, search, get, update, delete, delete_all and per-memory history exist in both the open-source and hosted clients [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S001: PyPI JSON metadata: mem0ai (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mem0ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. mem0ai 2.2.1 was released on 25 September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S001: PyPI JSON metadata: mem0ai (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mem0ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Open source and Platform diverge:* open-source v2.0.0 (14 April 2026) removed all external graph backends (Neo4j, Memgraph, Kuzu, Apache AGE, Neptune) and replaced them with built-in entity linking, which is a parallel entity collection that boosts retrieval, not a queryable graph [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S043: Open Source: Migrating to the New Memory Algorithm; SDK changelog; Highlights (Mem0) <https://docs.mem0.ai/migration/oss-v2-to-v3> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Graph memory, memory decay, temporal reasoning, Dream consolidation, webhooks and memory export are Platform-only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. The open-source extraction is now ADD-only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Certifications and deployment:* Mem0's own pages conflict on SOC 2: Type I on the homepage, Type II "in progress" in one article and Type II "for Enterprise" in one guide; HIPAA is claimed and no trust-centre report was seen [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S051: Enterprise AI Memory Options That Pass Security Review (Mem0) <https://mem0.ai/guide/enterprise-ai-memory-security-review-options> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S106: Mem0 guide: Solving SOC 2 Compliance for Enterprise AI Memory (and related mem0.ai pages) <https://mem0.ai/guide/solving-soc-2-compliance-enterprise-ai-memory> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No managed EU region was found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S106: Mem0 guide: Solving SOC 2 Compliance for Enterprise AI Memory (and related mem0.ai pages) <https://mem0.ai/guide/solving-soc-2-compliance-enterprise-ai-memory> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The vendor states private Kubernetes deployment in the customer's VPC, on-premises and air-gapped options, and BYOK encryption [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S049: Mem0 pricing <https://mem0.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S051: Enterprise AI Memory Options That Pass Security Review (Mem0) <https://mem0.ai/guide/enterprise-ai-memory-security-review-options> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Access control:* the Enterprise plan lists SSO and audit logs; the Platform has organisations and projects with member roles and a project-wide event feed of add, search and delete events; open source has no organisation or project concept [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S049: Mem0 pricing <https://mem0.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Strengths:* a wide choice of backing stores, so the canonical memory record can sit in the firm's existing L6 platform [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A large open-source community: the most GitHub stars of the products here, at 66,777 GitHub stars on 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S054: GitHub repository metadata (stars, forks, created, archived) retrieved via GitHub MCP search_repositories tool, 7 Oct 2026 <https://api.github.com/search/repositories> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Limitations:* the security evidence is vendor marketing only, and the SOC 2 type is unresolved [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S106: Mem0 guide: Solving SOC 2 Compliance for Enterprise AI Memory (and related mem0.ai pages) <https://mem0.ai/guide/solving-soc-2-compliance-enterprise-ai-memory> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. April 2026 brought breaking changes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. ADD-only extraction means memories accumulate unless the firm prunes them [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The vendor ships an "OSS-to-Platform" migration skill [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], which signals the commercial direction [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you want a framework-neutral memory API that you self-host on your own vector store, with your own policy gate in front [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need the managed Platform for regulated data before a SOC 2 Type II report is in hand, or you need a queryable graph in open source [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Zep/Graphiti, Supermemory, AgentCore Memory, Cognee.
- *FS note:* self-host the open-source server against your approved vector store, put the policy gate and subject index in your own wrapper, and request the SOC 2 report before any Platform use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical. Flag: none.**

**Zep and Graphiti (Zep).**
- *What it is now:* Zep is a managed "context infrastructure" platform built on a proprietary Context Graph Engine; Graphiti is the Apache-2.0 temporal knowledge-graph framework underneath [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Graphiti builds bi-temporal graphs: entities, facts with validity windows, episodes with provenance, and communities; old facts are invalidated rather than deleted; retrieval is hybrid semantic, keyword and graph search [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. zep-cloud 3.30.0 was released on 24 September 2026 with a 4.0.0b1 pre-release on 6 October 2026; graphiti-core is at 0.30.2 (8 September 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S002: PyPI JSON metadata: zep-cloud (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/zep-cloud/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Community Edition:* deprecated and unsupported; its code sits in a legacy folder under Apache-2.0. The deprecation date is not confirmed by an official source [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S044: Announcing a New Direction for Zep's Open Source Strategy; Zep FAQ <https://blog.getzep.com/announcing-a-new-direction-for-zeps-open-source-strategy/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Certifications and deployment:* SOC 2 Type II and a HIPAA BAA on the Enterprise plan only, not on Flex or Flex Plus [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S090: Zep Enterprise (and Emerging Companies programme page) <https://www.getzep.com/enterprise/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. BYOK and BYOC (AWS, GCP, Azure) on Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S090: Zep Enterprise (and Emerging Companies programme page) <https://www.getzep.com/enterprise/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. US hosting by default, with EU residency on request; DPAs with EU customers; right-to-be-forgotten and time-based retention purge (Zep Archive) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No ISO 27001 was found [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Access control:* IdP-based sign-in (SAML not named), RBAC for the dashboard and ABAC policies for data reads and writes. Audit logs cover web-app member actions only, not API or SDK calls; Enterprise keeps audit and API logs for one year [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* a close match to what a regulated firm needs from episodic and semantic memory: validity windows, provenance per episode, and history that survives updates [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Broad framework integrations, including Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, LangGraph and Strands [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Limitations:* "invalidate, not delete" preserves history, which is good for audit and awkward for erasure; erasure needs the platform's explicit right-to-be-forgotten feature or a delete in Graphiti's graph store [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Compliance is tier-gated [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Graphiti is pre-1.0 and the SDK 4.0 is in beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S002: PyPI JSON metadata: zep-cloud (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/zep-cloud/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Self-hosted Graphiti needs Neo4j, FalkorDB or Neptune, and the Kuzu backend is deprecated [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Choose when:* temporal reasoning and provenance matter, for example memory of how a client mandate or a fund's terminology changed over time; Graphiti self-hosted on Neo4j or Neptune where data must stay in-estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need API-level audit logs from the vendor, ISO 27001, or a supported self-hosted version of the full Zep platform [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Graphiti versus Cognee for self-hosted graph memory; Zep Cloud versus Mem0 Platform and Memory Bank.
- *FS note:* prefer self-hosted Graphiti on an approved graph store, and test that erasure removes invalidated facts and episodes, not only current ones. For Zep Cloud, buy Enterprise only and request EU residency [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical. Flag: Deprecated (Community Edition).**

**Letta (Letta).**
- *What it is now:* a stateful agent harness, not a standalone memory library. Letta (formerly MemGPT) announced "Letta's Next Phase" in March 2026: Letta Code is a model-agnostic harness with a git-backed memory filesystem (MemFS), and the legacy server memory tools, templates, server-side sleep-time agents and tool rules are deprecated [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S093: Letta's Next Phase (Mar 2026) <https://www.letta.com/blog/our-next-phase/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S042: Letta's Next Phase <https://www.letta.com/blog/our-next-phase/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The V1 API server was retired to an archive branch and the PyPI package `letta` now installs the Letta Code CLI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S060: letta-ai/letta README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S004: PyPI JSON metadata: letta (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/letta/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Letta Code 0.34.4 was released on 4 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S004: PyPI JSON metadata: letta (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/letta/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S077: npm registry metadata: @letta-ai/letta-code <https://registry.npmjs.org/@letta-ai/letta-code> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Memory model:* memory blocks and all context are tracked in MemFS, which can sync to a GitHub repository; message search works across agents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. AgentFile (.af) export and import were removed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Certifications and deployment:* no SOC 2 or trust centre was found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S118: Letta Privacy Policy (and docs on agent state persistence) <https://www.letta.com/privacy-policy/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Letta Cloud is the default backend storing agent state; `letta server` runs agents locally or self-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S060: letta-ai/letta README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The privacy policy states no specific retention periods [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S118: Letta Privacy Policy (and docs on agent state persistence) <https://www.letta.com/privacy-policy/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Access control:* RBAC and SAML/OIDC SSO on the Enterprise tier, plus permission modes for agent actions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S091: Letta pricing (docs) <https://docs.letta.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Audit logs are not documented [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Strengths:* memory as files under version control is a highly reviewable memory model: every change is a diff [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* the architecture has changed twice in eighteen months, and Letta Code is pre-1.0 with eight releases between 29 September and 4 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S077: npm registry metadata: @letta-ai/letta-code <https://registry.npmjs.org/@letta-ai/letta-code> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S004: PyPI JSON metadata: letta (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/letta/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. It is not a drop-in memory layer for other frameworks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Git history keeps deleted content unless history is rewritten, which complicates erasure [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Funding found is a US$10M seed in September 2024 [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S092: Letta Emerges from Stealth with $10M to Build AI Agents with Advanced Memory (Sep 2024) (BigDATAwire (press release)) <https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/this-just-in/letta-emerges-from-stealth-with-10m-to-build-ai-agents-with-advanced-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* you are evaluating a stateful coding or operations agent where the harness and its memory come together, outside regulated client data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need a memory service for an existing LangGraph, ADK or Strands workflow, or certifications [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* LangGraph with LangMem, AgentCore (runtime plus memory), Google ADK with Memory Bank.
- *FS note:* the git-backed memory idea is worth copying for "style memory" in your own repository; the product itself is not a regulated-workflow dependency today [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Experimental. Flag: Superseded (V1 server replaced by Letta Code).**

**Cognee (Cognee).**

Defaults are SQLite, LanceDB and an embedded graph package, with optional Neo4j, Amazon Neptune and Postgres/pgvector [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

It is an EU company with GDPR processes audited by heyData, a DPA on request, support for access, erasure and portability rights, encryption at rest and in transit, a private mode with zero external API calls, and air-gapped self-hosting [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S095: Cognee Cloud: Security & Data Protection (docs) and cognee.ai FAQ/GDPR pages <https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-cloud/functionality/data-and-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

Multi-tenant mode with authenticated users by default, and Enterprise SSO, SLAs and a dedicated support engineer [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S095: Cognee Cloud: Security & Data Protection (docs) and cognee.ai FAQ/GDPR pages <https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-cloud/functionality/data-and-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. RBAC and audit logs are not documented [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Strengths:* a clear in-estate option: graph and vector memory on the firm's own Postgres or Neo4j, with local extraction possible [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It spans memory and knowledge ingestion, which fits the H4 view that they share infrastructure [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* no certification, by the vendor's own statement [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S095: Cognee Cloud: Security & Data Protection (docs) and cognee.ai FAQ/GDPR pages <https://docs.cognee.ai/cognee-cloud/functionality/data-and-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The production Postgres graph is licensed, not open [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Seed-stage funding, with aggregators disagreeing on the amount [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S094: Cognee: $7.5 Million Seed Funding Raised (Feb 2026) (Pulse 2.0) <https://pulse2.com/cognee-7-5-million-seed-funding-raised-for-building-enterprise-grade-memory-layer-for-ai-agents/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Scoring notes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- **No independent product reaches Strategic.** The highest FS total is 3.50 (Zep), below the 3.6 guide. The independent products are held back by certification evidence (Mem0, Cognee, Supermemory, Letta) or lock-in (Zep Cloud). AgentCore Memory and Memory Bank (FS 3.20) are Strategic only on the condition "where this is your primary cloud": rubric rule 10 (CP3 Q2) makes the lead hyperscaler service in a category Strategic, conditional, when no criterion is 1. Their criterion scores are unchanged, and security stays at 4 under rule 8. This is consistent with the recommendation that memory be a governed record class on the firm's own stores: the platform service is the store, not the record.
- **CP2 Q1 hyperscaler presumption** gives AgentCore Memory and Memory Bank enterprise readiness of 4. Their security is scored under rule 8: AgentCore's certifications are service-level and in scope (SOC 2 type not stated); Memory Bank's are platform-level with its inclusion not stated. Both score 4, not 5.
- **Evidence caps and anchors.** Mem0 security is 2: the vendor confirms SOC 2 Type I, and its Type II claims conflict. Letta security is capped at 2 (no certification found). Cognee states it holds no certification, so it is scored as self-hosted software under rule 2 (its own recommended deployment); Cognee Cloud on its own would score 1. Supermemory security is 2 because the SOC 2 report type is unconfirmed. Cognee and Supermemory enterprise readiness is 3: verified SSO lifts the cap to a maximum of 3 under rule 7 (CP2 Q2), as for LlamaParse (L8) and Browserbase (L4); RBAC and audit logs are not documented. They had been held at 2 before the CP3 review.
- **Rule 7 at 4 (CP3 review).** Mem0 (SSO, audit logs and SLA on Enterprise; Platform roles [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S049: Mem0 pricing <https://mem0.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]) and Zep (IdP sign-in, RBAC and ABAC, audit logs, SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S107: Zep docs: Governance (and Audit logging page, Zep Archive blog) <https://help.getzep.com/governance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S089: Zep pricing <https://www.getzep.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]) have all three controls plus an SLA, so they score 4, as Firecrawl and Mistral OCR do in L8. The conditions are stated: Mem0's evidence is a pricing page and its open source has no organisation concept; Zep's audit logs cover web-app actions, not API or SDK calls.
- **AgentCore Memory cost** is 3, not 2: unit prices are published (short-term memory per GB from 6 October 2026; long-term US$0.75 or US$0.25 per 1,000 records a month and US$0.50 per 1,000 retrievals) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REVA-S005: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing (Memory) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **LangMem** is scored as a library under rule 2, and its maturity is 1: pre-1.0 with no release in eleven months.
- **No ownership-change reduction** applies in this layer; no acquisition was found for any of the eight products.

### 5.9 Decision tree

The tree is applied in four steps. Step 0 and step 4 are not product choices [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
STEP 0 [Rec]: Do you need long-term memory at all?
  Can the use case be met by session state (L3) + retrieval of approved knowledge (L6)?
  ├─ Yes → No L5 product. Keep conversation/working memory in the orchestrator's
  │        checkpoint store. Revisit after evaluation shows a gap.
  └─ No  → Write the memory allow-list (types, scopes, retention classes, prohibited
           content) and get it approved by data protection and the model owner.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Which kind of memory?
  Organisational / procedural (style, glossary, rules)?
  ├─ Yes → NOT agent memory. Versioned artefact in Git or the prompt store (C5),
  │        proposed by the agent, approved by a human, retrieved like knowledge (L6).
  └─ No  → per-user / per-entity episodic or semantic memory → STEP 2

STEP 2 [Rec]: Where does the agent runtime live?
  ├─ AWS AgentCore / Strands  → AgentCore Memory (CMK at creation, pruner on day one)
  ├─ Google ADK / Agent Engine → Memory Bank (regional endpoint + CMEK, TTL set,
  │                              residency confirmed in writing)
  └─ Elsewhere / multi-cloud / in-estate required
        Need temporal validity and provenance (how facts changed over time)?
        ├─ Yes → Graphiti self-hosted on Neo4j / FalkorDB / Neptune
        │        (Zep Cloud Enterprise only if managed is acceptable and API audit
        │         logs are not required from the vendor)
        └─ No  → Air-gapped or graph-plus-documents in one store?
                 ├─ Yes → Cognee self-hosted (no vendor certification: you supply controls)
                 └─ No  → Mem0 open source on your approved vector store (pgvector,
                          OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, MongoDB), behind your own API

STEP 3 [Rec]: Wrap whatever you chose
  Firm-owned memory API: write (via policy gate), recall (scoped), forget-by-subject,
  snapshot. Write log to C8. Every recall and write as a span in L9 traces.

STEP 4 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Erasure test across rows, vectors, graph, revisions, caches, backups ("beyond use")?
  Retention classes enforced by TTL or pruner?   No client identifiers in memory (C3)?
  Memory snapshot ID recorded per run?   ASI06 memory-poisoning red-team passed?
  Numbers never read from memory (L9 contradiction check)?
```

Letta, Supermemory and LangMem do not appear as defaults. Letta is a harness, not a memory service; Supermemory merges memory and knowledge behind one proprietary API; LangMem is stalled [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

|---|---|---|---|

Zep Cloud uses a proprietary graph engine [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; Mem0 makes memory export Platform-only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S080: Mem0 docs source: Platform vs Open Source (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/platform/platform-vs-oss.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]; Memory Bank memories are deleted with the Agent Runtime instance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Canonical record in the firm's own L6 store, or a regular export to it |
| Memory API | **Manageable** | Every product exposes add, search and delete; the semantics differ (ADD-only, invalidate, consolidate) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Thin firm-owned interface: write, recall, forget-by-subject, snapshot |
