### 5.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Data protection: erasure, retention and minimisation.**
- *The right to erasure.* Article 17(1) GDPR gives a data subject the right to obtain erasure without undue delay where one of the listed grounds applies, and Article 17(3) sets exceptions, including legal claims [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S007: Judgment C-26/22 (and C-484/24) on GDPR Articles 5(1)(e) and 17 (Court of Justice of the EU (EUR-Lex)) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A62022CJ0026> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Under UK GDPR the ICO expects erasure from live systems, steps for backups ("beyond use" until overwritten), clarity to the individual about what happens, and a response within one month; the ICO notes that this guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S005: Right to erasure (Information Commissioner's Office) <https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/individual-rights/individual-rights/right-to-erasure/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The DUAA's data protection provisions are in force [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S051: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: commencement (GOV.UK, SI 2025/904, SI 2026/82, ICO) (DSIT / legislation.gov.uk / ICO) <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/data-use-and-access-act-2025-plans-for-commencement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Storage limitation.* Personal data must be kept no longer than necessary, with periodic review and erasure or anonymisation, including in backups [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S006: Principle (e): Storage limitation (Information Commissioner's Office) <https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/data-protection-principles/a-guide-to-the-data-protection-principles/storage-limitation/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L5-S007: Judgment C-26/22 (and C-484/24) on GDPR Articles 5(1)(e) and 17 (Court of Justice of the EU (EUR-Lex)) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A62022CJ0026> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *What this means for memory.* A memory store is personal-data processing by default, because extraction picks up names, preferences and circumstances from conversation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Defaults in this layer run against storage limitation: no long-term TTL in AgentCore [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S111: Designing lifecycle policies for AgentCore memory (and AgentCore Memory docs: harness-memory, delete-memory, UpdateMemory, memory-record-streaming) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/designing-lifecycle-policies-for-agentcore-memory/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], no default TTL in Memory Bank [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], ADD-only accumulation in Mem0 open source [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], invalidation rather than deletion in Graphiti [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. The firm must therefore set retention classes, minimise at the write gate, and keep a subject index [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Records-keeping versus erasure.* Some content an agent sees may also be a business record the firm must keep. Whether a records obligation overrides an erasure request is a legal question for each record class [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The architectural answer is to keep memory and records apart: records belong in the records archive (C8), and memory holds only what the agent needs, under shorter retention [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Transfers.* Extraction calls send conversation content to a model. For EU and UK personal data sent to US-hosted services, the lawful basis rests on the Data Privacy Framework or SCCs, and the C-703/25 P appeal is pending [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Run extraction on in-region models through the gateway [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Model risk and reproducibility.**
- *SS1/23.* PRA SS1/23 requires independent validation (Principle 4) and covers vendor models; it applies to banks and PRA-designated firms with internal-model approval and is the natural benchmark for others [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *The memory problem for validation.* A system whose behaviour changes with accumulated memory is a moving target: the validated system and the running system diverge every time memory is written [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Two responses work. Either the memory used by a regulated workflow is frozen per release (versioned "style memory" that changes only through change control), or every run records a memory snapshot so validators can reproduce any output [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Free-form self-updating memory on a model-risk-relevant workflow should be treated as a material change process, with monitoring thresholds, not as configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and expressly excludes generative and agentic AI, leaving governance to the firm's own risk-management practices [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Memory governance is therefore the firm's own standard to set in the US as well [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- *Logging duties.* Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to keep logs for at least six months and to monitor operation; financial institutions fold logging into existing financial-services documentation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Application to memory.* For any high-risk use, the log must show what the system recalled, not only what it was asked, because recalled memory is part of the input [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Most asset-management uses, including attribution commentary, are not Annex III [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Building recall logging anyway serves MRM and complaints handling [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Operational resilience and outsourcing.**
- *Memory SaaS is an ICT third-party service.* A hosted memory service holding client conversation data belongs in the DORA register of information, with Article 30 terms and an exit plan if it supports a critical or important function [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. In the UK, SYSC 8 and FG16/5 expect data location, effective access and exit planning [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

### 5.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from L5 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary (allocation, selection, currency, benchmark-relative return) for a generic multi-asset fund. The plan asks L5 for "memory of fund-specific terminology and the PM's past edits, under governance" (plan §11.2). Read carefully, that is not free-form agent memory at all. It is a governed, versioned **style memory** [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
1. **Fund terminology glossary.** Preferred names for the benchmark, sleeves and asset classes, and phrases the PM always uses or never uses. Stored as a versioned file per fund (for example YAML in Git or the prompt store, C5), retrieved by fund ID, owned by the PM or product specialist.
2. **Style rules distilled from past edits.** The PM's edits are already captured as diffs on each trace by L9. A monthly job clusters recurring edits ("replaced 'outperformed' with 'returned more than' in 9 of 12 drafts") and proposes new style rules. The proposals are a pull request, not a memory write: the PM approves, rejects or amends them, and the approved version becomes the next release of style memory.
3. **Scoped episodic notes, if any.** Short notes such as "Q3 commentary must mention the mandate change agreed in July", entered by a person, with an expiry date. The agent may propose them; a person commits them.
4. **Recall by version.** Each run reads one pinned version of the glossary and style rules. The version hash is recorded in the trace and the evidence pack (C8), so any commentary can be regenerated with the memory it actually used. Validators review style memory changes as configuration changes.
5. **Session state only for the draft in hand.** Working memory for the current draft lives in the L3 workflow checkpoint and is discarded after approval, apart from what the evidence pack retains.

**Product implication [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** This slice needs no L5 product. Git or the prompt store, plus the L6 retrieval path and the L9 edit capture, deliver it with better governance than any memory service in 5.7. A memory product becomes useful only if the firm later adds per-user preference memory across many agents, at which point the decision tree in 5.9 applies.

**What L5 must never do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- remember client identifiers, holdings by client, or any personal data from the drafting conversation; C3 screens the write path and the allow-list excludes them
- serve a number, sign or direction ("detracted", "overweight") from memory; every figure comes from the attribution engine through the read-only L4 tool, and L9's contradiction check fails any draft where a recalled memory disagrees with tool output
- override the authoritative attribution output or an approved source when memory and data conflict; the workflow resolves conflicts in favour of the source, not the model
- change style memory without a human approval and a new version
- let a memory written for one fund be recalled for another; scope is the fund ID, enforced at C4
- keep memory after its retention class expires, or survive an erasure request in revisions, caches or graph history
