**H4 (memory may not be separate from retrieval and data architecture). Provisional view; verdict in synthesis.**

The evidence supports the hypothesis on four counts.

- **Memory products are retrieval stacks with an extraction step.** Every product stores memory in the same kinds of stores that L6 governs: SQL plus vector plus entity store (Mem0), Neo4j, FalkorDB or Neptune (Graphiti), SQLite, LanceDB, Postgres/pgvector or Neptune (Cognee), a LangGraph store (LangMem), a git-backed filesystem (Letta) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S053: Mem0 docs: Platform vs Open Source (and OSS v2-to-v3 migration notes) <https://docs.mem0.ai/platform/platform-vs-oss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S073: letta-ai/letta-code README (Letta (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/letta-ai/letta-code/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Recall uses the same hybrid semantic, keyword and graph search as knowledge retrieval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S001: PyPI JSON metadata: mem0ai (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mem0ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S064: supermemoryai/supermemory README (Supermemory (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **The products are converging with RAG.** Supermemory's default mode combines RAG and memory in one query, with connectors and file processing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S064: supermemoryai/supermemory README (Supermemory (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Cognee ingests documents, code and conversations into one graph [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S005: PyPI JSON metadata: cognee (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cognee/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Zep ingests chat history and business data into the same graph [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **The platforms are absorbing memory.** AWS and Google ship memory as a feature of their agent platforms; the AgentCore harness provisions memory automatically [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S048: Release notes for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/release-notes.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S108: Vertex AI Memory Bank in public preview (8 Jul 2025) (Google Cloud Blog) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/vertex-ai-memory-bank-in-public-preview> accessed 2026-10-07]. Model vendors ship memory in their own products and APIs: Anthropic's memory tool executes file operations on storage the developer controls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S069: Memory tool - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool> accessed 2026-10-07], and OpenAI persists conversation state through its Conversations API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S110: OpenAI API: Conversation state (and Help Center: Memory FAQ) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **The independent layer is thinning.** Mem0 removed graph stores from open source [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S081: Mem0 docs source: Open Source migration to the new memory algorithm (Mem0 (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mem0ai/mem0/main/docs/migration/oss-v2-to-v3.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S043: Open Source: Migrating to the New Memory Algorithm; SDK changelog; Highlights (Mem0) <https://docs.mem0.ai/migration/oss-v2-to-v3> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], Zep deprecated its Community Edition [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S059: getzep/zep README: Zep Cloud Examples & Integrations (Zep AI (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getzep/zep/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07], Letta pivoted to an agent harness [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S093: Letta's Next Phase (Mar 2026) <https://www.letta.com/blog/our-next-phase/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and LangMem has not released in eleven months [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: langmem (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langmem/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

The counter-evidence is real. Memory has a write path that retrieval does not have: extraction from interactions, consolidation, contradiction handling and decay [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S109: Vertex AI Agent Engine Memory Bank overview / generate memories / Memory Bank REST reference (docs.cloud.google.com, now 'Agent Platform Memory Bank') (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/agent-engine/memory-bank/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: graphiti-core (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/graphiti-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S064: supermemoryai/supermemory README (Supermemory (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/supermemoryai/supermemory/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Its governance is also different in kind. Knowledge bases are written by accountable owners and retained under the records policy; memory is written by an agent, is per-subject, and must be erasable per person [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Both hyperscalers chose to expose memory as a distinct service, not as a feature of their vector stores [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S047: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available (Oct 2025) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S108: Vertex AI Memory Bank in public preview (8 Jul 2025) (Google Cloud Blog) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/vertex-ai-memory-bank-in-public-preview> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Provisional recommendation.** Memory should not be a separate infrastructure layer in the reference architecture [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Physically, it belongs with retrieval and data stores (L6), and its organisational and procedural forms belong with prompt and configuration management (C5) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Logically, a thin **memory service** remains worth drawing, because it carries the controls that are unique to memory: the policy-gated write path, the subject index, retention and erasure, and per-run snapshots [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The suggested verdict is **merge physically into "Retrieval, knowledge and memory stores", keep memory governance as an explicit logical component tied to C3 and C8, and build it last** [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


## 4. Tools, protocols and agent connectivity

> **Conflict-of-interest disclosure.** The author is an Anthropic model. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent Skills both originated at Anthropic [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S018: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S028: Introducing Agent Skills (16 Oct 2025; updated 18 Dec 2025) (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/news/skills> accessed 2026-10-07]. Both were scored on the same rubric as every other product in this section. Independent criticism of both is recorded in their deep dives, and an independent alternative is named wherever either is recommended [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

> **Executive summary.** This layer is where an agent stops talking and starts acting: it calls tools, reads enterprise systems, browses, runs code and talks to other agents. Three things have changed since the original graphic. First, the protocols have moved to neutral homes. Anthropic donated MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation on 9 December 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S018: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S038: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) (The Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-announces-the-formation-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and A2A 1.0.0 (12 March 2026) joined AAIF in August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S116: A2A joins AAIF's open agentic stack (17 Aug 2026) (Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)) <https://aaif.io/blog/a2a-joins-aaif> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S117: A New Chapter for A2A: Joining the Agentic AI Foundation (27 Aug 2026) (A2A Project) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/blog/2026/08/27/a-new-chapter-for-a2a-joining-the-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Agent Skills has no neutral governance body and is not an AAIF project on available evidence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S046: Skills Over MCP (AAIF blog); Agent Plugins 1.0 post; agentskills.io specification (Agentic AI Foundation / agentskills.io) <https://aaif.io/blog/skills-over-mcp> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A3-S115: (Project Proposal) Agent Skills (aaif/project-proposals issue #47) (Agentic AI Foundation (GitHub)) <https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/47> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Second, MCP has grown an enterprise security model. The 2026-07-28 specification is stateless, deprecates Dynamic Client Registration and puts method and tool names in HTTP headers so that gateways can authorise them, and the Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension has been stable since June 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S057: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S017: Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-touch OAuth for MCP (18 Jun 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/enterprise-managed-auth/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Authorisation itself is still optional in the specification [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Third, ownership and risk have shifted among the tool vendors. Nebius closed its acquisition of Tavily on 19 February 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S084: Tavily is Joining Nebius (10 Feb 2026) <https://www.tavily.com/blog/tavily-is-joining-nebius> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S041: Nebius Group N.V. Form 20-F FY2025 (subsequent event: Tavily acquisition) (Nebius Group N.V. (SEC EDGAR)) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001513845/000110465926052948/nbis-20251231x20f.htm> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and Composio disclosed a May 2026 incident in which connected-account tokens and API keys were exposed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L4-S007: Composio May 2026 security incident update <https://composio.dev/blog/composio-may-2026-security-incident> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The graphic draws L4 as a row of tools. The real design problem is governing what those tools are allowed to do, on whose behalf [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** standardise on MCP for agent-to-tool connectivity, but only behind a firm-owned tool gateway that enforces authorisation, an allow-listed private registry and per-tool policy. Expose authoritative data through read-only tools. Run generated code only in a microVM sandbox with egress control. Treat every SaaS tool (search, browser, integration broker) as an outsourced data flow [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Independent alternatives to MCP are OpenAPI-described tools exposed through a gateway, and A2A for agent-to-agent delegation [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 4.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns.** L4 turns an agent's intent into a controlled action on a system outside the model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It has five jobs:

- **Tool invocation and external APIs.** Describe tools so a model can select them, validate arguments, call them and return results, including long-running work [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Enterprise-system connectivity.** Reach internal data stores, calculation engines and SaaS applications through a stable contract rather than bespoke glue [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Execution runtimes.** Provide isolated places to run generated code and drive web browsers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Protocol interoperability.** Let tools and agents built on different frameworks and vendors work together (MCP for agent-to-tool, A2A for agent-to-agent) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **The missing sub-layer: identity, authorisation and tool governance.** Decide which agent, acting for which person, may call which tool with which arguments, with which credential, and record the decision [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. This is hypothesis H3 (§4.13).

**Hand-offs.**
- *Above:* L3 orchestration decides when to call a tool; L4 decides whether the call is allowed and executes it. A deterministic workflow should name its tools explicitly; an autonomous agent selects from what L4 exposes, which is why the exposed set must be minimal [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Below and beside:* the tools reach data in L5 to L8 and enterprise systems of record. Tool spans go to L9 via OpenTelemetry, whose GenAI conventions cover tool execution and MCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S061: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (repository docs index) (OpenTelemetry (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/main/docs/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Control plane:* agent and user identity, token issuance and policy belong to C4; secrets custody, sandboxing standards and supply-chain controls belong to C7; the gateway product is often shared with C1, because the C1 gateways now carry MCP and A2A traffic as well as model calls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S061: agentgateway README (GitHub) (agentgateway project (Linux Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S051: LiteLLM README (GitHub) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. This section specifies what L4 needs from those controls and does not repeat their product analysis [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the layer does not own.** It does not own the agent's plan (L3), the content safety of the model's output (C2) or the identity provider (C4). It does own the enforcement point at which a tool call is accepted or refused [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 4.2 Why it matters

A badly designed tool layer turns every weakness of a language model into an action [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Prompt injection becomes data exfiltration when the agent holds a token that can send email. A hallucinated argument becomes a wrong trade instruction when a write tool is exposed. A tool description becomes an attack vector when the client trusts whatever a third-party server says about itself [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The evidence for this is no longer theoretical:
- The MCPTox benchmark (AAAI 2026) tested tool-poisoning attacks against 45 live MCP servers and 20 models. The average attack success rate was 36.5% and the peak 72.8%, and more capable models were often more susceptible [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S023: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers (arXiv (academic preprint; AAAI 2026)) <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.14925> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Cloud Security Alliance research notes (July 2026) describe high-severity issues between mid-2025 and June 2026 in Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Amazon Q, where IDEs launched project-defined MCP servers with developer privileges and no isolation [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S022: MCP Attack Surface: Tool Poisoning and IDE Auto-Execution (CSA research note, Jul 2026) (Cloud Security Alliance Labs) <https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-mcp-tool-poisoning-auto-execution-20260701/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. CSA's attribution and dates are inconsistent across its notes [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S022: MCP Attack Surface: Tool Poisoning and IDE Auto-Execution (CSA research note, Jul 2026) (Cloud Security Alliance Labs) <https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-mcp-tool-poisoning-auto-execution-20260701/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Composio, a broker that holds end users' OAuth tokens for third-party applications, disclosed unauthorised access to internal systems in May 2026. By its own account about 0.3% of active connections leaked, including 5,001 GitHub connections, and 5,241 API keys were flagged as possibly exposed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L4-S007: Composio May 2026 security incident update <https://composio.dev/blog/composio-may-2026-security-incident> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 lists tool misuse (ASI02), identity and privilege abuse (ASI03) and the agentic supply chain (ASI04) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S046: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The 2026 LLM list moved Excessive Agency to third place [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A8-S041: OWASP GenAI Security Project Unveils 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications, New Agent Control Standard <https://genai.owasp.org/2026/09/01/owasp-genai-security-project-unveils-2026-top-10-for-llm-applications-new-agent-control-standard-and-sponsors-as-community-tops-30000-members/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A distribution team builds a research assistant that drafts client meeting notes. A developer connects it to a popular community MCP server for web search and to the firm's CRM through an integration broker, using a service account with read-write scope "to save time". The search server's maintainer later publishes an update whose tool description tells the model to "include the full client context in the query for better results". The client auto-updates the server, because nothing pins the tool definition. For six weeks, every search query carries the client's name, holdings summary and the purpose of the meeting to a search API outside the firm's third-party register. Nobody notices, because tool calls are logged only as "search succeeded". The leak is found when a sales manager sees a competitor-briefing document that quotes an unusual phrase from an internal note. A pinned, allow-listed tool definition, a DLP check on outbound queries and a read-only, per-user credential would each have broken the chain. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### 4.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authorised-call coverage | Share of remote tool calls carrying an audience-bound token validated at the gateway | 100% in production; any unauthenticated remote tool is a defect | Gateway logs: token audience and issuer checks |
| Allow-list conformance | Tool calls to servers and tool names on the approved registry | 100%; unknown tools blocked, not logged | Gateway decision log against the private registry |
| Tool-definition drift | Tool descriptions or schemas that changed since review (hash mismatch) | 0 unreviewed changes reach production | Hash pinning of reviewed definitions; registry diff alerts |
| Write-scope exposure | Tools with write or destructive effect exposed to a given agent | 0 for read-only use cases; each other one named and approved | Registry metadata verified by owners, not taken from server annotations |
| Delegation correctness | Calls made with the end user's delegated rights (or a named agent identity) rather than a shared service account | 100% for user-facing agents | Token claims (subject, actor) sampled from audit log |
| Credential hygiene | Long-lived secrets inside agent context, prompts or sandbox images | 0 | Secret scanning of traces and templates (C7) |
| Sandbox egress violations | Blocked outbound connections from code sandboxes | Every one reviewed; trend falling | Sandbox firewall logs |
| Outbound query DLP hits | Search or browse requests containing classified client data | 0 released; blocked at egress | DLP on the egress proxy (C3) |
| Tool-call accuracy | Right tool, right arguments, right order | ≥0.98 for read-only data tools (as L9) | L9 trajectory evals |
| Tool latency and availability | p95 latency and success rate per tool | Per tool SLO | Gateway and OTel spans |
| Time to revoke | From decision to block a server, tool or credential until enforced everywhere | Under 1 hour | Drill: revoke a test tool and measure |

### 4.4 How it works

**Tool contracts.** MCP defines how clients (agent hosts) discover and call tools, resources and prompts exposed by servers over JSON-RPC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S058: MCP specification repository README (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Since the 2026-07-28 revision each request is self-describing and stateless, discovery via `server/discover` is optional, and long-running work uses the Tasks extension [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S057: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. The same revision deprecates Roots, Sampling, Logging, the legacy HTTP+SSE transport and Dynamic Client Registration, under a policy with a 12-month minimum deprecation window [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S057: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S031: MCP specification 2026-07-28 changelog (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-08]. Tool annotations (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open-world) are hints that clients must treat as untrusted unless the server is trusted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S020: Tool Annotations as Risk Vocabulary (16 Mar 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations/> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Gateways and headers.** The 2026-07-28 revision puts method and tool names in `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` HTTP headers so that gateways, rate limiters and web application firewalls can route and authorise without parsing bodies [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07]. This is the protocol change that makes a tool-governance plane practical [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Authorisation.** Authorisation is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. When it is used, the MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server; servers must publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728); clients must send Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) and use PKCE; servers must reject tokens not issued for them, and token passthrough is forbidden [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S056: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization Security Considerations (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S039: MCP Specification: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The 2026-07-28 revision adds RFC 9207 issuer validation and issuer-bound client credentials, and replaces Dynamic Client Registration with Client ID Metadata Documents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S057: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. OAuth 2.1 itself is still an IETF draft [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Enterprise-Managed Authorization (EMA).** The identity provider issues an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) during single sign-on, which the client exchanges for an MCP access token. The aim is central policy and one audit trail without per-server consent screens [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S017: Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-touch OAuth for MCP (18 Jun 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/enterprise-managed-auth/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Okta Cross App Access was the first identity provider, and Okta Agent SSO (XAA) reached GA on 24 August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S017: Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-touch OAuth for MCP (18 Jun 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/enterprise-managed-auth/> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S099: Okta brings first-class identity to AI agents with Agent SSO; Okta Introduces Agent SSO for Cross App Access (XAA) (Okta, Inc.) <https://www.okta.com/newsroom/press-releases/okta-brings-first-class-identity-to-ai-agents-with-agent-sso/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S035: Okta brings first-class identity to AI agents with Agent SSO (with Okta support article, OIE release notes, Oktane 2026 release) <https://www.okta.com/newsroom/press-releases/okta-brings-first-class-identity-to-ai-agents-with-agent-sso/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Agent-to-agent.** A2A lets a client agent discover a remote agent through its Agent Card at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`, send messages and manage long-running tasks with streaming and push notifications [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Agent Cards may be signed with JWS over canonicalised JSON, and clients should verify signatures when present [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S031: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification (A2A Project (Linux Foundation)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Runtimes.** Code runs in sandboxes such as E2B's Firecracker microVMs, one per sandbox, with a per-sandbox egress firewall [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S062: E2B Runtime README (e2b-dev/infra) (E2B (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e2b-dev/infra/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Browsers run as remote sessions that Playwright or Puppeteer drive over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, as in Browserbase [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S013: PyPI JSON metadata: browserbase (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/browserbase/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

```text
  Analyst / service ──SSO──► IdP (C4) ── ID-JAG / token exchange ─┐
                                                                   ▼
  L3 agent or workflow ──► MCP client ──► TOOL GATEWAY (L4 governance, often the C1 product)
                                          │ 1 authenticate caller, check token audience/issuer
                                          │ 2 allow-list: server + tool name + definition hash
                                          │ 3 policy (Cedar / OPA): who, which tool, which args
                                          │ 4 outbound credential from vault (C7), never from the model
                                          │ 5 audit + OTel span (L9); DLP on outbound args (C3)
             ┌──────────────┬─────────────┼───────────────┬───────────────────┐
             ▼              ▼             ▼               ▼                   ▼
     Internal read-only  Calculation   SaaS apps via   Web search /       Remote agents
     MCP servers         sandbox       per-user OAuth  browser (egress    (A2A, signed
     (data, engines)     (microVM,     (broker or      proxy, no client   Agent Cards)
                         egress deny)  gateway 3LO)    data)
```

The gateway is the design choice that matters most. Without it, every MCP client is its own policy engine, and the firm has as many security models as it has agent hosts [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 4.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security: identity and least privilege**

- Make authorisation mandatory in your estate even though the specification makes it optional. Every remote MCP server sits behind the gateway and accepts only audience-bound tokens [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Distinguish three identities on every call: the human (subject), the agent (actor) and the tool server (audience). The MCP roadmap of 22 August 2026 lists DPoP, Workload Identity Federation, ID-JAG and token exchange as agent-identity priorities, and states that today's model is "built around a person approving access in a browser" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S016: The New MCP Roadmap (22 Aug 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/mcp-roadmap/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Until those land, use EMA or token exchange for user-delegated calls and workload identity for autonomous ones [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Never pass a user's upstream token through to a tool. The MCP specification forbids token passthrough and documents the confused-deputy risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S056: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization Security Considerations (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- Issue outbound credentials from a vault at call time. AgentCore Identity keeps refresh tokens in a vault [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S047: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available (Oct 2025) (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/10/amazon-bedrock-agentcore-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Vault Enterprise 2.1 made agentic IAM GA on 1 September 2026, enforcing the intersection of user permissions and agent ceiling policies and recording both in audit logs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S034: HashiCorp Vault agentic IAM is now generally available (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/hashicorp-vault-agentic-iam-is-now-generally-available> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S061: HashiCorp Vault CHANGELOG (HashiCorp / IBM) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hashicorp/vault/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Auth0 Token Vault brokers third-party API tokens for agents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S097: Auth0 for AI Agents is Now Generally Available (GA); Auth0 May 2026 product innovations (Auth0 (Okta)) <https://auth0.com/blog/auth0-for-ai-agents-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Details are in C4 and C7 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Default deny at the tool level. AgentCore Policy evaluates every agent-to-tool call against Cedar policies before execution and filters denied tools out of `tools/list` [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. OPA is the vendor-neutral alternative policy engine [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S046: Open Policy Agent README (GitHub) (Open Policy Agent project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-policy-agent/opa/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- Read-only by default. Classify each tool's effect yourself; do not rely on the server's annotations [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S020: Tool Annotations as Risk Vocabulary (16 Mar 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations/> accessed 2026-10-07] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Security: supply chain and tool integrity**

- Pin reviewed tool definitions by hash and block on change. OWASP's MCP Top 10 (MCP03:2025 Tool Poisoning) recommends signing manifests and hash-pinning reviewed definitions against rug pulls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S045: OWASP MCP Top 10: MCP03:2025 Tool Poisoning <https://owasp.org/www-project-mcp-top-10/2025/MCP03-2025%E2%80%93Tool-Poisoning> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Run a private registry and allow-list. The official MCP Registry is still in preview, its API frozen at v0.1, and it moderates by denylisting [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S019: Introducing the MCP Registry (8 Sep 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-09-08-mcp-registry-preview/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S042: modelcontextprotocol/registry (GitHub README) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S036: Official MCP Registry API v0.1 sample response (v0.2 and v1 paths returned HTTP 404 on 7 Oct 2026) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?limit=1> accessed 2026-10-07]. GitHub Copilot can be pointed at an organisation or enterprise MCP registry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S043: Configure an MCP registry for your organization or enterprise (GitHub Docs) <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/administer-copilot/manage-mcp-usage/configure-mcp-registry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Microsoft documents a private registry on Azure API Center enforced in Copilot and VS Code [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S044: Locking Down MCP: Create a Private Registry on Azure API Center and Enforce It in GitHub Copilot And VS Code (Microsoft (All things Azure devblog)) <https://devblogs.microsoft.com/all-things-azure/locking-down-mcp-create-a-private-registry-on-azure-api-center-and-enforce-it-in-github-copilot-and-vs-code/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Never let a developer tool auto-launch project-defined MCP servers with developer privileges [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S022: MCP Attack Surface: Tool Poisoning and IDE Auto-Execution (CSA research note, Jul 2026) (Cloud Security Alliance Labs) <https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-mcp-tool-poisoning-auto-execution-20260701/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Treat skills as code. Anthropic warns that malicious skills can exfiltrate data and advises installing only from trusted sources [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S072: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills> accessed 2026-10-07]. No signing or provenance mechanism exists in the Agent Skills format [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S037: Agent Skills Specification (Agent Skills project (agentskills.io)) <https://agentskills.io/specification> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S061: agentskills/agentskills README (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Sandboxing and egress**

- Run generated code only in a microVM or equivalent isolation with default-deny egress and domain allow-lists, as E2B provides [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S062: E2B Runtime README (e2b-dev/infra) (E2B (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/e2b-dev/infra/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Route all web search and browsing through an egress proxy with DLP. Tavily's SDK accepts a custom HTTP session so that traffic can be proxied through an API gateway for central authentication, logging and policy [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: tavily-python (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/tavily-python/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. A search query is an outbound data transfer: it can reveal the firm's intent even when it contains no personal data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and resilience**

- Stateless MCP (2026-07-28) removes session affinity, so tool servers can sit behind ordinary load balancers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Each SaaS tool needs a fallback or a graceful "tool unavailable" path in the workflow. An agent that silently answers from model memory when a data tool fails is worse than one that stops [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance and observability**

- Every tool has a named owner, a risk class (read, write, destructive, external egress), a reviewed definition hash and a change process [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Emit one OTel span per tool call with tool name, server, arguments hash, decision and result size; full arguments go to the audit store only where policy allows [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Cost.** Most cost lies in hosting servers, the gateway and the authorisation server, and in per-call SaaS fees [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S100: Exa Trust Center (and exa.ai pricing/enterprise/FAQ pages) <https://trust.exa.ai/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S088: Tavily pricing, FAQ and help-centre security pages <https://www.tavily.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Tool-call volume, not token volume, drives SaaS tool spend [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Portability.** Keep tool contracts as OpenAPI or MCP schemas in your own repository and generate whichever form a client needs. Hold credentials in your own vault rather than a broker's [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** tool gateway with default deny; private registry with hash-pinned definitions; read-only data tools onto systems of record; per-user delegated tokens via EMA or token exchange; microVM sandbox with egress allow-list; egress proxy with DLP for search and browse; deterministic workflow that names its tools.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** a shared service account with write scope behind a user-facing agent; community MCP servers installed straight from a public index; trusting tool annotations; long-lived API keys in prompts or sandbox images; a SaaS broker holding every user's OAuth tokens with no exit plan; client data in web-search queries; the model computing figures that an engine already produces.

### 4.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Coverage of the plan's questions: tool invocation, enterprise connectivity, browser and code execution, identity propagation, protocol interoperability; for protocols, the authorisation profile and long-running work; for runtimes, isolation and egress control |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC and audit logs of tool calls (including denied ones); SCIM; SLA; admin APIs; for open specifications, what they enable in your estate (central IdP policy, registry control) |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in product scope; incidents and their remediation; credential custody; for specifications, the security model (mandatory or optional authorisation, signing, provenance) and project hygiene |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Self-host, BYOC or VPC for anything that touches client data; region choice for SaaS tools; air-gap for sandboxes |
| Ecosystem (5%) | MCP support on both sides; client adoption; OpenAPI conversion; OTel export |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | Spec stability and deprecation policy; release cadence; pre-1.0 SDKs; ownership changes |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Per-call pricing; minimum commitments; operations burden of self-hosting gateways and sandboxes |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Open specification and neutral governance; who holds the credentials; whether tool contracts live in your repository |

### 4.7 Product deep dives

**Model Context Protocol (AAIF / Linux Foundation; originated at Anthropic).**
- *Conflict of interest:* MCP originated at Anthropic and the author is an Anthropic model. It was scored on the same rubric as A2A and the commercial products, and the criticisms below are recorded in full [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *What it is now:* an open protocol for connecting agent hosts to tools, resources and prompts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S058: MCP specification repository README (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The current revision is 2026-07-28, with Tier 1 SDKs in TypeScript, Python, Go and C#; the Python `mcp` package is at 2.3.0 (2 October 2026) and the TypeScript SDK at 1.32.1 (5 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S011: PyPI JSON metadata: mcp (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mcp/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S074: npm registry metadata: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk <https://registry.npmjs.org/@modelcontextprotocol/sdk> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S037: The 2026-07-28 Specification; Key Changes changelog (Model Context Protocol (AAIF)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The specification and SDKs are MIT-licensed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S058: MCP specification repository README (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S011: PyPI JSON metadata: mcp (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/mcp/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Governance:* Anthropic donated MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation, a directed fund of the Linux Foundation, on 9 December 2025. The maintainer structure was unchanged and AAIF does not set technical direction [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S018: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S038: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) (The Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-announces-the-formation-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Both Lead Maintainers are Anthropic staff; an AWS engineer joined the Core Maintainers in April 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S082: Expanding the MCP Maintainer Team (8 Apr 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-04-08-maintainer-update/> accessed 2026-10-07]. AAIF had 247 members by August 2026, including Visa and Wells Fargo as Gold members [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S041: Agentic AI Foundation Welcomes 57 New Members, Gaining Major Financial Services Players and APAC Leaders (Aug 2026) (Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/agentic-ai-foundation-welcomes-57-new-members-gaining-major-financial-services-players-and-apac-leaders> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Security model:* authorisation is optional; when used, it is a strict OAuth 2.1 profile with audience-bound tokens, PKCE, RFC 9728 metadata and RFC 9207 issuer validation, and token passthrough is forbidden [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S056: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization Security Considerations (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S057: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. EMA (stable 18 June 2026) gives central IdP control; Anthropic's clients and VS Code support it, as do servers including Asana, Atlassian, Canva, Figma, Linear and Supabase [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S017: Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-touch OAuth for MCP (18 Jun 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/enterprise-managed-auth/> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S045: Enterprise-Managed Authorization: Zero-touch OAuth for MCP (Model Context Protocol (AAIF)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/enterprise-managed-auth/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Criticisms:* authorisation is optional in the specification [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Tool annotations are only hints [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S020: Tool Annotations as Risk Vocabulary (16 Mar 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-03-16-tool-annotations/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Tool poisoning succeeded in 36.5% of attempts on average in MCPTox [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S023: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers (arXiv (academic preprint; AAAI 2026)) <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.14925> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. OWASP maintains an MCP Top 10 in which tool and schema poisoning is MCP03 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S045: OWASP MCP Top 10: MCP03:2025 Tool Poisoning <https://owasp.org/www-project-mcp-top-10/2025/MCP03-2025%E2%80%93Tool-Poisoning> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Researchers argue that prompt-injection filtering plus OAuth correctness is not enough, citing newer variants (MCP-ITP, ShareLock, Potemkin) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S024: Labels Are Not Endpoints: Treatment Leakage and Construct Validity in MCP Agent Security Evaluation (Aug 2026) (arXiv (academic preprint)) <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.12880> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. IDE clients from several vendors, including Anthropic's Claude Code, had high-severity issues from auto-launching project-defined servers [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S022: MCP Attack Surface: Tool Poisoning and IDE Auto-Execution (CSA research note, Jul 2026) (Cloud Security Alliance Labs) <https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-mcp-tool-poisoning-auto-execution-20260701/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The official Registry has been in preview since 8 September 2025, its "Registry API v1 GA" item is at the "Ideating" stage with no target date, and `/v1` returned 404 on 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S019: Introducing the MCP Registry (8 Sep 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-09-08-mcp-registry-preview/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S114: MCP Registry Working Group charter (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/community/working-groups/registry.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S036: Official MCP Registry API v0.1 sample response (v0.2 and v1 paths returned HTTP 404 on 7 Oct 2026) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?limit=1> accessed 2026-10-07]. The 2026-07-28 revision contained breaking changes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07]. Adoption figures (about 0.5bn monthly SDK downloads, July 2026) are project-reported [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The TypeScript SDK published several High-severity advisories in 2026, including GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h (30 September 2026), in which an OAuth client could send stored refresh tokens and client secrets to an authorisation server named by a malicious MCP server; the fix also requires `expectedIssuer` to be configured [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REVA-S006: modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk security advisories (GitHub Advisory Database) (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* the de facto agent-to-tool contract, now with an enterprise-grade authorisation profile and gateway-friendly headers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Launch partners for 2026-07-28 include AWS, Cloudflare, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S015: The 2026-07-28 Specification (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Limitations:* the security that matters in a regulated firm (mandatory authorisation, allow-listing, definition pinning, policy) lives outside the specification, in gateways and registries [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Technical direction is concentrated in one vendor's staff [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S082: Expanding the MCP Maintainer Team (8 Apr 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-04-08-maintainer-update/> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you need one contract for tools across several agent frameworks and model vendors [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you would connect clients directly to third-party servers without a gateway and registry [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Independent alternatives:* OpenAPI-described tools exposed through a gateway and called through each model's native function calling; AgentCore Gateway, Apigee and APIM can convert existing APIs into tools [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Vendor-neutral private registries (Azure API Center, GitHub's enterprise registry setting) can hold the allow-list whichever protocol wins [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S043: Configure an MCP registry for your organization or enterprise (GitHub Docs) <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/administer-copilot/manage-mcp-usage/configure-mcp-registry> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S044: Locking Down MCP: Create a Private Registry on Azure API Center and Enforce It in GitHub Copilot And VS Code (Microsoft (All things Azure devblog)) <https://devblogs.microsoft.com/all-things-azure/locking-down-mcp-create-a-private-registry-on-azure-api-center-and-enforce-it-in-github-copilot-and-vs-code/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Competitors:* A2A (complementary, agent-to-agent), OpenAPI tool definitions, vendor function-calling schemas.
- *FS note:* adopt the protocol, not the ecosystem: internal servers only, behind the gateway, with authorisation mandatory and definitions pinned [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: only behind a gateway with mandatory authorisation, an allow-list and pinned tool definitions [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. No flag.** Tier set by the reader at Checkpoint 3 (CP3 Q1); the author's reviewers had resolved the borderline call against the Anthropic-originated item [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. MCP and its authorisation profile (C4) are one decision with one tier. FS 3.55 is below the 3.6 guide and security scores 2, which is why every part of the condition is mandatory; the independent alternative remains OpenAPI-described tools behind the same gateway [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A Project, AAIF / Linux Foundation).**
- *What it is now:* an open protocol for communication between opaque agent applications. Specification 1.0.0 was released on 12 March 2026 and 1.0.1 on 26 May 2026; the Python SDK `a2a-sdk` is at 1.2.2 (5 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S075: PyPI JSON metadata: a2a-sdk (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/a2a-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S039: Announcing Version 1.0 - A2A Protocol; What's New in v1.0; A2A blog 2026 archive (A2A Project (Linux Foundation / AAIF)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Specification and SDKs are Apache-2.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S075: PyPI JSON metadata: a2a-sdk (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/a2a-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S025: A2A Protocol Surpasses 150 Organizations, Lands in Major Cloud Platforms, and Sees Enterprise Production Use in First Year (Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/a2a-protocol-surpasses-150-organizations-lands-in-major-cloud-platforms-and-sees-enterprise-production-use-in-first-year> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Governance:* Google contributed A2A to the Linux Foundation in 2025, and it was accepted as a Growth Stage AAIF project (AAIF announcement 17 August 2026; A2A blog 27 August 2026) with its own TSC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S065: A2A GOVERNANCE.md (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/GOVERNANCE.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S116: A2A joins AAIF's open agentic stack (17 Aug 2026) (Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)) <https://aaif.io/blog/a2a-joins-aaif> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S117: A New Chapter for A2A: Joining the Agentic AI Foundation (27 Aug 2026) (A2A Project) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/blog/2026/08/27/a-new-chapter-for-a2a-joining-the-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S039: Announcing Version 1.0 - A2A Protocol; What's New in v1.0; A2A blog 2026 archive (A2A Project (Linux Foundation / AAIF)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The TSC has eight companies: Google, Microsoft, Cisco, AWS, Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP and IBM [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S065: A2A GOVERNANCE.md (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/GOVERNANCE.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. IBM's Agent Communication Protocol was merged into A2A in August 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S032: What is Agent Communication Protocol (ACP)? (IBM) <https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agent-communication-protocol> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Security model:* Agent Cards may be signed (JWS over RFC 8785 canonical JSON), and clients should verify signatures when present. Version 1.0 added device-code and PKCE flows and removed implicit and password flows. An authenticated extended Agent Card is available only after the client authenticates [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S031: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification (A2A Project (Linux Foundation)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The protocol "does not define the scope, representation, validity, or revocation semantics" of authorisation obtained in the AUTH_REQUIRED state [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Strengths:* the most neutral governance in this layer, with an eight-company TSC [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It handles long-running delegated tasks that MCP's tool model was not designed for [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* card signing is optional, so trust in a remote agent's identity is not guaranteed by the protocol [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Version 1.0 broke the interaction protocol (the Agent Card stayed backward-compatible) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S079: A2A CHANGELOG (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S030: A2A Protocol Ships v1.0: Production-Ready Standard (A2A Project (Linux Foundation)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and some SDKs lag the card restructuring according to implementer reports [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A3-S030: A2A Protocol Ships v1.0: Production-Ready Standard (A2A Project (Linux Foundation)) <https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/announcing-1.0/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* agents owned by different teams or vendors must delegate work to each other [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* a deterministic workflow calling tools would do; most regulated use cases today are in that category [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* MCP (agent-to-tool), framework-native multi-agent APIs (L3), agentgateway's A2A gateway [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S061: agentgateway README (GitHub) (agentgateway project (Linux Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *FS note:* require signed Agent Cards and verify them; bound and revoke delegated authority yourself, because the protocol does not [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: where cross-team or cross-vendor agent delegation is in scope (CP3 Q1) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. No flag.** Signed Agent Cards must be verified, and delegated authority scoped and revocable by the firm, because the protocol does not define it. Where a deterministic workflow calling tools would do, as in most regulated use cases today, A2A is not needed at all [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Agent Skills (SKILL.md format; originated at Anthropic, Anthropic-maintained).**
- *Conflict of interest:* Agent Skills originated at Anthropic and the author is an Anthropic model. It was scored on the same rubric as everything else [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *What it is now:* an open packaging format for procedural knowledge: folders with a `SKILL.md` file (name and description required) plus optional scripts, references and assets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S061: agentskills/agentskills README (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S037: Agent Skills Specification (Agent Skills project (agentskills.io)) <https://agentskills.io/specification> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Agents load only names and descriptions at start-up, read the full skill when a task matches, and may execute bundled scripts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S061: agentskills/agentskills README (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Anthropic launched it on 16 October 2025 and published it as an open standard on 18 December 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S028: Introducing Agent Skills (16 Oct 2025; updated 18 Dec 2025) (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/news/skills> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S029: Skills for organizations, partners, the ecosystem (18 Dec 2025) (Anthropic) <https://claude.com/blog/organization-skills-and-directory> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S040: Anthropic publishes Agent Skills as an open standard for AI platforms (The Decoder) <https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-publishes-agent-skills-as-an-open-standard-for-ai-platforms/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Repository code is Apache-2.0 and documentation CC-BY-4.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S061: agentskills/agentskills README (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Adoption:* the agentskills.io showcase lists 46 clients, including OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, VS Code and Cursor; OpenAI's and Google's own documentation confirm support [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S113: Agent Skills client showcase list (docs/snippets/clients.jsx) (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/docs/snippets/clients.jsx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S033: Codex: Build skills (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S034: Gemini CLI: Agent Skills (Google (Gemini CLI docs)) <https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S047: Codex: Build skills (OpenAI) <https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Governance (criticism):* there is no neutral governance body [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S046: Skills Over MCP (AAIF blog); Agent Plugins 1.0 post; agentskills.io specification (Agentic AI Foundation / agentskills.io) <https://aaif.io/blog/skills-over-mcp> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The maintainers are Anthropic employees, listing requests are reviewed by the Anthropic team, and an AAIF project proposal (issue #47, September 2026) has not been accepted on available evidence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S112: Agent Skills CONTRIBUTING.md (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/CONTRIBUTING.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S115: (Project Proposal) Agent Skills (aaif/project-proposals issue #47) (Agentic AI Foundation (GitHub)) <https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/47> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The specification is a "living document" with no tagged releases [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S115: (Project Proposal) Agent Skills (aaif/project-proposals issue #47) (Agentic AI Foundation (GitHub)) <https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/47> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Security (criticism):* no signing or provenance mechanism exists in the format [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S037: Agent Skills Specification (Agent Skills project (agentskills.io)) <https://agentskills.io/specification> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S061: agentskills/agentskills README (Agent Skills project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentskills/agentskills/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Anthropic warns that malicious skills can exfiltrate data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S072: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills> accessed 2026-10-07], and the Gemini CLI documentation gives similar advice [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S034: Gemini CLI: Agent Skills (Google (Gemini CLI docs)) <https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. OWASP runs an "Agentic Skills Top 10" project [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S046: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (OWASP Gen AI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* plain files that any team can review in Git; progressive disclosure keeps context small [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* a skill can carry executable code, so it is a software supply-chain item, not a document [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Organisation-wide provisioning is a vendor feature (for example Claude Team and Enterprise admins), not part of the standard [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S029: Skills for organizations, partners, the ecosystem (18 Dec 2025) (Anthropic) <https://claude.com/blog/organization-skills-and-directory> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Choose when:* you want to package house procedures (style rules, report templates, review checklists) once and use them across several agent clients [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* skills would come from outside the firm, or would carry scripts that run with the agent's credentials [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Independent alternatives:* Git-versioned instruction and prompt packages managed under C5; AGENTS.md, which was a founding AAIF project alongside MCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S038: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) (The Linux Foundation) <https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-announces-the-formation-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The AAIF "Skills Over MCP" working group is exploring delivery of skills through MCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S038: Skills Over MCP (Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)) <https://aaif.io/blog/skills-over-mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Competitors:* AGENTS.md, C5 prompt management, MCP prompts.
- *FS note:* internally authored, Git-reviewed, script-free skills only, until the format has signing, versioning and neutral governance [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical, conditional: internally authored skills only. Flag: none.** Governance and versioning keep it out of Strategic [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

(Composio (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ComposioHQ/composio/next/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S098: PyPI JSON metadata: composio (0.25.0; 2.0.0b0 pre-release 31 Aug 2026) (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/composio/json> accessed 2026-10-08].

These claims come from vendor marketing pages only, with no trust-centre report seen (V1 verification log, section 4), so they count as not publicly verified for scoring [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

It revoked OAuth2 tokens across about 100 toolkits and all user GitHub tokens, deleted API keys created before 22 May 2026, and asked customers to rotate keys and have end users rotate credentials at each provider; it said the full scope was not yet known [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L4-S007: Composio May 2026 security incident update <https://composio.dev/blog/composio-may-2026-security-incident> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

- *Strengths:* the broadest catalogue of SaaS connectors with per-user authentication [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The SDK is pre-1.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S008: PyPI JSON metadata: composio (Python Package Index (PyPI)) <https://pypi.org/pypi/composio/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Choose when:* a low-risk internal productivity agent needs many SaaS connectors quickly, self-hosted [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* the agent touches client data, or you cannot self-host in-region [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* AgentCore Gateway and Identity, Auth0 Token Vault (C4), Kong AI Gateway MCP controls (C1).

- **Tier: Experimental. No flag.** Security evidence and the May 2026 incident keep it out of production use for regulated data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scoring notes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- *Open specifications (rule 2).* MCP, A2A and Agent Skills were scored on project hygiene and on what they enable in the firm's estate, capped at 4. MCP security is 2 (it was 3 before the CP3 review): authorisation is optional, tool definitions cannot be signed, tool poisoning is a documented attack class, and the TypeScript SDK had several High advisories in 2026, one of which sent OAuth credentials to an authorisation server chosen by the MCP server [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S055: MCP Specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S023: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool Poisoning Attack on Real-World MCP Servers (arXiv (academic preprint; AAAI 2026)) <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2508.14925> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; B-REVA-S006: modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk security advisories (GitHub Advisory Database) (Model Context Protocol project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Advisories are published with fixes, which is good hygiene, but on protocol integrity MCP sits below A2A, so the borderline call was resolved against the Anthropic-originated item. A2A is 3 because card signing is optional and delegated authority has no revocation semantics; Agent Skills is 2 because skills carry executable code with no signing or provenance.
- *Evidence caps.* Composio security is capped at 2: V1 §4 lists its security claims as vendor marketing only, and the May 2026 incident would independently hold it at 2. E2B enterprise readiness is capped at 2: SSO, SCIM and RBAC are "planned" and no customer audit log was found (B-L4-S003). Tavily (RBAC roles, B-L4-S006) and Browserbase (SAML SSO, B-L4-S004) were lifted to 3 under CP2 rule 7 by one verified control each.
- *Hyperscaler presumption (rule 6).* AgentCore enterprise readiness is 4: platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service. Security is 4, not 5, because the ISO wording is inconsistent across AWS pages (rule 8). At the CP3 review, deployment fell from 3 to 2 (AWS-managed only) and maturity from 4 to 3 (one year of GA), to match the same service in C1 and AgentCore Memory in L5.
- *Deployment 1.* Exa and Tavily are SaaS-only with no processing region choice found.
- *Ownership change (rule 3).* Tavily's lock-in was reduced by 1 for the Nebius acquisition.
- *Tiers (CP3 decisions).* The reader set the protocol tiers at Checkpoint 3 (CP3 Q1). MCP is Strategic, conditional at 3.55 FS: only behind a gateway with mandatory authorisation, an allow-list and pinned tool definitions; it is one decision with the C4 authorisation profile. A2A is Strategic, conditional at 3.70 FS: only where cross-team or cross-vendor agent delegation is in scope. Criterion scores were not changed by either decision. AgentCore Gateway and Identity is Strategic, conditional: where AWS is your primary cloud, under rubric rule 10 (CP3 Q2), as AWS's lead service in this category; the same service in C1 has the same tier.
