### 4.9 Decision tree

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): one tool gateway (L4 governance; often the C1 product) with
authorisation mandatory, a private allow-listed registry, hash-pinned tool definitions,
default-deny policy (Cedar or OPA), vault-issued outbound credentials (C7), OTel spans (L9).

STEP 1 [Rec]: How does the agent reach this capability?
  Internal system of record or calculation engine?
  ├─ Yes → Build a READ-ONLY MCP server (or OpenAPI tool) owned by the system's team.
  │        Write needed? → separate tool, separate approval, human confirmation step (L3).
  └─ No  → SaaS application?
           ├─ Yes → Does the user's own access matter (per-user data)?
           │        ├─ Yes → Per-user delegated OAuth via EMA / token exchange (C4);
           │        │        credential vault in your estate. Broker (Composio) only if
           │        │        self-hosted and the data are not client data.
           │        └─ No  → Named agent identity with least-privilege scope.
           └─ No  → Public web?  → STEP 3.   Code to run? → STEP 4.   Another agent? → STEP 5.

STEP 2 [Rec]: Which gateway?
  AWS is the agent platform          → AgentCore Gateway + Identity + Policy
  Azure / Microsoft estate           → APIM AI gateway + Entra Agent ID (see C1, C4)
  Multi-cloud or self-hosted needed  → agentgateway or Kong AI Gateway (see C1)
  (Re-assess when MCP agent-identity work, DPoP and WIF, is published.)

STEP 3 [Rec]: Web search or browsing
  Could the query or page context contain client, holdings or deal data?
  ├─ Yes → Do not use external search. Use approved internal sources (L6–L8).
  └─ No  → Search API via egress proxy + DLP, ZDR enabled:
           EU processing required? → none found for Exa/Tavily; use L8 self-hosted crawl.
           Otherwise              → Exa (independent) or Tavily (Nebius-owned).
           Site has no API and must be operated? → Browserbase (domain allow-list,
           recordings to own bucket) or self-hosted Playwright in a sandbox.

STEP 4 [Rec]: Code execution
  Generated code at all? → microVM sandbox, default-deny egress, no standing secrets:
    E2B BYOC (AWS/GCP) or EU region; AgentCore or LangSmith sandboxes if already on them.
  Result is a figure that will be published? → reconcile to the authoritative engine (L9).

STEP 5 [Rec]: Agent-to-agent
  Can a deterministic workflow (L3) call tools instead? → Yes: do that.
  Otherwise → A2A 1.0 with signed Agent Cards verified, scoped and revocable delegation,
              through a gateway that understands A2A (agentgateway, Kong, APIM).

STEP 6 [Rec]: Packaging procedures
  House procedures for several agent clients → Agent Skills, internally authored,
  Git-reviewed, no scripts; alternative: C5 prompt packages or AGENTS.md.
```

(Browserbase (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/browserbase/stagehand/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07] | Scripts in Playwright; avoid vendor-only features |

### 4.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk.**
- *SS1/23.* SS1/23 covers vendor models and requires independent validation (Principle 4); Principle 1.1(b) allows its MRM aspects to apply to material, complex deterministic quantitative methods that are not models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S061: SS1/23 model definition and Principle 1.1(b); PS6/23 feedback (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2023/ss123.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. An attribution engine is such a method or a model in its own right [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The consequence for L4: an agent must call the validated engine through a tool and never recompute what the engine produces, or the firm has created an unvalidated shadow model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and expressly places generative and agentic AI outside its scope [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The firm's own tool-governance standard therefore has to stand on its own [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Validation scope.* The tool set exposed to an agent is part of the system being validated. Adding a tool is a material change that should trigger re-testing [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- *Deployer duties.* Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to keep logs for at least six months and monitor operation; Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Most asset-management uses, including attribution commentary, are not Annex III [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Practical effect.* Tool calls are the actions an auditor will ask about first. Log them to Article 26 grade regardless of classification [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**DORA, the UK CTP regime and outsourcing.**
- *Every SaaS tool is an ICT third-party service.* DORA requires a register of information covering all ICT third-party arrangements, with Article 30 terms where a critical or important function is supported [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Exa, Tavily, Browserbase, E2B Cloud and Composio each belong in the register [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Designated providers.* AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft entities are designated under DORA and the UK CTP regime; no AI model provider is [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. None of the independent tool vendors in this layer is designated, so oversight rests entirely on the firm [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Notifications.* PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Tavily's change of control and any switch away from a broker should be planned with that lead time [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Exit.* SS2/21 expects documented, tested exit plans [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A broker that holds end-user tokens has the hardest exit in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Residency, data egress and auditability.**
- *Search egress.* FG16/5 expects data location and effective access for outsourced IT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No EU processing region was found for Exa or Tavily [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S121: Exa Security Overview (and exa.ai/enterprise, exa.ai/dpa) <https://exa.ai/docs/reference/security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A3-S088: Tavily pricing, FAQ and help-centre security pages <https://www.tavily.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Composio's managed cloud is US-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S119: Composio: Two questions every security review asks us (and MCP gateway/governance pages) <https://composio.dev/blog/two-questions-every-security-review-asks-us> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. EU-to-US transfers rely on the Data Privacy Framework or SCCs, and appeal C-703/25 P is pending [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A search query can disclose confidential intent (a planned trade, a client's concern) even without personal data, so the control is "no client context in outbound queries", enforced at the egress proxy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Auditability.* Each tool call needs: subject, agent identity, tool, definition hash, arguments (or their hash), policy decision, result reference and timestamp [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Least privilege for non-human actors.**
- *Supervisory direction.* The NCCoE published a concept paper on software and AI agent identity and authorisation in February 2026, and CAISI's January 2026 agent-security RFI informs a planned SP 800-53 control overlay for AI agent systems [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-NIST-AIRMF: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1) and Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S006: Request for Information Regarding Security Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Agents (NIST CAISI via Federal Register) <https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/01/08/2026-00206/request-for-information-regarding-security-considerations-for-artificial-intelligence-agents> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The OCC observes banks adopting agentic AI in limited use cases "with guardrails and human-in-the-loop accountability" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-AGENCY-AI: US federal banking agency and NIST statements on generative and agentic AI, 2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S004: Semiannual Risk Perspective Spring 2026 (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://occ.gov/publications-and-resources/publications/semiannual-risk-perspective/files/pub-semiannual-risk-perspective-spring-2026.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *What to do.* Give each agent its own identity with an owner and sponsor, as Entra Agent ID models it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S057: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/what-is-microsoft-entra-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07], and grant tools to that identity, never to a shared service account [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Concentration.** IOSCO flags concentration risk from reliance on a few AI technology providers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S058: IOSCO FR/02/2026 Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (May 2026) <https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD823.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. In L4 the concentration is in governance, not in vendors: both Lead Maintainers of MCP are Anthropic staff [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S082: Expanding the MCP Maintainer Team (8 Apr 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-04-08-maintainer-update/> accessed 2026-10-07], and Agent Skills is Anthropic-maintained [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S115: (Project Proposal) Agent Skills (aaif/project-proposals issue #47) (Agentic AI Foundation (GitHub)) <https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/47> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A firm that also uses Anthropic models should note that one vendor then influences the model, the tool protocol and the skills format [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. This author is an Anthropic model, and the point applies in full [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Standards.**

### 4.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from L4 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary (allocation, selection, currency, benchmark-relative return) for a generic multi-asset fund. It is a deterministic workflow, not a free agent, and it needs exactly four tools:

1. **`get_attribution_results` (read-only MCP tool onto the attribution engine output).** Parameters: fund identifier, period, attribution model version. Returns the engine's published effects with a snapshot identifier and hash. The tool reads only the engine's approved output store; it cannot trigger a re-run or change parameters. The snapshot hash goes into the trace, so L9 can compare every figure in the draft with it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
2. **`get_fund_reference_data` (read-only MCP tool onto the fund data store).** Benchmark name, share-class currencies, sector and asset-class labels, and period dates. No client identifiers are returned [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
3. **`calculate` (sandboxed, E2B-style).** Used only if the draft needs a derived figure the engine does not publish, such as a sum of two effects or a contribution in basis points. Code runs in a microVM with no network egress and no credentials, on inputs passed from tool 1. The result is labelled "derived" and reconciled to the engine's totals before use; if reconciliation fails, the workflow stops and asks the analyst [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
4. **`search_approved_commentary` (retrieval, L6–L8).** Prior commentaries and the house style guide from the firm's own index [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**How the calls are governed.**
- The analyst signs in; the IdP issues an ID-JAG through EMA (or equivalent token exchange), so each tool call carries the analyst as subject and the commentary agent as actor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- The gateway allow-lists exactly these four tools for this agent identity, checks each definition hash, and applies a Cedar or OPA policy: fund identifiers must be within the analyst's entitlements [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Tool servers are owned by the data and engine teams, versioned in Git and change-controlled; adding a tool or a parameter is a model change under the firm's MRM process [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Every call produces an audit record (subject, actor, tool, hash, arguments, decision, snapshot ID) that joins the C8 evidence pack [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What L4 must never do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- expose any write, update or publish tool to the drafting agent; publication happens after human approval, outside the agent
- let the model compute a figure that the engine already produces, or use a sandbox result that has not been reconciled to the engine
- send fund names, holdings, client names or the commentary's purpose to an external web search or browser service
- install a community MCP server or a third-party skill into this workflow
- use a shared service account or a long-lived key; credentials are issued per call from the vault
- let a tool description or annotation decide the tool's risk class

The counter-evidence is that the products implementing the sub-layer are the C1 gateways and C4 identity services, not new L4 products. A separate box in L4 could duplicate them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Provisional recommendation.** Keep H3, implemented as a **tool-governance sub-layer inside L4** that is the enforcement point (gateway, private registry, definition pinning, policy evaluation, audit), with policy and identity decisions owned by C4, credentials by C7, and the gateway product shared with C1 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Draw it between L3 and the tools, so that no tool is reachable except through it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**

The graphic's single "agent framework" row hides the most important architectural choice in the stack: whether a process is a workflow or an agent [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** build regulated use cases as deterministic workflow graphs with bounded LLM steps, run them on a durable-execution substrate, and keep approval gates and state in firm-controlled stores. Standardise on one framework per language estate (LangGraph by default; Microsoft Agent Framework in Microsoft estates; Google ADK or Strands with AgentCore where Google Cloud or AWS is the primary cloud), use Temporal (or DBOS) for durability, and admit autonomous agent loops only as sandboxed sub-steps with read-only tools [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 3.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns.** L3 turns a business process into an executable, observable plan in which some steps are code and some are model judgements [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It owns seven things, matching the plan's research questions:

- **State and persistence.** What the run knows at each step, where that state is checkpointed, and how it is restored [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Workflows and planning.** Whether the sequence of steps is fixed in code, chosen by a router, or planned by the model at run time [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tool calling.** Which tools a step may call, with what arguments, and under whose approval; the tools themselves belong to L4 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Human-in-the-loop.** Interrupts, approvals, edits and resumption [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Multi-agent patterns.** Handoffs, agents-as-tools, supervisors and group collaboration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Durable execution and retries.** Resuming after a crash without repeating side effects, with timeouts and retry policy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Deterministic versus autonomous orchestration.** The explicit decision, per use case, of how much control flow the model is given [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**

- *Up* to the application and channel: L3 exposes a run API (start, stream, interrupt, resume) and returns outputs with run IDs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Down* to L4 for tools and MCP servers, to L5 for memory, to L6 to L8 for retrieval, and to L2/C1 for model calls through the gateway [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Sideways* to L9 (every node is a span), C2 (guardrails at node boundaries), C4 (agent identity for tool calls), C5 (prompt and graph versions) and C8 (the run record as evidence) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What L3 does not own.** It does not own tool authorisation, which is C4 and the L4 gateway; it does not own run-time content blocking, which is C2; and it does not own long-term memory policy, which is L5 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A framework that bundles these (LangSmith, AgentCore, Foundry) should be configured so that the firm's own controls stay authoritative [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 3.2 Why it matters

When this layer is badly designed, the system's behaviour stops being a property of its design and becomes a property of each run [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Three failure modes recur:

- **Autonomy where none was needed.** A task with a known sequence is given to an agent loop. Each run takes a slightly different path, so evaluation results do not transfer between runs and validation cannot cover the space of behaviours [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The plan's pair-6 tension states the counter-position: most enterprise agents should be deterministic workflows with one judgement step, and guardrails cannot fix a workflow that should never have been autonomous [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **No durable state.** A crash, deploy or timeout restarts the run from the beginning, so tools are called twice, approvals are lost or, worse, a half-finished run is silently abandoned [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The Claude Agent SDK, for example, keeps session transcripts on local disk, where they do not survive a container restart unless a session store is configured [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Approval as convention, not control.** A "human review" step that the code can skip, or that does not record who approved what, is not a gate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A team builds the monthly attribution commentary as a single autonomous agent with tools for the attribution engine, the document store and the publishing system. It works in testing. In month three, a container is recycled mid-run during the busiest reporting day. The agent had fetched attribution data and drafted text, but its state lived in process memory. The scheduler retries the run from the start. On the second run the attribution engine has been refreshed with a late price correction, so the numbers differ slightly from the first run. A fund's retry also picks up a stale draft left in a shared working directory, and because the agent has a publishing tool and a loosely worded instruction to "finalise when complete", it publishes the stale draft before the reviewer sees it. Nobody can reconstruct which data the published text came from, because the run had no checkpoint and the trace stopped at the crash. A deterministic graph with a checkpointed data snapshot, no publishing tool, and an approval interrupt that only a named human can resume would have made each of those steps impossible. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### 3.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Path conformance | Share of runs whose executed node sequence matches the approved graph | 100% for regulated workflows; any deviation is a defect | Compare trace node sequence with the graph version (L9) |
| Resume without re-execution | Share of interrupted runs that resume from the last checkpoint without repeating completed side-effecting steps | 100% in fault-injection tests | Kill-and-resume tests in CI; tool-call counts per run ID |
| Approval-gate integrity | Share of releases that carry a recorded human approval by an authorised approver | 100%; zero bypasses | Reconcile publish events against approval records (C8) |
| Autonomy budget | Steps per run where the model chooses the next action, and maximum tool calls per run | Declared per use case; often 0–1 for regulated flows | Static analysis of the graph plus run-time counters |
| Tool-call scope | Tool calls outside the allow-list for the workflow | Zero | Gateway and orchestrator logs (L4, C4) |
| Reproducibility | Ability to re-run a past run with the same inputs, versions and recorded tool outputs | Every regulated run replayable from its record | Replay from checkpoint and recorded activity results |
| Run success rate and p95 duration | Completed runs and end-to-end latency, by workflow version | Per use case | Orchestrator metrics |
| Cost per completed run | Tokens plus runtime compute per successful run | Budget per use case | Gateway and runtime billing joined on run ID (C6) |
| Framework currency | Days behind the pinned framework's latest security fix | Within the patch SLA (e.g. 30 days) | Dependency scanning (C7) |

The IOSCO toolkit lists "level and frequency of human intervention in AI-driven investment processes" among supervisory indicators for asset managers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S058: IOSCO FR/02/2026 Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (May 2026) <https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD823.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The approval-gate and autonomy-budget KPIs give that indicator a design-time and a run-time measure [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Durable execution.** A durable engine records the result of each side-effecting step (an "activity" in Temporal's terms) so that, after a failure, the workflow is replayed and completed steps return their recorded results instead of running again [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S019: PyPI JSON metadata: temporalio (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/temporalio/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S045: Pydantic AI Durable Execution (overview, Temporal, DBOS, Prefect) <https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/overview/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Temporal, DBOS ("ultra-lightweight durable execution") and Restate are the engines named in the fact base [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S019: PyPI JSON metadata: temporalio (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/temporalio/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S020: PyPI JSON metadata: dbos (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/dbos/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S104: PyPI JSON metadata: restate-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/restate-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. LangGraph achieves the same effect with checkpoints, and requires side effects to be wrapped in tasks so that the Functional API can reload saved results [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S039: LangGraph Persistence / Durable execution / Interrupts - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The design consequence is that model calls and tool calls must be idempotent or recorded, and that the checkpoint store holds the evidence of what the run saw [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Runtimes are now separate from frameworks.** AgentCore runs agents written with Strands, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen or custom code, and gives each user session its own microVM, which is terminated and its memory sanitised at session end [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S116: Bedrock AgentCore SDK README (GitHub) (AWS) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aws/bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; B-L3-S004: AgentCore Runtime sessions / microVMs / quotas / security best practices (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-sessions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Session state there is ephemeral by default and AWS says it should not be used for long-term durability [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S004: AgentCore Runtime sessions / microVMs / quotas / security best practices (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-sessions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A managed runtime is therefore an isolation and operations choice, not a substitute for durable workflow state [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Reference flow.**

```text
 request (run_id, user, use case) ──► L3 workflow engine (graph version pinned, C5)
                                         │
   ┌─────────────── deterministic graph (code owns control flow) ────────────────┐
   │ [fetch data]──►[retrieve context]──►[LLM step]──►[eval gate]──►[APPROVAL]──►[release]
   │  activity:       activity:            bounded      L9 checks    interrupt;      activity:
   │  read-only tool  read-only retrieval  judgement    deterministic resume only by write by
   │  (L4/C4)         (L6-L8)              via C1       + judge       named approver  release svc
   └──────┬───────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────┬───────────┬─────────────┘
          ▼               ▼                  ▼              ▼           ▼
   durable store: checkpoints + recorded activity results (firm-controlled DB / Temporal)
          ▼
   OTel spans per node (L9) ──► evidence pack (C8): graph version, inputs hash, outputs, approver
```

The key design choice is that the graph, not the model, owns the control flow, and that every edge where something irreversible happens is either a recorded activity or a human interrupt [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 3.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**

- Treat the checkpoint store as a security boundary. LangGraph has published three checkpoint deserialisation advisories since 2025 (CVE-2025-64439, CVE-2026-28277, CVE-2026-48775), all patched, and the default serializer is used by all shipped checkpointer backends [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S007: LangGraph security advisories (GitHub) and NVD entries (LangChain / GitHub / NIST NVD) <https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Restrict write access to the runtime identity, encrypt at rest and keep the packages current [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Give each agent run its own identity and the narrowest tool scope; tool authorisation lives in the L4 gateway and C4, not in the prompt [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. In AgentCore, code inside the microVM can reach the execution-role credentials through the metadata endpoint, so the execution role must be scoped tightly [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S004: AgentCore Runtime sessions / microVMs / quotas / security best practices (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-sessions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- Run autonomous loops that execute code or touch files in sandboxes with network control. Anthropic recommends sandboxed containers for the Claude Agent SDK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07], and the OpenAI Agents SDK separates the harness from compute so credentials stay away from model-generated code [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S053: The next evolution of the Agents SDK (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/the-next-evolution-of-the-agents-sdk/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Do not let a vendor's default tracing export client data. The OpenAI Agents SDK traces to OpenAI's dashboard by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S052: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (agents, sessions, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, running agents) <https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; replace it with a firm-owned exporter [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and cost**

- Hosting models differ sharply. The Claude Agent SDK runs one long-lived subprocess per concurrent session, so compute scales with concurrent sessions rather than requests [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07]. AgentCore Runtime sessions stop after 15 minutes idle by default and run up to 8 hours per lifecycle; longer runs need Runtime Instances (up to 14 days) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S004: AgentCore Runtime sessions / microVMs / quotas / security best practices (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-sessions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Size the runtime on concurrent sessions and run length, not on request rate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Multi-agent patterns multiply model calls per task; CrewAI's Crews are a direct example [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Set a per-run token and tool-call budget in the orchestrator [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Resilience**

- Put every side effect behind a recorded activity or task, so that a resumed run never repeats a tool call [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Self-hosting Temporal means operating Kubernetes and persistence stores and upgrading minor versions in sequence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S002: Temporal server repository; production deployment and Cloud overview docs (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://github.com/temporalio/temporal> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Temporal Cloud runs the same server, so the choice can be revisited without code changes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S002: Temporal server repository; production deployment and Cloud overview docs (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://github.com/temporalio/temporal> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Governance and observability**

- Version the graph as code, alongside prompts (C5), and record the graph version on every run [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Make approvals first-class interrupts with the approver's identity recorded; LangGraph interrupts, Microsoft Agent Framework HITL, ADK tool confirmation and OpenAI Agents SDK resumable approvals all support this pattern [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S118: LangGraph README (GitHub) (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S066: Microsoft Agent Framework README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/agent-framework/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S114: Agent Development Kit (ADK) 2.0 README (GitHub) (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S120: OpenAI Agents SDK README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/openai-agents-python/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Emit OpenTelemetry spans per node: Microsoft Agent Framework and LlamaIndex Workflows ship OTel instrumentation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S066: Microsoft Agent Framework README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/agent-framework/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S013: PyPI JSON metadata: llama-index-workflows (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/llama-index-workflows/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Portability**

- The plan's abstraction strategy warns against over-abstracting agent frameworks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Do not write a firm-wide wrapper over LangGraph, Agent Framework and ADK. Instead, keep the portable assets outside the framework: prompts (C5), tool contracts (MCP/OpenAPI, L4), evaluation suites (L9), and the workflow specification as a reviewed document [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** deterministic graph with one bounded LLM step; durable activities around every side effect; approval interrupt before any irreversible action; autonomous loop confined to a sandboxed sub-step with read-only tools; framework-agnostic managed runtime for isolation.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** an autonomous agent for a process with a known sequence; a "finalise" or "publish" tool reachable by the model; state held only in process memory or a container's disk; approvals recorded in chat text; framework abstractions written over other frameworks; adopting a hosted agent API whose residency or retention terms do not fit the data (for example a US-only, non-ZDR beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S055: OpenAI API Changelog (Agents API public beta, Sep 2026) and Introducing the Agents API <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]).

### 3.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Both deterministic and autonomous modes; checkpointing; HITL interrupts with resume; durable execution or a clean integration with a durable engine; multi-agent primitives; typed state; streaming |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | For libraries (rubric rule 2): what controls they enable in-estate, plus vendor support or LTS commitments. For managed runtimes: SSO, RBAC, audit, SCIM, SLA |
| Security and compliance (20%) | Library hygiene (advisories, patch cadence, licence clarity); sandboxing model; managed-runtime certifications and isolation; default telemetry destinations |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Runs in the firm's estate; managed options; on-prem; model-provider independence |
| Ecosystem (5%) | MCP, A2A, OTel, provider coverage; whether runtimes host it |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | 1.x stability commitments; major-version churn; Alpha/Beta classifiers; vendor focus |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Licence cost; runtime pricing units; operations burden of durable backends |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Licence; framework-specific APIs; model lock-in; whether state lives in a vendor cloud |

### 3.7 Product deep dives

**LangGraph (LangChain).**
- *What it is now:* a low-level, MIT-licensed runtime for long-running, stateful workflows or agents. It provides durable execution that resumes where it left off, human-in-the-loop via interrupts, short- and long-term memory, streaming, and a Functional API for workflow-style code; deterministic code and LLM-driven decisions can be combined in one graph [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S118: LangGraph README (GitHub) (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S039: LangGraph Persistence / Durable execution / Interrupts - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. langgraph 1.2.14 was released on 6 October 2026; 1.0.0 came on 17 October 2025 with a commitment to no breaking changes until 2.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S001: PyPI JSON metadata: langgraph (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langgraph/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S033: LangChain and LangGraph Agent Frameworks Reach v1.0 Milestones <https://www.langchain.com/blog/langchain-langgraph-1dot0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Managed runtime:* LangGraph Platform was renamed LangSmith Deployment on 14 October 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S031: Product naming changes: LangSmith Deployment and LangSmith Studio (LangChain) <https://changelog.langchain.com/announcements/product-naming-changes-langsmith-deployment-and-langsmith-studio> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S056: Product naming changes: LangSmith Deployment and LangSmith Studio (LangChain) <https://changelog.langchain.com/announcements/product-naming-changes-langsmith-deployment-and-langsmith-studio> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. It is available as cloud SaaS, BYOC/hybrid with the data plane in the customer VPC, and self-hosted on Kubernetes (Enterprise plan) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S036: LangSmith Plans and Pricing (LangChain) <https://www.langchain.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S037: LangSmith Deployment - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/deployment> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Existing Deployment customers moved to usage-based LSU pricing on 1 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S036: LangSmith Plans and Pricing (LangChain) <https://www.langchain.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Certifications and access:* LangSmith states SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA (BAA on Enterprise); ISO 27001 is claimed on some LangChain pages but omitted from others, so its scope is unconfirmed [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S034: LangSmith Regions FAQ (LangChain) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/regions-faq> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S035: LangChain Enterprise <https://www.langchain.com/enterprise> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S149: LangSmith Engine security - Docs by LangChain (with Trust Center, enterprise and shared-responsibility pages) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. LangSmith Enterprise offers SAML 2.0/OIDC SSO, SCIM 2.0 and custom-role RBAC; self-hosted v0.14 enables ABAC and OCSF audit logs by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S038: User management - Docs by LangChain (with self-hosted changelog) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/user-management> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Security hygiene:* three checkpoint deserialisation advisories (2025–26) were published and patched through GitHub security advisories [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S007: LangGraph security advisories (GitHub) and NVD entries (LangChain / GitHub / NIST NVD) <https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* the most complete coverage of the seven L3 questions in a stable 1.x framework [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* graph and checkpoint APIs are LangGraph-specific [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S039: LangGraph Persistence / Durable execution / Interrupts - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; the ecosystem pulls towards LangSmith for deployment and observability [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S118: LangGraph README (GitHub) (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S031: Product naming changes: LangSmith Deployment and LangSmith Studio (LangChain) <https://changelog.langchain.com/announcements/product-naming-changes-langsmith-deployment-and-langsmith-studio> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* you need deterministic graphs with bounded LLM steps, durable checkpoints and approval interrupts, in Python or TypeScript [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* a single model call would do, or you cannot control who writes to the checkpoint database [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Microsoft Agent Framework, Google ADK, Pydantic AI with Temporal.
- *FS note:* pin `langgraph` and `langgraph-checkpoint`, run the Postgres checkpointer in-region with write access limited to the runtime identity, and dual-export traces via OTel so evidence survives an exit from LangSmith [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. Flag: Renamed** (LangGraph Platform → LangSmith Deployment).

**LlamaIndex (LlamaIndex, Inc.).**
- *What it is now:* an MIT framework for agentic and RAG applications with Workflows, a lightweight, event-driven, step-based engine with typed state and OpenTelemetry instrumentation, standalone since June 2025 (llama-index-workflows 2.25.0) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S117: LlamaIndex README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/run-llama/llama_index/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S041: Announcing Workflows 1.0: a lightweight framework for agentic systems (LlamaIndex) <https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/announcing-workflows-1-0-a-lightweight-framework-for-agentic-systems> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S013: PyPI JSON metadata: llama-index-workflows (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/llama-index-workflows/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. llama-index-core is 0.14.25 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S002: PyPI JSON metadata: llama-index-core (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/llama-index-core/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

Version 2.0.0 shipped on 23 June 2026 and removed `pydantic_graph.persistence`; the v1 line still receives security fixes for at least six months [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S003: PyPI JSON metadata: pydantic-ai (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/pydantic-ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S074: Pydantic AI Upgrade Guide; Pydantic AI v2 article; Version Policy <https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/project/changelog/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

Commercial support is not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The only funding found is a US$12.5M Series A [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S046: Announcement: Pydantic Logfire launch & Series A Funding (and AI Gateway moving to Logfire) <https://pydantic.dev/articles/logfire-announcement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

The major-version churn and the absence of verified support are carried as conditions: pin the major version and run it inside a Temporal or DBOS workflow [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

It gives developers the agent loop, built-in file, shell and web tools, hooks, subagents, MCP, permissions, resumable and forkable sessions, skills and plugins that power Claude Code [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]. claude-agent-sdk 0.2.164 (6 October 2026) carries the PyPI classifier "Development Status: 3 - Alpha"; the TypeScript package is 0.3.293 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S023: npm registry metadata: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk <https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk> accessed 2026-10-07].

It is not a deterministic workflow engine [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Licence and terms:* the Python repository licence is MIT, the npm licence field reads "SEE LICENSE IN README.md", and Anthropic's docs state that use of the SDK is governed by Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S092: Claude Agent SDK (Python) LICENSE (Anthropic) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S023: npm registry metadata: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk <https://registry.npmjs.org/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S048: Agent SDK overview (License and terms section) (Anthropic) <https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-08]. Third-party products may not present themselves as Claude Code [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Data handling:* the SDK inherits the API arrangement; ZDR is available per organisation for eligible Claude API features, while Claude Managed Agents, the hosted alternative (beta), is excluded from ZDR because session transcripts persist until deleted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S123: API and data retention - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S124: Claude Managed Agents overview - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]. On Bedrock or Google Cloud, the cloud provider is the data processor [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S123: API and data retention - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Strengths:* permission modes and hooks give fine-grained approval over which tools run automatically [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]; it is a capable harness for file- and code-centric autonomous tasks [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* Alpha classification and 0.x versioning [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; Claude models only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07]; Commercial Terms despite the MIT repository licence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S092: Claude Agent SDK (Python) LICENSE (Anthropic) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07]; compute scales with concurrent sessions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07]; dependence on the bundled CLI's release cadence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; Managed Agents excluded from ZDR [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S123: API and data retention - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07]; enterprise support not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* a sandboxed autonomous sub-task (for example, code or document manipulation) sits inside a firm-owned workflow and Claude is already an approved model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need model portability, a workflow engine, or a non-Alpha dependency for a regulated process [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Independent alternatives:* LangGraph or Pydantic AI for the workflow and agent step (both model-agnostic, MIT); the OpenAI Agents SDK as a comparable harness from another model vendor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: where AWS is your primary cloud (CP3 rule 10; deployment and lock-in at 2 accepted as an existing platform commitment under rule 11). No flag.**

**Temporal (Temporal Technologies).**
- *What it is now:* a durable execution engine whose workflows record each activity so that execution resumes after failures [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S019: PyPI JSON metadata: temporalio (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/temporalio/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Agent frameworks run model calls, tool calls and MCP traffic as Temporal activities (Pydantic AI), offer Temporal integrations for long-running HITL agents (OpenAI Agents SDK), or build on it (Mistral Workflows) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S045: Pydantic AI Durable Execution (overview, Temporal, DBOS, Prefect) <https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/overview/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S052: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (agents, sessions, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, running agents) <https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S058: Workflows for work that runs the business (Mistral Workflows) (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/workflows/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The Python SDK (`temporalio` 1.34.0, 30 September 2026) dates from March 2022 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S019: PyPI JSON metadata: temporalio (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/temporalio/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Licence and deployment:* the server is MIT-licensed and can be self-hosted, or consumed as Temporal Cloud on 14 AWS and 6 GCP regions including Europe; Cloud runs the same server, so applications move between the two without code changes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S002: Temporal server repository; production deployment and Cloud overview docs (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://github.com/temporalio/temporal> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Certifications and access:* Temporal states SOC 2 Type 2 and HIPAA support with a signed BAA, and offers client-side payload encryption so that Temporal Cloud stores ciphertext; no ISO 27001 claim was found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S001: Temporal security / Trust Center / Cloud security model (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://trust.temporal.io/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Temporal Cloud supports SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM, account roles, namespace permissions, custom roles and exportable audit logs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S003: Temporal Cloud account access / SCIM / audit logs (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://docs.temporal.io/cloud/manage-access> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* separates reliability from agent logic, and is independent of every model vendor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* it is not an agent framework [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; self-hosting requires Kubernetes, persistence stores and sequential upgrades [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S002: Temporal server repository; production deployment and Cloud overview docs (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://github.com/temporalio/temporal> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; workflow code becomes a hard runtime dependency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; Cloud pricing not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; certification evidence rests on search extracts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S001: Temporal security / Trust Center / Cloud security model (Temporal Technologies Inc.) <https://trust.temporal.io/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* a regulated workflow must resume after failure without re-calling tools [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* the task is a short, stateless single call [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* DBOS (dbos 3.2.0, MIT) and Restate (restate-sdk 1.0.5) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S020: PyPI JSON metadata: dbos (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/dbos/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S104: PyPI JSON metadata: restate-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/restate-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; LangGraph's checkpointer for LangGraph-only estates.
- *FS note:* self-host in-region, or use Temporal Cloud with client-side encryption; request the SOC 2 report before use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. No flag.**

**Not profiled separately.** AutoGen (maintenance mode) and Semantic Kernel are Superseded by Microsoft Agent Framework [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S021: PyPI JSON metadata: autogen-agentchat (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/autogen-agentchat/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S068: AutoGen README (GitHub) (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/autogen/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. AG2, an independent AutoGen fork (Apache-2.0), continues outside Microsoft [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S103: PyPI JSON metadata: ag2 (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/ag2/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. EthicalAgents and Ragoos were removed from the analysis because they could not be verified (CP1 Q4).

**Scoring notes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- **Libraries under rubric rule 2.** LlamaIndex, Pydantic AI, the OpenAI Agents SDK, the Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Google ADK were scored as self-hosted software: security on project hygiene, enterprise readiness on what they enable in-estate plus support, both capped at 4. Microsoft Agent Framework reaches 4 on enterprise readiness because Microsoft has made a long-term support commitment [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S012: PyPI JSON metadata: semantic-kernel (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/semantic-kernel/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Library security sits at 3 where hygiene evidence is absent; it is not raised by the model vendor's platform certifications.
- **Bundled commercial platforms.** LangGraph is scored with LangSmith Deployment, and CrewAI with AMP, because their records include the managed runtime. LangGraph security is 4, not 5: ISO 27001 scope is unconfirmed (rule 8), and its patched checkpoint advisories show working CVE handling rather than a clean record [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S149: LangSmith Engine security - Docs by LangChain (with Trust Center, enterprise and shared-responsibility pages) <https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/engine-security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; B-L3-S007: LangGraph security advisories (GitHub) and NVD entries (LangChain / GitHub / NIST NVD) <https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **NPV cap.** Mistral enterprise readiness is capped at 2: no SSO, RBAC or audit evidence [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. CrewAI has SSO and RBAC verified but no SCIM, SLA or audit, so rule 7 gives 3.
- **Hyperscaler rules.** AgentCore takes enterprise readiness 4 under rule 6 (platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service) and security 4 under rule 8 (service in scope, SOC 2 type not stated) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L5-S003: Compliance validation for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (and AWS Services in Scope pages) (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/compliance-validation.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. It is Strategic, conditional under rule 10 as AWS's lead agent runtime, with deployment and lock-in at 2 allowed by rule 11 because the condition is an existing AWS commitment. This matches AgentCore Memory (L5) and AgentCore Gateway (C1) on security and deployment.
- **Conflict-of-interest calls on the Claude Agent SDK.** The draft resolved technical (3, not 4), deployment (3, not 4) and maturity (1, not 2) against it. The CP4 calibration review found technical 3 and deployment 3 to be peer-consistent: the OpenAI Agents SDK has Temporal and DBOS durability integrations and provider-agnostic models, and the Claude Agent SDK has neither [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S052: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (agents, sessions, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, running agents) <https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S122: Hosting the Agent SDK - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hosting> accessed 2026-10-07]. On maturity, the package is explicitly classified Alpha [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S006: PyPI JSON metadata: claude-agent-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07; B-REVC-S001: PyPI JSON API: claude-agent-sdk (with openai-agents; google-adk; sglang; pydantic-ai; langgraph) (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], while the OpenAI Agents SDK is also pre-1.0 but declares no Development Status classifier on PyPI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REVC-S001: PyPI JSON API: claude-agent-sdk (with openai-agents; google-adk; sglang; pydantic-ai; langgraph) (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/claude-agent-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The reader decided at Checkpoint 4 that both pre-1.0 SDKs score 2 (CP4-9): the Claude Agent SDK moves from 1 to 2 (FS 2.65 to 2.75), the Alpha label is recorded as a limitation, and the tier stays Experimental [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Calibration.** Six products have a criterion at 2 or below. LangGraph is the only 5 on technical; Temporal and LangGraph are the only 5s on deployment.
- **Tiers versus totals.** AgentCore (3.25) and Google ADK (3.35) are Strategic below 3.6 by rule 10, each conditional on its cloud being the primary cloud; Microsoft Agent Framework (3.65) is Strategic on score, conditional on a Microsoft estate. Each hyperscaler therefore has one conditional Strategic agent framework or runtime (CP4 calibration change for ADK, confirmed by the reader at CP4-4). Pydantic AI (3.55) was drafted as Tactical because of major-version churn; the reader upgraded it to Strategic, conditional, for Python teams wanting type-safe agents (CP4-4), with no score change.

### 3.9 Decision tree

```text
STEP 0 [Rec]: Classify the use case BEFORE choosing a framework
  Is the sequence of steps known in advance (even with branches)?
  ├─ Yes → DETERMINISTIC WORKFLOW. LLM steps are bounded nodes (draft, classify, extract,
  │        judge). Autonomy budget = 0 or 1 model-chosen step.             (most FS use cases)
  └─ No  → Can the open-ended part be isolated as one sub-step with read-only tools?
           ├─ Yes → Workflow with ONE sandboxed agent sub-step (autonomy budget declared)
           └─ No  → Autonomous agent. Requires: sandbox, tool allow-list, per-run budget,
                    approval before any write, and a named risk owner. Re-check STEP 0.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Framework (one per language estate; do not wrap frameworks in a firm abstraction)
  Microsoft / .NET estate, or Semantic Kernel / AutoGen to migrate?
  ├─ Yes → Microsoft Agent Framework (Workflows for the process; Agents for bounded steps)
  └─ No  → Python or TypeScript back end?
           ├─ Yes → LangGraph (default)
           │        alt: Pydantic AI + Temporal/DBOS where typed I/O matters most
           │             (Strategic, conditional: Python teams wanting type-safe agents)
           │        alt: Google ADK where Google Cloud / Agent Engine is the platform
           └─ TypeScript application tier streaming to a browser → Vercel AI SDK
              (+ Workflow SDK, or call a back-end LangGraph/Temporal workflow)
  Existing CrewAI or LlamaIndex code → keep, but put the process in Flows / Workflows
  and the regulated steps behind the firm's approval gate.

STEP 2 [Rec]: Durability
  Does the run last longer than one request, wait for a human, or call side-effecting tools?
  ├─ No  → framework checkpointing is enough (or none)
  └─ Yes → LangGraph only?          → Postgres checkpointer (firm-controlled, write-restricted)
           Multi-framework / long?  → Temporal (self-host in-region, or Cloud with
                                       client-side encryption); alt: DBOS, Restate
           Microsoft estate?        → Durable Task (when GA) or Temporal meanwhile

STEP 3 [Rec]: Runtime
  Primary cloud = AWS?   → AgentCore Runtime (microVM per session) for framework-built agents
  Primary cloud = Azure? → Foundry Hosted Agents
  Primary cloud = GCP?   → Vertex AI Agent Engine
  Otherwise / in-estate  → containers on the firm's Kubernetes (LangSmith Deployment self-hosted
                           if LangGraph and Enterprise licence)
  In every case: platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service.

STEP 4 [Rec]: Autonomous harnesses (OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, Mistral Agents API)
  Only as a sandboxed sub-step, model already approved, traces to the firm's collector,
  no hosted state outside approved residency (no US-only/non-ZDR beta for UK/EU client data).

STEP 5 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Path conformance tested? Kill-and-resume test passes without duplicate tool calls?
  Approval gate cannot be bypassed in code? Graph version recorded on each run?
```
