### 3.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk.**
- *SS1/23 scope.* PRA SS1/23 applies to banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval, and covers vendor models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Principle 1.1(b) says relevant MRM aspects can be applied to material, complex deterministic quantitative methods that are not models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *What that means here.* An agent workflow that informs a business output is a model use requiring inventory, validation and change control, and the deterministic parts of the workflow are not exempt merely because they are code [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. For FCA solo-regulated managers SS1/23 is not binding but is the natural benchmark [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Unit of validation.* The validated object should be the workflow version (graph, prompts, model versions, tool contracts), not the model alone [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A change to any of these is a change requiring re-evaluation (L9) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Reproducibility of autonomous runs.* Validation evidence only transfers between runs if the control flow is stable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Deterministic graphs make path conformance testable; autonomous loops need their autonomy budget, tool allow-list and trajectory checks to be validated instead [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and places generative and agentic AI expressly outside its scope, leaving their governance to the firm [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. US supervisors currently signal expectations by observation, such as adoption "with guardrails and human-in-the-loop accountability" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-AGENCY-AI: US federal banking agency and NIST statements on generative and agentic AI, 2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S004: Semiannual Risk Perspective Spring 2026 (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://occ.gov/publications-and-resources/publications/semiannual-risk-perspective/files/pub-semiannual-risk-perspective-spring-2026.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**EU AI Act.**
- *Deployer duties.* Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to use them per instructions, assign competent human oversight, keep logs for at least six months and monitor operation; Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Scope.* Attribution commentary is not an Annex III use, so the live duties are AI literacy and transparency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The orchestration layer is nevertheless where human-oversight assignment and run logging are implemented, so it should be built to Article 26 grade [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Provider risk.* Repurposing a system into a high-risk purpose can make the firm a provider under Article 25 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A general-purpose agent that teams extend with new tools is the most likely route to that outcome [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Operational resilience and outsourcing.**
- *Designations.* DORA's CTPP list and the UK CTP designations include AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft but no AI model provider [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Hyperscaler agent runtimes therefore sit under overseen providers; independent framework vendors' platforms (LangSmith, CrewAI AMP, Temporal Cloud) do not [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Register and notifications.* A managed agent runtime or durable-execution SaaS supporting an important business service belongs in the register of information, and from 18 March 2027 PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Exit.* SS2/21 expects documented and tested exit plans [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The open-source framework plus a portable durable engine is the exit route; vendor-hosted agent state is the part that does not exit cleanly [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Residency and auditability.**
- *Hosted agent services.* OpenAI's hosted Agents API is US-only with no ZDR at launch [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S055: OpenAI API Changelog (Agents API public beta, Sep 2026) and Introducing the Agents API <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Claude Managed Agents is excluded from ZDR [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S123: API and data retention - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07]; Mistral hosts data in the EU by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S075: Mistral Help Centre: SOC 2 / ISO 27001; data storage location; ZDR; Regional inference docs; Trust Center (Mistral AI) <https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347638-do-you-have-soc-2-or-iso-27001-certification> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. EU-to-US transfers rely on the DPF or SCCs, with appeal C-703/25 P pending [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Run record.* FG16/5 expects data location and effective access for outsourced IT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The checkpoint store and the durable-execution history are records of what the agent saw and did, so they need the same retention, access control and residency as the outputs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Concentration.** IOSCO flags concentration risk from reliance on a few AI technology providers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S058: IOSCO FR/02/2026 Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (May 2026) <https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD823.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Three of the twelve products are model-vendor harnesses that tie orchestration to the vendor's models or cloud [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Choosing a model-agnostic framework keeps the L1 fallback route open [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Human oversight and supervisory direction.** The Bank of England reported that 55% of AI use cases had some autonomous decision-making and 2% were fully autonomous [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-AI-STATEMENTS: FCA, Bank of England and PRA statements and initiatives on AI, 2024-2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S056: Financial Policy Committee Record April 2026; FSR July 2026; 2026 AI survey (Bank of England) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-policy-committee-record/2026/april-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The FPC has asked for further work on agentic AI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-AI-STATEMENTS: FCA, Bank of England and PRA statements and initiatives on AI, 2024-2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S056: Financial Policy Committee Record April 2026; FSR July 2026; 2026 AI survey (Bank of England) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-policy-committee-record/2026/april-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. ESMA expects ex-ante input controls and frequent ex-post output controls, and holds management bodies responsible for decisions taken by AI tools [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S059: ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) and 2026 briefings <https://www.esma.europa.eu/document/public-statement-ai-and-investment-services> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. An approval interrupt that only a named, authorised human can resume is the L3 implementation of that accountability [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Standards.**
- *OWASP Agentic 2026.* The Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 starts with ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-OWASP-AGENTIC: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S042: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (launched 9-10 December 2025) (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], followed by ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation and ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse; ASI08 Cascading Failures and ASI10 Rogue Agents are among the remaining entries reported in a summary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S005: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (launch post and exploit round-ups) (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/2025/12/09/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-the-benchmark-for-agentic-security-in-the-age-of-autonomous-ai/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Deterministic graphs mitigate goal hijack by giving the model no control over the next step, and tool allow-lists per node mitigate misuse [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. - *NIST and ISO.* NIST AI RMF and AI 600-1 provide a neutral risk taxonomy; ISO/IEC 42001 provides the management-system wrapper [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-NIST-AIRMF: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1) and Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S043: AI Risk Management Framework (NIST AI 100-1) and revision status <https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S044: NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile; NCCoE agent identity concept paper; CAISI agent security <https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-ISO-42001: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management systems; ISO/IEC 42005:2025 AI system impact assessment; ISO/IEC 42006:2025 requirements for AIMS audit and certification bodies (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S045: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management systems <https://www.iso.org/standard/42001> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

### 3.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from L3 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The plan specifies L3 for this agent as a deterministic workflow graph with a human approval gate, not a free agent. Concretely:

1. **A pinned graph, not a loop.** Nodes: authorise request (C4) → fetch attribution snapshot via read-only tool (L4) → retrieve prior commentary and house style (L6–L8) → **one LLM drafting step** via the gateway (C1) → automated evaluation gate (L9: numeric faithfulness, groundedness, style) → **mandatory human approval interrupt** → hand to release service. The graph version is recorded with every run [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
2. **One judgement step.** The model drafts and explains; it does not choose which tools to call or in what order. If drafting needs a second pass (for example, after an eval failure), that is an explicit, bounded edge back to the drafting node with a retry limit [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
3. **Read-only tools only.** The workflow holds no write, publish or e-mail tool. Release is performed by a separate service after approval, using the approver's identity, not the agent's [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
4. **Durable execution.** The attribution snapshot and retrieval results are recorded activities. If the run fails after fetching data, it resumes from the checkpoint and reuses the recorded snapshot rather than calling the attribution engine again, so the draft and the evidence refer to the same numbers. Implementation: LangGraph with a firm-controlled Postgres checkpointer, or Temporal activities around the same steps [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
5. **Eval gate as a hard edge.** A failed numeric-faithfulness check routes to "returned for revision" or to a human, never to approval [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
6. **Approval that cannot be bypassed.** The approval interrupt can only be resumed by an authorised approver; the decision, approver identity, timestamp and any edits are written to the evidence pack (C8) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
7. **Evidence.** Each run record holds the graph version, prompt and model versions, the snapshot hash, retrieved document IDs, eval results, approver and final text [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What L3 must never do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- publish, send or file a commentary without a recorded human approval
- call the attribution engine again on resume and mix two data versions in one draft
- let the model choose to call tools outside the node's allow-list, or add tools at run time
- hold run state only in process memory or a container's local disk
- run the drafting step on a hosted agent service whose residency or retention terms are not approved for client data

**H2 (an "agent framework" is not one layer; distinguish deterministic workflows from autonomous agents). Provisional view; verdict in synthesis.**

The evidence supports the hypothesis, with one refinement.

- **Every major framework now ships both modes**, and several vendors document the split explicitly: LangGraph (deterministic logic and LLM decisions in one graph), Microsoft Agent Framework (Agents versus Workflows), CrewAI (Flows versus Crews, with Flows recommended as the outer process), Google ADK 2.0 (Workflow Runtime), LlamaIndex Workflows, Mistral Workflows and Vercel's Workflow SDK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S039: LangGraph Persistence / Durable execution / Interrupts - Docs by LangChain <https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S066: Microsoft Agent Framework README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/agent-framework/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S050: CrewAI Introduction / Flows / Evaluating Use Cases - CrewAI docs <https://docs.crewai.com/en/introduction> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S114: Agent Development Kit (ADK) 2.0 README (GitHub) (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S041: Announcing Workflows 1.0: a lightweight framework for agentic systems (LlamaIndex) <https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/announcing-workflows-1-0-a-lightweight-framework-for-agentic-systems> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S058: Workflows for work that runs the business (Mistral Workflows) (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/workflows/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S071: Workflow SDK README (GitHub) (Vercel) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel/workflow/main/packages/workflow/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Anthropic's guidance separates workflows from agents in the same terms [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S030: Building effective agents (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Durability is separating from both.** Pydantic AI v2 removed its own graph persistence and delegates durability to Temporal, DBOS or Prefect; the OpenAI Agents SDK integrates Temporal and DBOS; Mistral built Workflows on Temporal [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S044: Pydantic AI v2: capabilities, a leaner core, and the Harness (with upgrade guide) <https://pydantic.dev/articles/pydantic-ai-v2> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S045: Pydantic AI Durable Execution (overview, Temporal, DBOS, Prefect) <https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/capabilities/durable_execution/overview/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S052: OpenAI Agents SDK documentation (agents, sessions, handoffs, guardrails, tracing, running agents) <https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S058: Workflows for work that runs the business (Mistral Workflows) (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/workflows/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Runtimes are separating from frameworks.** AgentCore hosts agents from several frameworks with per-session isolation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S116: Bedrock AgentCore SDK README (GitHub) (AWS) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aws/bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; B-L3-S004: AgentCore Runtime sessions / microVMs / quotas / security best practices (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-sessions.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Foundry Hosted Agents accepts agents built with any framework [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L3-S006: Foundry Hosted Agents (Agent Framework hosting docs and Foundry blog) (Microsoft) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/hosting/foundry-hosted-agent> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **Visual workflow builders are retreating.** OpenAI is retiring Agent Builder and points code users to the SDK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S054: OpenAI Deprecations (Agent Builder) and Introducing AgentKit update <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

The refinement is that the split is not two products but two modes inside one framework, so it should be drawn as two sub-layers of L3 rather than as two layers with separate vendors [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The counter-evidence is that autonomous harnesses (the OpenAI and Claude agent SDKs, Mistral's Agents API) remain single-mode and are moving fastest [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S053: The next evolution of the Agents SDK (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/the-next-evolution-of-the-agents-sdk/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S027: Agent SDK overview - Claude Code Docs (Anthropic) <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S057: Build AI agents with the Mistral Agents API (and Agents & Conversations / Handoffs docs) (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/agents-api/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Provisional recommendation.** Redraw L3 as three stacked concerns: (1) **deterministic workflow orchestration** (graph, state, approvals) as the default for enterprise processes; (2) **bounded autonomous agent steps**, admitted per use case with a declared autonomy budget; and (3) **durable execution and managed runtime** as a reliability substrate beneath both [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. This also answers the pair-6 tension: most enterprise "agents" should be deterministic workflows with one judgement step, and guardrails cannot rescue a process that should never have been autonomous [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


## 2. Inference, serving and model access

> **Executive summary.** This layer turns a model choice (L1) into a callable, capacity-backed endpoint in a known place, and gives applications a governed way to reach it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The graphic shows nine tiles as one undifferentiated "inference" box. The evidence now shows three distinct jobs. **Serving engines** run the model: vLLM (Apache-2.0, PyTorch Foundation-hosted since 7 May 2025) and SGLang (Apache-2.0, LMSYS-hosted, with RadixArk as commercial steward since May 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: vllm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/vllm/json> accessed 2026-10-07; ### 2.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns.** It makes a chosen model available as an endpoint with known capacity, latency, location and data handling [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. That breaks down into three jobs, which H1 proposes to separate:

- **Model serving.** Loading weights onto accelerators and executing inference efficiently: batching, memory management of the KV cache, quantisation and an API surface. vLLM and SGLang are the open engines here; both expose OpenAI-compatible APIs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Inference optimisation and orchestration.** Coordinating many engine replicas: routing requests to the replica that already holds the relevant KV cache, separating prefill from decode, tiering the KV cache to CPU or storage, and autoscaling against a latency target. NVIDIA Dynamo and llm-d are the dedicated products [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; LMCache is a KV-cache layer that Dynamo integrates [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S091: LMCache README (GitHub) (LMCache project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LMCache/LMCache/dev/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Model access.** Obtaining someone else's served model under a contract: per-token serverless APIs, dedicated endpoints, reserved capacity, and routers that aggregate many providers behind one API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S135: Fireworks - Pricing (and Serverless Pricing docs) (Fireworks AI) <https://fireworks.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S113: OpenRouter Docs: FAQ (pricing and fees) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/faq.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Hand-offs.** Above this layer sits the gateway (C1), which every application call passes through; C1 owns routing policy, fallback lists, budgets, inline guard calls and the request log [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The C1 section covers the gateway products; this section does not repeat them. Below this layer sits L1: the model families and their licences. Alongside it: C3 decides what data may reach which endpoint, C6 consumes capacity and token cost, C7 owns weight provenance and engine patching, and L9 consumes per-call telemetry and qualifies fallback models [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the layer does not own.** It does not own the choice of model family (L1), the policy on which route a request takes (C1), or the decision that a workload may use client data (C3 and C8) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Routers such as OpenRouter now carry budgets, allowlists, ZDR enforcement and regional routing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S111: OpenRouter Docs: Guardrails <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/guardrails.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], which overlaps with C1. This section treats them as model-access sources behind the firm's gateway, consistent with C1 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 2.2 Why it matters

When this layer is badly designed, three things fail, usually at once [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- **Data goes somewhere nobody approved.** Where a prompt is processed is a property of the endpoint, not of the model. The same model can be processed globally, in a data zone or in one geography, depending on the deployment type selected [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A provider's defaults can also store prompts: Together AI stores prompts and responses, and may use them for product improvement, unless zero data retention (ZDR) is switched on [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S130: Zero data retention / Privacy and security - Together AI docs (and EU data centers support article) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Capacity runs out at the worst moment.** Serverless per-token APIs carry no reserved capacity; Together AI's serverless tier has no SLA, while its Provisioned Throughput does [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. On Vertex AI, traffic above a Provisioned Throughput quota goes to the global endpoint by default, which removes the residency guarantee unless overridden [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **Exit is impossible in practice.** If applications call one vendor's SDK and endpoint directly, a change of provider becomes a code programme rather than a configuration change [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A fund-reporting team pilots the commentary drafter against a fast serverless open-model endpoint through a convenient hosted router, because it "just worked" during the proof of concept. Nobody checks the router's processing region or the downstream provider's retention default. Six months later the pilot is live for 40 funds. At month-end, every fund's draft is requested within the same two-hour window after attribution runs complete, and the serverless endpoint starts returning rate-limit errors. The router falls back to another provider, which is outside the approved region and stores prompts by default. Drafts are produced on time, so nobody notices for a week. Then third-party risk asks for the list of sub-processors that saw the month's client holdings, and the team cannot produce it. Everything had to be re-assessed, and the route was suspended for the next cycle. Three controls would have prevented it: an in-region managed endpoint with reserved capacity sized for the month-end peak, a fallback list restricted to qualified in-region endpoints, and the gateway, not the router, deciding the route. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### 2.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time to first token (TTFT), p95 | Time from request to first streamed token | Per use case; interactive drafting typically seconds, batch less critical | Gateway timing per route; engine metrics |
| Inter-token latency / output tokens per second, p95 | Streaming speed per request | Per use case | Engine metrics (self-hosted); gateway timing (managed) |
| Availability per route | Successful responses over attempted, excluding client errors | Set per route; at least the business SLA of the consuming process | Gateway logs, reconciled to provider status |
| Capacity headroom at peak | Reserved or provisioned throughput minus observed peak demand | Positive at the forecast month-end peak plus a margin | Capacity plan vs gateway peak-hour metrics |
| Throttle / 429 rate | Share of calls rejected for rate or quota | Near zero on reserved routes; alert on any sustained rate | Gateway logs |
| Fallback activation rate | Share of calls served by a fallback endpoint | Low and explained; every activation logged | Gateway route records |
| In-region processing rate | Share of calls with verified processing location inside the approved region | 100% for client-data routes | Processing-region evidence (e.g. CloudTrail inference region [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]) joined to gateway logs |
| ZDR coverage | Share of client-data calls to endpoints with contractually confirmed ZDR or equivalent | 100% for client-data routes | Third-party register and endpoint configuration |
| Cost per 1M tokens and per task | Loaded cost including reserved capacity utilisation | Budget per use case | C6 attribution |
| GPU utilisation (self-hosted) | Busy accelerator time over paid time | High enough to beat the managed alternative | Cluster telemetry |
| Engine patch latency (self-hosted) | Days from a security advisory to deployed fix | Within the firm's vulnerability SLA | C7 vulnerability management against advisories [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S004: Security Advisories - vllm-project/vllm (vLLM project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] |
| Exit drill time | Time to move a route to the qualified alternative | Hours, by configuration only | Scheduled drill through C1 |

### 2.4 How it works

**Serving mechanics.** A serving engine loads weights, schedules many requests into shared batches, and keeps each request's attention state (the KV cache) in accelerator memory [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. vLLM's documented features show what "serving" now includes: PagedAttention, continuous batching, prefix caching, quantisation (FP8, MXFP4, NVFP4, INT4/8, GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF), speculative decoding (n-gram, suffix, EAGLE, DFlash) and disaggregated prefill, decode and encode [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. SGLang lists RadixAttention prefix caching, prefill/decode disaggregation, speculative decoding and FP4/FP8/INT4 quantisation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA's engine, describes itself as a library for optimising LLM inference with quantisation and speculative decoding [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S099: PyPI JSON metadata: tensorrt-llm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/tensorrt-llm/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Optimisation and orchestration mechanics.** Above the engines, the orchestration products work at the level of a fleet [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- *KV-aware routing.* llm-d routes on prefix-cache hits and load rather than round-robin [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S062: Introducing the next generation of AI inference, powered by llm-d (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/enhancing-vllm-for-distributed-inference-with-llm-d> accessed 2026-10-07]; Dynamo provides KV-aware routing and a Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension plugin [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Disaggregation.* Both separate prefill from decode across instances [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *KV-cache tiering.* llm-d offloads to CPU or disk with global indexing; Dynamo's KV Block Manager offloads GPU to CPU to SSD to remote storage; LMCache runs as a separate daemon so the cache survives an engine crash [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S091: LMCache README (GitHub) (LMCache project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LMCache/LMCache/dev/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *SLO-driven scaling.* Dynamo's planner right-sizes pools against latency targets; llm-d offers SLO-aware autoscaling [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Access mechanics.** Managed access comes in four contract shapes, and the shape decides capacity and data location [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- *Serverless per-token*: shared capacity, often no SLA (Together AI serverless) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Dedicated endpoints*: per-replica billing whether or not traffic arrives (Together AI); per GPU-second with scale to zero (Fireworks); per-minute instance billing on AWS, Azure or GCP (Hugging Face Endpoints) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S135: Fireworks - Pricing (and Serverless Pricing docs) (Fireworks AI) <https://fireworks.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S083: Inference Endpoints Pricing (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hf-endpoints-documentation/main/docs/source/support/pricing.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Reserved or provisioned throughput*: Together AI PTU with an uptime SLA; Microsoft Foundry provisioned throughput units (PTUs); Vertex AI Provisioned Throughput [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Routers*: one API across many providers, with provider prices passed through (OpenRouter adds a fee on credit purchases; Hugging Face Inference Providers adds no markup) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S113: OpenRouter Docs: FAQ (pricing and fees) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/faq.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V1-S062: Simplifying Our Platform Fee (OpenRouter) <https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/simplifying-our-platform-fee/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A4-S076: Inference Providers Pricing and Billing (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/pricing.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

```text
                    Applications / L3 workflows
                               │  one endpoint, workload identity (C4)
                               ▼
     ┌──────────────── C1 AI traffic gateway (control plane) ────────────────┐
     │ route policy · region pin · fallback list · budgets · guards · logs   │
     └───────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────┘
             │ (A) managed access   │ (B) router (non-     │ (C) private route
             ▼                      ▼     confidential)    ▼
   Hyperscaler model service   OpenRouter / HF        ┌─ Optimisation / orchestration ─┐
   (Bedrock geo profile,       Inference Providers    │ llm-d or Dynamo: KV-aware      │
    Foundry Data Zone,              │                 │ routing, PD split, KV tiering, │
    Vertex regional) or             ▼                 │ SLO autoscaling (optional)     │
   inference cloud dedicated   many providers        └───────────────┬────────────────┘
   endpoint (Fireworks BYOC,   (processing location                  ▼
   Together EU dedicated)       per provider)            Serving engine: vLLM / SGLang
             │                                                       │
             ▼                                                       ▼
        Provider GPUs in approved region                    Own / private-cloud GPUs
                        (L1 model weights below every route)
```

The three sub-layers of H1 are visible in the diagram: route (C) has all three (engine, optimisation, access through the gateway); routes (A) and (B) buy serving and optimisation as a service and keep only access [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The gateway is drawn above L2 because it governs every route, including routes that bypass L2 products entirely [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 2.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**
- Treat model weights and engine images as supply-chain inputs. vLLM published several 2026 advisories in which a malicious model repository or crafted input could execute code, including CVE-2026-22778 (critical, fixed from 0.14.1) and CVE-2026-27893, where two model files hard-coded `trust_remote_code=True` (fixed in 0.18.0) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S004: Security Advisories - vllm-project/vllm (vLLM project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. SGLang's CVE-2026-3059 (critical, unauthenticated code execution through the multimodal ZMQ broker, 0.5.9 and below) lists no patched version in the GitHub advisory [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S009: SGLang multimodal generation module unauthenticated RCE via ZMQ broker (CVE-2026-3059) - GitHub Advisory Database <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], while NVD gives the vulnerable range as 0.5.5 to 0.5.9 and references the v0.5.10 release as the fix [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REVC-S002: NVD CVE-2026-3059 (with OSV and GitHub Advisory Database GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58) (NIST NVD) <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-3059> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Load only allow-listed, scanned weights from an internal mirror, keep remote code off, and run engines on internal-only networks [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Engines and local runtimes are not identity-aware. Ollama binds to localhost by default, and exposure is done by changing `OLLAMA_HOST` and fronting it with a proxy [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S007: FAQ - Ollama <https://docs.ollama.com/faq> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Never expose an engine port directly; front it with the gateway and network policy [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- KV caches hold prompt state. Shared prefix caches and tiered or persistent KV stores (LMCache, Dynamo KVBM, llm-d tiered cache) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S091: LMCache README (GitHub) (LMCache project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LMCache/LMCache/dev/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] can carry one request's context into another's memory or storage. Partition caches by tenant or data classification, encrypt offload tiers, and include them in data-retention scope [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Check provider defaults, not just options. Together AI's ZDR is off by default [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S130: Zero data retention / Privacy and security - Together AI docs (and EU data centers support article) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Fireworks' ZDR is on by default for open models, except the Response API, which stores conversations for 30 days unless `store=False` is set [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S134: Zero Data Retention / Data residency / Regions - Fireworks AI Docs <https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/security_compliance/data_handling> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; OpenRouter's ZDR does not cover tools such as web search [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S108: OpenRouter Docs: Zero Data Retention <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/zdr.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Record the retention setting per route [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and capacity**
- Self-hosting is a capacity and operating-model decision, not only a cost decision [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Owning GPUs buys guaranteed capacity and in-estate processing, but it also buys the duty to patch engines fortnightly (vLLM shipped 28 releases in 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: vllm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/vllm/json> accessed 2026-10-07], to staff on-call for accelerators, and to forecast peaks.
- Plan capacity against the peak, not the average. Month-end and quarter-end reporting create predictable bursts [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Reserved capacity is available on every major route: Microsoft Foundry's provisioned types give lower and more consistent latency than Global Standard [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Vertex AI sells Provisioned Throughput [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Together AI's PTU carries an uptime SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Make overflow behaviour explicit. Vertex AI's Single Zone Provisioned Throughput processes overflow in the purchased region at pay-as-you-go rates, but it is excluded from the Gemini online inference SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Choose which property matters for each route: residency or SLA [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Resilience**
- Two qualified endpoints per production route, in the same approved region, with different failure domains [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Bedrock's EU geographic profile spreads requests across EU Regions only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], which is a residency-safe resilience mechanism inside one provider; it does not remove provider concentration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Fail closed rather than fall back out of region. OpenRouter's in-region routing fails rather than falling back [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S150: In-Region Routing: keep your data in the US or EU (OpenRouter blog) and OpenRouter Pricing/Enterprise pages <https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/us-in-region-routing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; the firm's gateway should behave the same way (see C1.5) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance and observability**
- Record processing location per call. Bedrock writes the actual inference Region into CloudTrail (`inferenceRegion`) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; join that evidence to the gateway log [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Pin model versions and record engine versions for self-hosted routes, so L9 regression results refer to an exact serving configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Cost**
- Pricing units differ and do not compare directly: per 1M tokens (Together, Fireworks, Cerebras), per replica-minute (Together dedicated), per GPU-second (Fireworks), per instance-minute (Hugging Face Endpoints), per PTU-minute (Together PTU) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S135: Fireworks - Pricing (and Serverless Pricing docs) (Fireworks AI) <https://fireworks.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S139: Pricing - Build with Cerebras Inference (Cerebras Systems) <https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/support/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S083: Inference Endpoints Pricing (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hf-endpoints-documentation/main/docs/source/support/pricing.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Model cost at the forecast utilisation, including idle reserved capacity [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Routers add fees on top of provider prices: OpenRouter charges 5.5% on credit purchases (US$0.80 minimum), 8% on Business [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S062: Simplifying Our Platform Fee (OpenRouter) <https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/simplifying-our-platform-fee/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A4-S144: OpenRouter Business / plans (and pricing blog posts) <https://openrouter.ai/business> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Regional processing can carry a premium. On Google Cloud, non-global endpoints are priced 10% higher from 1 July 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Residency is a priced control; budget for it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Portability**
- Make the OpenAI-compatible API the contract between gateway and every endpoint. vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, Cerebras, OpenRouter and Hugging Face Inference Providers all expose it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S084: Ollama Cloud docs <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/cloud.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S139: Pricing - Build with Cerebras Inference (Cerebras Systems) <https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/support/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S075: Hugging Face Inference Providers <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/index.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Provider-specific features (Fireworks Response API, OpenRouter guardrails) sit behind the gateway, not in application code [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Keep at least one open-weight model qualified on a portable engine as the stressed-exit route, even if it is never the primary [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** managed in-region endpoint with reserved capacity behind the gateway; a second qualified in-region endpoint as fallback; a private vLLM route for open-weight models where residency or exit demands it; internal model mirror with scanning; capacity plan tied to the business calendar.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** a hosted router as the gateway of record; serverless endpoints for a fixed-time month-end batch; provider defaults left unchecked (ZDR off, Response API storage on); engines on a reachable network port with no authentication; self-hosting justified on token price alone; a "global" endpoint for client data because it launched first.

### 2.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Engines: batching, KV-cache management, quantisation, speculative decoding, disaggregation, model and hardware coverage. Access: dedicated and reserved capacity, batch, fine-tuning, routing and fallback |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC, audit logs, SCIM, SLAs on capacity; for engines, what they enable inside your estate and whether a supported distribution exists (rule 2) |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in scope for the inference product; ZDR default and contract; CMK; BAA where needed; for engines, advisory handling and patch cadence |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Region choice and processing-location guarantees; dedicated, VPC/BYOC, on-prem; EU processing available now, not announced |
| Ecosystem (5%) | OpenAI-compatible API; availability on hyperscaler marketplaces; engine support across managed services |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | 1.0 status, release cadence, governance (foundation vs single vendor), ownership changes, capacity SLAs |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Unit pricing transparency, reserved-capacity economics, router fees, GPU and staffing cost for self-hosting |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Open weights and engines, OpenAI-compatible APIs, billing intermediation, proprietary hardware, ownership neutrality |

### 2.7 Product deep dives

The eleven records are grouped by H1 sub-layer: serving engines, optimisation and orchestration, local runtimes, and model access. Hyperscaler model services are discussed afterwards as a pattern; they have no product record in this layer and are not scored here [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Self-hosted engines and orchestration layers (vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo, llm-d, and Ollama's local runtime) are scored under rubric rule 2: security on project hygiene, enterprise readiness on what they enable in your estate, and both capped at 4 unless a commercial support offer or hardened distribution exists. They inherit host controls [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

#### Sub-layer 1: serving engines

**vLLM (vLLM project, PyTorch Foundation).**
- *What it is now:* an Apache-2.0 inference and serving engine at 0.31.0, released 5 October 2026, with 28 releases in 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: vllm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/vllm/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. It has been a PyTorch Foundation-hosted project since 7 May 2025, and its governance document names a committee that acts as the Technical Steering Committee under Linux Foundation project governance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S146: PyTorch Foundation Welcomes vLLM as a Hosted Project (and umbrella-foundation press release, 7 May 2025) (PyTorch Foundation (Linux Foundation)) <https://pytorch.org/blog/pytorch-foundation-welcomes-vllm/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S064: PyTorch Foundation Expands to Umbrella Foundation and Welcomes vLLM and DeepSpeed Projects <https://pytorch.org/blog/press-release-pytorch-foundation-expands-welcomes-projects-vllm-deepspeed/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A4-S064: vLLM Governance Process (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/docs/governance/process.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Features include PagedAttention, continuous batching, prefix caching, quantisation, speculative decoding and disaggregated prefill/decode/encode, with an OpenAI-compatible server, the Anthropic Messages API and gRPC, over 200 model architectures, and NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs, CPUs and hardware plugins [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Position in the stack:* it is the engine underneath Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, llm-d and NVIDIA Dynamo [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S081: About Inference Endpoints (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hf-endpoints-documentation/main/docs/source/about.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Support and hygiene:* Red Hat ships a supported vLLM-based server, renamed Red Hat AI Inference in version 3.4 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S001: Red Hat AI Inference 3.4 release notes <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai_inference/3.4/html/release_notes/rhaii-340-ga-release-notes_release-notes> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Security disclosures go through GitHub Security Advisories [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. In 2026 these included a critical video-input code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-22778), several model-loading flaws that bypassed `trust_remote_code=False` (CVE-2026-22807, CVE-2026-27893, and an August 2026 advisory), and an assertion bypass under Python optimised mode fixed in 0.22.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S004: Security Advisories - vllm-project/vllm (vLLM project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* the broadest single-engine feature set, neutral governance, and the de-facto substrate other products build on [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* pre-1.0 with a fortnightly cadence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: vllm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/vllm/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; its main attack surface is untrusted model files and media inputs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S004: Security Advisories - vllm-project/vllm (vLLM project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; it has no identity, audit or tenancy of its own [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you self-host open-weight models on your own or private-cloud GPUs and want the widest model and hardware coverage [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you cannot run a monthly patch cycle and model-provenance controls, or you have no GPU and SRE capacity [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Inference Endpoints (managed vLLM).
- *FS note:* run behind the gateway on an internal network, load only allow-listed weights from a scanned mirror with remote code off, pin versions and track advisories; buy the supported distribution if your operating model needs a vendor on the hook [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: only with patch and model-provenance discipline, and only where a private route is justified (see 2.9). Flag: none.**

**SGLang (LMSYS; RadixArk as commercial steward).**
- *What it is now:* an Apache-2.0 serving framework at 0.5.21 (1 October 2026), first released in January 2024, with 21 releases in 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S128: SGLang LICENSE (SGLang project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgl-project/sglang/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07]. Features include RadixAttention prefix caching, PD disaggregation, speculative decoding and FP4/FP8 quantisation, with broad hardware support (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel Xeon, Google TPU, Ascend) and day-0 support for new open models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S065: SGLang README (GitHub) (SGLang project (LMSYS)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgl-project/sglang/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The project states it powers over 400,000 GPUs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; this is a project claim.
- *Governance:* the repository states it is hosted by the LMSYS non-profit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S065: SGLang README (GitHub) (SGLang project (LMSYS)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgl-project/sglang/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. RadixArk, founded by SGLang's creators, launched with a US$100M seed on 5 May 2026 to steward SGLang and build a commercial platform [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S147: RadixArk Launches with $100 Million in Seed Funding Led by Accel to Grow SGLang (Business Wire, May 2026) (RadixArk (Business Wire)) <https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260505077157/radixark-launches-with-100-million-in-seed-funding-led-by-accel-to-grow-sglang-and-democratize-frontier-ai-infrastructure> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S063: RadixArk Launches with $100 Million in Seed Funding Led by Accel (RadixArk (Business Wire)) <https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260505077157/radixark-launches-with-100-million-in-seed-funding-led-by-accel-to-grow-sglang-and-democratize-frontier-ai-infrastructure> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. No transfer of code, trademark or governance from LMSYS was found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S147: RadixArk Launches with $100 Million in Seed Funding Led by Accel to Grow SGLang (Business Wire, May 2026) (RadixArk (Business Wire)) <https://www.morningstar.com/news/business-wire/20260505077157/radixark-launches-with-100-million-in-seed-funding-led-by-accel-to-grow-sglang-and-democratize-frontier-ai-infrastructure> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S065: SGLang README (GitHub) (SGLang project (LMSYS)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgl-project/sglang/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Security hygiene:* CVE-2026-3059, a critical unauthenticated code-execution flaw through the multimodal generation module's ZMQ broker, affects 0.5.9 and below; the GitHub advisory lists no patched version [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S009: SGLang multimodal generation module unauthenticated RCE via ZMQ broker (CVE-2026-3059) - GitHub Advisory Database <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], but NVD gives the vulnerable range as 0.5.5 to 0.5.9 and references the v0.5.10 release and a fixing pull request, and OSV records a fixed commit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REVC-S002: NVD CVE-2026-3059 (with OSV and GitHub Advisory Database GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58) (NIST NVD) <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-3059> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. An earlier deserialisation flaw (CVE-2025-10164) was fixed in 0.5.4, but VulDB reports that the vendor did not respond to early disclosure, and a June 2026 issue reports a bypass of that fix [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S009: SGLang multimodal generation module unauthenticated RCE via ZMQ broker (CVE-2026-3059) - GitHub Advisory Database <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. On the NVD and OSV references the current 0.5.21 should include the fix; the patch itself was not read, so confirm the deployed version against the upstream advisory [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Strengths:* strong on prefix-heavy and agentic workloads and quick to support new models [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* the security-response evidence is weaker than vLLM's; no verified commercial support offer [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; governance sits with a non-profit plus a VC-backed steward rather than a neutral foundation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you need a second qualified engine, prefix reuse matters, or a new model is supported here first [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* the engine's internal ports could be reachable outside a locked-down serving namespace, or you need vendor support now [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo (as orchestrator over either).
- *FS note:* qualify SGLang as the alternative engine in the exit plan, confirm the CVE status of the deployed version, and keep its multimodal and weight-update endpoints disabled or isolated [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: as the qualified backup engine to vLLM, once CVE-2026-3059 is confirmed fixed in the deployed version. Flag: none.** Upgraded from Tactical by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-4); scores are unchanged (FS 3.65), and security 2 is carried as the tier condition rather than raised. Keep internal ports isolated and do not make it the default engine [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

*TensorRT-LLM (NVIDIA)* is noted without a record: an open-sourced library for optimising LLM inference with quantisation and speculative decoding, at 1.2.1 and classed beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S099: PyPI JSON metadata: tensorrt-llm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/tensorrt-llm/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

#### Sub-layer 2: inference optimisation and orchestration

**NVIDIA Dynamo (NVIDIA).**
- *What it is now:* "the orchestration layer above inference engines — it doesn't replace SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or vLLM" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. It provides disaggregated serving, KV-aware routing, a multi-tier KV Block Manager, an SLA-based planner and autoscaling, model-weight streaming, a Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension plugin and topology-aware scheduling [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. It is Apache-2.0; ai-dynamo 1.5.1 was published on 7 October 2026 with a Beta PyPI classifier [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S098: PyPI JSON metadata: ai-dynamo (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/ai-dynamo/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Maturity conflict:* the README presents Dynamo 1.0 as "production-ready" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07], while the package classifier says Beta [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S098: PyPI JSON metadata: ai-dynamo (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/ai-dynamo/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Treat the package classifier as the operative signal until NVIDIA states otherwise [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Support:* enterprise support is an NVIDIA AI Enterprise feature branch: each branch is supported for one month, fixes and security updates are not backported, a subscription is needed to raise cases, and only the `-enterprise` artifacts are covered. The software itself is free to use in development and production [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S003: Dynamo Support Coverage (NVIDIA) <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/dev/reference/enterprise/support-coverage> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* clear separation of the optimisation sub-layer, and engine-agnostic across three backends; integrates LMCache [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S091: LMCache README (GitHub) (LMCache project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LMCache/LMCache/dev/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Limitations:* NVIDIA-led and NVIDIA-GPU-optimised [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; month-long support windows force continuous upgrades [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S003: Dynamo Support Coverage (NVIDIA) <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/dev/reference/enterprise/support-coverage> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; project security policy not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you operate multi-node NVIDIA GPU serving at a volume where disaggregation and KV-aware routing pay back [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* single-node or modest volumes, where vLLM alone suffices; or when you need long-term-support releases [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* llm-d, vLLM's own disaggregation, SGLang's own disaggregation.
- *FS note:* keep the engine's OpenAI-compatible API as the contract to the gateway so Dynamo can be removed without touching applications [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Experimental. Flag: none.**

**llm-d (CNCF sandbox project).**
- *What it is now:* a Kubernetes-native distributed inference stack that provides "orchestration and optimizations above model servers" such as vLLM and SGLang [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Features: prefix-cache- and load-aware routing (with predicted-latency scheduling, which the README's feature list calls experimental and its v0.7 release note calls GA), tiered KV-cache offload to CPU or disk with global indexing, PD disaggregation and wide expert parallelism, SLO-aware autoscaling [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. It is Apache-2.0, joined the CNCF as a sandbox project in March 2026, and released v0.7 in May 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Founders are Red Hat, Google Cloud, IBM Research, CoreWeave and NVIDIA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Google launched it on 20 May 2025 alongside the GKE Inference Gateway [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S062: Introducing the next generation of AI inference, powered by llm-d (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/enhancing-vllm-for-distributed-inference-with-llm-d> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Support:* Red Hat supports distributed inference with llm-d on OpenShift 4.19+, AKS and CoreWeave Kubernetes Service only as a Technology Preview, without production SLAs, and does not recommend production use [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* neutral governance and a multi-vendor founding coalition; builds on the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension rather than a private router [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S062: Introducing the next generation of AI inference, powered by llm-d (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/enhancing-vllm-for-distributed-inference-with-llm-d> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Limitations:* pre-1.0 and sandbox stage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; Technology Preview support [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; needs Kubernetes and data-centre accelerators [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; security hygiene not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* Kubernetes is the platform standard and you are building a shared internal inference service across several models [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you need production-supported software today [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* NVIDIA Dynamo, KServe, vLLM alone.
- *FS note:* pilot in non-production; revisit at 1.0 and when Red Hat moves support to GA [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Experimental. Flag: none.**

*LMCache* is noted without a record: "a KV cache management layer", vendor-neutral, running as a separate daemon so the cache survives an engine crash, a PyTorch Foundation project since October 2025 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S091: LMCache README (GitHub) (LMCache project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LMCache/LMCache/dev/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Ollama (Ollama).**
- *What it is now:* an MIT-licensed local runtime and model packager [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S086: Ollama LICENSE <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07], plus **Ollama Cloud**, which runs larger models in Ollama's cloud through apps, CLI or API with an API key, and exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S084: Ollama Cloud docs <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/cloud.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Cloud features can be disabled (`OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1`) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S085: Ollama FAQ <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/docs/faq.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Usage-based cloud plans started on 31 August 2026: Free, Pro US$20/month, Max US$100/month and Team US$500/month [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S066: Pricing - Ollama; Ollama's transparent pricing (31 Aug 2026) <https://ollama.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A US$65M round was reported in July 2026 [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — V1-S071: Open-source AI developer tool Ollama raises $65M to grow its platform (SiliconANGLE) <https://siliconangle.com/2026/07/09/open-source-ai-developer-tool-ollama-raises-65m-grow-platform/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

The vendor states cloud compute runs in the US and Europe, plus Singapore for some Qwen models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S066: Pricing - Ollama; Ollama's transparent pricing (31 Aug 2026) <https://ollama.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Network exposure:* the server binds to 127.0.0.1:11434 by default; remote access means changing `OLLAMA_HOST` and fronting it with a proxy such as Nginx [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S007: FAQ - Ollama <https://docs.ollama.com/faq> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Built-in authentication was not documented in the sources read [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
