- *Limitations:* Ollama Cloud certifications, SSO and audit are not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; the server version was not retrieved [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* developer workstations and offline evaluation, with cloud disabled [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* any shared or production serving, and any client data on Ollama Cloud [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM for anything shared.
- *FS note:* allow only on managed devices with `OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD` enforced by device policy and localhost binding; Ollama Cloud is an unassessed third-party processor [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical (developer tier). Flag: none (descriptor out of date: no longer local-only).**

- *What it is now:* a desktop application for downloading and running local models with a local API server, plus the MIT-licensed `lms` CLI and SDKs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S087: lms CLI README (LM Studio) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S088: lms LICENSE (LM Studio) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lmstudio-ai/lms/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S016: PyPI JSON metadata: lmstudio (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/lmstudio/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. The app is proprietary: free for personal and internal business use since about July 2025, and it may not be modified, redistributed, sublicensed or offered as a service [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S145: LM Studio is free for use at work (blog) and LM Studio App Terms of Service <https://lmstudio.ai/blog/free-for-work> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V1-S076: LM Studio is free for use at work; LM Studio App Terms of Service (LM Studio (Element Labs)) <https://lmstudio.ai/blog/free-for-work> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A paid Enterprise plan adds SSO and model and MCP gating [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S145: LM Studio is free for use at work (blog) and LM Studio App Terms of Service <https://lmstudio.ai/blog/free-for-work> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

#### Sub-layer 3: model access

**Hugging Face (Hugging Face).**
- *What it is now:* one tile, four products [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S075: Hugging Face Inference Providers <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/index.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S081: About Inference Endpoints (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hf-endpoints-documentation/main/docs/source/about.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S073: Inference Endpoints: Text Generation Inference (TGI) engine page (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hf-endpoints-documentation/main/docs/source/engines/tgi.md> accessed 2026-10-07]:
  1. **Hub**: model and dataset hosting with private repositories, malware, pickle and secrets scanning; SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, RBAC and audit logs on Team and Enterprise; US and EU storage regions for Team and Enterprise organisations [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S074: Hugging Face Hub Security <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/hub/security.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S080: Hugging Face Single Sign-On (SSO) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/hub/security-sso.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S079: Hugging Face Audit Logs <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/hub/audit-logs.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S078: Storage Regions on the Hub (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/hub/storage-regions.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
  2. **Inference Providers**: an OpenAI-compatible router to partner clouds (including Cerebras, Fireworks, Groq, Together, Nscale, OVHcloud, Scaleway) with provider rates passed through and no Hugging Face markup; it does not store request or response bodies and keeps logs for up to 30 days [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S075: Hugging Face Inference Providers <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/index.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S076: Inference Providers Pricing and Billing (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/pricing.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S077: Inference Providers Security & Compliance (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/security.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

- *FS note:* a model-access source behind C1, not C1 itself; reassess the contract, data-processing roles and sub-processor list when the acquisition closes, and plan any notification under PS7/26 lead times [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical. Flag: Acquired (pending).**

#### Hyperscaler model services as the default enterprise access route (pattern, not scored)

No record exists in this layer for Amazon Bedrock, Microsoft Foundry or Google Cloud's model service (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI); Stage A could not fetch their primary pages (stream A4 notes, section d). The pattern can still be described from the L1 records' availability fields and four new primary sources [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- *Breadth.* Most L1 families are reachable through at least one hyperscaler. Claude is offered on Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S010: Models overview - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]. OpenAI's GPT-6 family is on Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S008: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6 Sol and Luna generally available on Amazon Bedrock (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/openai-gpt-6-astra-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A5-S009: GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna for production AI agents in Microsoft Foundry <https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-6-astra-sol-and-luna-for-production-agents-in-microsoft-foundry/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Gemini is on Google Cloud only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Mistral models appear on all three, with different subsets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S038: LiteLLM 1.104.1 model_prices_and_context_window map (PyPI wheel) (BerriAI / LiteLLM (community-maintained)) <https://pypi.org/project/litellm/1.104.1/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Chinese-origin open models are hosted by hyperscalers too, for example Qwen3 and GLM 5 on Bedrock in London [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S086: Introducing Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock; GLM 5.3 GA on Amazon Bedrock (Oct 2026); Bedrock model cards (GLM 5, DeepSeek, Qwen3) (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-kimi-k3-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Processing location is configurable, and that is the point.* On Bedrock, a geographic cross-Region inference profile keeps EU-originated requests within EU Regions; London-originated requests route between EU Regions and London; stored data, invocation logs and knowledge bases stay in the source Region; CloudTrail records the Region that processed each request; a global profile can route to any commercial Region [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. On Microsoft Foundry, "Global" deployments may process prompts in any geography, "Data Zone" deployments process only within the US or EU zone, and Standard and Regional Provisioned deployments process within the customer's chosen geography [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. On Google Cloud, regional and multi-region (US, EU) endpoints keep processing within a jurisdiction, while the global endpoint gives no residency guarantee [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *But "on a hyperscaler" does not always mean "processed by the hyperscaler".* On Microsoft Foundry, Kimi K3 is offered through Fireworks, with inference on Fireworks GPUs outside the customer tenant, while DeepSeek V4 is sold directly by Azure [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S087: Introducing DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro in Microsoft Foundry; Foundry Models sold by Azure; Data, privacy, and security for Foundry Models sold by Azure; Bring <https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/introducing-deepseek-v4-flash-and-v4-pro-in-microsoft-foundry/4515174> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Check who operates the model, not just whose catalogue lists it [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Model availability by region is uneven.* GPT-6 Astra on Bedrock is in-region only in us-east-1 and us-west-2 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S008: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6 Sol and Luna generally available on Amazon Bedrock (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/openai-gpt-6-astra-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S079: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with help article 'Data residency for the OpenAI API'; 'Expanding data residency access') <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Bedrock geographic profiles are not supported for some models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Kimi K3 on Bedrock has US, India and global cross-Region profiles but no in-Region option [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S086: Introducing Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock; GLM 5.3 GA on Amazon Bedrock (Oct 2026); Bedrock model cards (GLM 5, DeepSeek, Qwen3) (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-kimi-k3-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The approved model list is therefore a function of region [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Capacity products exist on all three.* Foundry provisioned throughput units, Vertex Provisioned Throughput (regional-only for partner models such as Claude) and Bedrock cross-Region inference for throughput [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Regulatory position.* AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft are designated under both the DORA CTPP list and the UK CTP regime; no model provider is [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Consuming a model through the hyperscaler therefore places the inference service inside an already-overseen, already-contracted relationship [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Assessment [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.* For a regulated firm, the lead model service of its primary cloud is the default access route: it inherits platform identity and audit (CP2 Q1 presumption; platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service), offers in-geography processing and reserved capacity, and avoids adding a new material third party. Its weaknesses are concentration on one cloud, a model catalogue that differs by cloud and by region, and price premiums for regional processing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. These services would score as the lead hyperscaler service in their category under rule 10 if profiled; this is left to the L1 writer and synthesis.

**Scoring notes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- *Rule 2 (self-hosted software).* vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo and llm-d are scored as software you run; they inherit host controls. vLLM's enterprise readiness reaches 4 because a supported distribution exists (Red Hat AI Inference) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S001: Red Hat AI Inference 3.4 release notes <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai_inference/3.4/html/release_notes/rhaii-340-ga-release-notes_release-notes> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Dynamo has commercial support, but only month-long feature branches [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S003: Dynamo Support Coverage (NVIDIA) <https://docs.nvidia.com/dynamo/dev/reference/enterprise/support-coverage> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], so it stays at 3. llm-d's Red Hat support is Technology Preview without production SLAs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], so the cap at 4 applies (not binding at 3). SGLang has no verified support offer, so the cap applies (not binding at 3).
- *Rule 2 security hygiene.* vLLM scores 3: a working advisory process with fixed versions, against a run of 2026 code-execution flaws [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S004: Security Advisories - vllm-project/vllm (vLLM project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. SGLang scores 2: a critical unauthenticated flaw whose fix is evidenced only by NVD and OSV references (the GitHub advisory still lists no patched version), plus disclosure-response concerns and a reported bypass of an earlier fix [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S009: SGLang multimodal generation module unauthenticated RCE via ZMQ broker (CVE-2026-3059) - GitHub Advisory Database <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-REVC-S002: NVD CVE-2026-3059 (with OSV and GitHub Advisory Database GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58) (NIST NVD) <https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-3059> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The reader kept the score at 2 at Checkpoint 4 and upgraded the tier instead, conditional on the fix being confirmed (CP4-4). Dynamo and llm-d score 2 because their security policies and CVE handling were not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *NPV caps (rule 1).* Ollama: enterprise readiness and security capped at 2 (Ollama Cloud SSO, audit and certifications NPV). LM Studio: security capped at 2. LM Studio's enterprise readiness could rise to 3 under rule 7 on its Enterprise SSO, but that evidence is a low-confidence extract with no audit or support evidence, so 2 is kept.
- *Rule 7 (partial evidence).* Cerebras is lifted to 3 on verified console roles despite no SSO. OpenRouter (SSO, SCIM, roles, Enterprise SLA), Fireworks (SSO, RBAC, audit logs with CLI) and Hugging Face (SSO, SCIM, RBAC, audit logs) reach 4.
- *Rule 8 (certification scope).* Together AI's SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are vendor-stated without product scope, so 3 rather than 4. Cerebras' SOC 2 is a trust-centre listing without product scope, so 2. Fireworks scores 3 because its ISO claims conflict and are not relied on (V1 section 4); with confirmed certificates it would be a candidate for 4.
- *Rule 3 (ownership change).* OpenRouter's lock-in falls from 3 to 2 for the pending Stripe acquisition, and the change is noted in its maturity rationale. No other product in this layer changed owner in 2025–26; RadixArk's stewardship of SGLang is not an acquisition, but it is reflected in SGLang's lock-in score of 4 rather than 5.
- *Tiers.* vLLM is Strategic (FS 4.30). Hugging Face is Strategic, conditional (FS 3.60), on the narrow basis of its Hub as governed open-weight supply. SGLang (FS 3.65) and Fireworks (FS 3.65) were drafted as Tactical (SGLang under rule 11, with security 2 and no platform-commitment condition; Fireworks pending ISO and residency due diligence under rule 13). The reader upgraded both to Strategic, conditional at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-4), with no score changes: SGLang as the qualified backup engine to vLLM, once CVE-2026-3059 is confirmed fixed; Fireworks for managed open-model inference, once its ISO certificates are confirmed. Dynamo and llm-d are Experimental on maturity.
- *Calibration (rule 5).* Every product except vLLM, Hugging Face, Together and Fireworks scores 2 or below on at least one criterion. For those four, the weakest scores (3 on security for all of them) are stated as conditions.

### 2.9 Decision tree

Plan §9 gives the starting example (managed API vs private-VPC managed inference vs own GPUs). The tree below extends it with the questions that decide it in a regulated firm: data classification, residency, capacity, and operating model [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): every route is called through the gateway (C1); the
OpenAI-compatible API is the contract; each route records model, version, endpoint,
processing region and retention setting; a fallback is qualified (L9) and in region.

STEP 1 [Rec]: What data will the route carry?
  ├─ Public / non-confidential only
  │     → Any approved managed API or router (OpenRouter, HF Inference Providers)
  │       with ZDR on; still through C1.  Go to STEP 3 for capacity.
  └─ Client, personal or confidential data → STEP 2

STEP 2 [Rec]: Is the model you need available, processed in your approved region,
              on your primary cloud's model service?
  ├─ Yes → MANAGED ACCESS (default): Bedrock geographic/in-Region profile,
  │        Foundry Data Zone or Regional deployment, or Vertex regional/multi-region
  │        endpoint. Confirm who operates the model (hyperscaler vs partner).
  │        Go to STEP 3.
  └─ No (model not in region, open-weight model needed, or exit route required)
        → Is the requirement an open-weight model?
           ├─ No  → Use the model vendor's own regional API only if contracted
           │        (DPA, ZDR, region) and registered as a material third party;
           │        otherwise choose a different model (L1).
           └─ Yes → Do you have, or will you fund, GPU capacity AND an SRE team that
                    can patch engines monthly and run on-call?
                    ├─ No  → PRIVATE-VPC MANAGED INFERENCE: Fireworks BYOC or EU
                    │        dedicated deployment (Strategic, conditional: once its ISO
                    │        certificates are confirmed); Together EU dedicated endpoint
                    │        (Scale/Enterprise, ZDR on); HF Inference Endpoints in an
                    │        approved region with PrivateLink.
                    └─ Yes → OWN GPUs: vLLM (supported distribution if your operating
                             model needs a vendor), weights from an internal mirror;
                             SGLang qualified as the backup engine (Strategic, conditional:
                             once CVE-2026-3059 is confirmed fixed in the deployed version).
                             Multi-node, high volume, Kubernetes standard?
                             ├─ Yes → pilot llm-d (CNCF) or Dynamo (NVIDIA estates)
                             │        as the optimisation layer; non-production first
                             └─ No  → vLLM alone

STEP 3 [Rec]: Capacity
  Is demand bursty but time-critical (month-end, quarter-end)?
  ├─ Yes → reserved / provisioned capacity sized for the peak (Foundry PTU,
  │        Vertex Provisioned Throughput with overflow pinned in region,
  │        Together PTU, Fireworks reserved), plus a qualified in-region fallback
  └─ No  → standard / serverless in-region; batch APIs for non-interactive jobs

STEP 4 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Processing region evidenced per call?  ZDR / retention confirmed in the contract,
  not just the console?  Fallback in the same region and qualified?
  Engine version pinned and on the advisory watch list (self-hosted)?
  Exit drill: route moved to the alternative by gateway configuration only?
  Developer runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio): cloud disabled, no client data?
```

### 2.10 Lock-in classification

| Element | Classification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Rationale | Abstraction to use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|---|
| Serving engine (vLLM, SGLang) | **Acceptable** | Apache-2.0, OpenAI-compatible, interchangeable for most open models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S009: PyPI JSON metadata: vllm (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/vllm/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S128: SGLang LICENSE (SGLang project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgl-project/sglang/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07] | OpenAI-compatible API to the gateway; engine config in Git |
| Optimisation layer (Dynamo, llm-d) | **Manageable** | Open source, but deployment manifests and CRDs are product-specific; Dynamo is NVIDIA-led [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] | Keep it removable: engine API stays the contract; Gateway API Inference Extension where possible [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S062: Introducing the next generation of AI inference, powered by llm-d (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/enhancing-vllm-for-distributed-inference-with-llm-d> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Managed inference cloud (Together, Fireworks, Cerebras) | **Manageable** | Open-weight models and standard APIs; contracts for reserved capacity are the switching cost [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S152: Custom SSO - Fireworks AI Docs (with Enterprise, Virtual Cloud and changelog pages) <https://docs.fireworks.ai/accounts/sso> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Gateway routing; open-weight model qualified on a second provider or engine |
| Hyperscaler model service | **Manageable, with concentration caveat** | Proprietary SDKs and IAM, but called through the gateway; the risk is concentration on one designated provider [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Gateway with provider adapters; second cloud or private route for the stressed-exit case |
| Router in the data path (OpenRouter) | **Unacceptable for client data unless residency and ZDR are contractual; billing intermediation unacceptable for regulated workloads** | It puts a third party between the firm and its model providers, and its owner is changing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V1-S062: Simplifying Our Platform Fee (OpenRouter) <https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/simplifying-our-platform-fee/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; V1-S059: Stripe agrees to acquire OpenRouter to help businesses optimize token routing and usage <https://stripe.com/newsroom/news/stripe-agrees-to-acquire-openrouter> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] | Direct provider contracts and BYOK through the firm's gateway (see C1.10) |
| Proprietary hardware (Cerebras CS-3 on-prem) | **Manageable for speed-critical niches; unacceptable as the only route** | Proprietary wafer-scale stack [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S095: PyPI JSON metadata: cerebras-cloud-sdk (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/cerebras-cloud-sdk/json> accessed 2026-10-07] | Same models qualified on GPUs |
| Closed frontier model only available through one cloud | **Manageable if a qualified alternative exists** | Gemini is on Google Cloud only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07] | Portfolio of models (L1) and the gateway exit drill |
| Desktop runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio) | **Acceptable** (developer tier) | Out of the production path [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | None needed; enforce device policy |

### 2.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk.**
- *SS1/23.* PRA SS1/23 applies to banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval, and covers vendor models with ongoing performance monitoring [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. For other asset managers it is the natural benchmark [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. In this layer, a change of endpoint, engine version, quantisation level or fallback model can change outputs; treat each as a model change that needs re-qualification by the L9 regression suite [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and places generative and agentic AI outside its scope [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The firm's own governance must therefore decide which serving changes count as material [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Quantisation is a model change.* Running an open-weight model at FP8 or INT4 on vLLM [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] is a different numerical system from the provider's reference. Record the quantisation in the model inventory (C8) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- GPAI obligations sit with model providers; the Commission's enforcement powers over GPAI apply from 2 August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A firm that only serves an unmodified open-weight model is generally a deployer of the system it builds, not a GPAI provider; fine-tuning and redistribution need legal review [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to keep logs for at least six months; Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Most asset-management uses, including attribution commentary, are not Annex III [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Per-call records of endpoint, model version and region from this layer, joined to the gateway log, are the evidence base anyway [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**DORA, the UK CTP regime and outsourcing.**
- *Designations.* The DORA CTPP list (18 November 2025) and the UK CTP designations (in force 13 July 2026) include AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft; no AI model provider is designated [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Managed access through those hyperscalers therefore sits inside an overseen relationship; direct contracts with model vendors, inference clouds and routers do not [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Register of information.* Every inference cloud or router used for a function is an ICT third-party arrangement for the DORA register, with Article 30 terms and exit strategies where it supports a critical or important function [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Notifications.* PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Adding an inference provider behind the gateway, or a change of owner such as Stripe–OpenRouter, should be routed through third-party risk with that lead time [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Exit plans.* SS2/21 expects documented and tested exit plans, including stressed exit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. In this layer, the credible stressed-exit route is an open-weight model already qualified on a portable engine (vLLM) in your own or a second provider's estate, switched by gateway configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. An exit plan that names a second provider but has never been drilled is not tested [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Effective access.* FCA FG16/5 expects data location, effective access and exit planning for outsourced IT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Inference providers must evidence processing location per request; Bedrock's CloudTrail inference-Region field is an example of the evidence to require [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Data residency of inference: where prompts are processed.**
- Storage residency and processing residency are different promises. Foundry stores data at rest in the chosen geography regardless of deployment type, but Global deployments may process prompts anywhere [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Bedrock keeps stored data in the source Region while geographic profiles move prompts between Regions inside the geography [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. OpenAI's UK endpoint provides storage only, with no UK processing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S079: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with help article 'Data residency for the OpenAI API'; 'Expanding data residency access') <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Contracts and configurations must name processing location, not only storage location [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- UK-specific gap: Bedrock's EU profile does not route to London as a destination for EU-originated requests, and London-originated requests can route to EU Regions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. A UK firm needing UK-only processing must check per model whether an in-Region London option exists [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; some models have one (Qwen3, GLM 5 on Bedrock) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S086: Introducing Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock; GLM 5.3 GA on Amazon Bedrock (Oct 2026); Bedrock model cards (GLM 5, DeepSeek, Qwen3) (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-kimi-k3-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Transfers: EU-to-US transfers rely on the Data Privacy Framework or SCCs, with an annulment appeal (C-703/25 P) pending [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Prefer in-geography processing over transfer mechanisms for client data [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Chinese-origin models: the model weights may be acceptable on approved infrastructure even where the vendor's own API is not; DeepSeek's own platform stores personal data in the PRC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S062: DeepSeek Privacy Policy; DeepSeek Open Platform Privacy Policy and Terms of Service <https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Serve such open weights only on approved infrastructure, and follow the L1 position on their use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**ZDR and retention.** ZDR defaults differ: off by default at Together AI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S130: Zero data retention / Privacy and security - Together AI docs (and EU data centers support article) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; on by default at Fireworks for open models, except the Response API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S134: Zero Data Retention / Data residency / Regions - Fireworks AI Docs <https://docs.fireworks.ai/guides/security_compliance/data_handling> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; enforceable per request or guardrail at OpenRouter, but not covering tools such as web search [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S108: OpenRouter Docs: Zero Data Retention <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/zdr.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]; privacy-policy level only at Cerebras [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S153: Cloud Console / Projects - Cerebras Inference docs (with Cerebras Privacy Policy) (Cerebras Systems) <https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/console/overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Require ZDR in the contract for client-data routes, and verify it in the endpoint configuration that the gateway calls [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Capacity risk.** Capacity is an operational-resilience issue, not only a performance one [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Serverless tiers may have no SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; reserved capacity carries one where offered [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S131: Pricing - Together AI docs (serverless, dedicated endpoints, GPU clusters) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/inference/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; and overflow behaviour can silently cross a residency boundary (Vertex default overflow to the global endpoint) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Capacity plans for important business services should name the peak, the reserved amount, the overflow behaviour and the degraded mode [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Concentration.** IOSCO flags concentration risk from reliance on a few AI technology providers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S058: IOSCO FR/02/2026 Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (May 2026) <https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD823.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. This layer concentrates in three ways: one cloud for all model access; one GPU vendor under every self-hosted and most managed routes (Dynamo is NVIDIA-optimised; Together and Fireworks depend on NVIDIA supply) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S132: Together AI Raises $800 Million at $8.3 Billion Valuation (press release, 1 Jul 2026; TechCrunch coverage) (Together AI (Business Wire)) <https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260701243402/en/Together-AI-Raises-00-Million-at-.3-Billion-Valuation-to-Make-Frontier-AI-Accessible-to-All> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S141: Fireworks Raises a $1.5 Billion Series D (press release; CNBC 16 Jul 2026) (Fireworks AI (Business Wire)) <https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260716264405/en/Fireworks-Raises-a-$1.5-Billion-Series-D-to-Lead-the-Specialized-Intelligence-Revolution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; and inference clouds with concentrated revenue or customers (Fireworks' reported Cursor share; Cerebras' OpenAI agreement) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S141: Fireworks Raises a $1.5 Billion Series D (press release; CNBC 16 Jul 2026) (Fireworks AI (Business Wire)) <https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260716264405/en/Fireworks-Raises-a-$1.5-Billion-Series-D-to-Lead-the-Specialized-Intelligence-Revolution> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A4-S154: Cerebras Systems Inc. The mitigation is a portfolio: the primary cloud's service, plus one private or second-provider route for a qualified open-weight model [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. *Disclosure:* the author is an Anthropic model; Claude is cited here only as an example of multi-cloud availability, and the same rule applies to every model family [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Standards.**
- *OWASP.* The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 is the operative list [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-OWASP-LLM: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (superseded by the OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); V2-S056: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026 (with press release 'OWASP GenAI Security Project Unveils 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications, New Agent Control Standard', URL dated 2 <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-genai-llm-top-10-2026/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. ### 2.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from L2 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The deterministic workflow drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary (allocation, selection, currency, benchmark-relative return) for a generic multi-asset fund. Its drafting calls need the following from this layer:
1. **Drafting through the gateway to a managed, in-region endpoint.** The workflow calls the C1 route `attribution-commentary-draft`; the route's primary endpoint is the primary cloud's model service in the approved UK or EU geography, using an in-Region or geographic deployment, never a global one (Bedrock geographic profile, Foundry Data Zone or Regional, or a Vertex regional endpoint) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
2. **A qualified fallback model.** The fallback is a different model family in the same geography, or an open-weight model on a private-VPC dedicated endpoint (or a vLLM route), which has passed the same L9 regression suite. If neither is available, the route fails closed and the analyst is told the draft is delayed.
3. **No client data to routers without contractual ZDR and residency.** OpenRouter and Hugging Face Inference Providers are excluded from this route. If a router is ever used for this content, it must be under a contract with ZDR and in-region routing, and the router must fail rather than fall back out of region [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
4. **A capacity plan for month-end peaks.** All funds' drafts are requested in a narrow window after attribution runs complete. Size reserved capacity (Foundry PTUs or Vertex Provisioned Throughput with overflow pinned in region) for the forecast peak plus margin, and use batch processing for non-urgent regeneration [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Rehearse the peak in the month before go-live, and track the throttle rate and capacity headroom KPIs (2.3).
5. **Evidence per call.** Endpoint, model and version, quantisation (private routes), processing region (for example from CloudTrail [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]), retention setting and fallback flag go to the gateway record, L9 and the C8 evidence pack.
6. **A stressed-exit route that works.** One open-weight model is kept qualified on vLLM in an approved environment, so that the commentary can still be drafted if the primary provider is withdrawn. The switch is a gateway configuration change, drilled twice a year.

**What L2 must never do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- process a draft that contains client holdings on a global endpoint, an unassessed router, or a provider with ZDR off
- overflow from reserved capacity to an out-of-region endpoint because the default allows it
- serve the drafting model from an engine version or quantisation that has not passed the regression suite
- load weights from an unscanned public source onto the private route
- generate or alter authoritative numbers; figures come only from the attribution engine through the read-only L4 tool, and the model only drafts narrative

**H1 (split L2 into model serving → inference optimisation → model gateway/routing, with the gateway promoted to a control-plane component). Provisional view; verdict in synthesis.**

The evidence supports the split on four counts.

- **The optimisation products define themselves as a separate layer.** Dynamo is "the orchestration layer above inference engines" and does not replace them [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; llm-d provides orchestration "above model servers" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S089: llm-d README (GitHub) (llm-d project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/llm-d/llm-d/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; LMCache calls itself "a KV cache management layer" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S091: LMCache README (GitHub) (LMCache project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LMCache/LMCache/dev/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **The access market has separated from serving.** Managed services expose engine choice as a setting (Hugging Face Endpoints offers vLLM, SGLang, TGI, llama.cpp and TEI) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S081: About Inference Endpoints (Hugging Face) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hf-endpoints-documentation/main/docs/source/about.md> accessed 2026-10-07], and routers aggregate many providers' served models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S075: Hugging Face Inference Providers <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/hub-docs/main/docs/inference-providers/index.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S113: OpenRouter Docs: FAQ (pricing and fees) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/faq.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Hyperscalers sell processing location and reserved capacity as properties of the access contract, independent of the model [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S005: Geographic cross-Region inference - Amazon Bedrock (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S006: Understanding deployment types in Microsoft Foundry Models <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **Routing and governance have moved upward.** OpenRouter added budgets, allowlists, ZDR enforcement and regional routing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S111: OpenRouter Docs: Guardrails <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/guardrails.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. The C1 evidence shows gateways now carry model, tool and agent traffic, and its provisional view promotes the gateway to the control plane as an "AI traffic gateway" (see C1.13).
- **The kinds of risk differ by sub-layer.** Engines carry supply-chain and patching risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L2-S004: Security Advisories - vllm-project/vllm (vLLM project (GitHub)) <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S009: SGLang multimodal generation module unauthenticated RCE via ZMQ broker (CVE-2026-3059) - GitHub Advisory Database <https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgq9-fqf5-fv58> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; optimisation layers carry maturity risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S098: PyPI JSON metadata: ai-dynamo (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/ai-dynamo/json> accessed 2026-10-07; B-L2-S002: Supported platforms for Distributed Inference with llm-d (Red Hat AI 3) <https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_ai/3/html/supported_product_and_hardware_configurations/llmd-supported-platforms_supported-configurations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; access carries third-party, residency and capacity risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S130: Zero data retention / Privacy and security - Together AI docs (and EU data centers support article) <https://docs.together.ai/docs/zero-data-retention> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; B-L2-S008: Data residency (with Deployments and endpoints; Single Zone Provisioned Throughput) - Vertex AI (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Different risks need different owners [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

The counter-evidence is twofold. First, optimisation techniques also ship inside the engines: vLLM and SGLang both include prefix caching, speculative decoding, quantisation and disaggregation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S063: vLLM README (GitHub) (vLLM project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S010: PyPI JSON metadata: sglang (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/sglang/json> accessed 2026-10-07], so for most firms "inference optimisation" is a configuration of the engine, not a separate product. Second, the boundary between optimisation-layer routing and the gateway blurs at the Kubernetes edge: Dynamo and llm-d both plug into the Gateway API Inference Extension [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S090: NVIDIA Dynamo README (GitHub) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S062: Introducing the next generation of AI inference, powered by llm-d (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/enhancing-vllm-for-distributed-inference-with-llm-d> accessed 2026-10-07]. That in-cluster router chooses a replica, while C1 chooses a provider, model and region [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Provisional recommendation.** Redraw L2 as three sub-layers: **model serving** (engines; vLLM and SGLang), **inference optimisation** (an optional fleet layer; llm-d, Dynamo, LMCache, and engine-native features), and **model access** (hyperscaler model services, inference clouds, dedicated endpoints and routers) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Move routing policy, fallback, budgets, guard invocation and the request log out of L2 into the control plane as C1, consistent with C1's provisional "AI traffic gateway" [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Mark the optimisation sub-layer as relevant only to firms that run their own GPU fleets [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


## 1. Foundation models

> **Conflict-of-interest disclosure.** The author is an Anthropic model, writing about Anthropic and its direct competitors. This is the layer where that conflict is most acute. Anthropic's Claude family was scored on exactly the same rubric as every other family. Where a score for Anthropic was borderline, it was resolved against Anthropic, and each such call is named in its rationale. Anthropic's limitations and controversies are recorded in the same detail as everyone else's. Anthropic's allegation against Chinese laboratories is presented only as an allegation. An independent alternative is named wherever a Claude model appears in a recommendation, and no vendor benchmark (including Anthropic's) is used as a decision input [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Tier and neutral scoring set by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-1); the author's pipeline had resolved three borderline scores against Anthropic. Security and cost now carry the neutral rubric values identified by the CP4 calibration review [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

> **Executive summary.** This layer supplies the language models that every agent, retrieval pipeline and evaluation judge above it depends on. Four things have changed since the original graphic. Run a tiered portfolio (frontier, mid, small and a self-hosted open-weight tier) from at least two unrelated vendors, all routed through the firm's gateway (C1), each qualified and re-qualified on the firm's own evaluation suite (L9), with pinned versions and a tested exit to the second vendor [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 1.1 Responsibility

**The problem this layer owns.** L1 turns a prompt and context into generated text, structured output or a tool-call decision, with known capability, cost, latency, data-handling terms and support lifetime [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. In practice an enterprise does not "own" this layer by building models; it owns the *choice, contract, configuration and qualification* of models it buys or self-hosts [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Five jobs follow:

- **Capability coverage.** Have a qualified model for each task class the firm runs: drafting and reasoning, extraction and classification, coding, multimodal input, and long-context synthesis [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Data-handling fit.** Know, for each model and route, where inference runs, what is retained, whether inputs train the model, and under which jurisdiction's law [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Version and lifecycle control.** Pin exact model versions, know each version's retirement date, and re-qualify before forced migration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Concentration management.** Keep at least one alternative qualified for every production use so that a vendor outage, suspension, withdrawal or regulatory event does not stop the business service [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Model-risk evidence.** Give the model inventory (C8) an identity for each model (vendor, family, version, route, region) so that validation and monitoring attach to something stable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.** L1 is consumed only through L2 (serving and model access) and the gateway (C1): applications never call a vendor API directly [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. L2 decides *how* a model is reached (vendor API, hyperscaler endpoint, or self-hosted serving engine). C1 decides *which* model a request goes to (routing, fallback, quotas, logging). L9 supplies the evaluation evidence that a model is fit for a task. C8 holds the inventory and approval. C3 and C2 sit in front of the model to mask client data and enforce content policy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the layer does not own.** It does not own grounding (L6–L8), tool permissions (L4, C4) or numeric correctness. A model is never the source of an authoritative figure in this architecture [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### 1.2 Why it matters

A badly designed model layer fails in four ways [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Single-vendor dependency.** A firm that hard-codes one vendor's API cannot respond when that vendor suspends a model, changes its retention terms, or becomes the subject of a government action. These are not hypothetical: Anthropic's top tier, Claude Fable 5, was made unavailable on 12 June 2026 and restored from 1 July 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S004: Claude Fable - Anthropic <https://www.anthropic.com/claude/fable> accessed 2026-10-08], and a US court upheld a federal supply-chain-risk designation of Anthropic on 25 September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S084: Anthropic PBC v. United States Department of War, No. 26-1049 (D.C. Cir., decided 25 Sept 2026) - opinion; with CNBC and Bloomberg coverage (US Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit) <https://media.cadc.uscourts.gov/opinions/docs/2026/09/26-1049-2194984.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Silent version drift.** Using an alias ("latest", "stable") lets the vendor change the model underneath a validated process. Google's own documentation recommends pinning versioned model IDs for predictable behaviour [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S003: Gemini 3.7 Flash model page and related lifecycle pages (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-7-flash> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **Residency by accident.** Two routes to the "same" model can process data in different jurisdictions. Anthropic's first-party API offers only global or US inference geography, while the same models run in EU regions on Google Cloud and Bedrock [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S013: Data residency - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S075: Data residency - Claude Platform Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/data-residency> accessed 2026-10-08; A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Microsoft Foundry runs DeepSeek V4 in the customer's geography but runs Kimi K3 and GLM-5.x through Fireworks outside the customer's tenant [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S087: Introducing DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro in Microsoft Foundry; Foundry Models sold by Azure; Data, privacy, and security for Foundry Models sold by Azure; Bring <https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/introducing-deepseek-v4-flash-and-v4-pro-in-microsoft-foundry/4515174> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Model as oracle.** Treating a fluent model as a source of numbers or facts. No model at any tier is fit to produce authoritative figures [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A UK asset manager standardises its client-reporting assistant on one vendor's top-tier model through that vendor's own API, because the evaluation scores were best. The contract, data-protection assessment and model validation all name that one model. Three weeks before quarter-end the vendor withdraws access to the tier while it fixes a safeguard issue. The gateway has no second route: the fallback model named in the design document was never qualified on the commentary evaluation suite, and its data-processing terms were never assessed. Engineers point the assistant at the vendor's next tier down, which formats percentages differently, and reviewers spend the quarter-end hand-checking every draft. The firm then discovers that its operational-resilience self-assessment listed the assistant as supporting an important business service with "multi-vendor fallback". The fix is not a better model; it is a second vendor qualified in advance, on the same evaluation suite, through the same gateway, with its own contract and residency assessment. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### 1.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qualified-alternative coverage | Share of production use cases with a second model from a *different vendor* that has passed the same evaluation suite within the last quarter | 100% for important business services | C8 inventory joined to L9 results |
| Task-level quality | Per-use-case evaluation score (faithfulness, groundedness, numeric checks, style) for the pinned model | Thresholds per use case; numeric checks 100% | L9 regression suite on every model change |
| Version pinning rate | Share of production calls that name an exact dated or versioned model ID, not an alias | 100% | Gateway logs (C1) |
| Retirement runway | Days between today and the earliest announced retirement of any pinned model | Never below the re-qualification lead time (e.g. 90 days) | Vendor deprecation pages (e.g. B-L1-S001, B-L1-S002, B-L1-S003) reconciled with inventory |
| Residency conformance | Share of calls processed in an approved region for their data class | 100% for client data | Gateway route metadata vs data classification (C3) |
| Cost per task | Loaded token cost per completed task, by tier | Budget per use case; falling trend | Gateway metering (C6) |
| Tier mix | Share of calls served by the small or self-hosted tier where quality allows | Rising until quality thresholds bind | Gateway logs |
| p95 latency and availability | Latency and success rate per model and route | Per use case; failover tested quarterly | Gateway and L9 traces |
| Failover drill success | Share of scheduled drills where traffic moved to the alternative model with quality within threshold | 100% | Drill records (C8) |
| Concentration ratio | Share of production tokens (or important services) served by the largest single vendor | Firm-set ceiling, reported to the risk committee | Gateway metering |

### 1.4 How it works

A foundation model is reached by one of three routes, and the route matters as much as the model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

1. **Vendor API.** The vendor runs the model and processes the data under its own terms and regions. Examples: OpenAI's EU endpoint, which stores and processes in region for new projects that use Modified Abuse Monitoring or ZDR [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S006: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with Enterprise privacy, EU/UK data residency announcements) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S079: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with help article 'Data residency for the OpenAI API'; 'Expanding data residency access') <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Mistral's EU endpoint, which commits inference location for a 10% surcharge [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S075: Mistral Help Centre: SOC 2 / ISO 27001; data storage location; ZDR; Regional inference docs; Trust Center (Mistral AI) <https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347638-do-you-have-soc-2-or-iso-27001-certification> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; DeepSeek's API, which stores data in the PRC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S062: DeepSeek Privacy Policy; DeepSeek Open Platform Privacy Policy and Terms of Service <https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
2. **Hyperscaler-hosted.** The model runs inside AWS, Azure or Google Cloud under the cloud's IAM, logging and regional controls. Claude is on Bedrock, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S010: Models overview - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]; GPT-6 is on Bedrock and Foundry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S008: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra / GPT-6 Sol and Luna generally available on Amazon Bedrock (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/09/openai-gpt-6-astra-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A5-S009: GPT-6 Astra, Sol, and Luna for production AI agents in Microsoft Foundry <https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/blog/gpt-6-astra-sol-and-luna-for-production-agents-in-microsoft-foundry/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Gemini is on Google Cloud only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S027: Generative AI pricing - Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI) <https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/generative-ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Some hyperscaler listings are pass-throughs: Foundry's Kimi K3 and GLM-5.x run on Fireworks outside the customer's tenant [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S087: Introducing DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro in Microsoft Foundry; Foundry Models sold by Azure; Data, privacy, and security for Foundry Models sold by Azure; Bring <https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/introducing-deepseek-v4-flash-and-v4-pro-in-microsoft-foundry/4515174> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and Bedrock offers Kimi K3 only through cross-Region profiles [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S086: Introducing Kimi K3 on Amazon Bedrock; GLM 5.3 GA on Amazon Bedrock (Oct 2026); Bedrock model cards (GLM 5, DeepSeek, Qwen3) (AWS) <https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-kimi-k3-on-amazon-bedrock/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

```text
 Application / agent (L3)
          │  prompt + approved context (no raw client identifiers: C3)
          ▼
 Gateway C1 ── policy: data class → allowed routes & regions; task → model tier
          │            pinned model IDs; fallback order; quotas; logging (L9, C6)
          ├────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
          ▼                    ▼                          ▼                         ▼
   Frontier tier         Mid tier (default)         Small tier               Self-hosted open-weight
   (gated, rare use)     vendor A in-region         classification,          tier (L2 serving)
   e.g. Astra / Fable    e.g. GPT-6.1 Sol,          routing, extraction      e.g. Gemma 4, Mistral
                         Sonnet 5.5, Gemini 3.8     e.g. Luna, Haiku 5.5,    Medium 3.5, gpt-oss
                         Flash, Mistral Medium 3.5  Flash-Lite, Ministral    (sensitive data stays
                              │                                               in estate)
                              └─► fallback: vendor B, same tier, same region,
                                  qualified on the same L9 suite
          ▼
 Response → guardrails (C2) → evaluation (L9) → inventory & evidence (C8)
```

**The portfolio principle.** Tiers trade capability against cost and latency within a family: OpenAI lists Luna for "high-volume summarisation, extraction, classification and routing" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S002: GPT-6 Astra: A new generation of intelligence (plus release notes, Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 for everyone) (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and list prices span two orders of magnitude, from US$0.10 to US$10 per 1M input tokens within both the OpenAI and Anthropic families [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S004: OpenAI API Pricing (and Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna pricing) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Vendors diversify across families. Self-hosting changes the data question entirely, because no data leaves the estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A portfolio therefore has two axes: *tier* (frontier, mid, small, open-weight) and *vendor* (at least two unrelated vendors at the mid tier) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
