### 1.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**

- Send no raw client identifiers to any external model; mask or tokenise at C3 before the gateway [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Prefer routes with contractual no-training and zero or short retention. OpenAI does not train on API data by default and retains up to 30 days unless ZDR is approved [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S006: Data controls in the OpenAI platform (with Enterprise privacy, EU/UK data residency announcements) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Anthropic does not train on commercial data without permission; ZDR is available on request, but Fable 5.1 is a "Covered Model" needing 30-day retention unless expressly authorised, which conflicts with its launch post [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S023: Updates to Consumer Terms and Privacy Policy (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/news/updates-to-our-consumer-terms> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S016: Introducing Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 (Anthropic) <https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1> accessed 2026-10-07]. xAI deletes within one hour under team-level ZDR [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S080: FAQ - API Security; Regional Endpoints; Enterprise Terms of Service (xAI/SpaceXAI) (xAI (SpaceXAI)) <https://docs.x.ai/developers/faq/security> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Mistral offers ZDR only for pay-as-you-go stateless calls at its discretion [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S075: Mistral Help Centre: SOC 2 / ISO 27001; data storage location; ZDR; Regional inference docs; Trust Center (Mistral AI) <https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/347638-do-you-have-soc-2-or-iso-27001-certification> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Meta's contributor tier trains on prompts and completions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S019: Meta Connect 2026: The end-to-end recap (with research.meta.ai 'Introducing Muse Spark 1.3') <https://developers.meta.com/blog/meta-connect-recap/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Block any training-on-data tier at the gateway [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Treat open-weight files as executable supply-chain artefacts: scan, sign or hash-pin, and serve from an internal registry (C7) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Gated cyber-capable tiers (Astra, Mythos, Argon) are off by default for a reason. Keep them disabled unless a named use case needs them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and resilience**

- Every production use case gets a primary and a fallback from a different vendor, on the same tier, in an approved region, qualified on the same evaluation suite [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Run failover drills; an untested fallback is not a fallback [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Spread across routes as well as vendors: the hyperscaler is a concentration point too, and DORA and the UK CTP regime designate the hyperscalers, not the model vendors [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance and lifecycle**

- Pin exact model IDs; never use "latest" aliases in production [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Google states that pinning versioned IDs gives more predictable behaviour [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S003: Gemini 3.7 Flash model page and related lifecycle pages (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-7-flash> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- Track retirement dates. Notice periods differ: OpenAI gives at least 6 months for GA models, at least 3 months for specialised variants and as little as about 2 weeks for previews [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S001: Deprecations (OpenAI API docs) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Mistral's Labs models may go with 1 month's notice [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S002: Models overview: deprecated and retired models (Mistral Docs) (Mistral AI) <https://docs.mistral.ai/models> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Anthropic publishes "not sooner than" retirement commitments of September/October 2027 for current models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S010: Models overview - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview> accessed 2026-10-07]; Google publishes per-model retirement dates, with recent Flash versions living about five to six months [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S003: Gemini 3.7 Flash model page and related lifecycle pages (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-7-flash> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- Never put a preview model (Gemini 3.1 Pro is still preview [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S032: Gemini Developer API pricing (and Gemini 3.1 Pro preview model page) (Google) <https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]) or a days-old preview (Mistral Large 4 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S076: Introducing Mistral Large 4 (and Mistral changelog) (Mistral AI) <https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]) behind an important business service [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Observability and cost**

- Log model ID, route, region, token counts and latency for every call at the gateway, and attach evaluation results in L9 [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Route by tier: classification and extraction to the small or self-hosted tier; drafting to the mid tier; the frontier tier only where evaluation proves the mid tier insufficient [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Portability**

- Keep prompts, tool schemas and output schemas vendor-neutral and in Git (C5); most vendors expose OpenAI-compatible interfaces [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S010: Models overview - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S077: Introducing Muse Spark (Meta, April 2026); Introducing Muse Spark 1.1 / Meta Model API (ai.meta.com); Meta Connect 2026 recap <https://about.fb.com/news/2026/04/introducing-muse-spark-meta-superintelligence-labs/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A5-S038: LiteLLM 1.104.1 model_prices_and_context_window map (PyPI wheel) (BerriAI / LiteLLM (community-maintained)) <https://pypi.org/project/litellm/1.104.1/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], so an OpenAI-shaped internal contract behind the gateway is the practical abstraction [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Keep at least one open-weight model qualified per critical use case, even if it is lower quality, as the stressed-exit route [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** two-vendor mid tier with gateway failover; small model for classification and routing; self-hosted open-weight tier for sensitive or air-gapped tasks; pinned versions with a retirement calendar; model-agnostic prompt templates; evaluation-gated promotion of any new version.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** a single vendor's API called directly from application code; aliases in production; choosing on vendor benchmark tables; frontier tier as the default; using a vendor's own API because it is cheapest without checking jurisdiction; treating a hyperscaler listing as proof of in-region, in-tenant processing; letting a vendor-owned test tool be the only independent check of that vendor's model (see L9 on Promptfoo [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S024: OpenAI to acquire Promptfoo <https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-promptfoo/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]).

### 1.6 Product selection criteria

The units of selection are *vendor families*, because individual versions are replaced within months. Scores follow the rubric in `08_scoring_rubric.md` and the CP2/CP3 rules [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this layer [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Breadth and depth of the current lineup against plan §5 (frontier vs open-weight; general vs specialist; reasoning, multimodal, coding, small models), on primary evidence of what the models do and independent government evaluations (CAISI). **Vendor benchmark numbers are not used.** |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | Admin and identity controls on the vendor API; whether the current generation is offered in-tenant on a hyperscaler (CP2 Q1 presumption); support and SLA terms |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scoped to the API; ISO 42001, CMK, ZDR, no-training terms; first-party and hyperscaler residency options; regulatory findings against the vendor |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Vendor API, hyperscaler (in-tenant vs pass-through), self-hosted and air-gapped open weights |
| Ecosystem (5%) | Hyperscaler distribution, OpenAI-compatible interfaces, open-serving engine support |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | GA vs preview, retirement policy and notice, availability events, ownership stability |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Transparent per-tier pricing, batch and caching, residency premiums, self-hosting burden. Chinese-vendor API prices are aggregator-level and not decision inputs (V2 §4 item 3) |
| Lock-in / portability / concentration (15%) | Open weights and licence terms; number of independent hosting routes; interface standardisation; ownership change (rule 3); licence thresholds (rule 4) |

**How the family scores were built [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.**
- *Enterprise readiness.* The hyperscaler presumption (rule 6) applies where the family's *current generation* is offered on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, operated by the cloud. Where it is not (Qwen3.8), the vendor's own evidence applies.
- *Security.* Scored on the model vendor's own certifications and terms, not the hyperscaler's. A family whose primary evidence is "not publicly verified" is capped at 2 (rule 1); a vendor with an unremediated serious regulatory finding against its hosted service scores 1.
- *Chinese-origin families.* Each rationale states the hosted API and the self-hosted weights separately. The family score reflects the vendor as counterparty; the tier condition says which route is acceptable.

### 1.7 Product deep dives

Families are grouped as: US frontier vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, SpaceXAI Grok); open-weight-led vendors from the US and EU (Mistral, Gemma, Meta); and Chinese-origin vendors (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scoring notes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- *Conflict of interest.* The draft resolved three borderline Anthropic criteria against Anthropic: technical (4 not 5: no open weights, audio or image output), ecosystem (4 not 5: not the de facto API) and cost (3 not 4: same tier prices as OpenAI, but a residency premium and a dearer recommended default). It also held security at 4 although the certificates meet the rule-8 threshold for 5. The CP4 calibration review found technical 4 and ecosystem 4 to be the neutral values on peers, and cost 4 and security 5 to be the neutral values. Tier and neutral scoring set by the reader at Checkpoint 4 (CP4-1); the author's pipeline had resolved three borderline scores against Anthropic. Anthropic now scores security 5 and cost 4 (FS 3.80, previously 3.55) and is Strategic, conditional; the residency gap and the ZDR conflict are carried as tier conditions.
- *Evidence caps.* Security is capped at 2 for Qwen, Kimi, GLM and Meta (certifications NPV, rule 1). DeepSeek scores 1: certifications NPV *and* an unremediated Garante limitation on a service that stores data in the PRC. Qwen's enterprise readiness is capped at 2 because Qwen3.8 is on no hyperscaler and Model Studio's controls are NPV.
- *Hyperscaler presumption (rule 6)* gives enterprise readiness 4 to every other family, because each has a current-generation model operated by a hyperscaler (for DeepSeek, Microsoft Foundry in-tenant; for Kimi and GLM, Bedrock, cross-Region). **Hosting caveat (kept by the reader at CP4-3):** on Azure, Kimi K3 and GLM-5.x run on Fireworks outside the customer tenant, so the Azure route does not support their 4; DeepSeek V4 on Foundry is sold directly and processed in-tenant in the customer's geography [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S087: Introducing DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro in Microsoft Foundry; Foundry Models sold by Azure; Data, privacy, and security for Foundry Models sold by Azure; Bring <https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-blog/introducing-deepseek-v4-flash-and-v4-pro-in-microsoft-foundry/4515174> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The vendors' own APIs would score 2 for DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Meta. Platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service.
- *Certification scope (rule 8).* Mistral's certificates are stated without product scope, so security is one point below the anchor. OpenAI's ISO 42001 scope does not name the API, so it does not count toward 5. Anthropic meets the test for 5 (SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 scoped to the API, Bedrock and Google Cloud, plus CMEK) and scores 5 (CP4-1).
- *Ownership change (rule 3).* Grok's lock-in was reduced by 1 and it carries the Acquired flag.
- *Licence risk (rule 4).* Revenue or usage thresholds in Medium 3.5, Llama 4, Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 flagship and GLM-5.3 are stated in the lock-in rationales.
- *Hyperscaler lead service (rule 10).* Gemini is Strategic, conditional on Google Cloud being the primary cloud, at FS 3.35, the lowest Strategic total in the layer: rule 10 is a platform-commitment rule, not a quality judgement (kept by the reader at CP4-2).
- *Calibration (rule 5).* Criteria at 2 or below appear for seven of the eleven families (Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM and Meta). Enterprise readiness is flat at 4 for ten families because of rule 6, not because the vendors' own controls are equal.
- *No vendor benchmark* was used for any score. Independent CAISI evaluations were used only for technical and risk rationale.

### 1.9 Decision tree

The tree builds a portfolio in four steps. Step 0 is a precondition, not a product choice [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): all model calls go through the firm's gateway (C1) with pinned
model IDs, data-class → route/region policy, logging to L9, and a model inventory entry (C8).
Applications never call a vendor API directly.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Which routes may this data class use?
  Client / personal / confidential data?
  ├─ Yes → only (a) hyperscaler-hosted, in an approved UK/EU region, in-tenant, no-training,
  │        ZDR or short retention; or (b) self-hosted open weights in the estate.
  │        Never: a vendor's own API without a first-party EU region and ZDR;
  │               any Chinese-origin vendor's own API; any "trains on data" tier.
  └─ No (public or internal low-risk) → vendor API also allowed, after due diligence.

STEP 2 [Rec]: Mid-tier primary and fallback (two different vendors, same region)
  Primary cloud?
  ├─ Azure  → primary: GPT-6.1 Sol (Foundry EU Data Zone)
  │           fallback: Mistral Medium 3.5 (Foundry or EU endpoint)
  │           (EU processing for Claude on Foundry is not verified; its Azure-hosted
  │            deployment is still "In-Process Q4 2026" for certification)
  ├─ AWS    → primary: Claude Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6 tier on Bedrock in an EU region
  │           (confirm per-model regional availability; Astra is US-only on Bedrock)
  │           fallback: the other of those two, or Mistral via Bedrock / EU endpoint
  ├─ Google → primary: Gemini 3.8 Flash (EU region, logging/caching off)
  │           fallback: Claude Sonnet 5.5 via Google Cloud EU (GPT-6 is not on Google Cloud)
  │           independent alternative: Mistral on Google Cloud (confirm model and region)
  └─ Multi-cloud or none → primary: OpenAI EU endpoint (ZDR) or Mistral EU endpoint
              fallback: the other; add a hyperscaler route when available
  Independent alternatives to any Claude choice (Anthropic Strategic, conditional, CP4-1):
  GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Mistral Medium 3.5. Never Claude as the only qualified vendor.

STEP 3 [Rec]: Small and open-weight tiers
  High-volume classification / extraction / routing?
    → small tier of the primary vendor (Luna, Haiku 5.5, Flash-Lite) or self-hosted Gemma 4
  Data must never leave the estate, or air-gap required?
    → self-hosted: Gemma 4 (Apache 2.0), Mistral Medium 3.5 / Large 3, gpt-oss-120b
    → Chinese-origin weights (DeepSeek MIT, Qwen3.8-27B, GLM-5.3-Flash) only if the
      firm's sovereignty policy explicitly allows them, never with tool access,
      and GLM only after sanctions review
  Frontier tier (Astra, Fable 5.1, Argon)?
    → only when evaluation shows the mid tier fails a named use case; keep disabled otherwise

STEP 4 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Second vendor qualified on the same L9 suite?  Failover drill passed?
  Every pinned model's retirement date > re-qualification lead time?
  Contract, DPA, register-of-information / MTP entry and exit plan done for each vendor?
```

### 1.10 Lock-in classification

| Element | Classification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Rationale | Abstraction to use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|---|
| A single proprietary frontier vendor for an important business service | **Unacceptable** | Suspension, retirement, legal or residency events at one vendor stop the service; the Fable 5 suspension [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S004: Claude Fable - Anthropic <https://www.anthropic.com/claude/fable> accessed 2026-10-08] and short Gemini Flash lifetimes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S003: Gemini 3.7 Flash model page and related lifecycle pages (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/gemini/3-7-flash> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] show the risk is real | Two-vendor mid tier through the gateway; exit plan tested |
| Proprietary frontier API, consumed through a gateway with a qualified second vendor | **Manageable** | Switching cost is re-qualification, not re-engineering, if prompts and schemas are neutral | OpenAI-shaped internal contract at C1; prompts in Git (C5); L9 suite per use case |
| Vendor-specific features (prompt caching formats, vendor tool-use extensions, vendor agent runtimes) | **Manageable, if wrapped** | Each vendor's features differ; using them directly embeds the vendor | Use only behind adapters; keep a feature-free fallback path |
| Hyperscaler route for models | **Manageable** | Concentrates on a designated CTP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; region and model availability differ per cloud | Second route (vendor EU endpoint or self-host) for important services |
| Open weights under Apache 2.0 or MIT | **Acceptable** | The firm holds the weights and can keep running them | Internal model registry with hash pinning (C7) |
| Open weights under custom licences with thresholds (Kimi K3, Qwen3.8 flagship, GLM-5.3, Llama 4, Medium 3.5) | **Manageable** | Thresholds rarely bind an asset manager's internal use but must be read [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Legal review recorded in the inventory |
| Chinese-origin vendor's own hosted API | **Unacceptable for client data** | Jurisdiction, unverified certifications and, for DeepSeek, an unremediated GDPR limitation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S062: DeepSeek Privacy Policy; DeepSeek Open Platform Privacy Policy and Terms of Service <https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A5-S048: Provvedimento del 30 gennaio 2025 (10098477) (and press releases 10097450, 10096856) (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali (Italy)) <https://www.garanteprivacy.it/web/guest/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/10098477> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] | Not used; weights only where policy allows |
| Training-on-data tiers (e.g. Meta contributor tier) | **Unacceptable** | Data-use condition, not a price [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S019: Meta Connect 2026: The end-to-end recap (with research.meta.ai 'Introducing Muse Spark 1.3') <https://developers.meta.com/blog/meta-connect-recap/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] | Gateway deny-list by model ID |

### 1.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk.**
- *Is an LLM a "model"?* PRA SS1/23 applies to all models used to inform business decisions, in-house or vendor, is technology-agnostic, and lists explainability and transparency as complexity factors for AI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S037: Bank of England/PRA letter to DSIT and HMT on AI (2024) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/letter/2024/dsit-hmt-letter.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. It applies directly to banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. BoE AI Consortium minutes record that GenAI systems are often classified as high risk under SS1/23 frameworks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S037: Bank of England/PRA letter to DSIT and HMT on AI (2024) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/letter/2024/dsit-hmt-letter.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Consequence for L1.* A foundation model used in a business process should be inventoried as a vendor model with its version, route and region, validated for its intended use, and monitored (SS1/23 Principles 1, 4 and 5) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. For an FCA solo-regulated manager SS1/23 is not binding but is the natural benchmark [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and expressly places generative and agentic AI outside its scope; for those, the firm's own risk-management practices should determine governance [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S049: Supervisory Letter SR 26-2 on Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management -- April 17, 2026 (with SR2602a1 attachment, OCC Bulletin 2026-13a) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The agencies' planned AI request for information had not been published by 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. US bank-owned managers therefore have no US supervisory model-risk standard for LLMs, and should govern them to SS1/23 quality anyway [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Validation independence.* Validation of a vendor model must not rely solely on the vendor's own evaluations or tooling; vendor benchmarks are not evidence [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Version changes are model changes.* Every model-version change (including a forced retirement) is a change requiring re-validation on the L9 suite; notice periods range from about 2 weeks for previews to at least 6 months for GA models at OpenAI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-L1-S001: Deprecations (OpenAI API docs) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**EU AI Act.**
- *Providers versus deployers.* GPAI obligations (technical documentation, downstream information, copyright policy, training-content summary; extra duties for systemic-risk models) fall on the model providers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S013: AI literacy: the Digital Omnibus rewrites Article 4 of the AI Act (with dastra.eu, vaia.be commentary) (Law & Technology / independent commentary) <https://lawandtechnology.eu/en/ai-literacy-digital-omnibus-article-4-ai-act/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The Commission's enforcement powers over GPAI apply from 2 August 2026, and models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 must comply by 2 August 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *The firm is normally a deployer.* Its duties are AI literacy, Article 50 transparency where relevant and, for any Annex III high-risk use, the Article 26 deployer duties from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Fine-tuning or repurposing a model into a high-risk purpose can make the firm a provider under Article 25 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Due-diligence data point.* The GPAI Code of Practice signatories include Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Mistral AI and OpenAI; xAI signed only the Safety and Security chapter [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EU-GPAI-COP: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (AI Act Articles 53 and 55) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S015: The General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (contents and signatory list) (European Commission) <https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/contents-code-gpai> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The status of Meta, DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot and Z.ai was not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Record each vendor's status and request its Model Documentation Form [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**DORA, the UK CTP regime and outsourcing.**
- *Designations.* DORA's first CTPP list (18 November 2025) includes AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft and no AI model provider [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S051: European Supervisory Authorities designate critical ICT third-party providers under DORA (EBA/EIOPA/ESMA press release; with Morgan Lewis, TLT) (EBA / EIOPA / ESMA) <https://www.eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/european-supervisory-authorities-designate-critical-ict-third-party-providers-under-digital> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The UK designated AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft and Oracle as CTPs with effect from 13 July 2026, and no model vendor [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S052: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (with Lewis Silkin, National Law Review, Library of Congress) (UK Government (legislation.gov.uk)) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *Consequence.* A model consumed through a hyperscaler sits under a designated, directly overseen provider; a model consumed through the vendor's own API does not, which leaves more of the oversight burden on the firm [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. ### 1.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from L1 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary (allocation, selection, currency and benchmark-relative return) for a generic multi-asset fund. A portfolio manager approves every draft. From this layer it needs four model roles, each pinned, each routed by the gateway, and each with a documented alternative:

| Role | What it does | Requirements | Example configurations (choose by primary cloud) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Primary drafting model** (mid tier) | Writes the narrative from the attribution engine's figures and retrieved house style | In-region (UK/EU), in-tenant, no training, ZDR or short retention; strong instruction following; pinned version with ≥ 6 months' runway | Azure: GPT-6.1 Sol in a Foundry EU Data Zone. AWS: Claude Sonnet 5.5 via a Bedrock EU regional endpoint. Google Cloud: Gemini 3.8 Flash in an EU region |
| **Fallback drafting model** (different vendor) | Takes over on outage, suspension or retirement | Same region and data terms; passed the same evaluation suite in the last quarter | Azure: Mistral Medium 3.5. AWS: a GPT-6 tier on Bedrock (confirm EU availability) or Mistral. Google Cloud: Claude Sonnet 5.5 via Google Cloud EU, or Mistral on Google Cloud as the independent alternative (confirm model and region) |
| **Small classifier** | Classifies reviewer edits, tags commentary sections, routes requests | Cheap, fast, deterministic settings; no client identifiers | GPT-6 Luna, Claude Haiku 5.5 or Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite in-region; or self-hosted Gemma 4 E4B |
| **Self-hosted open-weight model** | Any step that touches unmasked client or holdings data (e.g. checking a draft against client-specific mandate wording) | Runs in the firm's estate; Apache 2.0 or MIT; hash-pinned | Gemma 4 31B or Mistral Medium 3.5 on the firm's GPUs via L2 |

A Claude model appears as the AWS primary, the Google Cloud fallback and one small-classifier option; in each cell an independent alternative from another vendor is named alongside it (GPT-6 or Mistral on AWS, Mistral on Google Cloud, Luna, Flash-Lite or Gemma 4 for classification) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Flow.** The attribution engine produces the figures through a read-only tool (L4). The drafting model receives those figures as structured input, with client identifiers masked (C3), and writes prose around them. The L9 numeric-faithfulness check compares every figure, sign and direction word in the draft with the engine's output. On a mismatch the draft fails, whatever the model tier [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the model must never do [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- generate, round, recompute or "correct" any number; every figure comes from the attribution engine and is traceable
- present its own inference (e.g. a market explanation) as source data; inference must be distinguishable and grounded in approved sources
- be swapped for another model or version without the regression suite passing
- run on an alias ("latest") or a preview model
- receive unmasked client identifiers through any external route
- be a Chinese-origin vendor's hosted API, a training-on-data tier, or a gated frontier tier that nobody approved for this use

**Evidence per commentary (to C8).** Model ID and version, route and region, fallback used (yes or no), prompt and template version, token counts and cost, evaluation results, and approver [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hypothesis note.** No hypothesis (H1–H8) is assigned to L1. The layer's findings bear on **H1** (promote the gateway to a control-plane component): a model portfolio with residency routing, version pinning, fallback and deny-lists is unworkable without a firm-owned gateway, which supports H1 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. They also bear on the LinkedIn pair-8 tension, "treat models as a portfolio, not a bet". The counter-argument is that a portfolio multiplies validation and contract work; the answer is to keep the portfolio small (two mid-tier vendors, one small model, one open-weight model) and make the L9 suite do the re-qualification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


# Cross-cutting enterprise controls (C1–C8)


## C1. AI / LLM gateway

> **Executive summary.** The gateway is the single point through which every model call, and now every tool and agent call, leaves an application. It owns provider abstraction, routing and fallback, quotas and budgets, caching, policy enforcement and the request log [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The original graphic has no gateway. Its only nod to one is OpenRouter in L2, a hosted router that now carries budgets, allowlists, zero-data-retention and regional routing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S111: OpenRouter Docs: Guardrails <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/guardrails.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Four things have changed since then. First, the gateways now carry three kinds of traffic: LiteLLM, Kong, Azure API Management, Apigee and agentgateway all govern LLM, MCP and A2A traffic [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S061: agentgateway README (GitHub) (agentgateway project (Linux Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Second, ownership is moving towards security vendors: Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition of Portkey on 29 May 2026 and sells it as Prisma AIRS AI Gateway [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S011: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Portkey to Secure AI Agents (and 30 Apr 2026 announcement) <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2026/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-portkey-to-secure-ai-agents> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S012: Palo Alto Networks Inc - Form 10-K - FY2026 (fiscal year ended 31 July 2026) (US SEC EDGAR / Palo Alto Networks) <https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001327567/000132756726000023/panw-20260731.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S025: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Portkey to Secure AI Agents (with PANW FY2026 10-K and 10-Q, SDxCentral) <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2026/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-portkey-to-secure-ai-agents> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Third, the gateway has proved to be an attack target in its own right: malicious LiteLLM 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published to PyPI on 24 March 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S008: Security Update: Suspected Supply Chain Incident (and Security Townhall Updates) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S027: LiteLLM PyPI supply chain attack (with NetSPI, Comet, Snyk/Datadog reporting) (FutureSearch) <https://futuresearch.ai/blog/litellm-pypi-supply-chain-attack/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Fourth, the hyperscaler offerings are real but uneven: the Azure API Management AI Gateway tier is preview with no SLA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S020: Azure API Management AI gateway docs and Tech Community announcements (AI Gateway tier preview; Build 2026 updates) (Microsoft) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/ai-gateway-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S073: AI Gateway tier (preview) overview - Azure API Management (with Tech Community 'AI Gateway tier of API Management now in public preview') (Microsoft) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/ai-gateway-overview> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and no AWS product called "AI gateway" was found: AWS offers an MCP gateway with new inference targets and a LiteLLM-based reference pattern instead [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S022: Guidance for Multi-Provider Generative AI Gateway on AWS; Implementing resilience patterns with Amazon Bedrock and LLM gateway (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/solutions/guidance/multi-provider-generative-ai-gateway-on-aws/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S105: AgentCore Gateway: Inference targets; Inference connector/provider targets; Add rate limits to a gateway (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-targets-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. **Recommendation:** run one firm-controlled gateway of record for all production LLM and MCP traffic, deployed in-region, failing closed, with pinned and signed builds. Choose LiteLLM (hardened and Enterprise-licensed), Kong, Apigee or the GA AI gateway policies in Azure API Management according to your existing API and cloud estate, and keep the model-switch route tested, because the gateway is what makes an exit plan executable [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C1.1 Responsibility

**The problem this control owns.** The gateway decides, for every outbound AI request, who may make it, which model or tool receives it, in which region, at what cost ceiling, under which policies, and what record is kept [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It breaks down into seven jobs:

- **Provider abstraction.** One API (in practice the OpenAI-compatible format) in front of many providers, so applications do not hold provider SDKs or keys [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S049: Portkey AI Gateway README (GitHub) (Portkey (Palo Alto Networks)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Portkey-AI/gateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S063: Envoy AI Gateway / Agent Router README (GitHub) (Envoy AI Gateway project (Agentic AI Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Routing, fallback and load balancing.** Choose a model per route, retry, fail over and balance across deployments [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S049: Portkey AI Gateway README (GitHub) (Portkey (Palo Alto Networks)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Portkey-AI/gateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Quotas, rate limits and budgets.** Tokens per minute, requests per minute and spend per key, team, user or customer [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S020: Azure API Management AI gateway docs and Tech Community announcements (AI Gateway tier preview; Build 2026 updates) (Microsoft) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/ai-gateway-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S105: AgentCore Gateway: Inference targets; Inference connector/provider targets; Add rate limits to a gateway (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-targets-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Caching.** Exact and semantic response caching, which saves cost but is also a confidentiality and correctness risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S025: Apigee release notes (all; hybrid) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Policy enforcement.** Invoke guardrails (C2), DLP (C3) and authorisation (C4) inline, before and after the model call [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S017: Kong AI Gateway changelog; Kong Gateway changelog; AI Proxy Advanced plugin docs (Kong Inc.) <https://developer.konghq.com/ai-gateway/changelog/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Logging and observability.** One record per request with caller, route, model, tokens, cost, latency, policy outcomes and errors, exported to L9 and C8 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tool and agent traffic.** MCP tool federation and A2A agent calls, with per-caller tool exposure [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S061: agentgateway README (GitHub) (agentgateway project (Linux Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Hand-offs.** Above the gateway sit the applications and agent workflows (L3), which call one endpoint with a workload identity from C4 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Below it sit the model endpoints (L1 vendors, L2 hosted or self-served models), MCP tool servers (L4) and other agents [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Alongside it: C2 and C3 supply detectors it calls inline; C4 supplies identity and tool-call policy; C5 holds the routing configuration under change control; C6 consumes its cost records; L9 and C8 consume its logs as evidence; C7 owns its supply-chain assurance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the control does not own.** It does not decide whether a workflow should be autonomous (L3), and it does not validate output quality (L9). A gateway that blocks a harmful string cannot tell whether an attribution figure is right [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C1.2 Why it matters

When the gateway is missing or badly designed, three things fail together [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Exit becomes theoretical.** Provider SDKs and keys spread through application code, so switching model means a programme of code changes. The exit plan that SS2/21 expects to be documented and tested [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] cannot be executed in the time a stressed exit allows [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Cost and residency are invisible.** Without per-request attribution nobody can say what a task costs or where the data went [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **The control becomes the risk.** A gateway holds every provider credential and sees every prompt. The March 2026 LiteLLM incident shows that a gateway is a high-value supply-chain target: release credentials were stolen through a compromised CI scanner and two malicious versions were published [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S008: Security Update: Suspected Supply Chain Incident (and Security Townhall Updates) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S010: Your AI Gateway Was a Backdoor: Inside the LiteLLM Supply Chain Compromise (Trend Micro Research) <https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/c/inside-litellm-supply-chain-compromise.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A central component that fails open, or is itself compromised, turns one weakness into an estate-wide one [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A fund-reporting team routes commentary drafting through a self-hosted gateway. The primary model is pinned to an EU region, and an engineer adds a second provider to the fallback list during a month-end capacity problem without checking where it processes data. Budgets are configured, but the gateway's spend database is unavailable after a restart, and the budget check silently passes. The team also turns on semantic caching to cut cost. Next month-end the EU endpoint is rate-limited; the gateway fails over to the US-hosted fallback for about a day; and two commentaries for similar funds receive a cached paragraph describing the wrong currency effect. Nothing alerts: requests succeeded, latency was normal and the guardrails passed. The data-protection team finds the out-of-region processing in a quarterly log review; the cached paragraph is caught at PM review only because the PM remembered the other fund. Three controls would have prevented it: a residency-constrained fallback list that fails closed, budget enforcement that fails closed, and no semantic cache on client-specific routes. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident. (Each of its mechanisms is documented: LiteLLM's `max_budget` fails open without a database, and its docs warn that semantic caching "goes badly wrong on agentic traffic" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].)

### C1.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gateway coverage | Share of production LLM, MCP and A2A calls that pass through the gateway | 100% in scope; any direct provider key in an application is a defect | Provider usage reports reconciled with gateway logs; secret scanning for provider keys |
| Availability | Gateway uptime for gated workflows | At least that of the business service it supports (e.g. ≥99.95%) | Synthetic probes per route and region |
| Added latency | p95 gateway overhead excluding model time | Tens of milliseconds without inline guards; budget per guard separately | Gateway spans vs upstream spans |
| Residency conformance | Requests processed outside the approved region for the route | 0; out-of-region fallback is a blocking defect | Route policy plus provider region in each log record |
| Qualified fallback | Fallback events landing on a model that passed the route's regression suite | 100% | Fallback log joined to L9 qualification register |
| Cost attribution coverage | Requests carrying workflow, team and business-object tags | ≥99% | Gateway log completeness check; C6 reconciliation to invoices |
| Budget enforcement | Budget breaches that were not blocked or alerted | 0; fail closed on loss of the spend store | Breach log; chaos test of the spend store |
| Log completeness | Gateway records reconciled with L9 traces and provider usage | ≥99.9% | Daily three-way reconciliation |
| Time to switch provider | Time to move a route to a pre-qualified alternative by configuration | Hours, not weeks; tested at least annually | Exit drill evidence (C8) |
| Credential exposure | Provider keys held outside the gateway's secret store | 0 | Secret scanning; vault inventory (C7) |
| Supply-chain hygiene | Gateway builds deployed from pinned, verified artefacts | 100% | Image signature verification at admission; package hash pinning |

### C1.4 How it works

A request passes through five stages [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

1. **Authenticate and identify.** The caller presents a workload identity or virtual key. LiteLLM uses virtual keys and JWT/OIDC [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; AgentCore Gateway accepts IAM or custom JWT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S074: AWS API model: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore control plane (botocore service-2.json) (Amazon Web Services (via boto/botocore)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boto/botocore/develop/botocore/data/bedrock-agentcore-control/2023-06-05/service-2.json> accessed 2026-10-07]; Azure's AI Gateway tier requires Entra sign-in [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S020: Azure API Management AI gateway docs and Tech Community announcements (AI Gateway tier preview; Build 2026 updates) (Microsoft) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/ai-gateway-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
2. **Apply pre-call policy.** Token and request limits per counter key (Azure's `llm-token-limit` is GA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S020: Azure API Management AI gateway docs and Tech Community announcements (AI Gateway tier preview; Build 2026 updates) (Microsoft) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/ai-gateway-overview> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; AgentCore estimates tokens up front and reconciles them with provider usage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S105: AgentCore Gateway: Inference targets; Inference connector/provider targets; Add rate limits to a gateway (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-targets-inference.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]), budgets, and inline guards. LiteLLM runs guardrails pre-call, during the call or post-call across chat, embeddings, MCP and A2A routes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
3. **Route.** Pick the model or tool by route rules, then retry, load-balance or fail over. Apigee adds circuit breaking across clouds [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07]; Agent Router uses a two-tier design with a Tier One gateway for auth, top-level routing and global rate limits [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S063: Envoy AI Gateway / Agent Router README (GitHub) (Envoy AI Gateway project (Agentic AI Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
4. **Apply post-call policy.** Output guards (C2), DLP (C3), cache write.
5. **Record.** Emit the request record and spans (tokens, cost, latency, policy outcomes) to the firm's collector, and cost records to C6. OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions now cover client inference, agents, tool execution and MCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S061: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (repository docs index) (OpenTelemetry (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/main/docs/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07], so the gateway can emit the same schema as the rest of the stack [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

For MCP the gateway becomes a tool federator. It presents one MCP endpoint to agents and exposes only the tools each caller is allowed. Kong does this with MCP Server Bundling and per-caller tool exposure [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; AgentCore Policy removes denied tools from `tools/list` and is deny-by-default for tool calls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The MCP 2026-07-28 authorisation spec forbids token passthrough and requires audience validation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], so a gateway that fronts MCP servers must mint or exchange tokens per upstream server rather than forward the client's token [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
 L3 workflow / agent (workload identity from C4)
          │  one OpenAI-compatible endpoint  +  one MCP endpoint
          ▼
 ┌──────────────────────── C1 gateway (firm-controlled, in-region) ─────────────────────────┐
 │ authN/Z ─► limits & budgets ─► pre-call guards (C2, C3) ─► route/fallback ─► post-call guards │
 │   (fail closed)    (fail closed)      (inline, time-boxed)     (residency-   (C2, C3)          │
 │                                                                 constrained)                   │
 │   secrets (C7 vault) · routing config (C5, change-controlled) · cache (off on client routes) │
 └───────────┬───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
             ▼                           ▼                              ▼
   model endpoints (L1/L2)      MCP tool servers (L4)            A2A agents
   primary + qualified          read-only tools, per-caller
   fallback, same region        token exchange (C4)
             │
             └──► request records + OTel spans ──► collector ──► L9 platform, C6 FinOps, C8 evidence
```

**Two placements.** A centralised gateway gives one policy point and one log, but is a shared single point of failure and a concentration of credentials [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A sidecar or per-domain gateway limits blast radius but multiplies configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. For an asset manager the practical answer is one logical gateway with at least two independent deployments (per region or per criticality tier) sharing configuration from C5 [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C1.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**

- Treat the gateway as Tier-1 security infrastructure: it holds every provider credential and sees every prompt [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Install from pinned, verified artefacts. LiteLLM's images on GHCR are cosign-signed from v1.83.0 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S051: LiteLLM README (GitHub) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S009: v1.83.0 - Official Release (Post Supply Chain Incident) (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/v1.83.0/v1-83-0> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; verify signatures at admission and mirror packages internally [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Configure fail-closed behaviour explicitly. LiteLLM limits are unset by default, `max_budget` fails open without a database, prompt-injection guardrails are off by default, and the proxy admin key bypasses budget checks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Its A2A agents are open to all callers until an allowlist is defined [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Set allowlists before enabling A2A [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Never forward a caller's token to an upstream MCP server; exchange it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Treat the semantic cache as attack surface and a confidentiality boundary. Apigee shipped an SSRF fix in its semantic-cache lookup on 30 September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S025: Apigee release notes (all; hybrid) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Partition caches by tenant and turn them off for client-specific routes [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and resilience**

- The gateway is on the critical path of every AI-dependent service. Run at least two independent deployments and decide in advance whether a gateway outage degrades to "no AI" (preferred for regulated outputs) or to a direct path (never, for client data) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Make fallback lists residency-aware and qualification-aware. A fallback model must be in the same approved region and must have passed the route's L9 regression suite [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. OpenRouter's in-region routing shows the right behaviour: it fails rather than falling back out of region [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A4-S109: OpenRouter Docs: In-Region Routing (EU/US) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenRouterTeam/docs/main/guides/features/in-region-routing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A4-S150: In-Region Routing: keep your data in the US or EU (OpenRouter blog) and OpenRouter Pricing/Enterprise pages <https://openrouter.ai/blog/announcements/us-in-region-routing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Multi-instance rate limits and budgets need shared state (database plus Redis or Valkey in LiteLLM's case) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; test what happens when that state is lost [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance**

- Routing rules, model allowlists and budgets are production configuration. Keep them in C5 under change control with approval for any change to a regulated route [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Log policy decisions as well as requests: AgentCore Policy logs decisions to CloudWatch [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; LiteLLM Enterprise logs changes to keys, teams, users and models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S007: LiteLLM pricing / Enterprise / Audit Logs docs (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://www.litellm.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Observability and cost**

- Emit OTel GenAI spans and reconcile request counts with L9 traces and provider invoices [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Tag every request with workflow, team and business object so C6 can attribute cost per task [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S010: litellm on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / BerriAI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/json> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Watch log costs: Cloudflare changed AI Gateway log pricing for gateways created from 24 September 2026 and announced per-GB pricing from 1 December 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S052: Cloudflare AI Gateway docs: Pricing (source mdx) (Cloudflare, Inc.) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-docs/production/src/content/docs/ai-gateway/reference/pricing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S074: Pricing - Cloudflare AI Gateway docs (with AI Gateway changelog 2026-09-01; Cloudflare observability blog) <https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/reference/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Portability**

- Standardise applications on the OpenAI-compatible request format and one MCP endpoint, and keep provider-specific features behind route configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Policies written in a proprietary dialect (APIM XML, Apigee policies) are part of the exit cost [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07]; document their intent so they can be re-expressed [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** one gateway of record with two deployments; residency-constrained, qualification-checked fallback; fail-closed budgets; per-caller MCP tool exposure with token exchange; gateway as the only holder of provider keys; routing config in Git; three-way reconciliation of gateway, trace and invoice.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** provider SDKs and keys in application code; "fallback to anything available"; semantic cache across tenants or clients; a SaaS gateway in the data path for client data without verified log residency; unpinned `pip install` of the gateway; one gateway instance as an unmonitored single point of failure; guardrails configured but off by default; a "god gateway" that also hosts agent logic.

### C1.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Provider breadth; routing, fallback, load balancing, circuit breaking; token-aware limits and budgets per key/team/user; semantic cache with partitioning; inline guard hooks before and after the call; MCP federation with per-caller tool exposure and token exchange; A2A; OTel output |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC and audit of configuration changes; SCIM; admin API; SLA; multi-team tenancy; which of these are licence-gated |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 naming the gateway; CMK; supply-chain hygiene (signed images, release process) for self-hosted; fail-closed defaults |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Self-hosted or customer-run data plane so prompts and logs stay in region; hybrid; multi-region |
| Ecosystem (5%) | OpenAI-compatible API, MCP and A2A support, OTel export, integration with the firm's API gateway |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | GA status of the AI-specific features (several are preview); configuration-model stability; incident history |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Licence model (per capacity vs per call vs fee on spend); log pricing; operations burden (database, Redis) |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Open-source core; policy dialect; ownership stability; whether billing runs through the gateway vendor |

**Scoring notes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- *Hyperscaler presumption (CP2 Q1).* Azure APIM, AgentCore Gateway and Apigee score 4 on enterprise readiness: platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service.
- *NPV caps and rule 7.* Cloudflare's cap was lifted to 3 on its verified identity-based controls. At the CP3 review two scores rose to 4, because rule 7 gives 4 for all three of SSO, RBAC and audit logs plus SCIM, an SLA or an admin API (as for Firecrawl in L8 and LiteLLM here): Kong, now that Konnect SSO and teams-based roles are verified [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-REVA-S004: Konnect platform authentication and authorization (Kong Inc.) <https://developer.konghq.com/konnect-platform/authentication/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] alongside its audit logs and 99.99% SLA; and Portkey, whose SSO, SCIM, roles and audit logs the writer evidenced (B-C1-S001 to S003). Portkey's condition is stated: much of the evidence is vendor pages, and post-acquisition terms are not public.
- *Scope rule (CP2 Q4).* Azure APIM's ISO 27001 and SOC 2 are platform-level without naming the service, but FedRAMP High names it, so security is 4. Portkey's certification tier coverage is unclear, so 3. AgentCore is held at 4 rather than 5 because its ISO evidence is a partly garbled search extract and FedRAMP status conflicts.
- *Rule 2 (self-hosted open source).* LiteLLM, agentgateway and Agent Router are scored as software you run. LiteLLM and agentgateway have commercial support, so the cap at 4 does not bind; agentgateway's and Agent Router's security is 2 because their release hygiene is not verified.
- *Rule 3 (ownership change).* Portkey's lock-in is reduced by 1 (MIT core, but not neutral governance).
- *Strategic despite weaknesses.* LiteLLM is Strategic with security and maturity at 3 because of the March 2026 compromise; the condition is stated in its deep dive. Kong (cost 2) and Apigee (lock-in 2) are Strategic only where they are already the API standard.
- *Hyperscaler lead services (CP3 Q2, rubric rule 10).* Azure APIM's AI gateway (FS 3.25) and AWS AgentCore Gateway (FS 3.00) are now Strategic, conditional: "where Azure (or AWS) is your primary cloud", as each cloud's lead service in this category with no criterion at 1. Apigee's condition was reworded to match. No criterion scores changed, and security stays at 4 under rule 8. The conditions carry the weaknesses: APIM on GA policies only, not the preview tier; AgentCore for tool traffic only until its inference targets are GA (maturity 2).
- *Calibration.* Every product scores 2 or below on at least one criterion except LiteLLM and Portkey, whose weakest points (security and maturity at 3) are stated.

### C1.9 Decision tree

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): one gateway of record for ALL production LLM and MCP traffic;
provider keys live only in the gateway's vault (C7); routing config in Git under C5;
budgets and limits fail closed; fallback lists are residency- and qualification-checked.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Which gateway of record?
  Does the gateway see client or personal data that must stay in-estate or in UK/EU?
  ├─ Yes → Do you already run an enterprise API gateway?
  │        ├─ Kong        → Kong AI Gateway, hybrid mode (customer data plane)
  │        ├─ Apigee      → Apigee hybrid in a UK/EU region
  │        ├─ Azure APIM  → APIM AI policies in existing GA tiers (not the preview tier)
  │        └─ None / mixed→ LiteLLM self-hosted + Enterprise licence, pinned and signed
  │                         (alt: agentgateway + Solo Enterprise if MCP/A2A-led and Kubernetes-native)
  └─ No  → Managed is acceptable: Cloudflare AI Gateway (BYOK) or Portkey SaaS,
           with a documented route back to a self-hosted gateway

STEP 2 [Rec]: Tool and agent traffic
  Agents on AWS with tools behind AgentCore? → AgentCore Gateway for MCP + AgentCore Policy;
                                                model traffic stays on the Step 1 gateway
  Envoy Gateway already your platform?       → Agent Router for in-cluster routing, behind Step 1
  Otherwise                                  → the Step 1 gateway's MCP endpoint, with
                                                per-caller tool exposure and token exchange

STEP 3 [Rec]: Security-vendor bundle?
  Already standardised on Prisma AIRS?  → Portkey/Prisma AIRS AI Gateway is a reasonable choice,
                                          but keep the open-source gateway config as the exit route

STEP 4 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Two independent deployments? Fail-closed tested (spend store down, guard timeout)?
  Fallback model qualified (L9) and in the same region? Semantic cache off on client routes?
  Gateway logs retained per records policy (≥ 6 months where AI Act Art. 26 applies) and in region?
  Exit drill: route switched to the alternative provider by configuration only?
```

|---|---|---|---|
| Application-to-gateway API | **Acceptable** on the OpenAI-compatible format | Every product here exposes or accepts it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S049: Portkey AI Gateway README (GitHub) (Portkey (Palo Alto Networks)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Portkey-AI/gateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S061: agentgateway README (GitHub) (agentgateway project (Linux Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentgateway/agentgateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S063: Envoy AI Gateway / Agent Router README (GitHub) (Envoy AI Gateway project (Agentic AI Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/envoyproxy/ai-gateway/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] | One client library; no provider SDKs in application code |
