## C3. DLP and PII protection

> **Executive summary.** This control finds, classifies and transforms sensitive data wherever it can enter or leave a GenAI system: at ingestion, in prompts, in tool results, in model outputs, in memory and in traces [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The original graphic has no such control; it shows ingestion, memory, retrieval and evaluation boxes that each copy data, and none of them says what happens to client identifiers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Four things have changed in the candidate products. Presidio is no longer a Microsoft project: it is community-governed under the "Data Privacy Stack" organisation, MIT-licensed, and states that it is "not owned or operated by a commercial entity" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S040: Presidio has transitioned to a community-owned project (project_transition.md) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/docs/project_transition.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S030: Presidio has transitioned to a community-owned project (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/docs/project_transition.md> accessed 2026-10-08]. Microsoft folded "DSPM for AI" into a unified Purview Data Security Posture Management, generally available in May 2026, which needs Microsoft 365 E5 or the Purview Suite [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S090: What's new in Microsoft Purview <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/whats-new> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S091: Considerations for deploying Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI; Get started with DSPM (classic); Purview for Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dspm-for-ai-considerations> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S036: What's new in Microsoft Purview (with DSPM task mapping page; Tech Community 'Beyond Visibility: the new Microsoft Purview DSPM experience') <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/whats-new> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Google's Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP) is positioned for GenAI prompts and responses and underpins Model Armor's sensitive-data screening [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S067: Model Armor product page (incl. pricing) (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/model-armor> accessed 2026-10-07]. Protegrity's AI Team Edition is still documented as Tech Preview and deploys on AWS only, and Skyflow sells an "LLM Privacy Vault" with EU vaults, with no funding round verified after March 2024 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S093: Protegrity AI Team Edition to Secure Agentic Workflows; AI Team Edition docs (Tech Preview); Protegrity Expands Team (April 2026) <https://www.protegrity.com/news/protegrity-ai-team-edition-to-secure-agentic-workflows> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S095: Skyflow GDPR Compliance; Data Privacy Vault; LLM Privacy Vault; SOC 2 solution pages; Why Skyflow (docs) <https://www.skyflow.com/gdpr-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S096: Skyflow Raises $30 Million led by Khosla Ventures for Data Privacy in AI and Global Data Residency (Business Wire press release) (Skyflow (via Business Wire)) <https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240328765469/en/Skyflow-Raises-$30-Million-led-by-Khosla-Ventures-for-Data-Privacy-in-AI-and-Global-Data-Residency> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Meanwhile, DLP has started to appear inside gateways and guardrails: Cloudflare AI Gateway, Kong AI Gateway, Bedrock Guardrails and Model Armor all inspect prompts or responses for sensitive data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S052: Cloudflare AI Gateway docs: Pricing (source mdx) (Cloudflare, Inc.) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cloudflare/cloudflare-docs/production/src/content/docs/ai-gateway/reference/pricing.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S072: AWS API model: Amazon Bedrock control plane (botocore service-2.json) - guardrail shapes (Amazon Web Services (via boto/botocore)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/boto/botocore/develop/botocore/data/bedrock/2023-04-20/service-2.json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S067: Model Armor product page (incl. pricing) (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/model-armor> accessed 2026-10-07]. **Recommendation:** build one firm-owned privacy service (detect, transform and, under policy, re-identify) and call it from every enforcement point, rather than buying a different detector per layer. Use Presidio as the in-estate detection engine, with Google Sensitive Data Protection as the managed engine in a Google Cloud estate. Add a vault or tokenisation platform (Protegrity, Skyflow) only where reversible pseudonymisation at scale is required, and use Purview DSPM for posture over Microsoft 365 Copilot and SaaS AI apps in a Microsoft estate [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C3.1 Responsibility

**The problem this control owns.** It ensures that personal data and confidential business data reach a model, a store or a third party only in the form that the firm's policy allows for that destination [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. This breaks down into five jobs:

- **Classification.** Knowing which sources, documents and fields are sensitive, and how sensitive, before they are used [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Discovery and profiling across data stores is a product feature of Sensitive Data Protection and Purview DSPM [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S091: Considerations for deploying Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI; Get started with DSPM (classic); Purview for Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dspm-for-ai-considerations> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Detection.** Finding sensitive entities in free text, images and structured data at run time [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Presidio uses NER, regular expressions, rules and checksums with context [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S068: Presidio README (GitHub, data-privacy-stack) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/README.MD> accessed 2026-10-07]. Sensitive Data Protection has more than 200 predefined detectors [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Transformation.** Redacting, masking, generalising or tokenising the entity so that the downstream step still works [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Sensitive Data Protection offers masking, tokenisation and bucketing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07]. Protegrity and Skyflow offer policy-based protect/unprotect and vault tokenisation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S082: protegrity-developer-python - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/protegrity-developer-python/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Controlled re-identification.** Reversing a token only for an entitled principal and a recorded purpose [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Skyflow detokenises under role-scoped credentials [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07], and Protegrity grants Unprotect per role and data element [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C3-S004: Policy Management and Enterprise Security Administrator (ESA) documentation 10.1 (Protegrity) <https://docs.protegrity.com/10.1/docs/pmg/_print/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- **Residency and evidence.** Keeping each copy of sensitive data in an approved location, and recording what was detected, transformed and re-identified [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Where it sits in the flow.** C3 is not a box; it is a service called at six enforcement points [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

| Point | Layer | What C3 does there [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|
| E1 Ingestion | L8 | Classify and detect before parsing, route by classification, and tag every chunk with classification and PII flags (the L8 metadata envelope) |
| E2 Prompt egress | C1 gateway | Detect and tokenise before any external model call; block what policy forbids |
| E3 Tool results | L4 | Transform tool outputs that carry client data before they enter the context window |
| E4 Model output | C1 / C2 | Detect sensitive data in responses (including leakage from retrieval or memory), re-identify placeholders only for entitled users |
| E5 Memory writes | L5 | Stop raw identifiers being written to long-term memory; keep memory erasable |
| E6 Telemetry | L9 | Redact at the firm-owned OTel Collector before traces leave the estate |

**Hand-offs.** C3 supplies classification policy and detectors to L8 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It shares detectors and test sets with C2 guardrails, which own content safety and injection defence [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It relies on C4 for the identity and entitlement of whoever asks for re-identification, and on C7 (Vault or the firm's KMS) for the keys [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It passes detection and re-identification logs to C8 as evidence and to L9 as metrics [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the control does not own.** It does not decide who may read a source document; that is entitlement filtering in L6 and identity in C4 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It does not decide whether a prompt is malicious; that is C2 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C3.2 Why it matters

GenAI multiplies copies of data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. One analyst question can place the same client identifier in a prompt, a retrieved chunk, a tool result, a model provider's processing region, a trace store, an evaluation dataset and a memory record [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Each copy has its own retention, location and access model, and each becomes a place an erasure request or a breach investigation must reach [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Badly designed, the control fails in four ways [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Detection gaps.** Detectors miss domain identifiers (internal client codes, account numbers, mandate references) because they were tuned for generic PII. Presidio's own README warns that detection is not guaranteed to find all sensitive data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S068: Presidio README (GitHub, data-privacy-stack) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/README.MD> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Single-point placement.** DLP sits only at the gateway, so ingestion, memory and traces carry raw data.
- **Irreversible damage to utility.** Blunt redaction removes the information the model needs ("[REDACTED] outperformed [REDACTED]"), so teams switch the control off.
- **Uncontrolled reversal.** Re-identification is done by whoever holds a key or token map, without a recorded purpose.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A client-service team pilots an assistant that drafts replies to institutional clients. The gateway has a content-safety filter but no DLP. Analysts paste client letters that include the client's legal name, an account number and a named contact. The prompts go to a model API in a region outside the UK and EU, traces go to a SaaS observability tool on its default region, and the agent's memory stores "Client X prefers quarterly calls with Y". Six months later the named contact makes a subject access and erasure request. The firm can delete the CRM record, but it cannot list every trace, memory entry and evaluation case that holds the contact's name, and it cannot say under which transfer mechanism the prompts left the UK. Tokenising identifiers at the gateway and redacting at the collector would have kept the name out of four of the five stores. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### C3.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detection recall per entity class | Share of seeded sensitive entities found, by class (client name, account number, national ID, IBAN, contact details, internal client code) | ≥0.98 for identifiers that must never leave; per class, not averaged | Labelled test corpus in CI, re-run on every detector or model change |
| Detection precision | Share of detections that are true positives | Set per class; low precision drives users to bypass | Same test corpus plus sampled production review |
| Residual sensitive-data rate | Sensitive entities found by a second-pass scanner after transformation | Zero for "must mask" classes | Sampled chunks, prompts and traces scanned by an independent detector |
| Enforcement-point coverage | Share of model calls, ingestion jobs, memory writes and trace exports that pass through the privacy service | 100% for external egress | Gateway and collector logs reconciled to privacy-service logs |
| Untokenised egress | External model calls carrying a "must tokenise" identifier in clear | Zero; any event is an incident | Gateway post-call audit scan |
| Re-identification attribution | Detokenisation events with user, agent, purpose and policy decision recorded | 100% | Privacy-service audit log joined to C4 identity |
| Placeholder integrity | Outputs where a placeholder was altered, invented or dropped by the model | Zero accepted into final text | Deterministic check before re-identification |
| Added latency | p95 latency added by detection and transformation per call | Budget per use case, e.g. under 10% of model latency | Gateway spans |
| Erasure reach | Time and completeness to locate and erase a data subject across stores (memory, traces, eval sets, caches) | Within the statutory deadline, with evidence | Erasure runbook drills |
| Location conformance | Share of processing (model calls, DLP calls, traces) in approved regions | 100% for UK/EU personal data unless a transfer assessment exists | Configuration evidence and gateway routing logs |

### C3.4 How it works

**Mechanics.** Four steps run at each enforcement point, against one policy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

1. **Classify.** Labels come from the source (a sensitivity label, the approved-source register in L8) or from discovery jobs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Sensitive Data Protection profiles BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage and Agent Platform data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07]. Purview DSPM assesses AI interactions, prompts and responses for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Entra-registered AI apps and ChatGPT Enterprise [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S091: Considerations for deploying Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI; Get started with DSPM (classic); Purview for Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dspm-for-ai-considerations> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
2. **Detect.** Pattern, checksum and context rules find structured identifiers; NER or LLM-based recognisers find names and free-text entities [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Presidio supports spaCy, Stanza or Hugging Face NER models and has added LLM-based recognisers (LangExtract) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S005: presidio-analyzer - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/presidio-analyzer/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S040: Presidio has transitioned to a community-owned project (project_transition.md) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/docs/project_transition.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S041: Presidio CHANGELOG.md (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Firm-specific identifiers need custom recognisers in every engine [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
3. **Transform.** The method depends on whether the model needs the value and whether anyone must reverse it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

| Method | Reversible? | Use for [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Product support |
|---|---|---|---|
| Redact (remove) | No | Values the model never needs (national ID, bank details) | All five products [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S068: Presidio README (GitHub, data-privacy-stack) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/README.MD> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S082: protegrity-developer-python - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/protegrity-developer-python/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Mask (partial) | No | Values a human may need to recognise, not the model | SDP masking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07]; Protegrity masking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S082: protegrity-developer-python - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/protegrity-developer-python/json> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Generalise (bucket) | No | Values whose range matters (age band, AUM band) | SDP bucketing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Consistent placeholder or token | Yes, with a key or map | Identities the model must keep distinct ("CLIENT_A" vs "CLIENT_B") and a reviewer must see restored | SDP tokenisation with KMS-wrapped keys [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07; B-C3-S002: De-identify and re-identify sensitive data (Sensitive Data Protection) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspect-sensitive-text-de-identify> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]; Protegrity protect/unprotect [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S082: protegrity-developer-python - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/protegrity-developer-python/json> accessed 2026-10-07]; Skyflow vault tokens with authorised rehydration [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S095: Skyflow GDPR Compliance; Data Privacy Vault; LLM Privacy Vault; SOC 2 solution pages; Why Skyflow (docs) <https://www.skyflow.com/gdpr-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |

4. **Re-identify under policy.** After the model returns, placeholders are checked (none altered, none invented) and restored only for a principal entitled to see them, with the decision logged [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
                    ┌──────────────── Privacy service (firm-owned API) ────────────────┐
                    │ policy (classes → action per destination) · detectors · token keys │
                    │ (KMS/HSM, C7) · audit log (C8) · metrics (L9)                       │
                    └───▲──────────▲───────────▲───────────▲───────────▲──────────▲───────┘
                        │E1        │E2         │E3         │E4         │E5        │E6
  sources ─► L8 ingest ─┘   prompt ─┘  L4 tool ─┘  model   ─┘  L5 memory ─┘  OTel   ─┘
             classify,      at C1      results     output       writes        Collector
             tag chunks     gateway    in context  check +      (no raw IDs)  redaction
                            tokenise               re-identify                 (L9)
                                │
                                ▼
                     external model (L1/L2): sees CLIENT_A, ACCT_7, never the values
```

**Engine options behind the service.** An in-estate library (Presidio) keeps text inside the firm's boundary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S068: Presidio README (GitHub, data-privacy-stack) (Presidio / Data Privacy Stack) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/data-privacy-stack/presidio/main/README.MD> accessed 2026-10-07]. A managed DLP API (Sensitive Data Protection) sends text to the cloud provider's service and is billed per GiB inspected [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S065: Sensitive Data Protection pricing (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. A vault (Skyflow) stores the sensitive values with the vendor and returns tokens [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. These are three different trust models, and the choice is a residency decision before it is a feature decision [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**The LLM-specific twist.** Traditional DLP blocks or masks. GenAI needs transformations that keep the text useful to a model and reversible for the reviewer, and it needs a second inspection of the output, because the model can reproduce sensitive data from retrieval, memory or its own training [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C3.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**

- Run detection for "must not leave" classes inside the estate, before any external call, and fail closed on external egress if the privacy service is unavailable [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Keep token keys and maps in the firm's KMS, HSM or Vault (C7), not only in a vendor's service [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Sensitive Data Protection allows the de-identification key to be wrapped by a Cloud KMS key held globally or in the request region [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C3-S002: De-identify and re-identify sensitive data (Sensitive Data Protection) (Google Cloud) <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspect-sensitive-text-de-identify> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- Treat re-identification as a privileged action with its own entitlement, checked through C4 and logged [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Cover confidential business data, not only personal data. In an asset manager the most sensitive content is often holdings, client mandate terms and unpublished performance, none of which a PII detector looks for [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Treat tokenised data as personal data in the records of processing and transfer assessments, because the firm can reverse it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and resilience**

- Detection adds latency on every call. Measure it per enforcement point and run pattern detectors before NER or LLM recognisers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Managed DLP is priced per volume: content inspection costs US$3.00 per GiB after the first free GiB, falling to US$2.00 above 1 TiB, as of 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S065: Sensitive Data Protection pricing (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Model this against prompt and trace volumes [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Self-hosted detection is horizontally scalable as stateless services, while a vault is a stateful dependency on the critical path [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance**

- Write the policy once (entity classes, action per destination, re-identification rights) and enforce it at all six points [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Version detectors and recognisers like models: test sets, recall per class, and release gates in CI [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Log detections as types, counts and positions, never the values [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Map every store that may hold personal data (prompts, traces, memory, eval sets, caches) into the erasure runbook [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Observability and cost**

- Publish detection counts by class and enforcement point to L9; a sudden fall in detections is as suspicious as a rise [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Purview DSPM requires Microsoft 365 E5 or the Purview Suite; the Business Premium add-on's coverage is reported inconsistently, so confirm licensing before relying on it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S091: Considerations for deploying Microsoft Purview DSPM for AI; Get started with DSPM (classic); Purview for Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dspm-for-ai-considerations> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A6-S092: DSPM for AI with Business Premium Add-On - Microsoft Q&A (Microsoft Q&A (community forum)) <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5813926/dspm-for-ai-with-business-premium-add-on> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Portability**

- Put a thin, firm-owned API in front of the engines (detect, transform, re-identify) so that engines can be swapped or combined [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Prefer reversible methods whose keys the firm holds; a vendor-held token map makes the vendor part of every future read of that data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** privacy service with a firm-owned API; consistent placeholders per conversation so the model can reason about distinct entities; double inspection (prompt and output); collector-side redaction for traces; classification carried in the chunk metadata envelope from L8; second-detector sampling to measure residual leakage.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** DLP only at the gateway; redacting everything so the output is useless; a different detector and policy per product; re-identification keys held by application teams; raw identifiers in eval datasets "because it is internal"; relying on a model provider's zero-retention promise instead of not sending the data.

### C3.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Detection quality for firm-specific and UK/EU identifiers; custom recognisers; modalities (text, images, structured); transformation range (redact, mask, bucket, token); reversible tokenisation; discovery and classification of stores; output inspection |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC over policies and over re-identification, audit of every protect and unprotect, admin APIs; which of these are licence-gated |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in the product's scope; customer-held keys; regional processing; because these products see the most sensitive data in the estate, 5 needs customer-managed keys or equivalent |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | In-estate or self-hosted option for "must not leave" data; region choice for managed services |
| Ecosystem (5%) | Integration with gateways, guardrails, ingestion and the OTel Collector; APIs and SDKs |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | GA status, release cadence, governance or funding stability |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Per-GiB or per-record pricing at prompt and trace volumes; licence prerequisites (E5); operating cost of self-hosting |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Who holds the token map and keys; whether tokenised data can be detokenised in bulk on exit; proprietary labels |

Signed releases are not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

- *Choose when:* you need in-estate detection behind your own privacy service, with custom recognisers for firm identifiers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

Pricing is not published [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Tokenised data depends on Protegrity policies to reverse [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* Protegrity already tokenises your structured data and you want the same tokens and policies in the AI path [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you are not on AWS for the AI editions, or need a current SOC 2 Type II report as a gate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Skyflow, Google Sensitive Data Protection, Presidio.
- *FS note:* request the current ISO certificate and any SOC 2 report, and treat AI Team Edition as a pilot until it is GA [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical** (core platform for existing customers; AI Team Edition Experimental until GA) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **No flag.**

**Skyflow.**
- *What it is now:* a data privacy vault. It stores sensitive data and returns tokens, detokenises under role-scoped credentials, and its Detect APIs de-identify text and files [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Its LLM Privacy Vault tokenises or masks data before it reaches models, prompts, RAG, tools, traces and agent workflows, with authorised rehydration [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S095: Skyflow GDPR Compliance; Data Privacy Vault; LLM Privacy Vault; SOC 2 solution pages; Why Skyflow (docs) <https://www.skyflow.com/gdpr-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Residency:* EU data privacy vaults are offered, and vault infrastructure is described as available in more than 100 countries [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S095: Skyflow GDPR Compliance; Data Privacy Vault; LLM Privacy Vault; SOC 2 solution pages; Why Skyflow (docs) <https://www.skyflow.com/gdpr-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Certifications:* the security page lists ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Type II and PCI DSS Level 1; the reports themselves are not public [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C3-S005: Skyflow Security (trust page) and certification posts <https://www.skyflow.com/security> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A6-S095: Skyflow GDPR Compliance; Data Privacy Vault; LLM Privacy Vault; SOC 2 solution pages; Why Skyflow (docs) <https://www.skyflow.com/gdpr-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Version and company:* Python SDK 2.1.3 was released on 4 August 2026, and SDK v1 reaches end of life on 31 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. The latest verified funding is a US$30m Series B extension on 28 March 2024; no later round or acquisition was found [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S096: Skyflow Raises $30 Million led by Khosla Ventures for Data Privacy in AI and Global Data Residency (Business Wire press release) (Skyflow (via Business Wire)) <https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240328765469/en/Skyflow-Raises-$30-Million-led-by-Khosla-Ventures-for-Data-Privacy-in-AI-and-Global-Data-Residency> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S095: Skyflow GDPR Compliance; Data Privacy Vault; LLM Privacy Vault; SOC 2 solution pages; Why Skyflow (docs) <https://www.skyflow.com/gdpr-compliance> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* the only product here built around reversible tokenisation of LLM traffic with residency by vault region [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* the vendor holds the sensitive values, so it is on the critical path of every re-identification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Self-hosting is not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. SSO and audit logs are not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Pricing is not published [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you need reversible pseudonymisation across many applications with per-region vaults, and accept a specialist vendor as a data processor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* policy requires identifiers to stay in the firm's own estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Protegrity, Google Sensitive Data Protection, a firm-built token service.
- *FS note:* migrate off SDK v1 before 31 October 2026, test bulk detokenisation as part of the exit plan, and assess the vendor's financial resilience as a material outsourcing [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Tactical. No flag.**

### C3.9 Decision tree

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): one firm-owned privacy-service API (detect / transform /
re-identify), one policy (entity classes → action per destination), keys in the firm's
KMS/HSM or Vault (C7), called at E1 ingestion, E2 prompt, E3 tool results, E4 output,
E5 memory writes, E6 trace export.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Detection engine behind the API
  May raw client text leave the estate for inspection?
  ├─ No  → Presidio in-estate + firm recognisers (client codes, account numbers);
  │        second detector on samples for residual-leakage KPI
  └─ Yes → Is Google Cloud the data platform?
           ├─ Yes → Sensitive Data Protection (pinned region, KMS-wrapped keys);
           │        Presidio as the in-estate pre-filter for "must not leave" classes
           └─ No  → Presidio; or the cloud guardrail's PII filter where already in the
                    gateway path (e.g. Bedrock Guardrails on AWS), behind the same API

STEP 2 [Rec]: Transformation
  Does anyone need the original value back after the model call?
  ├─ No  → redact / mask / bucket in the privacy service
  └─ Yes → Volume and number of applications?
           ├─ One or few apps   → consistent per-conversation placeholders; map held
           │                      in the firm's store, keys in KMS; deterministic check
           │                      before re-identification
           ├─ Already a Protegrity customer → Protegrity policies and tokens (core
           │                      platform; AI Team Edition only after GA)
           └─ Many apps, per-region vaults acceptable as a processor → Skyflow (EU vault)

STEP 3 [Rec]: Posture over SaaS AI (Copilot, ChatGPT Enterprise)
  Microsoft 365 E5 / Purview Suite already licensed? → Purview DSPM
  Otherwise → CASB/SSE tooling (outside this control's scope) plus usage policy

STEP 4 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Recall per class ≥ target on the firm's test set?  Output inspection on?
  Collector redaction on?  Erasure runbook covers memory, traces, eval sets, caches?
```

|---|---|---|---|
| Detection engine | **Acceptable** | Detectors are replaceable if the test set and recognisers are the firm's | Privacy-service API; recognisers and test corpus in Git |
| Policy (classes and actions) | **Manageable** | Every product has its own policy model (Protegrity data elements [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C3-S004: Policy Management and Enterprise Security Administrator (ESA) documentation 10.1 (Protegrity) <https://docs.protegrity.com/10.1/docs/pmg/_print/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], Purview labels) | Firm-owned policy as code, compiled into engine configuration |
| Token map and keys held by a vendor | **Unacceptable unless bulk detokenisation on exit is contractually and technically tested** | A vendor-held map makes the vendor part of every future read of the data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}; Skyflow detokenises under its own credentials [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S081: skyflow - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/skyflow/json> accessed 2026-10-07] | Keys in the firm's KMS/HSM; contractual exit with tested bulk export |
| Managed DLP API | **Manageable** | Proprietary API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S066: Sensitive Data Protection product page (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/security/products/sensitive-data-protection> accessed 2026-10-07]; outputs are portable text | Same API; per-region configuration |

### C3.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Data protection and transfers.**
- *UK regime.* UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 applies; the ICO states all DUAA data protection provisions were in force as of 19 June 2026, including changes to the third-country transfer test (s.85) and automated decision-making (s.80) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S051: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: commencement (GOV.UK, SI 2025/904, SI 2026/82, ICO) (DSIT / legislation.gov.uk / ICO) <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/data-use-and-access-act-2025-plans-for-commencement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S076: The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 - commencement dates and planned guidance for 2026 (Kennedys; with Stephenson Harwood tracker, A&O Shearman) <https://www.kennedyslaw.com/en/thought-leadership/article/2026/the-data-use-and-access-act-2025-commencement-dates-and-planned-guidance-for-2026> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *EU–UK.* The EU renewed its UK adequacy decisions on 19 December 2025, valid until 27 December 2031 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S052: Receiving personal information from the EEA (UK adequacy renewal); Commission adequacy page; EDPB Opinion 27/2025 (ICO / European Commission / EDPB) <https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/international-transfers/receiving-personal-information-from-the-eea/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S055: European Commission renews UK data adequacy decisions (with Freeths, eucrim) (Hunton Andrews Kurth) <https://www.hunton.com/privacy-and-cybersecurity-law-blog/european-commission-renews-uk-data-adequacy-decisions> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *EU–US.* The Data Privacy Framework remains in effect, but the appeal C-703/25 P against the General Court's judgment is pending as of 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S053: Case C-703/25 P Latombe v Commission (appeal against T-553/23) (EUR-Lex / Court of Justice of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/C/2025/6610/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S054: European General Court dismisses Latombe challenge, upholds EU-US DPF (with A&O Shearman, WilmerHale) (IAPP / law firms) <https://iapp.org/news/a/european-general-court-dismisses-latombe-challenge-upholds-eu-us-data-privacy-framework> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S059: European Court of Justice to Review Challenge to EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (with ieu-monitoring on Microsoft intervention, digitalpolicyalert) (WilmerHale) <https://www.wilmerhale.com/en/insights/blogs/wilmerhale-privacy-and-cybersecurity-law/20251201-european-court-of-justice-to-review-challenge-to-eu-us-data-privacy-framework> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Tokenising identifiers before a US-hosted model call reduces the personal data exposed to that transfer risk [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Processing location as a priced control.* At least one first-party LLM API (Anthropic's Claude API) offers a US-only inference option at 1.1 times the price for Claude 4.6 and later, with workspace geography currently US only [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DATA-TRANSFERS: UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy decisions for the UK (GDPR and LED); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S036: Data residency (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/data-residency.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The author is an Anthropic model; this is cited only as evidence that processing location is now a contract and configuration item, and other providers' equivalents are assessed in L1 and L2 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Residency of prompts and logs.* Prompts, traces and memory are personal-data stores in their own right [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Residency must be configured for each: the model endpoint (L2/C1), the trace store (L9), the memory store (L5) and the DLP service itself [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to keep logs for at least six months and monitor operation; Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Long retention of logs that contain personal data conflicts with minimisation unless the logs are tokenised [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Tokenised traces with a controlled re-identification path satisfy both [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Supervisory expectations.**
- ESMA expects "ex-ante input controls and frequent ex-post output controls" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S059: ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) and 2026 briefings <https://www.esma.europa.eu/document/public-statement-ai-and-investment-services> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Prompt-side tokenisation is the input control; output inspection is the output control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- FG16/5 expects data location, effective access and exit planning for outsourced IT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A vault vendor holding client identifiers is an outsourcing with data-location and exit implications [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Operational resilience and concentration.**
- DORA's CTPP list and the UK CTP designations cover hyperscalers and no AI model provider [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. - PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require material third-party notifications from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A specialist vault on the critical path of client-data access is a candidate for material classification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- SS2/21 expects documented and tested exit plans [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. For a vault, the exit test is bulk detokenisation [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Model risk.** PRA SS1/23 applies to banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval, and is technology-agnostic [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; SR 26-2 places generative and agentic AI outside its scope [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. SS1/23 and the EU AI Act are therefore the operative anchors [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. NER and LLM-based detectors are models whose recall drifts with data, so they should be inventoried and tested as such [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C3.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from C3 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary for a generic multi-asset fund. Most of its inputs are fund-level numbers, which are confidential but not personal data. Client identifiers appear when a commentary is produced for a segregated mandate, and personal data appears in the approval record. It needs six things:
1. **Tokenise before any model call.** Client names, mandate references, account numbers and named client contacts are replaced with consistent placeholders (CLIENT_A, MANDATE_1) at the gateway, so the model can write "the mandate's currency overlay" without seeing who the client is. Fund-level attribution figures are not tokenised; they are confidential data whose protection is the model endpoint's residency and contract.
2. **Detect again in the output.** The draft is inspected before re-identification. Any clear-text identifier that was not in the approved inputs blocks the draft. Placeholders must match the input set exactly: none invented, none altered.
3. **Re-identify only for the reviewer.** Placeholders are restored in the reviewer's view, under the reviewing PM's entitlement checked through C4, and the re-identification is logged.
4. **Clean retrieval and memory.** Prior commentaries indexed by L8 carry classification flags; segregated-mandate commentaries are retrievable only for the same mandate. Long-term memory of the PM's edits stores style preferences, never client identifiers.
5. **Redacted traces and evidence.** The OTel Collector redacts before export; the C8 evidence pack stores the tokenised prompt and the token-map reference, so the run is reproducible without copying clear identifiers into the archive.
6. **Location evidence.** Configuration evidence that the model endpoint, trace store and DLP calls ran in approved regions.

**What C3 must never allow [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- an untokenised client name or account number in a prompt to an external model
- a model-invented or altered placeholder being "re-identified" into the final text
- re-identification by the agent itself, or by anyone without the entitlement
- raw identifiers in traces, memory or the regression dataset
- the privacy service failing open on an external call

## C4. Identity and access for agents

> **Executive summary.** This control answers the question every incident review and every regulator will ask: who did this, on whose authority, and with what permission [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}? For an agent that means five things: the agent has its own identity, it acts on behalf of a named human where a human started the work, its permissions are the least needed for the task, it holds no standing secrets, and every action is attributable to both the agent and the human [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The original graphic has no such control; it shows MCP and A2A as connectivity in L4 without saying who is allowed to call what [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Since then the products have reached general availability. Microsoft Entra Agent ID became GA in April 2026, with its security features tied to Microsoft Agent 365 licences [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S058: What's new in Microsoft Entra Agent ID (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S059: Microsoft Entra Agent ID licensing (include file) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/includes/licensing-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S032: Microsoft Entra releases and announcements (with What's new in Entra Agent ID; Entra blog 'Build AI agents for production with secure identities from day one';  <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/whats-new> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. **Conflict of interest.** The author is an Anthropic model, and MCP originated at Anthropic. MCP authorisation is scored on the same rubric as every other product, and independent alternatives are named in its deep dive [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The reader then set the tier at Checkpoint 3 (CP3 Q1): MCP and its authorisation profile are one decision, Strategic, conditional, only behind a gateway with mandatory authorisation, an allow-list and pinned tool definitions [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**
- *C1 gateway:* the main enforcement point, which validates tokens, filters the tool list and calls the policy decision point [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *L4 tools and MCP servers:* resource servers that must validate audience and scope and must not pass the caller's token through [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *L3 orchestration:* carries the user context through the workflow and pauses for approvals [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *C7 security:* owns secrets storage and dynamic credentials (HashiCorp Vault), which C4 consumes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *C2 guardrails:* judge whether an action is safe or on-task; C4 decides whether it is permitted. Both are needed [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *C3 DLP:* re-identification is a privileged action whose entitlement C4 decides [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *L6 retrieval:* entitlement filters at query time use the same user principal [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *C8 governance:* receives the attribution chain and approval records as evidence [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What the control does not own.** It does not decide whether a tool is safe to install (C7 supply chain) or whether a model's plan is sensible (C2, L3) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C4.2 Why it matters

Agents turn identity mistakes into actions [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A human with excessive access usually does nothing with it; an agent with excessive access may be steered into using it by text it reads [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 lists ASI03 "Identity & Privilege Abuse", where leaked or excessive credentials let agents operate beyond their intended scope, next to ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack and ASI02 Tool Misuse and Exploitation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S005: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (release post and related OWASP pages) (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/2025/12/09/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-the-benchmark-for-agentic-security-in-the-age-of-autonomous-ai/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; R-OWASP-AGENTIC: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S042: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (launched 9-10 December 2025) (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The 2026 OWASP LLM list is reported to have moved Excessive Agency to third place, on a contributor's account; the full 2026 list was not retrieved [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — R-OWASP-LLM: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (superseded by the OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); V2-S056: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026 (with press release 'OWASP GenAI Security Project Unveils 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications, New Agent Control Standard', URL dated 2 <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-genai-llm-top-10-2026/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Badly designed, the control fails in four ways [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Shared service accounts.** Every agent runs as one technical user, so logs cannot say which human started an action.
- **Standing credentials.** API keys and refresh tokens live in agent configuration or prompts and outlive the task.
- **Token passthrough.** An MCP server forwards the caller's token downstream, creating a confused deputy; the MCP specification forbids this [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Ungoverned agents.** Agents created by developers have no owner, no review and no revocation path.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A portfolio-analytics team builds an agent that answers questions about exposures. To move fast, it runs under a service account that the team already uses for reporting jobs, with read and write access to the portfolio-management system's API. A market note retrieved for context contains hidden instructions to "rebalance to target weights using the order tool". The order tool is on the same MCP server as the read tools, the agent has the permission, and it creates draft orders. A trader notices them before release. The investigation finds only the service account in the logs, cannot say which analyst's session started the run, and finds the service account's key copied into two other agents. With per-agent identity, OBO tokens scoped to read-only tools, a policy that removes write tools from the agent's tool list, and an audit chain, the injected instruction would have had nothing to call. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### C4.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registered-agent coverage | Agents in production with a registered identity and a named owner or sponsor | 100%; unregistered agents are blocked at the gateway | IdP agent registry reconciled to gateway callers |
| Delegated-call share | Tool calls in user-initiated workflows carrying a user-bound OBO token rather than an agent-only credential | 100% for user-initiated work | Token claims in gateway logs |
| Standing credentials | Long-lived secrets (API keys, static tokens) held by agents | Zero; exceptions time-limited and owned | Secret scanning; Vault and IdP inventory |
| Token lifetime | p95 lifetime of access tokens used for tool calls | Minutes, not hours | IdP token logs |
| Privilege breadth | Tools and scopes granted versus tools actually used over 30 days | Unused grants removed at each review | Policy and gateway logs |
| Policy-decision coverage | Tool calls evaluated by the policy decision point before execution | 100% | PDP decision logs reconciled to tool calls |
| Attribution completeness | Audit events with user, agent, tool, arguments hash, decision and trace ID | ≥99.9% | Audit store completeness check |
| Agent access review | Agents certified by their owner in the review cycle | 100% per cycle | Access-certification campaigns (e.g. Okta AI-agent campaigns [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S007: Okta help: AI agents (add manually; configure; update) and access certifications for AI agents (Okta, Inc.) <https://help.okta.com/OIE/en-us/content/topics/ai-agents/ai-agent-add-manually.htm> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]) |
| Orphaned agents | Agents whose owner or sponsor has left or moved | Zero after 30 days | HR joiner/mover/leaver feed to IdP |
| Time to revoke | Time from decision to revoke an agent to its last successful call | Under 15 minutes | Revocation drills |
| Approval integrity | Approvals where approver differs from requester and is entitled | 100% | Approval records joined to identity |

### C4.4 How it works

**Three identity patterns.** Entra Agent ID documents the distinction clearly: `client_credentials` for autonomous agents, `jwt-bearer` for on-behalf-of delegation, and `refresh_token` for long-running user-delegated work, with no interactive flows for agent entities [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S060: Authentication protocols for agents (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/agent-oauth-protocols.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. It also supports agent user accounts with owners, sponsors and managers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S057: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/what-is-microsoft-entra-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

| Pattern | When [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Risk [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|
| **Delegated (OBO)** | A human starts the work; the agent acts for them | Lowest: effective permission is at most the user's; attribution is native |
| **Autonomous (agent's own credentials)** | Scheduled or event-driven work with no human in the loop | The agent's own grants are the ceiling, so they must be narrow and reviewed |
| **Agent as a user account** | Agents that need a mailbox, a seat or a licence | Highest: it looks like a person in logs and in access reviews |

**Request flow for a delegated tool call.**

```text
 Analyst ──SSO──► Agent app (L3)              Corporate IdP (Entra / Okta)
                    │  user token (aud=agent app)        ▲   │
                    │                                     │   │ ID-JAG / OBO token
                    └── token exchange (RFC 8693 / OBO) ──┘   │ aud = attribution MCP server
                                                              ▼ scope = attribution.read, 5-min TTL
 Agent runtime (SPIFFE SVID, mTLS) ──► C1 gateway ──────────────────────────────┐
                                        │ 1 validate token (iss, aud, exp)       │
                                        │ 2 PDP: OPA / Cedar  input = {user,      │
                                        │   agent, tool, args, purpose}  → allow  │
                                        │ 3 filter tools/list to allowed tools    │
                                        ▼                                         │
                              MCP server (L4, resource server)                    │
                                validates aud + scope; no token passthrough;      │
                                own downstream credential (Vault dynamic secret) │
                                        ▼                                         │
                              Attribution engine (read-only)                      │
 Audit event (C8): user · agent · tool · args hash · decision id · trace id ◄─────┘
```

**Mechanics in the standards.**
- *MCP authorisation.* The MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server that must publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728); clients must use PKCE and Resource Indicators (RFC 8707) so tokens are audience-bound; servers must reject tokens not issued for them [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Revision 2026-07-28 adds RFC 9207 issuer validation, binds client credentials to the issuer and deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S032: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (changelog) (Model Context Protocol project (Agentic AI Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Enterprise-Managed Authorization.* The corporate IdP issues an Identity Assertion JWT Authorization Grant (ID-JAG), which the client exchanges for an access token at the MCP server's authorisation server, using RFC 8693 and RFC 7523 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S035: MCP extension: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (overview) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S079: MCP ext-auth: Enterprise-Managed Authorization specification (Stable) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. This puts the decision about which MCP servers an employee can use in the IdP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S035: MCP extension: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (overview) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Policy at the gateway.* AgentCore Policy evaluates every agent-to-tool call before execution using identity claims and tool arguments, removes denied tools from `tools/list` by partial evaluation, and logs decisions to CloudWatch [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. OPA does the same job as a general-purpose engine evaluating Rego against JSON input [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S046: Open Policy Agent README (GitHub) (Open Policy Agent project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-policy-agent/opa/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Human approval.* OpenID CIBA lets an agent request asynchronous approval from a human out of band; Auth0's AI SDKs implement it [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S078: Auth0 AI for JavaScript README (GitHub) (Auth0 (Okta)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/auth0/auth0-ai-js/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S076: auth0-ai - PyPI JSON metadata (Python Package Index) <https://pypi.org/pypi/auth0-ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Effective permission.* HashiCorp Vault's agentic IAM (GA in Vault Enterprise 2.1 on 1 September 2026) enforces the intersection of the user's permissions, an agent ceiling policy and request-scoped authorisation details, and records both user and agent in audit logs [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S033: Vault release notes 2.x; IBM Vault Self-Managed 2.x.x lifecycle page (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/updates/release-notes> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S034: HashiCorp Vault agentic IAM is now generally available (HashiCorp (IBM)) <https://www.hashicorp.com/en/blog/hashicorp-vault-agentic-iam-is-now-generally-available> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. This intersection is the right mental model for every product here [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C4.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**

- **Deny by default.** No tool is callable unless a policy allows this agent, for this user, with these arguments [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Least privilege per task.** Grant scopes per tool and per workflow, and hide tools the agent may not call; partial evaluation of `tools/list` (AgentCore) and per-caller tool exposure (Kong) are product forms of this [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- **Intersection, not union.** Effective permission is the intersection of the user's entitlements and the agent's ceiling [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **No standing credentials.** Use short-lived tokens, workload identity and dynamic secrets; never put a key in a prompt, a tool description or agent memory [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **No token passthrough.** Each hop gets a token for its own audience [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- **Turn authorisation on.** MCP leaves authorisation optional [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], and its security policy places access control and least privilege on server developers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S004: Model Context Protocol Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08]. Make both mandatory by firm policy [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Open defaults are a finding.** LiteLLM's A2A agents are open to all callers until an allowlist is defined [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; check every gateway's default [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Scalability and resilience**

- The IdP and the PDP are now on the critical path of every tool call. Cache decisions briefly, run the PDP as a sidecar or library where possible, and define break-glass procedures [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Token exchange adds round trips; reuse tokens within their short lifetime rather than lengthening it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance**

- Every agent has an owner and a sponsor, a business purpose and a review cycle, and is revoked when its owner leaves [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Entra and Okta both model owners or sponsors [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S057: What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? (Microsoft Learn source) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/agent-id/what-is-microsoft-entra-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07; B-C4-S007: Okta help: AI agents (add manually; configure; update) and access certifications for AI agents (Okta, Inc.) <https://help.okta.com/OIE/en-us/content/topics/ai-agents/ai-agent-add-manually.htm> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- Segregation of duties: an agent never approves its own output; the approver differs from the requester; the person who writes a policy does not deploy it alone [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Policies are code: in Git, unit-tested, reviewed. Natural-language policy authoring (AgentCore converts it to Cedar and checks it with automated reasoning [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]) is an authoring aid, not an approval [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Observability**

- Emit one audit event per tool call with user, agent, tool, argument hash, policy decision ID and trace ID, and join it to the L9 trace [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Cost**

- Identity features carry licence prerequisites: Entra's agent security features need Agent 365 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S059: Microsoft Entra Agent ID licensing (include file) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/main/docs/includes/licensing-agent-id.md> accessed 2026-10-07]; Okta's Cross App Access is included in core SSO while Okta for AI Agents is a separate subscription [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S099: Okta brings first-class identity to AI agents with Agent SSO; Okta Introduces Agent SSO for Cross App Access (XAA) (Okta, Inc.) <https://www.okta.com/newsroom/press-releases/okta-brings-first-class-identity-to-ai-agents-with-agent-sso/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; AgentCore Policy costs US$0.000025 per authorisation request, as of 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Portability**

- Stay on OAuth, OIDC and token exchange at the interfaces, and keep policies in an open language (Rego or Cedar) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** agent registry in the workforce IdP; OBO token exchange per tool audience; PDP at the gateway with tool-list filtering; workload identity for runtimes; dynamic secrets for downstream systems; asynchronous human approval for consequential actions; quarterly agent access certification.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** shared service accounts for agents; developer personal tokens in agent configuration; one broad scope for all tools; Dynamic Client Registration left open; read and write tools on the same server with no policy; approval by the requester; agents with no owner.

### C4.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Agent identity model; OBO and autonomous flows; token exchange; audience binding; tool-level policy; async approval; workload identity; MCP and A2A support |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC and audit for agent administration; agent lifecycle (owners, reviews, revocation); SCIM; admin APIs |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in product scope; for open software, project hygiene; FedRAMP or similar raises the ceiling because the IdP is the root of trust |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | SaaS only versus self-hostable PDP and workload identity; regional data location for identity logs |
| Ecosystem (5%) | IdP integration, gateway support, MCP EMA adopters, framework SDKs |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | GA status, spec churn, SDK stability, foundation governance |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Licence prerequisites (Agent 365, Okta for AI Agents), per-decision pricing, operating effort |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Standards at the interfaces (OAuth, OIDC, RFC 8693, ID-JAG); open policy languages; proprietary agent constructs |
