**SPIFFE and SPIRE (CNCF).**
- *What it is now:* SPIFFE is the specification and SPIRE its runtime. SPIRE attests running software and issues SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs through the Workload API, so workloads can establish mTLS or signed-JWT trust and authenticate to secret stores, databases or cloud services; it also implements Envoy SDS [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S087: SPIRE README (GitHub) (SPIFFE project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spiffe/spire/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. SPIRE v1.15.3 was released on 21 August 2026 under Apache-2.0, and the project is CNCF graduated [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S043: Go module proxy: github.com/spiffe/spire @latest (Go module proxy (proxy.golang.org)) <https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/spiffe/spire/@latest> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S089: SPIRE LICENSE (SPIFFE project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spiffe/spire/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S087: SPIRE README (GitHub) (SPIFFE project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spiffe/spire/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Project hygiene:* Cure53 audited it in February 2021, and CNCF security assessments ran in 2018 and 2020 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S087: SPIRE README (GitHub) (SPIFFE project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spiffe/spire/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Security fixes are supported for the current and previous minor release series, with private reporting [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S002: SPIRE Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (SPIFFE project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spiffe/spire/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Strengths:* removes static secrets between agent runtimes, gateways and tool servers, across clouds and on-premises [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* it is machine identity; it carries no delegated user authority [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S087: SPIRE README (GitHub) (SPIFFE project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spiffe/spire/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. No agent-specific SPIFFE profile was verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Operating SPIRE is a platform-team commitment [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* agents and tools run across Kubernetes, VMs and clouds and need workload identity without secrets [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* a single cloud's workload identity already covers every runtime [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* cloud workload identity federation (Entra, AWS IAM), HashiCorp Vault.
- *FS note:* use SVIDs for runtime-to-gateway and gateway-to-tool mTLS, never as a substitute for the user's delegated token [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. No flag.**

**MCP authorisation (Model Context Protocol project).**
- *Conflict of interest:* MCP originated at Anthropic and the author is an Anthropic model. MCP was donated to the Agentic AI Foundation (a Linux Foundation directed fund) on 9 December 2025, and both Lead Maintainers are Anthropic staff; an AWS engineer joined the Core Maintainers in April 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S018: MCP joins the Agentic AI Foundation (9 Dec 2025) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2025-12-09-mcp-joins-agentic-ai-foundation/> accessed 2026-10-07; A3-S082: Expanding the MCP Maintainer Team (8 Apr 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-04-08-maintainer-update/> accessed 2026-10-07]. The rubric was applied exactly as for other open specifications, and alternatives are named below [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *What it is now:* the authorisation profile for MCP. The server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server; it must publish Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728); clients must use PKCE and Resource Indicators (RFC 8707); servers must reject tokens not issued for them, and token passthrough is forbidden [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Revision 2026-07-28 adds RFC 9207 issuer validation and issuer-bound client credentials, deprecates Dynamic Client Registration in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents, makes the protocol stateless, and deprecates Roots, Sampling and Logging under a 12-month deprecation window [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S032: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Key Changes (changelog) (Model Context Protocol project (Agentic AI Foundation)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S031: MCP specification 2026-07-28 changelog (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/changelog.mdx> accessed 2026-10-08]. The Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension is Stable [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S035: MCP extension: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (overview) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S079: MCP ext-auth: Enterprise-Managed Authorization specification (Stable) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Maturity:* authorisation is OPTIONAL; OAuth 2.1 is cited as draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13, and the ID-JAG grant is also an IETF draft; the specification had breaking revisions on 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S079: MCP ext-auth: Enterprise-Managed Authorization specification (Stable) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-auth/main/specification/stable/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The MCP roadmap of 22 August 2026 lists DPoP, workload identity federation, ID-JAG and token exchange as agent-identity priorities [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S016: The New MCP Roadmap (22 Aug 2026) (Model Context Protocol project (blog)) <https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/mcp-roadmap/> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Trust model:* the project's security policy states that clients trust the servers they are configured to use, that server developers are responsible for access control and least privilege, and that an LLM invoking tools the user did not explicitly request is expected behaviour [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S004: Model Context Protocol Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Implementations:* AgentCore Gateway and Kong AI Gateway 2.1.0 support revision 2026-07-28, and Okta's XAA implements EMA [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S017: Kong AI Gateway changelog; Kong Gateway changelog; AI Proxy Advanced plugin docs (Kong Inc.) <https://developer.konghq.com/ai-gateway/changelog/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S099: Okta brings first-class identity to AI agents with Agent SSO; Okta Introduces Agent SSO for Cross App Access (XAA) (Okta, Inc.) <https://www.okta.com/newsroom/press-releases/okta-brings-first-class-identity-to-ai-agents-with-agent-sso/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* audience binding and the passthrough ban address confused-deputy attacks, and EMA puts the corporate IdP in charge [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S034: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization security considerations (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/security-considerations.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S035: MCP extension: Enterprise-Managed Authorization (overview) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/extensions/auth/enterprise-managed-authorization.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Limitations:* optional authorisation, draft dependencies and frequent breaking revisions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S033: MCP specification 2026-07-28: Authorization (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/docs/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The trust model leaves fine-grained authorisation to implementers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S004: Model Context Protocol Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (Model Context Protocol project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Choose when:* MCP is the firm's tool protocol [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* tools are REST or OpenAPI services behind a gateway, where a plain OAuth 2.0 resource-server pattern is enough [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Independent alternatives:* gateway-native tool authorisation (Kong MCP access controls and token exchange [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S017: Kong AI Gateway changelog; Kong Gateway changelog; AI Proxy Advanced plugin docs (Kong Inc.) <https://developer.konghq.com/ai-gateway/changelog/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; AgentCore Gateway with IAM or OAuth [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Azure API Management credential manager for MCP [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07]), and the plain OAuth 2.0 resource-server pattern for REST tools [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A2A is a peer protocol whose own specification does not define scope, validity or revocation semantics for authorisation obtained mid-task [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A3-S078: A2A Protocol Specification (source, latest released version 1.0.0) (A2A Project (GitHub)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/a2aproject/A2A/main/docs/specification.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *FS note:* make authorisation mandatory by firm policy, require EMA, and pin the specification revision at the gateway with a re-test on each revision [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Put the durable control in the workforce IdP (via EMA) and the gateway PDP, so it survives a change of tool protocol [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: only behind a gateway with mandatory authorisation, an allow-list and pinned tool definitions; mandatory wherever MCP is the tool protocol [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. No flag.** Tier set by the reader at Checkpoint 3 (CP3 Q1); the author's reviewers had resolved the borderline call against the Anthropic-originated item. MCP (L4) and its authorisation profile are one decision with one tier. FS 3.45 and reliability 2 are unchanged: authorisation is optional in the specification, it rests on IETF drafts and it has had four breaking revisions in about 16 months, so the condition includes pinning the specification revision at the gateway and re-testing on each revision. The durable controls remain the workforce IdP (via EMA) and the gateway policy decision point [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Open Policy Agent (CNCF).**
- *What it is now:* a general-purpose policy engine that evaluates Rego policies against JSON input and returns allow/deny or richer decisions, as a library, sidecar or daemon, across services, APIs, Kubernetes and infrastructure [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S046: Open Policy Agent README (GitHub) (Open Policy Agent project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-policy-agent/opa/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. v1.21.1 was released on 29 September 2026; it is Apache-2.0 and CNCF graduated since February 2021 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S048: Go module proxy: github.com/open-policy-agent/opa @latest (Go module proxy (proxy.golang.org)) <https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/open-policy-agent/opa/@latest> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S088: Open Policy Agent LICENSE (Open Policy Agent project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-policy-agent/opa/main/LICENSE> accessed 2026-10-07; A6-S046: Open Policy Agent README (GitHub) (Open Policy Agent project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-policy-agent/opa/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Project hygiene:* a published security policy covers reporting and disclosure [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S001: OPA Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (Open Policy Agent project (CNCF)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-policy-agent/opa/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Strengths:* one vendor-neutral PDP for gateway, tool-server and infrastructure decisions, with testable policy code [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* no agent-specific features are verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A reported 2025 move of its original maintainers to Apple is not verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* you want one PDP across clouds and runtimes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* your agents run entirely on AgentCore and you want managed, automated-reasoning-checked policy [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Cedar, gateway-native policy (Kong, AgentCore Policy).
- *FS note:* model the input as {user, agent, tool, arguments, purpose} and keep policies and tests in Git under change control [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. No flag.**

These are the sources C1 and L4 use for AgentCore Gateway [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Pricing:* Cedar is free; AgentCore Policy costs US$0.000025 per authorisation request and US$0.13 per 1,000 input tokens for natural-language policy processing, as of 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S021: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Pricing; AgentCore GA announcement (Oct 2025); AgentCore Gateway docs (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agentcore/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Project hygiene:* Cedar's security policy promises a non-automated acknowledgement within one business day and an initial assessment within five, with embargoed advisories [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C4-S003: Cedar Security Policy (SECURITY.md) (Cedar project) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cedar-policy/cedar/main/SECURITY.md> accessed 2026-10-08].
- *Strengths:* the most complete managed tool-call authorisation found, with analysable policies [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* Cedar cannot do external lookups at evaluation time, and AWS recommends Lambda interceptors for those cases; enforcement is tied to AgentCore Gateway [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S026: Policy in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available; AgentCore Policy docs; Why Policy in AgentCore chose Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/03/policy-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-generally-available/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The Cedar 2 to 4 migration was breaking for Verified Permissions users [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S104: Amazon Verified Permissions now supports policy store aliases and named policies and policy templates; Cedar 4 FAQ; differences from Cedar (Amazon Web Services) <https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/04/amazon-verified-permissions-policy-store/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Choose when:* your agents run on AgentCore Gateway [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you are multi-cloud and want one PDP, or your policies need live external data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* OPA, gateway-native policy (Kong).
- *FS note:* review AI-generated policies before activation, keep Cedar source in Git, and avoid Dogwood-only constructs where portability matters; platform controls presumed (CP2 Q1); confirm per service [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: where AWS is your primary cloud and agents run on AgentCore Gateway (CP3 Q2, rubric rule 10) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. No flag.** FS 3.70. AgentCore Policy is AWS's lead managed policy service for agent tool calls. At the CP3 review it was held at Tactical only because its enforcement point, AgentCore Gateway, was Tactical in C1; under rule 10 that gateway is now Strategic on the same condition (C1 and L4), so the policy engine follows it. OPA remains the Strategic, cloud-neutral default; keep Cedar source in Git so policies stay portable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C4.9 Decision tree

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): every agent registered with an owner and sponsor; deny-by-default
tool policy at the gateway; no standing credentials in agents; one audit event per tool call
(user · agent · tool · args hash · decision · trace id).

STEP 1 [Rec]: Where do agent identities live?
  Which IdP holds the workforce?
  ├─ Entra → Entra Agent ID (+ Agent 365 for Conditional Access / ID Protection on agents)
  ├─ Okta  → Okta for AI Agents + Agent SSO (XAA); Auth0 for customer-facing agents
  └─ Other → keep agents in the workforce IdP via standard OAuth clients; add HashiCorp Vault
             agentic IAM (C7) for user-and-agent intersection and attribution

STEP 2 [Rec]: How does the agent act?
  Did a human start the work?
  ├─ Yes → OBO / token exchange per tool audience; scopes = task, TTL = minutes
  │        Consequential action? → async human approval (CIBA or workflow gate in L3)
  └─ No  → autonomous agent credential with a narrow ceiling, reviewed each cycle;
           never an agent "user account" unless a licence or mailbox requires it

STEP 3 [Rec]: Tool protocol
  MCP? ├─ Yes → MCP authorisation mandatory by policy; EMA (ID-JAG) via the IdP;
       │        DCR disabled; pin the spec revision at the gateway
       └─ No  → OAuth 2.0 resource-server pattern on REST/OpenAPI tools behind the gateway

STEP 4 [Rec]: Policy decision point
  Agents on AWS AgentCore Gateway? ├─ Yes → AgentCore Policy (Cedar), source in Git
                                   └─ No  → OPA at the gateway (sidecar or library)

STEP 5 [Rec]: Runtime identity and secrets
  Multi-cloud or on-prem runtimes? ├─ Yes → SPIFFE/SPIRE SVIDs for mTLS
                                   └─ No  → the cloud's workload identity federation
  Downstream systems → dynamic credentials from Vault (C7), never stored in the agent
```

### C4.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Accountability for non-human actors.**
- The FCA has no AI-specific rules and relies on existing frameworks, including SM&CR and Consumer Duty [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-AI-STATEMENTS: FCA, Bank of England and PRA statements and initiatives on AI, 2024-2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S055: FCA announces second cohort for AI Live Testing (April 2026); FS25/5; Mills Review (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://www.fca.org.uk/news/press-releases/fca-announces-second-cohort-ai-live-testing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No rule names an accountable person for an agent, so applying SM&CR-style accountability to agents is a judgement: every agent should map to a sponsor and, through the business area, to a Senior Manager [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- The FPC said in 2026 that agentic AI had not yet been adopted in a way presenting systemic risk, but that risks are likely to increase, potentially rapidly, and asked for further work on agentic AI in payments and markets [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-UK-AI-STATEMENTS: FCA, Bank of England and PRA statements and initiatives on AI, 2024-2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S056: Financial Policy Committee Record April 2026; FSR July 2026; 2026 AI survey (Bank of England) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/financial-policy-committee-record/2026/april-2026> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- Segregation of duties carries over directly: an agent may draft but not approve; the approver must be a different, entitled human; policy changes need a second person [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to monitor operation and keep logs for at least six months; Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Logs without user and agent identity cannot show who operated the system [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Build the attribution chain to Article 26 quality even where the use case is not high-risk [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Model risk.**
- SR 26-2 places generative and agentic AI outside its scope [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. PRA SS1/23 applies to banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval, and covers vendor models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. With the EU AI Act, it is the operative anchor [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. An agent's permissions are part of its risk tier: the same model with write access is a different risk from one with read-only access [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Operational resilience and concentration.**

### C4.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from C4 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary for a generic multi-asset fund, started by an authorised analyst and approved by a portfolio manager.
1. **A registered agent identity.** The commentary agent is registered in the workforce IdP with the reporting product owner as owner and the head of performance reporting as sponsor, and is certified in each access review.
2. **Acting on behalf of the analyst.** The analyst signs in through SSO; the workflow exchanges the analyst's token for a token whose audience is the attribution-engine MCP server, with a read-only scope (for example `attribution.read`) and a lifetime of minutes. The agent's effective permission is the intersection of the analyst's entitlements and the agent's ceiling, so it cannot read a fund the analyst cannot.
3. **Read-only tools only.** The gateway policy allows `get_attribution_effects`, `get_benchmark_returns` and retrieval of approved commentary for this fund and period; write tools are not in the agent's tool list at all. Retrieval in L6 filters by the analyst's principal.
4. **No standing credentials.** The agent holds no API keys or refresh tokens; the runtime authenticates to the gateway with a workload identity; the MCP server uses its own dynamic credential to the attribution database.
5. **A named approval recorded with identity.** The draft goes to a named PM, who approves through SSO with step-up authentication; the approval event records the PM's identity, the draft hash and the time. The PM must differ from the analyst who started the run, and the agent cannot approve.
6. **One attribution chain.** Each tool call writes an audit event with analyst, agent, tool, argument hash, policy decision and trace ID; the C8 evidence pack links requester, agent identity, approver and every decision.

**What C4 must never allow [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- the agent running under a shared service account or a developer's personal token
- a write or order tool reachable by the agent, even if never called
- the analyst's token passed through to the attribution engine
- an approval recorded without the approver's identity, or by the requester or the agent
- the agent continuing to act after the analyst's or the agent's access has been revoked

## C5. Prompt and configuration management

> **Executive summary.** This control decides which instructions, model, parameters, tools and retrieval settings a GenAI system runs with, who may change them, and how a change is tested, released and rolled back. The original graphic has no box for it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. What exists in the market today is mostly a capability inside other products. Langfuse and LangSmith each ship a prompt registry inside their L9 platforms [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. LaunchDarkly delivers model and prompt configuration through its feature-flag service and renamed the product from AI Configs to AgentControl in 2026, with the API unchanged [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S117: LaunchDarkly: Introducing AgentControl; AI Configs is now GA; AgentControl API docs <https://launchdarkly.com/blog/introducing-agentcontrol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S045: AgentControl API docs (LaunchDarkly) <https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/agentcontrol> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. PromptLayer remains an independent registry [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. The "prompts as code" pattern keeps prompt files (Prompty, Dotprompt) in the application repository and tests them in CI [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S066: Dotprompt README (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/dotprompt/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S068: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Two ownership changes touch the control: ClickHouse announced its acquisition of Langfuse on 16 January 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S075: Langfuse README (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S041: ClickHouse welcomes Langfuse (with langfuse.com 'Langfuse joins ClickHouse', Orrick) <https://clickhouse.com/blog/clickhouse-acquires-langfuse-open-source-llm-observability> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and OpenAI announced its acquisition of Promptfoo on 9 March 2026, with no closing date published [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S068: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S042: OpenAI to acquire Promptfoo (with TechCrunch via Yahoo Finance, SDxCentral, Security Boulevard) <https://openai.com/blog/openai-to-acquire-promptfoo> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. The central argument of this section is that a prompt, an embedding-model version and a retrieval setting are all production configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A change to any of them can change the output as much as a model upgrade, so each needs versioning, review, an evaluation gate and rollback [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** make Git the system of record for every approved prompt and configuration item, approved by pull request with a second reviewer and an L9 eval gate, and released as one pinned manifest. Use a registry (Langfuse or LangSmith, whichever is the L9 platform) only to deliver approved versions at run time and to link each trace to the version that produced it. Use feature-flag rollout (LaunchDarkly AgentControl, PromptLayer release labels) only to choose between versions that have already been approved [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C5.1 Responsibility

**The problem this control owns.** It owns the *configuration of record* for every GenAI system: the exact set of settings that, together with the input data, determines the output [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. That set is wider than the prompt [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- **Prompts.** System prompt, task templates, few-shot examples, output schemas, house-style instructions.
- **Model configuration.** Provider, model identifier pinned to a dated version, temperature, token limits, reasoning or effort settings.
- **Tool configuration.** The tool allow-list for each workflow step, tool descriptions as the model sees them, and argument schemas (L4).
- **Retrieval configuration.** Embedding model and version, reranker and version, chunking parameters, top-k, filters and fusion weights (L6, L7).
- **Routing configuration.** Primary model, fallback model, region constraints and cost tier, as enforced by the gateway (C1).
- **Policy references.** The guardrail policy version (C2) and the evaluation thresholds that gate release (L9).

**The four jobs.** For that set, the control provides versioning (every item has an immutable version identifier), environment management (development, test and production see different approved versions), change control (review, approval, evaluation gate, release, rollback) and progressive delivery (a new version reaches a segment first, with a kill switch) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**
- *To L3 orchestration and the gateway (C1):* the release manifest that the workflow and gateway load at start-up or fetch at run time [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *To L7:* the pinned embedding and reranker versions. The L7 section already concludes that the embedding model version is production configuration, because changing it forces the whole corpus to be re-embedded, and it asks C5 to hold the pin [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *To L9:* the version identifier, which every trace and every evaluation result must carry. Langfuse links prompt versions to traces so that performance can be analysed by version [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. L9 consumes C5 versions "because each result must reference the exact version it tested" [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *To C8:* change records, approvals and the evidence that the eval gate passed, which form part of model-risk change management [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *From C4:* the identities of the author, the approver and the release pipeline, so that segregation of duties can be enforced [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What C5 does not own.** Secrets and credentials belong to C7 and must never sit in a prompt or configuration file [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Access policy belongs to C4. The evaluation logic and thresholds belong to L9; C5 only records which threshold version applied [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C5.2 Why it matters

Prompts are code that non-engineers can edit, that compilers cannot check, and whose effect is visible only in outputs [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. When this control is weak, four things break [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Unreviewed production changes.** Registry vendors sell the ability to change prompts without a deployment. Langfuse states that "prompt updates deploy instantly, without needing to involve engineering" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. That is useful for iteration and dangerous for a regulated output, unless the production label is protected [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **No reproducibility.** If the trace records only "the latest prompt", nobody can say which version produced a past output [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Silent configuration drift.** A store auto-embedding with an unpinned default model, a model alias that moves to a new snapshot, or a top-k changed in one environment all change outputs without any prompt change [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **No exit.** Prompts held only in a vendor UI must be re-created during a stressed exit, exactly when time is shortest [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A fund-reporting team keeps its commentary prompts in a hosted registry and fetches the version labelled `production` at run time. During month-end, a product analyst notices that drafts describe currency effects too briefly and edits the prompt in the registry UI, moving the `production` label to the new version. The registry has no protected labels, because the team did not buy that tier. The edit also removes a sentence telling the model to state when an effect is below the materiality threshold. Forty commentaries are generated that evening. Several now describe immaterial currency effects as drivers of performance. Reviewers approve most of them because the wording reads well and the numbers still match the attribution engine. Three weeks later, a portfolio manager challenges one commentary. The trace store records the prompt name but not its version, and the registry's history shows several label moves that week, so the team cannot say with confidence which commentaries used which text. Every commentary from that cycle has to be re-reviewed. A protected production label, a pull request with a second approver, a style regression test in the eval gate and a version ID on every trace would each have stopped or contained it. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### C5.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Configuration coverage | Share of production model calls whose prompt, model, tool and retrieval settings all resolve to an approved version ID | 100% for regulated outputs | Version IDs on gateway logs and traces, reconciled to the manifest |
| Unapproved change rate | Production configuration changes without a recorded second approver | Zero | Registry audit log and repository history versus change tickets |
| Eval-gated change share | Production changes that passed the L9 regression suite before release | 100% (emergency changes evaluated within 24 hours) | CI records linked to the release tag |
| Pin compliance | Model and embedding references pinned to a dated version rather than a moving alias | 100% | Static check of the manifest in CI |
| Trace-to-version linkage | Traces carrying prompt, model, retrieval and policy version IDs | ≥99.9% | Trace store query (L9) |
| Rollback time | Time from decision to roll back to the previous approved version serving all traffic | Minutes, not a release cycle | Rollback drill twice a year |
| Change lead time | Time from proposed prompt change to production for a standard change | Days, not weeks; a falling trend | Repository and ticket timestamps |
| Environment drift | Differences between the test manifest and production, other than the change under release | Zero at release | Manifest diff in CI |
| Fallback activation rate | Requests served by a cached or code-side default because the configuration service was unavailable | Near zero; every activation alerted | SDK metrics |
| Emergency change rate | Changes made under the emergency path | Low, and each reviewed after the event | Change records |

### C5.4 How it works

There are two delivery models, and the recommended design combines them [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Registry-first (runtime fetch).** The application asks a registry for "the version with label X" and receives the template.
- *Langfuse.* Every version gets a version ID, and labels assign versions to environments (staging, production), tenants or experiments [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. SDKs cache prompts client-side, so a fetch adds no network latency on the hot path [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Fetching a label that no version carries returns an error rather than falling back to another version, so a typo fails loudly; the SDKs support a fallback prompt for that case [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Protected prompt labels let project admins and owners stop labels from being moved or deleted; they are an Enterprise feature when self-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *LangSmith.* Prompts are stored as commits with diffs. Staging and Production are reserved commit tags assigned through a promotion step, and each environment keeps an ordered rollback history [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. "Owners only" mode limits who may tag, promote or delete a prompt, webhooks fire on every commit, and prompts can be synchronised with a GitHub repository [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *PromptLayer.* Release labels such as `prod` select the served version, and support staged rollouts and segmenting users to specific versions [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S088: PromptLayer docs: Release Labels <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/features/prompt-registry/release-labels.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *LaunchDarkly AgentControl.* The application requests a configuration for a user context. The service returns model name, parameters and messages, with a code-side default used if the service is unavailable, and a tracker records tokens, latency and success per configuration [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Git-first (prompts as code).** Prompt files live in the application repository. A `.prompty` file is markdown with YAML front matter for model, connection and template settings; Dotprompt is an executable template format extending Handlebars [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S066: Dotprompt README (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/dotprompt/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Changes go through code review and CI, where a CLI such as Promptfoo runs evaluations against the files [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S068: Promptfoo README (Promptfoo (OpenAI)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/promptfoo/promptfoo/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. The release tag pins prompt and configuration together with the code [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**The recommended hybrid [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** Git is the record. CI evaluates every change against the L9 suite, then publishes the approved version to the registry and moves the environment label using a release-pipeline identity, which is the only identity allowed to move protected production labels. The application fetches by label, with a cached copy and a code-side default. Every trace carries the manifest version.

```text
 author (analyst / engineer)
     │  edit prompt, model pin, top-k, embedding version, fallback route
     ▼
 Git repository (system of record) ── pull request ── 2nd approver (risk owner via CODEOWNERS)
     │                                     │
     │                                     ▼
     │                         CI: L9 regression + style + numeric-faithfulness evals
     │                                     │ pass
     ▼                                     ▼
 release manifest vN (prompt vX, model id@date, embed model@ver, reranker@ver, k, policy vY)
     │  signed tag
     ├──► registry: publish vX, move protected label "production" (release identity only)
     ├──► gateway C1: routing + fallback config
     └──► C8 evidence: approval, eval results, diff
                                   │
 runtime:  L3 workflow ── fetch label (SDK cache, code-side default) ──► L1/L2 via C1
                                   │
                                   ▼
                 trace (L9) carries manifest vN + prompt vX  ──► rollback = move label to vN-1
```

**Progressive delivery.** Feature-flag style rollout is useful for prompts in the same way as for code: release a new version to an internal segment, compare evaluations and reviewer edit rates, then widen [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. AgentControl and PromptLayer release labels provide the targeting mechanics [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S088: PromptLayer docs: Release Labels <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/features/prompt-registry/release-labels.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. For a regulated output, the variants being compared must both have passed the approval and eval gate; rollout is a way to limit exposure, not a substitute for approval [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C5.5 Enterprise design principles

**Security**
- Never put secrets, client identifiers or credentials into prompt templates or configuration files [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The OWASP 2025 list names System Prompt Leakage (LLM07) as a risk category, cited for traceability [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A8-S040: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-llm-applications-2025/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; assume any prompt can be extracted [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Treat the production label or branch as a privileged resource. Langfuse's protected labels and LangSmith's owners-only mode exist for this purpose [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- A third-party registry that proxies model calls (PromptLayer's SDK can proxy provider SDK calls for logging [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07]) becomes part of the data path for prompts and outputs. Decide that deliberately, not by default [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Resilience**
- The configuration service must not be a single point of failure. Client-side caching (Langfuse [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]) and code-side defaults (LaunchDarkly [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07]) are the two patterns; use one, and alert when it activates [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- The default must itself be an approved version. A stale hard-coded default is an unreviewed configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Governance**
- **Everything that changes the output is configuration.** Prompt, model version, embedding version, reranker, top-k, tool list and guardrail policy are versioned together in one manifest [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Pin, never float.** Model and embedding references must name a dated version, so that the provider's alias moving does not silently change the system [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Segregation of duties.** The author cannot approve their own production change [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Classify changes.** A wording change that passes the regression suite is a standard change. A model, embedding or tool change is a material change that triggers re-validation. A change of purpose goes to the model-risk owner (C5.11) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Observability and cost**
- The version ID belongs on every trace span and every evaluation result, otherwise the evaluation evidence in L9 cannot be tied to a configuration [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Pricing models differ: AgentControl meters every model call and judge run as an "AI run" [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S118: LaunchDarkly Pricing; subscriptions and plans; calculating billing <https://launchdarkly.com/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; LangSmith prices per seat plus traces [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A1-S035: LangSmith Plans and Pricing (LangChain, Inc.) <https://www.langchain.com/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; Langfuse's governance controls sit in its paid Enterprise tier [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Model the cost at production volume [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Portability**
- Keep the canonical prompt text in a file format you control, so the registry is a cache of Git, not the other way round [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. LangSmith's GitHub synchronisation is the only registry-to-Git bridge documented in the fact base [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** Git as record with CI publishing to a registry; one release manifest per system; protected production label moved only by the pipeline identity; version ID on every trace; dual-run or segment rollout for material changes; rollback drills.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** editing production prompts in a vendor UI; floating model aliases; embedding models chosen by a store default; prompts assembled from string literals scattered through the code; feature-flag variants that were never evaluated; a "fallback" prompt nobody has reviewed for a year; separate, unlinked version numbers for prompt, model and retrieval.

### C5.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Immutable versions and diffs; environment labels; promotion and rollback history; approval or owner controls; segmentation and progressive rollout; coverage beyond prompts (model, parameters, tools, retrieval settings); trace linkage; webhooks for CI |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC with a separate right to move production labels, audit log of label moves with before-and-after versions, SCIM, SLA; whether these are licence-gated |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in product scope; residency of prompt text and any proxied traffic; CMK; FedRAMP or ISO 42001 for 5 |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | Self-host or customer-cloud deployment so that prompt text and configuration stay in-estate; behaviour when the service is unreachable |
| Ecosystem (5%) | SDK languages, framework integrations, Git synchronisation, webhooks |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | Time in GA, renames and repositioning, ownership stability |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Pricing unit (seats, traces, runs); which governance controls are in paid tiers |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Export to plain files; Git sync; open file formats; whether runtime fetch can be replaced by a file read |

### C5.7 Product deep dives

The Langfuse and LangSmith platforms are profiled in L9 §9.7 (ownership, certifications, pricing, deployment). The records below cover only their prompt-management capability and refer back to §9.7 for the rest [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Langfuse Prompt Management (ClickHouse).**
- *What it is now:* a capability of the Langfuse platform (docs v4; Python SDK 4.17.0, 5 October 2026) that stores, versions and serves prompts. Each version gets a version ID, and labels select which version the SDK fetches [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S009: langfuse on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / Langfuse) <https://pypi.org/pypi/langfuse/json> accessed 2026-10-07]. Prompt versions are linked to traces [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. Platform profile: see §9.7.
- *Governance controls:* protected prompt labels, project-level RBAC, audit logs, SCIM and the Org Management API need an Enterprise licence key when self-hosted [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. The core, including prompt management, is MIT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S075: Langfuse README (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Run-time behaviour:* prompts are cached client-side by the SDK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. A missing label is an error, not a silent fallback, and the SDKs support a fallback prompt [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Hosting:* Cloud regions in the US, EU (Ireland), Japan and a HIPAA region; self-hosted in any region, including fully offline [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S073: Langfuse Security and Compliance overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/security/index.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07].
- *Strengths:* prompt versions, traces and evaluation results in one store, which is the shortest path to "which version produced this output" [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* the controls that make it safe for regulated prompts are the paid part [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07]. No pull-request approval flow or Git synchronisation is documented in the fact base [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* Langfuse is your L9 platform of record [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* you will not license Enterprise, since then any writer can move the production label [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* LangSmith prompts, PromptLayer, prompts as code.

- **Tier: Strategic, conditional: only where Langfuse is the L9 platform and the Enterprise licence is bought (FS 3.85 after the CP3 alignment with L9). Flag: Acquired.**

### C5.9 Decision tree

Steps 0 and 3 are not product choices; they are applied whatever is selected [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): Git is the system of record. One release manifest per system pins
prompt, model id@date, embedding model@version, reranker@version, retrieval params, tool list,
fallback route and guardrail policy. PR with second approver; L9 eval gate in CI.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Do you need run-time delivery (change without redeploying the application)?
  ├─ No  → Prompts as code only (Prompty or Dotprompt files, loaded at build or start-up)
  └─ Yes → Which L9 platform of record did you choose?
           ├─ Langfuse  → Langfuse prompts, Enterprise licence, protected "production" label
           ├─ LangSmith → LangSmith prompts, owners-only mode, GitHub sync on
           └─ Other / none → Must prompt text stay in-estate?
                    ├─ Yes → PromptLayer in your AWS account (after SOC 2 report review),
                    │        or self-hosted Langfuse used only as a registry
                    └─ No  → PromptLayer SaaS or the L9 platform's own registry

STEP 2 [Rec]: Do you need segment rollout, A/B or kill switches for model/prompt variants?
  ├─ LaunchDarkly is the firm's feature-flag standard → AgentControl, selecting only
  │                                                    between approved, pinned variants
  ├─ PromptLayer chosen in step 1                      → release labels / dynamic release labels
  └─ Otherwise                                         → registry labels per segment, or gateway
                                                         (C1) weighted routing between pinned models

STEP 3 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Production label movable only by the release identity?  Version ID on every trace?
  Cached or code-side default is an approved version?  Rollback drilled?
  Embedding/reranker versions in the manifest, matching the index's model_version tag (L7)?
```

### C5.10 Lock-in classification

| Element | Classification [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Rationale | Abstraction to use [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prompt text and templates | **Unacceptable if held only in a vendor registry; acceptable in Git** | They are the firm's intellectual property and the content of any stressed exit | Canonical files (Prompty or Dotprompt) in the repository; the registry is a cache |
| Template syntax | **Manageable** | Prompty, Dotprompt and registry syntaxes differ [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S066: Dotprompt README (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/dotprompt/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] | Keep templates simple (variables, sections); avoid vendor-specific logic in templates |
| Runtime fetch API | **Manageable** | Each registry has its own SDK [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] | A thin internal `get_config(system, env)` interface with a file-based fallback |
| Rollout and targeting rules | **Manageable** | Targeting logic in a flag service is proprietary [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] | Keep rules simple and documented in the manifest; record variation on traces |
| Change history and approvals | **Unacceptable if only in a vendor audit log** | It is model-risk evidence with a retention requirement | Repository history plus export of registry audit logs to the C8 archive |
| Model and embedding pins | **Acceptable** | They name provider versions, which is the point [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Manifest field per system; gateway enforces |

### C5.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Model risk: a prompt change can be a model change.**
- *SS1/23.* PRA SS1/23 applies to all models used to inform business decisions, including vendor models, and sets five principles: identification and classification, governance, development and implementation, independent validation, and risk mitigants [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S037: Bank of England/PRA letter to DSIT and HMT on AI (2024) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/letter/2024/dsit-hmt-letter.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. It applies to banks, building societies and PRA-designated investment firms with internal-model approval for credit, market or counterparty credit risk capital; insurers are not covered [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Applying it here.* For an LLM-based system, the "model" a validator approved is the combination of foundation model, prompt, retrieval configuration and tools [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Changing the system prompt or the embedding model can change outputs as much as changing the foundation model [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The firm's change policy should therefore define which configuration changes are material and trigger re-validation, and record each change against the inventory entry [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 superseded SR 11-7 on 17 April 2026 and expressly excludes generative and agentic AI. For those tools, the firm's own risk-management practices determine governance and controls [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. No US regulator therefore defines prompt change control; the firm must set its own standard [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Writing it to SS1/23 quality is the defensible choice [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Effective challenge.* SR 26-2 retains effective challenge by independent reviewers for in-scope models [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The equivalent here is that a second person, ideally the risk owner for the use case, approves production configuration changes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Segregation of duties.** The control must stop one person from writing, approving and releasing a production prompt [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The products offer different mechanisms: protected labels (Langfuse Enterprise) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S072: Langfuse docs: Prompt version control (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/features/prompt-version-control.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S074: Langfuse docs: Enterprise License Key (self-hosted) (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/self-hosting/license-key.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], owners-only promotion (LangSmith) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07], custom roles (LaunchDarkly Enterprise) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C5-S001: Using SSO with LaunchDarkly; Configure SAML SSO; Creating custom roles <https://launchdarkly.com/docs/guides/account/sso> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] and pull-request approval rules in source control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Whichever is used, the release-pipeline identity should be the only one that can move a production label (C4) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**EU AI Act.**
- *Deployer logging.* Article 26 requires deployers of high-risk systems to keep logs for at least six months, folded into financial-services documentation for financial institutions; Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-EU-OMNIBUS-AI: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 ('Digital Omnibus on AI') amending Regulations (EU) 2024/1689, 2018/1139 and 2023/1230 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Configuration version IDs are what make those logs interpretable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Changing purpose through configuration.* Under Article 25, a deployer becomes a provider if it substantially modifies a high-risk system or changes the intended purpose of an AI system so that it becomes high-risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-EUAIA: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S011: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EUR-Lex / Official Journal of the EU) <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. A system prompt is where intended purpose is most easily changed [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A prompt change that extends a commentary tool into, for example, HR screening is a regulatory event, not a wording change [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Purpose-changing edits should be routed to the AI inventory owner (C8) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Scope for this use case.* Attribution commentary is not an Annex III use; the live duties are AI literacy and transparency [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Operational resilience, DORA and outsourcing.**
- *Third-party status.* A SaaS registry or configuration service that delivers prompts to a production system is an ICT third-party service and belongs in the DORA register of information, with Article 30 terms and an exit strategy where it supports a critical or important function [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. DORA's CTPP list and the UK CTP designations cover hyperscalers, not model or AI-tooling vendors [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Run-time dependency.* A configuration service on the request path is a new availability dependency. Cached prompts and code-side defaults turn it into a degraded mode rather than an outage [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S089: LaunchDarkly Server-Side AI SDK for Python README <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/launchdarkly/python-server-sdk-ai/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Exit.* SS2/21 expects documented, tested exit plans that cover unexpected termination [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Portable prompts and configuration, together with the gateway (C1) and the eval suite (L9), are what make a stressed exit from a model vendor feasible [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Residency and auditability.**
- *Prompt text can be sensitive.* Prompts may embed house views, client segment rules or examples drawn from real commentary [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. FG16/5 expects data location and effective access for outsourced IT [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S049: FCA Handbook SYSC 8.1; FG16/5; Reporting material third party arrangements (Financial Conduct Authority) <https://handbook.fca.org.uk/handbook/sysc8/sysc8s1> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
