An approved, pinned configuration is the ex-ante control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C5.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from C5 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary (allocation, selection, currency, benchmark-relative return) for a generic multi-asset fund. From this control it needs six things:
1. **A versioned commentary prompt set.** System prompt, section templates (allocation, selection, currency, outlook) and the house-style rules, stored as Prompty or Dotprompt files in the commentary repository. The style rules include the materiality-threshold sentence from the C5.2 scenario as a tested requirement.
2. **A release manifest per monthly cycle.** For example, `commentary-release 2026.10`: prompt set v14, drafting model pinned to a dated version with temperature 0, fallback model pinned, embedding model and reranker versions matching the `model_version` tag on the prior-commentary index (L7), top-k 8, read-only tool list (attribution engine, approved market notes), guardrail policy v6 and eval threshold set v3. The values are illustrative.
3. **Approval by pull request.** The author is the reporting analyst or engineer. A second approver from the investment-risk function is mandatory through CODEOWNERS. The pull request shows the diff of prompt text and of every manifest field.
4. **An eval gate, linked to L9.** CI runs the regression suite of past commentaries, the deterministic numeric-faithfulness check and the house-style checks against the new manifest, and attaches the results to the pull request. A failing check blocks the merge. A material change (model, embedding or tool) also requires the validator's sign-off.
5. **Pinned per release, delivered at run time.** On merge, the pipeline tags the release, publishes the prompt set to the registry and moves the protected `production` label. Month-end runs fetch by label, with a cached copy, and fall back to the previous approved release if the registry is unreachable. The release is frozen for the duration of the month-end cycle.
6. **Version on every trace and in the evidence pack.** Each draft's trace carries the manifest and prompt version, and the C8 evidence pack records them with the approver and the eval results. Rollback means moving the label to the previous release and re-running the affected funds.

**What C5 must never allow [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- a production prompt edited in a registry UI outside the pull-request path
- a drafting, fallback or embedding model referenced by a moving alias
- the author approving their own production change
- a feature-flag variant reaching portfolio managers before it has passed the eval gate
- a commentary whose trace cannot name the manifest that produced it
- a vendor auto-fix (LangSmith Engine, Braintrust Loop; see L9 §9.12) changing a production prompt outside change control

### C5.13 Original → current → recommended

| Original (graphic) | Current (October 2026) | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| (absent) prompt management | A capability inside L9 platforms: Langfuse prompts and LangSmith prompts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07] | Registry for run-time delivery and trace linkage, fed from Git by CI [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| (absent) configuration management | LaunchDarkly AI Configs, renamed AgentControl in 2026 and repositioned towards agent operations [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S117: LaunchDarkly: Introducing AgentControl; AI Configs is now GA; AgentControl API docs <https://launchdarkly.com/blog/introducing-agentcontrol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S045: AgentControl API docs (LaunchDarkly) <https://launchdarkly.com/docs/api/agentcontrol> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] | Tactical: progressive rollout between approved variants where LaunchDarkly is the standard [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| (absent) standalone registry | PromptLayer, independent, with Enterprise identity and customer-AWS deployment [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S086: PromptLayer docs: Enterprise Identity overview <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/why-promptlayer/enterprise-identity/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S087: PromptLayer docs: Deploy PromptLayer on AWS <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagnivOrg/prompt-layer-docs/main/enterprise-deployments/aws.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07] | Tactical: framework-neutral registry where no L9 registry exists [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| (absent) Git-based patterns | Prompty v2 and Dotprompt as open formats; Promptfoo configs in CI, with OpenAI's acquisition announced 9 March 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S067: Prompty README (Microsoft) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/prompty/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S066: Dotprompt README (Google) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/dotprompt/main/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07; V2-S042: OpenAI to acquire Promptfoo (with TechCrunch via Yahoo Finance, SDxCentral, Security Boulevard) <https://openai.com/blog/openai-to-acquire-promptfoo> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] | Strategic: Git as the system of record for all production configuration [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
| Embedding models shown only as a component (L7) | Embedding version is production configuration (L7 §7.13) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | Embedding and reranker versions pinned in the C5 manifest [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |

**Relevant hypotheses: H6 (embeddings and reranking as one retrieval-optimisation layer) and H8 (evaluation and observability are cross-cutting). Provisional view; verdict in synthesis.**

- **H6.** L7 proposes naming embedding-model versioning as a governed configuration item [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. C5 is where that governance lives: the manifest pins the embedding and reranker versions, and the release process enforces the dual-index migration that L7 describes [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. This supports H6 and adds a dependency: the retrieval-optimisation layer needs C5 to hold its pins [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **H8.** Every prompt registry in the market is part of an observability platform (Langfuse, LangSmith) or adds evaluation and tracing of its own (PromptLayer, AgentControl's online evals) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S071: Langfuse docs: Prompt Management overview (Langfuse (ClickHouse)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/main/content/docs/prompt-management/overview.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S076: LangSmith docs: Manage prompts (LangChain) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/docs/main/src/langsmith/manage-prompts.mdx> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S004: promptlayer on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / PromptLayer) <https://pypi.org/pypi/promptlayer/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S117: LaunchDarkly: Introducing AgentControl; AI Configs is now GA; AgentControl API docs <https://launchdarkly.com/blog/introducing-agentcontrol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Vendors treat prompt management and evaluation as one loop, which supports H8 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Is C5 a control or a product category?** The evidence suggests C5 is a responsibility, not a product box [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Its products are features of L9 platforms or of feature-flag services, while the record that matters for regulators is the firm's own repository and approval trail [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Provisional recommendation.** Keep C5 as a named control in the reference architecture, defined by responsibility (the configuration of record and its change control) rather than by product [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Draw it next to C8, because its output is change evidence, with run-time delivery shown as a capability of the L9 platform [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Provisional; verdict in synthesis.**


## C6. AI FinOps

> **Executive summary.** This control makes the cost of GenAI visible, attributable, bounded and improvable: what each task costs, who pays for it, when spending must stop, and which design choices would make it cheaper without making it worse. The original graphic has no box for it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Four things have changed in the market. First, the measurement point has settled on the gateway: every model call passes through it, and gateways now ship budgets, rate limits and spend tracking per key, team and user [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S019: Cloudflare AI Gateway docs: Pricing, Features, Changelog; Cloudflare blog spend limits (Cloudflare, Inc.) <https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/reference/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. Second, the independent tooling is consolidating. Helicone was acquired by Mintlify on 3 March 2026 and is in maintenance mode [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S112: Helicone Blog: Helicone acquired by Mintlify (and Mintlify announcement) (Helicone / Mintlify) <https://www.helicone.ai/blog> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S043: Helicone Joins Mintlify (with mintlify.com 'Mintlify acquires Helicone'; PostHog comparison) (Helicone / Mintlify) <https://www.helicone.ai/blog/joining-mintlify> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]], and Portkey was acquired by Palo Alto Networks on 29 May 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S011: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Portkey to Secure AI Agents (and 30 Apr 2026 announcement) <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2026/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-portkey-to-secure-ai-agents> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; V2-S025: Palo Alto Networks Completes Acquisition of Portkey to Secure AI Agents (with PANW FY2026 10-K and 10-Q, SDxCentral) <https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/company/press/2026/palo-alto-networks-completes-acquisition-of-portkey-to-secure-ai-agents> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Third, the cloud-cost vendors Vantage and CloudZero have added AI-provider integrations, described mainly in their own blog posts [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S114: CloudZero blog posts on AI cost (token-based pricing, Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) <https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/token-based-pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Fourth, the open billing standard is catching up but is not there yet. FOCUS 1.4 was ratified on 4 June 2026. FOCUS 1.5, which has no ratification date, adds AI model-identity properties, and a first-class input/output token-type column has been deferred [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S046: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope: Confirmed and Stretch Features (with Introducing FOCUS 1.4; FOCUS for AI) (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; A7-S116: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope; FOCUS for AI; Introducing FOCUS 1.2; Introducing FOCUS 1.4 (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The central argument is that the metric that matters is cost per task, not cost per token [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. A cheaper token that needs three retries and a longer human review is not cheaper [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. **Recommendation:** meter and enforce at the gateway (C1), with virtual keys per use case and fund; join gateway records to L9 traces to report cost per completed task; reconcile monthly against provider usage APIs and cloud bills; land everything in a FOCUS-shaped dataset the firm owns; and pair every budget with an enforcement point that fails closed. Treat a FinOps SaaS tool (Vantage, CloudZero) as an optional reporting layer, not the system of record [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C6.1 Responsibility

**The problem this control owns.** It owns the economics of the GenAI estate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:

- **Token economics.** Understanding what drives the bill: input versus output tokens, cached versus fresh input, model tier, batch versus interactive, region premiums, judge-model calls and retries [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Cost attribution.** Every unit of spend tagged to a use case, cost centre, fund or client segment, and to a completed task [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Budgets and enforcement.** Financial limits paired with technical limits that stop or degrade spend when breached [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Showback and chargeback.** Reporting cost to the owners who generate it, and where policy allows, charging it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Optimisation.** Caching, routing to smaller models, batching, prompt and context trimming, and removing waste such as retries and runaway loops, each validated so that quality does not fall [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Unit economics.** Cost per task, per approved output and per business outcome, compared with the cost of the process it replaces [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Hand-offs.**
- *From C1 gateway:* per-request token counts, model, key and metadata; enforcement of budgets and rate limits [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *From L9:* the trace that groups model calls, tool calls and evaluation calls into one task, and the outcome of that task (approved, edited, rejected) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. L9 reports cost per task to C6 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *From L3:* per-run step and token ceilings, which are the agent-level enforcement point [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *From L1/L2 providers and clouds:* usage and cost APIs and billing exports, which are the reconciliation source [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07; B-C6-S004: Amazon Bedrock user guide: Application inference profiles; Best practices for cost attribution (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-application-inference-profiles.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; B-C6-S005: Plan and manage costs - Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/manage-costs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
- *To C5:* a cost-driven change (a cheaper model, a shorter prompt) is a configuration change and goes through C5 change control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *To C8 and procurement:* spend by provider for concentration analysis and the outsourcing register [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What C6 does not own.** It does not choose models; L1 and the model-risk process do, with cost as one input [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It does not own the gateway, only the rules the gateway enforces for spend [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C6.2 Why it matters

GenAI spend behaves differently from cloud infrastructure spend [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. It scales with usage and with agent behaviour rather than with provisioned capacity; it can grow by orders of magnitude when an agent loops; and prices change quickly [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The FinOps Foundation's State of FinOps 2026 reports that 98% of respondents now manage AI spend and that FinOps for AI is the top forward-looking priority [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. CloudZero states that its customers typically end up at 1.5 to 2 times their initial Amazon Bedrock estimates [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S114: CloudZero blog posts on AI cost (token-based pricing, Bedrock, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) <https://www.cloudzero.com/blog/token-based-pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; that is a vendor statement and not a decision input [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

When this control is weak, four things break [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
- **Runaway spend.** An agent in a retry loop consumes tokens until someone notices the invoice.
- **No accountability.** A single provider account and one API key per environment means nobody can say which use case spent what.
- **Wrong optimisation.** Teams chase price per token, switch to a cheaper model, and lose more in retries and review time than they save.
- **Weak exit and concentration evidence.** Without spend by provider, the firm cannot show regulators how concentrated it is, or size an exit.

**Illustrative scenario [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** A research team runs an agent that summarises broker notes overnight. On a Friday a document-store tool starts returning a malformed error. The agent's planner treats each error as a reason to re-read the full document set and try again, and the workflow has no step limit. The team had set a monthly budget on the gateway, but the gateway was deployed without the database its budget feature needs, so the budget was never enforced. The fact base records that LiteLLM's `max_budget` fails open without a database, and that the proxy admin key bypasses budget checks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The loop runs for 60 hours. Nothing breaks visibly: the provider keeps answering, and the summaries are simply never produced. On Monday, the provider's rate limit for the shared organisation account has been consumed, and the client-facing assistant, which uses the same account, is throttled during market open. The finance team sees the spend two weeks later on the invoice. A per-run step and token ceiling in the workflow, a gateway budget tested to fail closed, an anomaly alert on tool calls per task, and separate keys and limits per use case would each have stopped or contained it. The scenario is invented; it is not a reported incident.

### C6.3 Goals and KPIs

| KPI | Definition | Target guidance [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} | How it is measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cost per completed task | All model, judge and tool-call cost for one task that reached its outcome, divided by completed tasks | Per use case; falling trend at constant quality | Gateway records joined to L9 traces by run ID |
| Cost per approved output | Cost per task including failed and regenerated attempts, per output a human approved | Per use case; compared with the manual baseline | Trace outcome (approved, edited, rejected) |
| Attribution coverage | Share of AI spend tagged to a use case and cost centre | ≥98% | Gateway key metadata reconciled to invoice |
| Invoice reconciliation variance | Difference between gateway-metered cost and provider or cloud billing | Within ±2% monthly | Provider usage API and billing export versus gateway |
| Budget enforcement coverage | Share of production keys with an enforced budget and rate limit that fails closed | 100% | Gateway configuration audit and a fail-closed test |
| Time to detect anomalous spend | From the start of an anomaly to an alert | Under 1 hour for agent workloads | Alert timestamps versus trace data |
| Retry rate and tool calls per task | Model retries and tool invocations per completed task | Stable band per workflow; spikes alerted | Traces; FinOps Foundation lists both as waste diagnostics [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] |
| Cache hit rate | Share of input tokens served from provider prompt cache or gateway cache | Rising for stable prompts | Provider usage data (cached vs uncached input) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07] |
| Model mix | Share of spend on the smallest model that passes the eval gate for each step | Rising | Gateway records by model |
| Forecast accuracy | Forecast versus actual monthly spend per use case | Within ±15% | Budget versus actual |
| Provider concentration | Share of AI spend with the largest provider | Reported quarterly to the third-party risk committee | FOCUS-shaped dataset by provider |

**Target guidance from the FinOps Foundation.** Its tokenomics guidance is to instrument and measure for 30 to 60 days, set budgets at 110% to 120% of that baseline, and alert at 80% and 100% [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. It also states: "Pair every financial cap with an engineering enforcement point. A budget without a quota is a number, not a control." [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

### C6.4 How it works

The mechanics have five stages: meter, attribute, reconcile, enforce and optimise [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

1. **Meter at the gateway.** Every model call goes through the gateway with a virtual key per use case (and, where needed, per fund or client segment) and request metadata carrying the run ID [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. LiteLLM provides virtual keys, budgets at key, user, team and customer level, TPM and RPM limits, and spend tracking; a database is required for global budgets and spend tracking [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Managed gateways offer equivalents: token limits and quotas per consumer key in Azure API Management [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07], token-limit enforcement and consumption monitoring in Apigee [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S024: Apigee AI solutions: gateway to enterprise-ready AI (Google Cloud) <https://cloud.google.com/solutions/apigee-ai> accessed 2026-10-07], token budgeting and rate limiting in Kong [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S016: Kong AI Gateway 2.0 Is Now GA — And It's Already Moving Faster (Kong Inc.) <https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/kong-ai-gateway-2-0-ga> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], and cost-based spend limits and identity-based per-user budgets in Cloudflare AI Gateway [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S019: Cloudflare AI Gateway docs: Pricing, Features, Changelog; Cloudflare blog spend limits (Cloudflare, Inc.) <https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/reference/pricing/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
2. **Attribute to tasks.** The gateway knows tokens per call; L9 knows which calls form a task and what the task's outcome was [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Joining them on run ID gives cost per task and cost per approved output [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
3. **Reconcile with the provider and the cloud.** Gateway prices are estimates from a price table; invoices are the truth [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
   - *Direct provider APIs.* Anthropic's Usage & Cost Admin API reports usage by API key, workspace, model and service tier, separating uncached input, cached input, cache creation and output tokens; it needs an Admin API key, and workspace keys do not work [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07].
   - *Amazon Bedrock.* Application inference profiles carry cost allocation tags into Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report. Granularity is per usage type per day, not per request, so per-request attribution needs invocation logs or gateway data [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S004: Amazon Bedrock user guide: Application inference profiles; Best practices for cost attribution (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-application-inference-profiles.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
   - *Microsoft Foundry.* Azure OpenAI is token-metered by model, deployment type and meter. Project-level cost attribution tags each Foundry project's usage automatically (preview, models sold by Azure only), and cost data appears with a delay of about five hours [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S005: Plan and manage costs - Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/manage-costs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].
   - *Google Vertex AI.* Labels for model cost attribution were not verified in this run [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
4. **Normalise to a FOCUS-shaped dataset.** FOCUS has no AI-specific columns today; tokens are carried by SKU IDs indicating token charges, ConsumedUnit and ConsumedQuantity, and FOCUS 1.2 added columns for virtual currencies such as credits and tokens [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S116: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope; FOCUS for AI; Introducing FOCUS 1.2; Introducing FOCUS 1.4 (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. FOCUS 1.5 is scoped to add AI pricing dimensions (cached versus fresh tokens, global versus regional serving) on SkuPriceDetails and four model properties, ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily, ModelId and ModelVersion, with no new columns; a token-type column is deferred and no ratification date has been published [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S046: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope: Confirmed and Stretch Features (with Introducing FOCUS 1.4; FOCUS for AI) (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Map tokens to SKU and ConsumedQuantity now, and add the model properties when 1.5 is ratified [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
5. **Enforce and optimise.** Budgets act at three levels: per run (step and token ceilings in the L3 workflow), per key (gateway budgets and rate limits) and per month (financial budget and alerts) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Optimisation proposals go through C5 change control and the L9 eval gate before release [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
 L3 workflow (run_id, step ceiling, token ceiling per run)
      │ every model / judge call, metadata: use_case, fund, run_id
      ▼
 C1 gateway ── virtual key per use case ── budget + RPM/TPM limit (must fail CLOSED) ── alert
      │ per-request tokens, model, cost estimate
      ├──────────────► L9 traces (task grouping, outcome: approved / edited / rejected)
      │                         │ join on run_id
      ▼                         ▼
 AI cost dataset (FOCUS-shaped, firm-owned) ◄── reconcile monthly ── provider usage APIs
      │   cost per task · per approved output · per fund      cloud billing (Bedrock tags,
      │                                                       Foundry project tags)
      ├──► showback / chargeback to owners          (optional: Vantage / CloudZero reporting)
      ├──► concentration by provider → C8 / outsourcing register
      └──► optimisation backlog → C5 change + L9 eval gate → release
```

**Where the money goes in an agent.** For a multi-step agent, the cost of one task is the sum of every planning call, tool-result summarisation call, retry, evaluation-judge call and regeneration after a reviewer rejection [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. That is why the unit has to be the task, and why the trace is the only record that can assemble it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C6.5 Enterprise design principles

**Unit economics first**
- Report cost per completed task and per approved output, not cost per token or per call [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Include judge calls and regenerations [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Compare against the cost of the process being replaced, including human review time. For most drafting use cases, reviewer time is larger than the token bill [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Enforcement that fails closed**
- Pair every budget with an enforcement point [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Test it: deploy the budget, exceed it in a test environment, and confirm requests are refused [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Know the failure modes of the chosen gateway. In LiteLLM, `max_budget` without a database does not enforce, prompt-injection guardrails are off by default, and the proxy admin key bypasses budget checks [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Restrict the admin key to break-glass use under C4 [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Put step and token ceilings in the workflow (L3), because a gateway budget sized for a month will not stop a loop within an hour [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Separate experimental from run-rate AI spend; the FinOps Foundation recommends this split [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].

**Attribution design**
- One virtual key per use case and environment as the minimum; per fund or client segment where chargeback needs it [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Shared keys destroy attribution [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Use cloud-native tagging where models are consumed through a cloud: Bedrock application inference profiles [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S004: Amazon Bedrock user guide: Application inference profiles; Best practices for cost attribution (Amazon Web Services) <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-application-inference-profiles.html> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] and Foundry project tags [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S005: Plan and manage costs - Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/manage-costs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

**Optimisation levers (each needs an eval gate) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}**
- *Prompt caching.* Provider cache reads are far cheaper than fresh input. Claude Opus 5.5 lists US$4 per 1M input tokens and US$0.20 per 1M cache-read tokens (as of 7 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Kimi K3 is reported at US$3 and US$0.30; Chinese-vendor API prices are on the verifiers' do-not-rely list, so this is Reported and not a decision input [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A5-S069: Kimi K3 Tech Blog; Kimi K3 API quickstart and pricing; moonshotai/Kimi-K3 LICENSE (Hugging Face) (Moonshot AI) <https://www.kimi.com/en/blog/kimi-k3> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Stable system prompts and style guides placed first in the context benefit most [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Gateway caching.* LiteLLM offers exact and semantic caching, and Azure API Management offers semantic caching [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S015: LiteLLM docs: MCP Overview, Agent Gateway (A2A), Caching, Budgets/Rate Limits, v1.89.0 release notes (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A6-S053: AI gateway capabilities in Azure API Management (Microsoft Learn source, ms.date 29 May 2026) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs/main/articles/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. A semantic cache returns an answer to a *similar* question, which is unacceptable for outputs that must reflect this month's data [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Use exact caching only for regulated outputs [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Routing to smaller models.* The price spread inside one vendor's range is large: gpt-6-luna lists US$0.10 input and US$0.50 output per 1M tokens, against US$10 and US$50 for gpt-6-astra (as of 7 October 2026) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S004: OpenAI API Pricing (and Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna pricing) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Classification, extraction and judging steps can often use the small model if the eval gate agrees [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Batching.* Anthropic's and OpenAI's batch APIs are 50% off list price [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S004: OpenAI API Pricing (and Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna pricing) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Azure offers discounted Flex processing for delay-tolerant workloads [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — B-C6-S005: Plan and manage costs - Microsoft Foundry <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/manage-costs> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]]. Month-end drafting that is reviewed the next morning is a batch workload [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Context discipline.* Long prompts can move into a higher price band: Claude Haiku 5.5 is US$0.10/US$0.50 per 1M for prompts up to 100K tokens and US$0.50/US$2.50 above [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Retrieve less, better (L7) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Residency has a price.* Anthropic's US-only inference geography costs 1.1 times standard [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07]. Budget for residency choices explicitly [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Prices move.* OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna were priced 50% below GPT-5.6 promotional pricing [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S001: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol / GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna (with help-centre preview article and API changelog) (OpenAI) <https://openai.com/index/previewing-gpt-5-6-sol/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Re-run the cost model quarterly and keep the price table in the gateway under change control [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Security**
- Provider admin keys are powerful credentials. Vantage's Anthropic integration uses an Admin API key, which has revocable read-write access [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Grant third-party cost tools the least privilege the provider allows and rotate keys (C4, C7) [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- Cost exports should carry metadata, not prompts or outputs [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** gateway metering with virtual keys per use case; run ID joined to traces; FOCUS-shaped firm-owned dataset; monthly reconciliation; three-level enforcement (run, key, month); cost dashboards that show cost per approved output next to quality KPIs; optimisation as a change through C5 and L9.

**Anti-patterns [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:** one API key per environment; budgets that alert but never block; optimising price per token without measuring retries and review time; semantic caching of regulated outputs; a FinOps SaaS tool as the only record; a cheaper model swapped in by the platform team without re-validation.

### C6.6 Product selection criteria

| Scorecard criterion | What to evaluate in this control [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"} |
|---|---|
| Technical (15% FS) | Per-request metering; budgets and rate limits at key, team, user and customer level; fail-closed behaviour; token-type breakdown (cached, uncached, output); allocation rules; task-level joins; forecasting and anomaly detection |
| Enterprise readiness (15%) | SSO, RBAC scoped to cost data, audit of budget and key changes, SCIM, SLA |
| Security and compliance (20%) | SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in scope; privilege required on provider admin keys; whether prompts or outputs are ingested |
| Deployment flexibility (15%) | In-estate metering (self-hosted gateway); SaaS region for billing metadata |
| Ecosystem (5%) | Providers and clouds covered; FOCUS export or mapping; API access to the cost data |
| Reliability and maturity (10%) | Ownership stability (Helicone, Portkey), maintenance status, supply-chain history |
| Cost / TCO (5%) | Pricing basis (percentage of spend, tiers, free), operations burden |
| Lock-in / portability (15%) | Whether allocation rules and history can be exported in an open schema |

### C6.7 Product deep dives

**Gateway-native and provider-native cost attribution (pattern).**
- *What it is now:* the gateway issues virtual keys per team, project or user and records token usage and cost per request, enabling budgets and multi-tenant spend reports; provider admin APIs supply organisation-level usage and cost for reconciliation [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S010: litellm on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / BerriAI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07]. Example implementations as of 7 October 2026: LiteLLM 1.104.1 (MIT core), the Portkey SDK 2.3.4 and Anthropic's Usage & Cost Admin API [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S010: litellm on PyPI (JSON API) (PyPI / BerriAI) <https://pypi.org/pypi/litellm/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S081: portkey-ai on PyPI (PyPI / Portkey) <https://pypi.org/pypi/portkey-ai/json> accessed 2026-10-07; A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07]. The gateway products are profiled in C1.
- *Implementations and controls:* LiteLLM Enterprise adds SSO, RBAC, SCIM and audit logs of key, team, user and model changes [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S007: LiteLLM pricing / Enterprise / Audit Logs docs (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://www.litellm.ai/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. It announced an updated SOC 2 Type 2 report in September 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A6-S108: Our Updated SOC 2 Type 2 Report Is Available; LiteLLM + Vanta: SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 Recertification; Data Privacy and Security; Trust Center (BerriAI (LiteLLM)) <https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/soc2-type-2-report> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. There have been six public releases since v0.5 in June 2023, on a semi-annual cadence [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S049: FOCUS Specification CHANGELOG (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS Working Group)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/working_draft/CHANGELOG.md> accessed 2026-10-07]. focus-validator 2.2.1 was released on 5 August 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S050: focus-validator on PyPI (PyPI / FinOps Foundation) <https://pypi.org/pypi/focus-validator/json> accessed 2026-10-07].

FOCUS 1.5 has no ratification date. Its confirmed AI scope is pricing dimensions on SkuPriceDetails and four model properties (ModelDeveloper, ModelFamily, ModelId, ModelVersion), with no new columns. A first-class input/output token-type column is deferred, not rejected; the split stays in separate SKUs distinguished by SkuMeter [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S046: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope: Confirmed and Stretch Features (with Introducing FOCUS 1.4; FOCUS for AI) (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]].

(FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]].
- *Strengths:* the only neutral schema available; it keeps the cost dataset independent of any tool [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Limitations:* it is a data model, not a control; AI fields are still in progress [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — V2-S046: FOCUS 1.5 Release Scope: Confirmed and Stretch Features (with Introducing FOCUS 1.4; FOCUS for AI) (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS)) <https://focus.finops.org/focus-1-5-release-scope/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Adoption by AI providers is not publicly verified [NPV]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Choose when:* always, as the target schema [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Avoid when:* not applicable; do not wait for 1.5 before starting [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Competitors:* Vantage and CloudZero proprietary schemas; gateway-native data models.
- *FS note:* a FOCUS-shaped dataset makes provider spend comparable for concentration analysis and the outsourcing register [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- **Tier: Strategic. No flag.**

### C6.9 Decision tree

Steps 0 and 4 are not product choices; they apply whatever is selected [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

```text
STEP 0 [Rec] (not optional): define the unit. For each use case, name the task, its outcome
states (approved / edited / rejected) and its business owner. Report cost per completed task.

STEP 1 [Rec]: Metering point
  Is all model traffic routed through a gateway (C1)?
  ├─ Yes → Gateway metering: virtual key per use case (+ per fund / segment if chargeback);
  │        run_id in request metadata; budgets + RPM/TPM limits per key
  └─ No  → Fix that first (C1). Interim: cloud-native tags
           (Bedrock application inference profiles; Foundry project tags) + provider usage APIs

STEP 2 [Rec]: Record of cost
  Build a firm-owned, FOCUS-shaped AI cost dataset:
  tokens → SKU + ConsumedUnit/ConsumedQuantity now; add ModelId/ModelVersion when 1.5 ratifies.
  Join gateway rows to L9 traces on run_id → cost per task / per approved output.

STEP 3 [Rec]: Reporting and chargeback layer
  Is Vantage or CloudZero already the cloud FinOps tool?
  ├─ Vantage   → add AI integrations + Managed AI Tags; feed it gateway exports
  ├─ CloudZero → add AI integrations; document allocation rules outside the tool
  └─ Neither   → BI on the FOCUS dataset is enough; do not buy a tool for AI alone
  Helicone → do not adopt; migrate existing use.

STEP 4 [Rec]: Checks before go-live
  Budget exceeded in test → requests refused (fail closed)?  Admin key restricted?
  Per-run step and token ceiling in L3?  Anomaly alert on retries / tool calls per task?
  Monthly reconciliation to invoice within tolerance?  Optimisations routed via C5 + L9?
```

### C6.11 Regulated FS lens (POV 2)

**Operational resilience: budgets are a resilience control.**
- *Unbounded consumption.* The OWASP 2025 list includes Unbounded Consumption (LLM10), cited for traceability [R]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Reported — A8-S040: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-llm-applications-2025/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]; the operative lists are now the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 and the Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-OWASP-LLM: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (superseded by the OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); V2-S056: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026 (with press release 'OWASP GenAI Security Project Unveils 2026 Top 10 for LLM Applications, New Agent Control Standard', URL dated 2 <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-genai-llm-top-10-2026/> accessed 2026-10-08 [search-tool extract]; R-OWASP-AGENTIC: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S042: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 (launched 9-10 December 2025) (OWASP GenAI Security Project) <https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Runaway agents are both a cost and an availability risk, because they can exhaust shared provider rate limits and starve other services (C6.2) [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *DORA.* DORA requires an ICT risk-management framework with ongoing monitoring that extends to services from ICT third parties [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Spend and rate-limit controls on AI providers belong in that framework, with tested enforcement [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Important business services.* Where an AI service supports an important business service, separate keys and limits per service stop a low-priority workload from consuming the capacity a critical one needs [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Model risk: cost optimisation is a model change.**
- *SS1/23.* SS1/23 covers vendor models used to inform business decisions and expects development, implementation and use to be controlled [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS123: PRA Supervisory Statement SS1/23 'Model risk management principles for banks' (published with PS6/23) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S008: SS1/23 Model risk management principles for banks (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2023/may/model-risk-management-principles-for-banks-ss> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S037: Bank of England/PRA letter to DSIT and HMT on AI (2024) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/letter/2024/dsit-hmt-letter.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Routing a step to a cheaper model, trimming the context or turning on a cache changes the system's behaviour [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Cost optimisations therefore go through C5 change control and the L9 eval gate, and material ones through re-validation [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *SR 26-2.* SR 26-2 excludes generative and agentic AI and leaves their governance to the firm's own practices [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-US-MRM: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management: Federal Reserve SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13 / FDIC FIL-15-2026 (supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S001: SR 26-2: Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management (17 April 2026) (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System) <https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S002: OCC Bulletin 2026-13 Model Risk Management: Revised Guidance (attachment bulletin-2026-13a.pdf) (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency) <https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/bulletins/2026/bulletin-2026-13.html> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The firm's own standard should state that no cost-driven model change bypasses validation [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Outsourcing registers and concentration.**
- *Registers.* DORA requires a register of information covering all ICT third-party arrangements; competent authorities report registers to the ESAs annually by 31 March from 2026 (reference date 31 December) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. PRA PS7/26 and FCA PS26/2 require notification of material third-party arrangements and an annual register from 18 March 2027 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); R-FCA-SYSC8: FCA Handbook SYSC 8 (Outsourcing); FG16/5 'Guidance for firms outsourcing to the cloud and other third-party IT services'; PS26/2 operational incident and third-party reporting (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S062: PS7/26 Operational incident and third-party reporting (PRA) and FCA PS26/2; revised SS2/21 (March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA; FCA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/prudential-regulation/publication/2026/march/operational-incident-and-third-party-reporting-policy-statement> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Spend per AI provider, from the FOCUS-shaped dataset, is one of the inputs to materiality and to these registers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Concentration.* IOSCO flags concentration risk from reliance on a few AI technology providers [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-INTL-AI-ASSETMGMT: IOSCO Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (FR/02/2026) and ESMA Public Statement on AI and investment services (30 May 2024) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S058: IOSCO FR/02/2026 Supervisory Toolkit for AI Use in Capital Markets (May 2026) <https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD823.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The provider-concentration KPI (C6.3) makes that risk measurable [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. DORA and the UK CTP regime designate hyperscalers but no model vendor [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-DORA: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S021: Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) pages and RoI reporting FAQ (ESMA / EBA / EIOPA) <https://www.esma.europa.eu/esmas-activities/digital-finance-and-innovation/digital-operational-resilience-act-dora> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; R-UK-CTP: UK Critical Third Parties regime (FSMA 2023 / FSMA 2000 s312L; PRA/FCA/BoE CTP rules) and the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S023: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (SI 2026/777); BoE/FCA/HMT announcements (HM Treasury / legislation.gov.uk / Bank of England) <https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/777/made> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], so oversight of direct model-vendor spend falls on the firm [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Exit sizing.* SS2/21 expects documented and tested exit plans [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-PRA-SS221: PRA SS2/21 'Outsourcing and third party risk management' (revised by PS7/26, March 2026) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S048: SS2/21 Outsourcing and third party risk management (and PS7/26, March 2026) (Bank of England / PRA) <https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/prudential-regulation/supervisory-statement/2021/ss221-march-21.pdf> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Cost per task by model is what lets the firm price the fallback route in its exit plan [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Cost allocation to funds is a conduct question.**
- Charging AI costs to funds, rather than to the management company, is a fund-documentation and conduct decision, not a FinOps one [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Chargeback to funds should be agreed with compliance and fund governance before it is built; showback by fund is safe to build first [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Residency, security and auditability.**
- *Cost tools see metadata.* Provider usage data is keyed by API key, workspace and model [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S070: Usage and Cost Admin API (Claude Platform docs) (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-cost-api> accessed 2026-10-07]; it should not carry prompts or client data, and exports to SaaS cost tools should be checked for that [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Admin credentials.* A third-party cost tool holding a provider admin key with read-write access is a privileged-access risk [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S113: Vantage blog: Managed AI Tags; Support for Anthropic Costs; Support for Claude Enterprise Costs; OpenAI cost tools <https://www.vantage.sh/blog/managed-ai-tags> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Treat it under C4 and C7, and list the tool in the register of information [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- *Evidence.* The cost record for each regulated output (cost per commentary, model mix, retries) should sit in the same evidence pack as the trace and approval (C8), so that unusual cost can be investigated alongside unusual behaviour [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**Standards and guidance.**
- The FinOps Framework 2026 adds a FinOps for AI category, and FOCUS is the open data standard [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A7-S048: FOCUS Specification README (FinOps Foundation (FOCUS Working Group)) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FinOps-Open-Cost-and-Usage-Spec/FOCUS_Spec/working_draft/README.md> accessed 2026-10-07].
- NIST AI RMF 1.0 and AI 600-1 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-NIST-AIRMF: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1) and Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S043: AI Risk Management Framework (NIST AI 100-1) and revision status <https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]; A8-S044: NIST AI 600-1 Generative AI Profile; NCCoE agent identity concept paper; CAISI agent security <https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] and ISO/IEC 42001 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — R-ISO-42001: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management systems; ISO/IEC 42005:2025 AI system impact assessment; ISO/IEC 42006:2025 requirements for AIMS audit and certification bodies (see regulatory_facts.json); A8-S045: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management systems <https://www.iso.org/standard/42001> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] provide the management-system frame into which AI cost governance fits; neither prescribes cost controls [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
- The EU AI Act sets no cost-specific obligation for deployers [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

### C6.12 Worked-example slice (POV 3)

**What the commentary agent needs from C6 [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.** The agent drafts the monthly Brinson-style attribution commentary for a generic multi-asset fund, with a human approval gate. From this control it needs five things:
1. **Cost per commentary and per fund.** Each fund's commentary run has a run ID. The gateway tags every call with `use_case=attribution-commentary`, the fund code and the run ID, and the L9 trace groups the drafting call, the judge calls and any regenerations. The reported unit is cost per approved commentary, per fund per month.
2. **A worked cost model (illustrative arithmetic).** Assume one draft uses about 40,000 input tokens (attribution output, retrieved prior commentary, style guide and prompt) and 3,000 output tokens. At US$2 input and US$10 output per 1M tokens, which is the list price of both Claude Sonnet 5.5 and gpt-6.1-sol as of 7 October 2026 [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S004: OpenAI API Pricing (and Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna pricing) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]], one draft costs about US$0.08 + US$0.03 = US$0.11. Three judge calls of about 10,000 input and 500 output tokens on a small model at US$0.10/US$0.50 per 1M (Claude Haiku 5.5 or gpt-6-luna list prices) [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S004: OpenAI API Pricing (and Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna pricing) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] add under US$0.01. With an average of 2.5 drafts per approved commentary, the token cost is roughly US$0.30 per approved commentary, or about US$12 a month for 40 funds. The token figures and the arithmetic are the author's own [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. The conclusion is that tokens are not the cost driver here; reviewer time is, so the metric that matters is the regeneration and edit rate [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
3. **A monthly budget.** Measure for two month-end cycles, then set the budget at 110% to 120% of the baseline with alerts at 80% and 100%, as the FinOps Foundation recommends [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. Experimental work on new prompts uses a separate key and budget [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A7-S115: FinOps Framework 2026; State of FinOps 2026; FinOps for AI technology category; Tokenomics working group; Who sets the AI budget? (FinOps Foundation) <https://www.finops.org/insights/2026-finops-framework/> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]] [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
4. **Alerts on anomalous agent loops.** A per-run ceiling in the L3 workflow (for example 6 model calls and 150,000 tokens per fund; illustrative) fails the run and pages the owner. The gateway key has an RPM and TPM limit sized for month-end peaks, and a budget tested to fail closed. Alerts fire on drafts per fund above 3, tool calls per run above the workflow's fixed count, or any call outside the month-end window [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.
5. **Optimisation, under change control.** Month-end drafting is reviewed the next morning, so the batch APIs (50% off) fit [VF]{custom-style="Claim Label"}^[Verified fact — A5-S011: Pricing - Claude API Docs (Anthropic) <https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07; A5-S004: OpenAI API Pricing (and Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna pricing) <https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing> accessed 2026-10-07 [search-tool extract]]. The style guide and system prompt are stable and placed first, so prompt caching applies [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}. Moving the judge calls to a smaller model, or switching to batch, is a C5 change and passes the L9 regression suite before release [Rec]{custom-style="Claim Label"}.

**What C6 must never allow [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:**
- a cost-driven model or prompt change released without the L9 eval gate and C5 approval
- semantic caching of commentary text, which could return last month's narrative
- a budget that alerts but cannot block, on the commentary key
- the commentary sharing a key or rate limit with exploratory work
- chargeback of AI costs to fund expenses without compliance and fund-governance approval
- cost exports that contain client data or draft text

**Relevant hypothesis: H1 (the gateway is promoted to a control-plane component). Provisional view; verdict in synthesis.**

The evidence supports H1 from the cost side [AJ]{custom-style="Claim Label"}:
